architecture.responsibility: Runs on the user's own machine, cheapest arm first: Arm 0 activation from transcripts ($0, minutes: which artifacts were eligible / loaded complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store / read / followed-proxy, per Claude Code ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl, Hermes .usage.json + skill_ledger, ECC observations, OpenViking memory_diff); Arm 1 paired sandbox replay on sessions whose terminal verification is re-executable (git snapshot + sandbox re-execution, externals served from the recording, A-vs-A' floor, 3-5 replays, matched budget for the without-store arm); Arm 2 sealed held-out on tasks mined from the user's history (SkillOpt-Sleep miner pattern) with store-at-t reconstruction from ledger hashes; outputs per-artifact keep / never-loaded / loaded-but-ignored / regresses / unknown-needs-N-more with cost printed; opt-in aggregate upload of numbers only.
architecture.interfaces: `turnstile audit --claude-code|--hermes|--ecc|--openviking [--replay] [--sealed]`; reads stores read-only; never uploads content

architecture.responsibility: One JSON record for candidate / evidence / verdict / disposition / activation / cost / rung / closure, expressed as a profile over existing standards (in-toto Statement v1 + DSSE so cosign/Rekor verify it, OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result attributes, Every Eval Ever instance-level fields incl. candidatesCompared/candidatesCleared selection denominator); converters from the 12 incompatible formats (OpenClaw evaluator envelope, Claude Code aggregate-result.json schemaVersion 1, agentskills evals.json, SEA certificate, Hermes skill_ledger JSONL, Prime refinements.jsonl, Reef release events, SkillOpt evidence.jsonl, AHE change_manifest, Meta-Harness evolution_summary.jsonl, Continual Harness evolution_log.jsonl, autoresearch results.tsv).
architecture.interfaces: `turnstile ledger convert --from <fmt>`; JSON Schema published; proposed as an `evidence/` convention inside a SKILL.md bundle

architecture.responsibility: Static site with two tracks (gate track: acceptor adapters run against streams; loop track: whole loops run multi-generation on a Harbor stream with sealed held-out, BWT/FWT, safety decay, cost) plus an audit registry (aggregate opt-in audit statistics, no user data); submissions are PRs carrying receipts and pinned versions; sealed streams rotate per release with public generators and hidden seeds; matched-budget parallel-K and 'do not evolve' rows always present as baselines.
architecture.interfaces: `turnstile submit`; GitHub PR template; Harbor task family versioned; results as EEE-compatible JSONL

acceptor-benchmark.integration_surface: Turnstile never lives on the hot path of a harness; it attaches at the seams that already exist and reads the stores that already exist. CLAUDE CODE (the builder's own harness, first adapter): SessionStart and InstructionsLoaded hooks emit a per-session load receipt (which CLAUDE.md / MEMORY.md / skills resolved, store identity + hash, bytes available vs loaded, complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store) which is the $0 activation arm and the fix for #82056's indistinguishable failure modes; UserPromptSubmit tags human turns as trusted origin for provenance taint; PreToolUse with permissionDecision on writes under the memory/skills dirs stages the write as a candidate (ask/deny/allow) and updatedInput serves recorded inputs during cassette replay; PostToolUse updatedToolOutput serves recorded results for EXTERNAL and NONDETERMINISTIC calls during replay (verified on 2.1.258, $0.007/replay); Stop closes the cassette, records the terminal verification and runs the cheap lint arm; `claude plugin eval` is wrapped as the consumer for the with/without arms (isolated home, history_file resume from a cassette prefix, runs=3, `--json` schemaVersion 1 converted into evidence records; its per-case threshold, haiku judge and lack of sequential stats are exactly what Turnstile's scorer adds on top). HERMES: the pending queue (~/.hermes/pending/{skills,memory}/<id>.json) is a candidate source and `/skills approve|reject` the disposition sink; a plugin registered via ctx.register_hook runs Turnstile-ref as the approver with a default disposition so only holds reach the human; `pre_tool_call` (fail-closed) enforces path-level authority so write_file/patch/terminal cannot bypass skill_manage; the curator's YAML summary is reconciled against the ledger; skill_ledger JSONL (sha256 before/after manifests) and .usage.json feed the audit and the real-ledger stream; the RFC in #96704 (evals/skills/, three arms, activation-only arm first) is the landing zone. OPENCLAW: a `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin receives the candidate BundleSnapshot + baseline with tree hashes, runs lint + canary + (optionally) sealed paired eval, returns {evaluatorVersion, mode: "baseline-comparison", decision: pass|revise|block, metrics, findings}; because only a completed `block` vetoes and error/skipped fail open, the plugin converts its own timeouts/failures into an explicit block when policy is fail-closed; `skill_proposal_changed` / `skill_changed` events with expectedRevisionHash and correlationId are the ledger source; `before_tool_call` (block:true terminal) covers direct edits in auto mode. DEEPSEEK HARNESS: a dsh plugin on tools/pre-execute (typed allow/deny/ask) and tools/post-execute (accept/block/replace/attach) plus agent/turn-stopping, using the hook-protocol bridge so the same Claude Code/Codex hooks.json runs unchanged; the deny-only guard rule is respected (listener order cannot resurrect a denied write); Cordis revertible effects give atomic rollback of a rejected runtime self-modification; the zstd session log ('model-visible <=> logged') is the cassette source. PI / PRIME AGENT: `session_before_refine` intercepts the planner's refinement plan and routes each edit through accept(); pi tool_call (block) and tool_result (modify) provide the write gate and replay injection; harness_state.json versions with before/after snapshots and refinements.jsonl are ledger sources, which also makes '/refine is invisible' (#1208/#684) a rendered diff feed. REEF: Turnstile ships `decide` as a PACE-style e-process with per-task floor and `evaluate` as the sealed paired evaluator with control arm, drop-in for the recipe API (propose(nodes, samples, models, manifest, rejected, sources, requests) -> Mutation; evaluate; decide publishes iff clears); the immutable release chain and x-reef-agent-record-id receipts are stream and activation sources; the benchmark spec answers #357 and the reference pipeline #358. GEPA/DSPy, SkillOpt, Self-Harness, auto-harness, agentdescent: acceptor adapters at their existing call-sites (custom proposer / gate function / run_acceptance_gate.py / gating.py / AcceptancePolicy). CODEX: PostToolUse block/replace and Stop; memories dir read for the audit (Codex memories have no seam, so audit-only). HARBOR: streams and the protected corpus are Harbor task families so six CLIs plug in as one-line adapters and Reef #447's record-to-task converter feeds real tasks. Everything is off by default except recording and the $0 audit arm; blocking is opt-in per surface.

acceptor-benchmark.killer_demo: Five minutes, on the presenter's own laptop, with only API keys. Minute 0-1: `pipx install turnstile && turnstile audit --claude-code`. It reads ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl and the memory/skills dirs with zero model calls and prints a table of every learned artifact: created-by (auto-memory / skill-creator / hand-written), age, sessions eligible -> loaded (complete / truncated / not_loaded / wrong_store) -> read. Typical lines: 'MEMORY.md: loaded TRUNCATED in 14/31 sessions (index 31 KB > 25 KB cap); the 9 newest entries never reached the model'; 'skills/chrome-devtools: eligible in 6 sessions, Skill tool_use in 0'. Forty seconds, $0. Minute 1-3: `turnstile audit --replay --sessions 12`. For the 12 sessions whose final verification (the tests the user ran) is re-executable, it restores the git snapshot, replays with-store vs without-store at matched budget, 3 replays each, externals served from the recording, plus an A-vs-A' floor; live tri-state bars fill in. Result line: 'with-store 9.3 +/- 0.6 of 12, without-store 9.0 +/- 1.0, A-vs-A' floor +/- 1.2 -> INCONCLUSIVE (needs ~28 more sessions); attributed: skills/pytest-flow helps (+2 tasks, 3/3), memory line #47 regresses test_hooks (2/3 confirmed); cost $4.10'. Minute 3-5: `turnstile bench --acceptors greedy,skillopt-gate,reef-decide,pace,turnstile-ref --streams null,regress,unsafe,tamper --budget 40`. A confusion matrix fills in live: greedy strict-> commits 44% of null candidates, SkillOpt's strict held-out gate 38% at its native n=1 slice, Reef's W/L margin 31%, PACE 4% (but MIR at +10pp 61%, shown honestly), Turnstile-ref 3%; on the regression stream Reef lets the 'close ALL Chrome windows' edit through in 3 of 5 seeds because the pooled tally hides the flipped task; on the tamper stream every acceptor whose evaluator the candidate can reach (auto-harness gating.py, greedy) accepts 5/5 forged results, only sealed-evaluator gates block; on the unsafe stream scanner-only acceptors admit ~40/40 laundered payloads (the MLAS finding, reproduced) and the canary blocks 37/40 at 96 probes per candidate. Last screen: evals-per-decision on the x-axis with a 'do not evolve, spend the evals on parallel-K' line, the leaderboard URL, and `turnstile submit`.
acceptor-benchmark.research_contribution: TITLE: 'Judge the Gate, Not the Agent: Benchmarking the Acceptors of Self-Modifying Agents and Auditing What They Kept'. CLAIMS: (C1, gate track) Under planted ground truth and a sealed paired evaluator with a same-config control arm, the acceptors shipped in the field's most-used self-improvement loops (strict-improvement on a noisy split: SkillOpt, Self-Harness, Reef, auto-harness, GEPA minibatch; LLM-judge: Hermes background review, Prime refine, SkillClaw-style; scanner-only: Hermes/OpenClaw regex) commit 30-45% of null candidates and 40-100% of planted-regression candidates at their native budgets, admit nearly all laundered unsafe artifacts, and are tamper-blind wherever the candidate can reach the evaluator; a paired anytime-valid gate with a k-of-n protected floor, activation smoke and a safety canary attains FCR <= alpha, HCR_regression < 10%, HCR_unsafe < 10% at fewer evaluations per decision than fixed-n testing, at the price of a reported, bucketed missed-improvement rate at small lifts. (C2, loop track) Over G=15 generations, gating with C1's reference acceptor is the difference between harness-induced forgetting (negative BWT) plus safety decay and a flat-or-positive BWT with no safety decay, and neither gated nor ungated loops beat matched-budget parallel-K by more than the control-arm noise on the sealed slice. (C3, audit) For >= 10 consenting production stores (Hermes, ECC, OpenViking, Claude Code memory), the matched-budget counterfactual lift of the store is indistinguishable from the A-vs-A' floor for the majority of stores; where lift exists it is concentrated in < 20% of artifacts and is predicted by activation rate; a large fraction of artifacts are never loaded or loaded truncated. EXPERIMENT: 12+ acceptors x 6 stream families (null, planted-regression, planted-unsafe, planted-tamper, planted-overfit, cached-real-good) x 2 consumers (Claude Code, Hermes) x 5 seeds on a 40-task protected Harbor corpus plus a sealed rotating held-out slice; loop track with 5 loops x G=15 x 3 seeds; audit with temporal store-at-t split, 3-5 replays, tri-state outcomes. BASELINES: greedy strict-> (n=1, n=2), fixed-n McNemar, online-FDR, LLM-judge-only, regex-scanner-only, human-queue (always hold), PACE as published, parallel-K and sequential-K test-time scaling at matched rollouts, 'do not evolve'. FALSIFIERS: C1 is false if the shipped strict-improvement acceptors show FCR <= 10% on the null stream and HCR_regression <= 10% at native budget, or if the reference gate offers no Pareto improvement (its extra MIR at +10pp exceeds its FCR/HCR savings at matched evals-per-decision); C2 is false if ungated loops show no worse BWT or safety decay than gated ones across seeds, or if gated loops beat parallel-K by more than 2x the control noise (then harness evolution is a design premium, not a search premium, and the paper says so); C3 is false if >= half of the audited stores show lift > 2x the A-vs-A' floor at matched budget. Pre-registered before the full matrix runs; all ledgers, streams, receipts and generators released; sealed seeds escrowed and rotated.
acceptor-benchmark.adoption_path: Follow the one exception to 'adoption is anti-correlated with gating': gates spread when they are registry-side, free to the user, and off the hot path (ClawHub scanning reached a 389k-star ecosystem within weeks). Step 1, land where the demand already exists in writing: SkillOpt #155 (maintainers endorsed an agentic replay backend twice with three binding requirements we satisfy: pass/fail/inconclusive, execution off by default, worktree is not a security boundary; a contributor volunteered, a draft PR is welcomed), Reef #357/#358 (benchmark spec + reference pipeline opened 2026-09-09 with zero comments, asking explicitly to distinguish committed from used artifacts and to define repetition and variability reporting; we supply the spec and a decide/evaluate recipe PR), Hermes #96704 (community RFC for evals/skills/ with three arms and 'the cheapest arm needs no model runs'; we ship Arm 0 in-tree). Step 2, be the first third-party implementer of OpenClaw's skill_proposal_evaluate seam (zero exist as of 2026-09-14) and the first dsh plugin in the evaluator slot dsh explicitly deferred; both run one policy engine, so every result is comparable across substrates. Step 3, the practitioner wedge: the $0 audit arm answers the most-filed user complaints (Claude Code #82056 loaded/truncated/wrong-store, Hermes #12238 'track how my agent evolved', Prime #1208 '/refine is invisible') without any model call, so it is installable as a Claude Code plugin and a Hermes command with no cost objection; the paired-replay arm is opt-in and prints its cost. Step 4, the research wedge: release streams, corpora and receipts on Harbor so every harness-evolution paper can add a Turnstile row for free; make the matched-budget parallel-K and 'do not evolve' rows unavoidable so reviewers ask for them; submit to the RSI workshop / NeurIPS D&B and file the in-toto artifact-acceptance predicate next to #554 and an `evidence/` convention PR to agentskills.io so registries have a field to display. Step 5, the leaderboard: acceptors submit adapters, not scores; we run them under sealed rotating streams and publish receipts, which is why Reef, SkillOpt, agentdescent and Hermes have a reason to submit (a dominated row is embarrassing but a fixed row is free marketing). Language: Python core (Hermes, GEPA, SkillOpt, agentdescent are Python), TypeScript shims only where the seam is TS (OpenClaw, dsh, pi); MIT license; no proxy, no config mutation, no writes to any store unless a blocking policy is explicitly enabled.

nearest_competitors.name: PACE (arXiv 2606.08106)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: PACE is a gate and evaluates only its own prompt-evolution loop on 0.5B-3B Qwen with binary GSM8K outcomes and no code; its two regimes (planted improvement among noise, no-real-gain stochastic) and its greedy 30-42% false-commit number are the seed of our null and good streams. Turnstile benchmarks ANY acceptor (PACE included) on real harness artifacts inside real consuming agents, adds regression/unsafe/tamper/overfit families, phantom accepts, cost per decision, multi-generation retention, and releases the corpora; PACE's per-candidate alpha is extended with a run-level CTHS spend and per-task floors in our reference gate.

nearest_competitors.name: SEA: Self-Evolving Agents with Anytime-Valid Certificates (2607.00871)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SEA is one loop with certificates, no public code, and its harness-edit gate ALG4 accepted zero edits at ~50 tasks and was switched off. We reuse its certificate schema and spend schedule, but our object is the acceptor's measured confusion matrix, and our design rule (accumulate evidence across cheap rounds, hold not reject on budget exhaustion, continue post-acceptance) is a direct response to SEA's failure mode.

nearest_competitors.name: Causal Agent Replay (2606.08275)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: CAR is a record-replay attribution debugger for failures, mocked tools only, and its CI-gated locus rule abstains ~80% on real traces. We use its intervention vocabulary and its abstention discipline, but replay sandbox-first with real side-effectful tools (git snapshot + re-execution, externals served from the recording), for gating and auditing rather than failure localization.

nearest_competitors.name: The Replay Gap (2608.08239)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A measurement that log-stitched replay is invalid (3-8% state validity for early forks). We adopt its control arm and fork-position lessons and then measure the middle case it did not: harness edits (smaller than model swaps) under branched re-execution, with the divergence point reported as 'behavior changed' rather than as a fitness signal.

nearest_competitors.name: Counterfactual Trace Auditing (2605.11946)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: CTA pairs with/without-skill traces on 49 SWE-Skills-Bench tasks, r=1, and its own replication found its divergence detectors fire identically on A-vs-A' pairs and 0/34 runs read the skill. We take the pipeline shape and the null-floor lesson, require r>=3 and uptake verification before any effect claim, and generalize from one skill on one benchmark to any artifact in any consumer, including the user's own store.

nearest_competitors.name: SkillMisevo-Gym / SafeEvolve (2608.12851)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: The closest in spirit: a lifecycle gym with adapters for Claude Code/Codex/OpenClaw/Hermes measuring unsafe artifact authoring across 6 evolution methods, code not surfaced. It scores the evolution METHOD's safety; Turnstile scores the ACCEPTOR's confusion matrix on capability, noise, tamper and cost axes as well as safety, adopts its clean-session probe protocol as the unsafe stream's verifier, and its GovernableStore hook contract as one of our consumer adapters.

nearest_competitors.name: Reef (Human-Agent-Society/reef)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Reef is release infrastructure with a propose->paired-evaluate->decide contract, a pooled W/L margin, one-step rollback and no benchmark (#357/#358 open, zero comments). Turnstile is the benchmark Reef asked for and ships a decide/evaluate recipe pair; Reef's pooled tally is one of the acceptors we measure (and #356's masked seed-suite regressions are a stream we plant).

nearest_competitors.name: SkillOpt / SkillOpt-Sleep (microsoft/SkillOpt)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SkillOpt's strict held-out gate prevented a 0.554->0.026 collapse and was Goodharted in the same run (#154/#175); its evalkit has McNemar + bootstrap CIs the gate ignores, gate_no_regression is opt-in, and replay is single-turn text. We benchmark its gate as shipped, plant its documented failures as streams, and deliver the AgenticReplayBackend its maintainers specified in #155 (tri-state outcomes, execution off by default).

nearest_competitors.name: agentdescent (Birfy/agentdescent)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A Beta-posterior gate with a hard regression guard, in-process, whose default 'oracle' is the same eval_fn on the same held-out set and whose trust signal pinned at 1.0 with zero audits. We adopt its full-held-out invariant and kappa discount, then measure it as one submitted acceptor against sealed streams it cannot see, including a tamper stream its declared blast radius cannot detect.

nearest_competitors.name: auto-harness (neosigmaai/auto-harness)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A CLI gate (gating.py exit 0/1) whose best score, regression suite, config and PROGRAM.md live in the agent's writable surface. We measure exactly that: it is the canonical tamper-blind acceptor in our matrix, and our receipts + sealed evaluator are the drop-in that makes its ratchet honest.

nearest_competitors.name: Hermes Agent (NousResearch)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: The largest deployed learning loop with no outcome evaluation, a scanner that let 40/40 laundered payloads persist (MLAS), a loop silently dead for weeks (#95976), and a community RFC (#96704) for a paired-arm harness. Hermes is an audit target and its scanner+curator+write_approval pipeline is an acceptor row; we land the RFC's Arm 0 in-tree rather than building a competing loop.

nearest_competitors.name: Prime Agent (/refine, harness_state)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Typed, versioned, snapshotted supplemental state with no fitness, expectedOutcome never checked, and '/refine is invisible' closed unfixed. Its refinements.jsonl is a ledger source, its review gate an acceptor row, and the audit renders the diff feed users asked for.

nearest_competitors.name: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: No learning loop and an evaluator slot the authors consciously deferred pending 'authority, isolation, and provider contract'. Turnstile's dsh plugin occupies that slot on tools/pre-execute + post-execute with the hook-protocol bridge, so the same policy runs under Claude Code, Codex and dsh; dsh's replayable session log is a cassette source.

nearest_competitors.name: HarnessDev (2609.01437) / EvoHarnessBench (2609.04280) / AI2 Rethinking (2607.12227) / RSI-Exam
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: All score the agent or the harness after evolution and need expensive sealed agent runs (HarnessDev's 73 versions and 26,679 trajectories are unreleased; EvoHarnessBench runs only through a hosted SDK; RSI-Exam is a one-shot terminal exam). We reuse their protocol pieces (score-path isolation, BWT/FWT, matched-budget parallel-K, two-image sealing) and turn them on the acceptor per candidate, self-hosted on Harbor, at 50-100x lower cost per decision measured; HarnessDev's skipped counterfactual (apply a noise-aware held-out gate to its 73 versions) is a stream once its corpus is released.

nearest_competitors.name: Claude Code `claude plugin eval` (v2.1.269)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A first-party paired with/without evaluator with per-case thresholds, a haiku judge, no sequential statistics, no sealed split and a case format its own docs call incompatible with skill-creator's. We wrap it as the Claude Code consumer arm, convert aggregate-result.json into acceptance records, and add the statistics, control arm, receipts and cross-substrate comparability it lacks.

nearest_competitors.name: HackProbe (2609.04665) / PROCTOR (2609.02246) / Blind Curator (2607.07436)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Detectors and rules for reward hacking and judge failure, none with public code. We treat them as components (probe bank as a harmful stream, mechanical-override as a design rule, judge false-pass cliff as a reported metric) rather than as competing benchmarks.

risks: Label validity: 'neutral' paraphrases can change LLM behavior and 'good' labels rest on 5-seed sealed estimates on 40 tasks; mitigated by verifying neutrality with 5/5 agreement on the protected corpus, bucketing lift, and reporting 'real-unlabeled' separately, but a reviewer can still argue the planted streams are too easy or too artificial.

Benchmark Goodhart: an acceptor can be tuned to the public stream generators; mitigated by hidden seeds, per-release rotation, receipts on submissions and adapter-not-score submissions, but a leaderboard that matters invites gaming and we will be a small team policing it.

Consumer coupling: an acceptor's confusion matrix is a property of the (acceptor, consumer harness, model) triple (Lin et al.), so results do not transfer across harness versions that change weekly (Hermes 947 commits in four days, dsh 14 tags in 12 days); adapters will rot and rows must be re-run per pinned version.

Cost creep: the null and tamper streams are cheap, but sealed paired evaluation with control arms and multi-generation loop runs are not; if the full matrix drifts above a few hundred dollars per acceptor, submissions stop; the Pareto x-axis must include our own overhead honestly.

Abstention dominance: CAR abstained ~80% at K<=8 and SEA's gate accepted nothing at ~50 tasks; the audit may return 'inconclusive' for most stores, which is scientifically correct but reads as a non-result to practitioners; the tri-state output and 'needs N more sessions' estimate are the mitigation, not a cure.

Replayability: on the builder's machine the idempotent prefix was 0-1 calls per session; sandbox-first replay handles workspace ops but sessions dominated by external/nondeterministic calls will be non-replayable, shrinking the audit's paired arm to a biased subset of sessions.

Privacy and consent: user stores and cassettes hold secrets and private code; the audit runs locally and uploads numbers only, but recruiting >= 10 consenting stores for the paper and releasing any real-ledger stream requires scrubbing and legal care; a single leak would end adoption.

Political reception: a benchmark that reports Reef/SkillOpt/Hermes acceptors as dominated, and an audit that says most stores are placebo, will not be welcomed by every maintainer; the mitigation is to land inside their own open threads first, publish adapters they can fix, and keep a 'fixed' row free.

Safety-canary overfit and judge circularity: the same models that author artifacts judge them; cross-family judges, mechanical overrides and hidden probe rotation help, but 'More Convincing, Not More Correct' shows judge exploits survive ensembles; the canary is a regression test, not a proof.

Scope temptation: the practitioner lens lists ten adjacent gaps (undo, ownership, spend caps, approval UX, DLP); each is real and each would dilute a 1-3 person team; Turnstile must ship load receipts and the audit but must not become the harness-management suite.
open_questions: What is the right per-candidate alpha versus run-level spend for an archive that proposes hundreds of candidates, and should the leaderboard fix alpha or let acceptors choose and report certificate validity at their chosen level?
How many protected tasks with observed stability >= 0.9 exist in real coding streams, and does the A-vs-A' control arm give a stable per-task noise estimate at 3 replays, or is 5 the floor?
Are paraphrase-preserving edits ever truly neutral for a frozen LLM consumer, or must the null stream be restricted to byte-identical and ordering changes?

Does the $0 activation arm (loaded/read from transcripts) predict paired-replay lift well enough to be a triage signal, or is 'loaded but ignored' the dominant state (CTA 0/34, Lin 25% load rate) so that activation alone says little?

What fraction of real user sessions are replayable to a decision point under sandbox-first replay, and does the divergence-point distribution for real refiner edits sit closer to the VCR-naive or the Replay-Gap-hopeless end?

Can memory entries (free-text lines in MEMORY.md/CLAUDE.md, Codex memories) be gated with the same streams as skills, or do they need a memory-specific canary and activation detector since no vendor exposes a memory seam?

Should the audit run inside each harness (as Hermes #96704 proposes for evals/skills/) or outside as a cross-harness tool reading stores read-only, given the practitioner demand for one contract across Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, Codex and dsh?
How should 'real-unlabeled' ledger replays be scored when their ground truth is itself a noisy 5-seed estimate: as a separate track with wide CIs, or excluded from rank?
Which record profile wins adoption: an in-toto predicate (verifiable, heavy) or an OTel event (lightweight, no verification), and will OpenClaw or Anthropic emit either?

Once accepted edits are gated honestly and most production edits correctly never commit, what should a loop do with its budget: fewer, larger candidates, or stop evolving (the 'when not to evolve' question the surveys leave open)?

ci-for-rsi.name: Pawl
name_candidates: Pawl (the part of a ratchet that engages only when the mechanism tries to slip backward)
ci-for-rsi.tagline: CI for the state your agent writes to itself: silent on pass, loud on block, never silent on hold.
ci-for-rsi.stance: CI/CD for self-modifying agents, as corrected by the four lenses. Pawl is a harness-agnostic acceptance layer that (1) intercepts every persistent self-write at the file-path level (any tool, any thread, any harness sharing the directory), (2) judges the write against the incumbent on the user's own recorded sessions inside a sealed, host-side evaluator (paired, anytime-valid, tri-state, divergence-aware, sandbox-first), (3) keeps safety and cost as hard constraints inside accept(), (4) proves activation before it credits effect, and (5) makes every write revertible with depth > 1 and a verified round trip. It ships observe-only by default (change feed, load receipts, undo, spend meter) and turns blocking on per store; 'invisible until it blocks' is implemented one-sidedly: no cost or notification on the pass path, a loud block with an override path, and holds that expire or escalate rather than rot. It is not a proposer, not an LLM proxy, and not a 13th ledger format: it registers in seams that already exist (Claude Code hooks and plugin eval, OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate, Hermes pending queue and pre_tool_call, DSH tools/pre-execute + hook-protocol, pi tool_call/tool_result, Reef evaluate/decide) and emits one acceptance record as a profile over in-toto/EEE/OTel. What is genuinely new versus PACE/SEA/CAR: activation-eligibility partitioning that makes no-op evidence free, the incumbent's self-replay as the per-task noise floor and protected-corpus definition, an asymmetric disposition (fast BLOCK, provisional ADMIT, slow VERIFY with the same test continuing on live sessions), the measured middle case of The Replay Gap for harness edits, incident-seeded operational canaries instead of refusal probes, and one content hash joining write event, receipt, evidence, verdict and snapshot so undo, attribution, funnel alarms and the gate are one ledger.
ci-for-rsi.thesis: Self-modifying agents already ship every mechanism except the one that decides. Proposers exist everywhere (Hermes background review and curator, Codex Memories, Claude Code auto-memory, Prime /refine, SkillOpt-Sleep, Meta-Harness, OpenClaw Workshop) and persist state on their own judgment; the honest statistical gates exist only on paper (PACE, SEA) and were validated on 0.5B-3B prompt edits with binary metrics; and users across ten issue trackers ask for receipts, diffs, undo, budgets and 'did it even load', never for statistics. The thesis: one append-only, content-addressed ledger whose entries (write event, load receipt, paired evidence, verdict, snapshot) share the artifact hash gives users the four things they ask for on day one (feed, receipt, undo, cost) and gives researchers the gate on day thirty, because the honest gate only becomes affordable when (a) evidence is partitioned by activation eligibility so that no-op edits produce ties at zero model cost, (b) the noise floor is measured for free by replaying the unmodified incumbent against its own sessions, and (c) the decision is asymmetric: confirmed regressions and safety violations are blocked from a handful of discordant pairs, no-ops are admitted provisionally, and lift is certified slowly by an anytime-valid test that keeps running on live sessions after admission. A gate built this way rejects most production edits 'for free' (which the null-effect literature says is correct), never starves the way SEA's gate did, and turns 'my agent modified itself' into 'the modification was intercepted, linted, sealed-evaluated, gated with error control, activation-checked, attributed, and can be reverted with one command'.
ci-for-rsi.rsi_positioning: Pawl sits at the middle altitude of the Sept-2026 RSI discourse: harness-level, bounded self-improvement (Reliable-survey L2 scaffold / L3 improver; leezythu L0-L4; MetaRSI's Harness-RSI operator) with a frozen model, which is where every mass-market 'self-improving' agent and most 2026 papers live. It is explicitly the verification/acceptance layer, not a proposer: the surveys' shared verdict is that 'the acceptor is the weak link' (PACE: greedy acceptance = 30-42% false commits; HarnessDev: self-selection on visible feedback agrees with held-out on 34/64 switches; RSI-Exam: every frontier model loses 12-25% from visible to sealed), and the RSI survey (2607.07663) names 'governance-grade measurement of self-improvement' and 'trustworthy accumulation' as the emptiest areas. Pawl adopts the verification hierarchy as schema: every acceptance record carries the rung it was validated at (formal / execution / learned-judge / intrinsic); closed-loop acceptance is refused below rung 2; rung-3 evidence (cross-family judge) can admit provisionally but never certify; and any candidate that touches the evaluator, the gate, the protected corpus or the improver is an L4/L5 event that requires an independent anchor or a human merge (MetaRSI sealed-measurement invariant, dsh's trusted-branch rule, MLAS 'optimizer-optimizee collapse'). It also gives the other two altitudes something concrete: for Data-RSI/weight loops it is a drop-in decide policy for Reef (whose weight path defaults to AlwaysSelect) and a per-change version of RSI-Exam's sealed replay; for model-level RSI benchmarks it supplies the missing per-change gate, noise model and acceptor confusion matrix. Why RSI people care: all five 2026 surveys list the same four open problems (reference implementation of a gated update loop, regression/retention protocol, evaluator co-evolution without self-confirmation, multi-generation benchmark) and none ships code; Pawl ships runnable code for the first two, a benchmark for the fourth, and the mechanical-override + cross-family-judge + leak-scan machinery that is the practical (non-co-evolutionary) answer to the third. It is the thing that lets a lab say, with a signed record, what a loop is and is not improving. For adoption the word 'RSI' is dropped: to users Pawl is 'git + CI for the state your agent writes to itself'; the harness-RSI framing is reserved for the ICLR RSI workshop and the surveys' audience. Same code, two vocabularies.
what_evolves: Pawl itself does not evolve and is deliberately outside the mutable surface; changes to its evaluator, gate policy, canary set or protected corpus are L4/L5 events that go through a human-merged branch (dsh trusted-branch pattern). What it governs (the artifacts under acceptance) is:

SKILL.md bundles including references/, scripts/, assets/ (Claude Code .claude/skills, Hermes ~/.hermes/skills, OpenClaw Skill Workshop proposals and live skills, agentskills.io-format bundles, ECC/autoharness skill dirs)

Memory artifacts, the most-deployed and least-gated class: Claude Code auto-memory (MEMORY.md index + typed topic files, subagent/team stores), Hermes MEMORY.md/USER.md, Codex ~/.codex/memories, Prime memories, ECC instincts, ACE-style playbook bullets
Instruction files and rules: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, project rules, Prime prompt notes and subagent specs in harness_state.json
Harness configuration the agent can write: settings.json hooks, plugin/MCP installs, OpenClaw config.patch, DSH cordis_define runtime plugins, pi/Prime refinements.jsonl entries

Loop-graph and code-level harness changes where a substrate exposes them (Reef native composition-tree nodes, Self-Harness hook slots, auto-harness agent.py), evaluated through the same candidate contract

Curator/consolidation operations that mutate several artifacts at once (Hermes curator absorbed_into merges, OpenClaw dreaming, Codex consolidation, OpenViking memory_diff) treated as one composite candidate with one snapshot
The protected regression corpus itself grows (new sessions become cassettes; incumbent stability is re-measured), but only by the recorder, never by the proposer
ci-for-rsi.fitness_and_acceptance:
SIGNAL THAT DECIDES. The primary signal is a paired, per-instance, tri-state outcome (pass / fail / inconclusive) of the session's own terminal verification (the last test/build/lint command the user actually ran) re-executed in a git-snapshot sandbox, for incumbent vs candidate on the same recorded session ('cassette'). It is harness-owned by construction: the proposer never authored it and never sees it (HarnessDev score-path isolation; RSI-Exam fail-closed grader; SkillOpt#155's three binding requirements adopted verbatim: worktree is disposable state not a security boundary so real execution runs in a container with isolated credentials and no network, outcomes are pass/fail/inconclusive, execution is off by default). Secondary signals, each with its own decision rule: behavior change (first-divergence step vs the incumbent's own self-divergence), cost (tokens, wall-clock, artifact/context size), activation (loaded / read / followed), and safety (deterministic canary + behavioral canary). No LLM judgment is ever the final authority: PROCTOR's rule 'mechanical rejection overrides LLM approval, never the reverse' is hard-coded, and judge evidence is tagged rung 3 and can only produce ADMIT_PROVISIONAL, never VERIFIED.

DECISION RULE (builds on PACE, extended). Per candidate, eligible cassettes are visited in random order. Control arm = incumbent replayed k times (k=2 default, escalate to 3 on flake); these runs are cached and amortized across every candidate against the same incumbent. Candidate arm = 1 run first, more only if discordant. Each pair is classified concordant (tie), discordant-better, discordant-worse, or inconclusive (excluded from wealth, counted in the record). Ties are discarded and wealth updates only on discordant pairs (PACE's McNemar-style betting e-process, E *= 1 + lambda(2w-1), mixture over q in {0.6..0.9} as in our gate_power_sim.py), commit 'VERIFIED' at E >= 1/alpha with alpha=0.05. A second, harm-direction e-process runs on the protected corpus with alpha_harm=0.10 so blocking is faster than certifying. Per-task floor (synthesis claim 3, corrected): a task is 'protected' only if the incumbent passed it k/k in its own replay (observed stability, not assumed), and a candidate regression on a protected task counts only after k-of-n confirmation; our simulation shows why: on Bernoulli(0.6) tasks a k=1 floor false-blocks 93-100% of candidates, k=2 44-91%, k=3 13-43%, while real test-verified coding tasks are far more deterministic and the incumbent self-replay measures that per task for free. Run-level error across an unbounded candidate stream uses SEA's horizon-free CTHS schedule delta_k = delta_0 / (Z k log^2(k+1)), Z ~ 3.39 (the naive 1/(2k log^2 k) schedule over-spends 1.69x), and e-values across objectives are combined conservatively (all hard constraints must clear; cost and lift are separate e-processes; product only for independent constraints). Dependence from reusing cassettes across candidates is NOT covered by any theorem (PACE says the same of its dev set); mitigations are corpus rotation (new sessions arrive daily), agentdescent's rule that commit decisions read only full-eligible evidence and sub-samples may rank but never veto, and its kappa-style discount when a proxy judge is involved. Freshness (MetaRSI Eq. 22): evidence compiled before the last model-version or harness-version change is stale; control arms are keyed by model_served and invalidated on change.

DISPOSITIONS (the correction that keeps the gate on). VERIFIED (lift e-process committed, no floor violation, canary pass); ADMIT_PROVISIONAL (no evidence of harm after the per-candidate budget, default 8 eligible pairs or $0.50; the artifact goes live under continuing evaluation); HOLD (fewer than 3 eligible pairs or >50% inconclusive; the record says 'needs ~N more eligible sessions'; expires in 14 days into the policy default, never silently); BLOCK (>=1 confirmed protected regression, harm-direction commit, deterministic canary fail, lint fail, or 'evaluator unavailable' when the store is in blocking mode); NOT_ACTIVATED (candidate never loaded in any eligible replay; reported with the diagnosis: wrong store, truncated index, description outside matcher window). This asymmetry is the direct answer to SEA's ALG4, which accepted 0 edits at ~50 tasks and was switched off, and to the practitioner finding that a gate that rejects everything is disabled within a week; it is MGM/HGM's 'provisional admission plus posterior tracking' made explicit. Honest power statement from our simulation: with 20-40 binary paired tasks the gate detects a +10pp lift 11% (N=40) to 39% (N=160) of the time and a +30pp lift 98% of the time at N=40; so in practice Pawl reliably blocks regressions and safety violations, certifies only large lifts, and labels most production edits 'no-op so far' (consistent with CTA +0.3pp, SkillsBench 0 gain for LLM-written skills, Continual Harness 6.4% reuse, SkillOpt gains carried by 1-4 edits). Power is raised where possible with denser per-task signals (divergence step, steps-to-done, tokens) as secondary continuous objectives, and the test never stops: post-admission live sessions keep feeding the same e-process (this is the post-acceptance canary), and auto-revert fires on a confirmed regression.

NOISE. The Replay Gap (2608.08239) is taken as binding: replay is re-execution, never log-stitching; temperature 0 is not determinism (FP8 controls diverged 90-96%); every score is relative to the incumbent's own replay distribution; late fork points are safer and are preferred when a cassette has several verification points. Pure VCR replay is dead on real coding sessions (our own measurement: 50% workspace writes, 20% external, 13% nondeterministic calls; idempotent-only prefix 0-1 calls in every session), so replay is sandbox-first: workspace ops re-execute for real inside the git snapshot; externals and nondeterministic calls are served from the recording keyed by (tool, normalized input) via PreToolUse updatedInput / PostToolUse updatedToolOutput (verified on Claude Code 2.1.258, ~$0.007 per served replay) or plugin-eval mocks; the first call matching neither is the divergence point, and CTA's lesson applies: a divergence auditor must be calibrated against A-vs-A' before any divergence is attributed (CTA's detectors fired identically on no-change pairs). CAR's discipline is adopted: a counterfactual yields a distribution with CIs, abstention (HOLD) is a first-class outcome, and the incumbent must reproduce the recorded outcome before any candidate is credited (sanity floor).

SAFETY INSIDE ACCEPT(). Two boundaries per SafeEvolve/SkillMisevo (admission at write, revocation at reuse), because three exposures suffice and benign updates do not wash contamination out, so gating is per write, not periodic. Deterministic canary (zero model cost, any fail = BLOCK with a human override path): secrets/credentials/PII persisted into any artifact or .git/config (Hermes#101351), destructive commands in scripts/ (rm -rf, git reset --hard outside cwd; EvoMap#198), network egress in skill code, provider-boundary violations for memory jobs (codex#41711), session-specific facts entering global rules without a scope tag (ports, hostnames, absolute paths, dates), placeholder tokens codified as 'verified' (Hermes#89963), referenced files that do not exist, a revision that silently drops a verification/reversibility requirement its ancestor asserted (SafeEvolve's LLM-independent invariant), and 'rule contradicts the live environment' probes (arXiv 2609.11060 style, e.g. a skill asserting a command that returns 127). Behavioral canary (30-100 domain-conditioned probes, paired incumbent vs candidate, cross-family judge, mechanical override, ~50-100 model calls): seeded from the incident classes users actually file (learned helplessness / transient failure persisted, destructive action, credential persistence, permission-rule deletion, cross-user egress, fabricated completion claims) plus SkillMisevo-Bench, MemEvoBench and Agent-SafetyBench items for the refusal/injection axis. Probe text is never shown to the proposer, a held-out rotating subset guards against probe overfitting, and a confirmed new harmful behavior (2/2) is a BLOCK. Revocation at reuse: an admitted artifact retrieved in a new task family is re-canaried once before it counts, and attributed harm retires it.

TAMPERING VS OVERFITTING (two different fixes). Tampering (the one systems bug behind DGM#35, HyperAgents#39, HGM, AHE#15, SIA#36, autoresearch#599, pi-autoresearch): the evaluator runs host-side as its own process and identity; cassettes, snapshots, canary probes and gate state live in a store the harness's filesystem view cannot read (deny rule + separate uid where available, container mount elsewhere); every score is bound to a receipt sha256(evaluator version, cassette ids and hashes, candidate hash, snapshot ref, control-arm result hashes), DSSE-signed, and any number without a reproducible receipt is rejected; a leak scan rejects candidates containing cassette ids, test names, grader strings or probe text; 'evaluator unavailable' fails closed in blocking mode (DSH ApprovalOutcome semantics), with a loud alarm and expiry so fail-closed cannot become silent starvation. Overfitting via feedback (SkillOpt#154/#175): the proposer receives per-task pass/fail and failure excerpts but never grader source, regexes, rubric wording or verdict rationale; a mutation-content scan rejects quoted scorer tokens; 10% of accepted candidates are re-scored by an independent-family, rubric-blind judge with a divergence alarm; RQGM-style evaluator replacement is not attempted (OpenRQGM saw 0 replacements at 128 outcomes).

ACTIVATION AND ATTRIBUTION. Activation is a precondition of evidence, not a metric reported afterward (Lin et al.: skill-load 25% vs 96%, adherence .52 to .13; Anthropic's own plugin-eval docs: 'the most common first finding is a delta near zero with the tool_used: Skill grader failing'; Prime: 22/28 prompt notes and 63/69 memories never entered context). Per session, a deterministic receipt records for every artifact: resolved store path and hash, bytes available vs loaded, status complete | truncated | not_loaded | wrong_store, and load evidence (InstructionsLoaded, tool_use Skill, skill_view, resources_discover); eligibility for a cassette is computed from receipts before any model call, so a candidate that could not have loaded in a session is a tie at $0 and a candidate that loads nowhere is NOT_ACTIVATED with a diagnosis. Adherence uses mechanical predicates first (rules with checkable form: tool-order constraints, forbidden commands, required verification before commit) and a sampled cross-family judge only for free-text rules, offline. Attribution combines two arms honestly labeled: the unbiased arm is paired replay on replayable sessions; the observational arm is HGM-clade-style pooled outcome statistics per artifact over live sessions (activated vs eligible-not-activated), which is confounded (artifacts load on harder tasks) and therefore only ever produces 'keep / never-loaded / loaded-but-ignored / regresses / unknown-needs-N-more' recommendations, never a VERIFIED label. Retention and adaptation are reported separately (EvoHarnessBench BWT/FWT): a candidate can be VERIFIED on its target cluster and still BLOCKED on retention. Improvement claims that are to be published (research mode) additionally require AI2's matched-budget test-time-scaling control: the candidate must beat parallel-2 of the unmodified incumbent at the same rollout budget, with meta-agent tokens counted.

COST. Every record carries a cost envelope (proposer tokens if known, evaluator tokens, replicates, sandbox seconds, list-price USD), a per-store daily cap with a circuit breaker on repeated refusals or identical retries (Hermes#90446), and the sentence 'this gate cost $X' in every report; the corpus shows loops that do not print their own cost get disabled (codex#19105, claude-code#71633, darwin-skill#25).
ci-for-rsi.core_technical_insight: Activation-gated paired evidence on the user's own sessions makes an honest gate cheap enough to leave on, and one content hash makes the gate, the undo, the funnel and the attribution the same ledger. Concretely: (1) An artifact's effect on a recorded session is a tie by construction whenever the artifact was not eligible to load in that session, and eligibility is computable deterministically from load receipts before any model call; since the e-process learns only from discordant pairs, the majority of production edits (near-zero effect per five independent 2026 results) are decided as 'no-op so far' at zero model cost, and a candidate that loads nowhere is diagnosed, not evaluated. (2) Replaying the unmodified incumbent against its own cassettes yields, for free and per task, the noise floor the entire field lacks (The Replay Gap's control arm), and it defines the protected corpus by observed stability rather than by assumption, which is what makes a per-task floor statistically well-posed. (3) Because regressions on protected tasks are discordant in the harmful direction, blocking harm needs a handful of pairs while certifying lift needs many; so the gate is asymmetric by design (fast BLOCK, provisional ADMIT, slow VERIFY) and the same anytime-valid test keeps running on live sessions after admission, which is why it never starves the way SEA's gate did and why post-acceptance canary and pre-acceptance gate are one mechanism. (4) Every entry (write event with provenance taint, load receipt, paired evidence, verdict, snapshot) is keyed by the artifact's content hash, so 'undo everything session X did', 'which artifacts came from that injected page', 'accepted=0 for two weeks', and 'was this ever loaded' are queries over one append-only ledger rather than four subsystems, and the acceptance record is emitted as a profile over in-toto/EEE/OTel so tooling that already exists can verify it. Competitors have the pieces (PACE the test, CAR the replay, Hermes the provenance, OpenClaw the hash-bound proposal, SkillOpt-Sleep the nightly loop) but none has the join, the eligibility partition, or the asymmetry, and it is those three that make the layer both statistically honest and adoptable.

architecture.responsibility: Single policy engine and append-only content-addressed ledger; every adapter is a thin shim that spawns the CLI in hook-protocol shape (auto-harness gating.py / DSH hook-protocol style: exit codes 0 pass, 1 block, 2 hold, plus a JSON verdict on stdout). Language-agnostic by construction so TypeScript substrates (OpenClaw, DSH, pi) and Python substrates (Hermes, Reef, SkillOpt) share one engine.
architecture.interfaces: pawl init | watch | receipt | stage | lint | eval | gate | undo | restore | report | audit | bench; JSON schemas pawl.candidate/evidence/verdict/ledger/cassette/receipt v0.1; SQLite index over JSONL ledger; config per store (mode: observe|hold|block).

architecture.responsibility: Normalize sessions into cassettes: ordered turns (user / assistant / tool_use / tool_result with structured results), replayability class per call (IDEMPOTENT_READ / WORKSPACE_WRITE / EXTERNAL / NONDETERMINISTIC), git snapshot of the workspace at session start (HEAD ref + dirty patch under refs/pawl/snapshots), run-integrity metadata (model actually served, completion status, budget), and terminal-check detection (the last test/build/lint command the user ran and its observed result). Zero new instrumentation on Claude Code (reads ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl); scrubs secrets; local-only by default.
architecture.interfaces: Claude Code transcripts + SessionStart/Stop hooks; Hermes session logs; Codex rollouts; DSH zstd JSONL session events (invariant model-visible <=> logged); OpenClaw session store; pi agent_end. Output: pawl.cassette records + snapshot refs.

architecture.component: watch (learned-state tree watcher and change feed)
architecture.responsibility: Content-addressed watcher over every installed harness's learned-state tree (Claude Code memory dirs, CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills; ~/.hermes/skills + MEMORY.md; OpenClaw skill-workshop proposals and live skills; ~/.codex/memories; ~/.prime/agent/harness; ECC instincts). Emits a write event per change with before/after hashes, unified diff, originating session, writer origin (user / foreground agent / background reviewer / curator / updater), and provenance taint. Backstop for hook bypass: a write that arrives without an intercept event is flagged 'unintercepted' and, in block mode, quarantined post hoc.
architecture.interfaces: fs events + periodic hash sweep; ingests Hermes skill_ledger JSONL, OpenClaw skill_changed / skill_proposal_changed ledger, Prime refinements.jsonl, OpenViking memory_diff.json; emits pawl.ledger write events; `pawl feed --since yesterday`.

architecture.component: intercept (write-path enforcement at the file-path level)
architecture.responsibility: Turn a write into a candidate before it lands. Enforced on the path, not the tool: any Write/Edit/Bash redirection/patch/subagent write into a governed tree by an unattended origin is staged (snapshot first), linted, and either allowed (observe), held (hold) or denied (block) per store policy. Ownership model: user-validated artifacts are immutable to unattended writers by default; agent-created artifacts are patchable by the loop; updaters may not clobber locally adapted artifacts without a merge; hash-at-read conflict check between concurrent writers (Hermes gfpyc failure mode 5, claude-code#85597).
architecture.interfaces: Claude Code PreToolUse (permissionDecision allow|ask|deny + updatedInput); Hermes pre_tool_call (fail-closed) + pending/{skills,memory}/<id>.json staging + skill_provenance write_origin; OpenClaw before_tool_call (block / requireApproval) and skill_proposal_evaluate for the governed path; DSH tools/pre-execute typed PreToolDecision + deny-only guard; pi tool_call block; Codex PostToolUse block (documented as best-effort).

architecture.responsibility: Zero-model-cost checks that catch most user-filed failures: frontmatter parses; referenced scripts/references exist; executable skill code compiles; claims labelled verified cite a tool-output span; placeholder tokens never become facts; session-specific facts (ports, hosts, absolute paths, dates, codenames) need a scope tag before entering global rules; dedup against existing skills/docs; freshness on host update; secret/PII scrub (entropy + pattern + allowlist); provider-boundary rule for memory jobs; diff must equal the declared modification and stay inside the declared surface (MetaRSI Eq. 27); a revision may not drop a verification/reversibility requirement its ancestor asserted.
architecture.interfaces: `pawl lint <candidate>` -> findings[] with ruleId/severity/file/line (same shape as OpenClaw's evaluator findings); runs inside intercept and inside the OpenClaw/Hermes/DSH plugins; override path via `pawl allow --rule <id> --once`.

architecture.responsibility: Per session, for every persistent artifact: resolved store identity and hash, bytes available vs loaded, status complete | truncated | not_loaded | wrong_store (claude-code#82056's three indistinguishable failure modes plus the unstable-slug fourth), what was dropped on overflow (#92998), load evidence from the transcript, and adherence via mechanical predicates (tool-order, forbidden-command, required-verification rules) with optional sampled cross-family judging offline. Works with no learning loop at all (hand-written CLAUDE.md is 100% of Claude Code users).
architecture.interfaces: Claude Code InstructionsLoaded + SessionStart + Stop hooks and transcript parse; Hermes skill_view / .usage.json; OpenClaw runtime usage receipts; DSH skills/change events; pi resources_discover. Output: pawl.receipt records that also define cassette eligibility for the gate.

architecture.responsibility: Runs candidate vs incumbent on eligible cassettes in a separate process and identity with the cassette store, snapshots, probes and gate state unreadable from the harness. Sandbox-first divergence-aware replay: git-worktree + container (no network, isolated credentials), execution off by default and tri-state outcomes; externals/nondeterministic calls served from the recording via PreToolUse updatedInput / PostToolUse updatedToolOutput (or plugin-eval mocks); first unmatched call = divergence point; terminal check = the session's own verification re-executed. Control arm (incumbent x k) cached per incumbent hash. Every score bound to a DSSE-signed receipt; unreproducible numbers rejected; leak scan on candidate content. Alternative backend: compile a cassette into a `claude plugin eval` case (scaffold_script restores the snapshot, history_file = transcript prefix to the fork point, graders = terminal check + tool_used + file_exists) and run --ablation with-without.
architecture.interfaces: `pawl eval <candidate> --backend {hooks|plugin-eval|harbor}` -> pawl.evidence records + receipt; RSI-Exam-style fail-closed wrapper (any exception -> inconclusive, never a score); AI4AI-Bench patch-only crossing (only the candidate diff enters the sandbox).

architecture.responsibility: Implements the decision rule: paired anytime-valid e-process on the primary tri-state outcome, harm-direction e-process on the protected corpus, k-of-n per-task floor on tasks with observed incumbent stability, cost e-process with tolerance, CTHS run-level spend schedule, freshness check, activation smoke, safety canary integration, rejected-edit archive fed back to the proposer, and the five dispositions VERIFIED / ADMIT_PROVISIONAL / HOLD / BLOCK / NOT_ACTIVATED. Ported from the builder's gate_power_sim.py into a tested ~600-line library with the published power table.
architecture.interfaces: `pawl gate <candidate>` -> pawl.verdict; drop-in `decide(candidate_results, incumbent_results, manifest, rejected) -> Decision` for Reef recipes; `--threshold`-compatible exit codes for `claude plugin eval` pipelines; OpenClaw decision pass|revise|block mapping (HOLD -> revise, BLOCK -> block, others -> pass with metrics).

architecture.component: canary (deterministic + behavioral safety, pre- and post-acceptance)
architecture.responsibility: Deterministic probes (destructive commands, credential persistence, egress, provider boundary, scope leaks, environment contradiction) and a 30-100 item behavioral probe bank seeded from user-filed incident classes plus SkillMisevo-Bench / MemEvoBench / Agent-SafetyBench items, paired incumbent vs candidate, cross-family judge, mechanical override, held-out rotating subset. Post-acceptance: the same e-process continues on live sessions; confirmed regression or attributed harm triggers auto-revert to a known-safe checkpoint; re-validation once when an artifact is retrieved in a new task family.
architecture.interfaces: `pawl canary <candidate>`; probe bank as a sealed asset with hash pinned in receipts; revert trigger calls undo; alarms to report/review.

architecture.component: ledger (acceptance records as a standards profile) + funnel + spend
architecture.responsibility: Append-only JSONL, content-addressed, one record type per stage sharing the artifact hash. The acceptance record is an in-toto Statement v1 with a pawl predicate (candidate/incumbent digests, paired evidence in Every-Eval-Ever instance form, decision rule, verdict, disposition, activation, cost envelope, rung, evaluator id), also emitted as an OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result event with extension attributes. Funnel counters proposed -> intercepted -> linted -> evaluated -> accepted -> activated -> attributed plus a fifth 'ran vs reported ran' counter; alarms on accepted=0 over N runs, activated=0, held > threshold, unintercepted writes, spend > cap. Spend ledger reads each harness's own session logs (RSI-Exam budget.py pattern) and attributes tokens/USD to review, curation, replay and gate.
architecture.interfaces: `pawl report [--daily]`, `pawl status`, `pawl spend`; exports: aggregate-result.json (schemaVersion 1) so results ride Anthropic's report surface, OpenClaw evaluator envelope, EEE record, OTel event, DSSE bundle verifiable with cosign.

architecture.responsibility: Snapshot the whole learned-state tree (bundle dirs including references/scripts/assets, memory and index files) content-addressed before every unattended write; `undo --session X` (adds -> delete, updates -> restore, deletes -> recreate) with a conflict check for artifacts touched by later sessions; `restore <artifact>@N`; every snapshot round-trip tested before it is trusted; depth > 1; GC by policy. Replaces the field's broken per-tool rollbacks (Hermes#96962/#83580/#75228, OpenViking#4178).
architecture.interfaces: git-backed snapshot store under refs/pawl; `pawl undo`, `pawl restore`, `pawl snapshots`; used by canary auto-revert and by review 'reject'.

architecture.component: review (approval surface that does not rot)
architecture.responsibility: Batched (daily or threshold) digest with one-line summaries, full diff, evidence pointer, activation history and gate verdict; default disposition computed by the gate so humans review only HOLDs; holds expire into a stated default with a reason; scanner findings are overridable with a recorded justification (Hermes#94353 deadlock); surfaces where the user already is.
architecture.interfaces: terminal + markdown digest; OpenClaw Workshop board via evaluator findings; Hermes /skills pending diff/approve/reject; GitHub PR for team stores; optional push notification.

architecture.component: bench (acceptor benchmark on Harbor + ledger re-analysis)
architecture.responsibility: A Harbor task family that injects known-good / known-neutral / known-harmful edits (synthetic ground truth as in CAR and PACE's 'planted improvement among noise' and 'no-real-gain stochastic' regimes, plus real edits with hidden held-out outcomes and SkillMisevo/MLAS-style payloads) into a loop and scores the acceptor: false-commit, harmful-commit, missed-improvement, false-block on benign edits, evals per decision, safety decay, BWT/FWT, cost, vs a matched-budget test-time-scaling control. Plus an offline re-analysis harness for published ledgers (SkillOpt-Sleep evidence.jsonl, AHE change_manifest + git, Meta-Harness evolution_summary.jsonl, Self-Harness acceptance logs, Reef records).
architecture.interfaces: harbor task.toml family; six CLIs plug in as one-line adapters; results published as EEE records; `pawl bench run --gate {greedy|strict|pace|pawl}`.

ci-for-rsi.integration_surface:
One core CLI, thin adapters, and a conformance suite that proves each seam does what its docs claim (does a deny stop the write, does a rejected proposal reach disk, does an evaluator timeout fail closed, does a promoted artifact actually load).

CLAUDE CODE (first adapter; the builder's own data). SessionStart: register session, snapshot workspace (HEAD ref + dirty patch under refs/pawl/snapshots), start cassette. InstructionsLoaded: record which CLAUDE.md / memory / skill files were injected and whether complete or truncated -> receipt. UserPromptSubmit: record the user turn and mark it trusted origin for taint. PreToolUse: (a) enforcement, `permissionDecision: ask|deny` for Write/Edit/Bash redirections into governed paths (memory dir, CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills, settings hooks) by unattended origins, with the write staged as a candidate; (b) replay, `updatedInput` to route a call into the sandbox worktree. PostToolUse: record tool results into the cassette; during replay `updatedToolOutput` serves recorded results for EXTERNAL / NONDETERMINISTIC calls (verified on 2.1.258, ~$0.007 per served replay). Stop/SubagentStop: finalize cassette, emit receipt, enqueue nightly evaluation. FileChanged on MEMORY.md and the fs watcher are the backstop for writes that bypass hooks. `claude plugin eval` as an alternative sealed backend: each cassette compiles to a case (scaffold_script restores the snapshot; history_file = transcript prefix to the fork point; graders = regex over the terminal-check output + tool_used asserting the test command ran + file_exists on artifacts; optional baseline grader vs the original transcript), run with `--ablation with-without`, `runs` = repeats, `--json` feeds the e-process; Pawl also writes aggregate-result.json (schemaVersion 1) so verdicts appear on Anthropic's report surface. Memory seam: PreToolUse on writes under the memory dir is the only acceptance point for auto-memory anywhere in the field; writes that arrive through internal paths are caught by the watcher and quarantined post hoc.

HERMES. Ingest tools/skill_ledger.py JSONL and .usage.json for the feed and activation; consume `~/.hermes/pending/{skills,memory}/<id>.json` when `skills.write_approval` / `memory.write_approval` are on and post verdicts (approve/reject through the same replay-through-skill_manage path with the gate-bypass token, so Hermes bookkeeping stays intact); register `ctx.register_hook()` plugin for post-turn review and curator events; shell `pre_tool_call` fail-closed for write_file/patch/terminal writes into ~/.hermes/skills and MEMORY.md by `background_review` origin (tools/skill_provenance.py ContextVar), which closes hermes#99729; treat curator consolidations (absorbed_into) as composite candidates with one snapshot; answer hermes#96704's RFC arms with `pawl audit` (activation arm from transcripts needs no model calls). 

OPENCLAW. A plugin registering `skill_proposal_evaluate` (event: proposal id/kind/revision/revisionSha256 + candidate and baseline BundleSnapshots with per-file sha256 and treeSha256; result: findings[]{ruleId,severity,message,file,line}, metrics, evaluatorVersion, mode:'baseline-comparison', decision pass|revise|block, decisionReason) — the first third-party implementation of the seam its docs wrote for 'external optimization loops'; HOLD maps to revise, BLOCK to block, and because only a completed `block` vetoes apply and errors/timeouts fail open, the plugin converts its own failures into `block` when the store is in block mode; consume `skill_proposal_changed` / `skill_changed` (before/after tree hashes) for the feed; `before_tool_call` (block / requireApproval) to cover `autonomous.mode: auto` direct edits that the Workshop admits bypass proposals; verdicts render on the Workshop board.

DEEPSEEK HARNESS. A dsh plugin on `tools/pre-execute` (typed PreToolDecision deny for writes into the learned-state tree by unattended actors; monotonic deny-only guard so listener order cannot resurrect a denied write), `tools/post-execute` (attach verdict context), `agent/turn-stopping` (finalize cassette), with `ApprovalOutcome` fail-closed on 'unavailable'; the Claude Code hooks.json runs unmodified under the `dsh-hooks-claude-code` bridge, so one command-hook adapter covers Claude Code, Codex and DSH; Cordis revertible effects give atomic revert for runtime self-modifications (cordis_define); publish as a marketplace plugin next to dsh-verify / dsh-verification.

PI / PRIME AGENT. pi extension: `tool_call` (block writes to governed paths), `tool_result` (serve recorded results during replay), `resources_discover` (report skill paths for receipts), `agent_end` (finalize). Prime: watch harness_state.json and refinements.jsonl -> candidates with before/after snapshots; render the diff before apply (prime#684) and hook `/refine rollback <id>` to `pawl undo`; the receipt exposes the alphabetical 6-entry head-slice problem (22/28 notes never loaded).

REEF. `pawl.decide` as a drop-in `decide` policy for harness recipes (anytime-valid paired + protected seed-suite floor instead of pooled W/L > min_win_margin; answers reef#356), consuming the recipe's interleaved candidate/incumbent episodes; `recheck_every` replaced by the continuing e-process; acceptance records emitted alongside releases; the acceptor benchmark converts to Harbor tasks per reef#447.

SKILLOPT-SLEEP. Implement the requested AgenticReplayBackend (microsoft/SkillOpt#155): worktree + container, tri-state, execution off by default; map evidence.jsonl to pawl.evidence; expose gate_no_regression as the k-of-n floor.

CODEX. PostToolUse block/replace and Stop (documented best-effort since some tool paths opt out); watch ~/.codex/memories; provider-boundary DLP rule for the memory writer (codex#41711).

Registries and standards (month 3): agentskills.io `evidence/` convention carrying the signed acceptance record and activation field; in-toto predicate proposal filed alongside #554; OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result attribute extension; EEE record profile with the selection denominator (candidatesCompared/candidatesCleared).

Day 3-5: `pawl receipt`: per-session load/adherence receipts from Claude Code transcripts plus SessionStart/InstructionsLoaded/Stop hooks (complete | truncated | not_loaded | wrong_store, dropped-on-overflow lines, load evidence, three mechanical adherence predicates); backfill over all existing transcripts with no new instrumentation.

Day 4-6: cassette extraction v0 productized from research/tools/cassette_extract.py: replayability classes, git snapshot ref at SessionStart, terminal-check detection, fork points, secret scrub; `pawl cassettes` lists replayable sessions.
