ci-for-rsi.killer_demo: Five minutes on a Claude Code + Hermes user's laptop, nothing pre-arranged. (0:00) `pipx install pawl && pawl init`. Pawl backfills from transcripts that already exist and prints, in ten seconds and with no model calls: 'Found 212 Claude Code sessions (41 replayable with a terminal check) and 3 stores. CLAUDE.md: loaded complete in 212/212. Auto-memory: truncated in 9 of the last 12 sessions; the newest 6 entries (your corrections from Tuesday) never reached the model. 14 skills: 5 never loaded in 60 days; 1 loaded in 31 sessions and contradicted in 12 (rule: run pytest before commit). 18 unattended writes last week from Hermes background review, 1 of them bypassed skill_manage bookkeeping.' (1:00) Trigger one real Hermes background review (or one Claude session that saves a skill). Pawl intercepts the write before it lands, snapshots the tree, and the lint blocks half of it instantly: a placeholder 'HH:MM' codified as 'Verified 2026-09-14', and a hostname from this session entering a global rule without a scope tag. The rest is staged as a candidate with its diff, writer origin and taint shown. (2:00) `pawl gate cand_…` runs the sealed evaluator against the 6 cassettes where this skill is eligible to load (the other 35 are ties at $0): the incumbent's own replay is already cached (3/3 stable on 5 of 6), the candidate replays in a worktree container with externals served from the recording, and the per-task diff table appears: tri-state outcome, divergence step, tokens, versus the incumbent's noise floor. Verdict: BLOCK — confirmed regression 2/2 on cas_8a1 (the flaky-test session you fixed last Tuesday), incumbent stable 3/3, cost of this gate $0.31, one-line reason, an override path. (3:30) `pawl undo --session <the review's session id>` restores every file the review touched, including references/ and scripts/, and prints the verified round trip. (4:00) `pawl report` shows the week: '12 self-modifications: 2 verified, 5 admitted provisionally (no-op so far, $0), 2 blocked (would have regressed on your own past tasks), 1 blocked by canary (a token persisted into .git/config), 1 held (needs ~6 more sessions, expires Friday), 1 never activated: the memory index overflowed and dropped it — here is the line. Total cost $2.14. Undo any of these with one command.' (4:30) Switch to the OpenClaw Workshop board: the same verdict renders in the evaluator slot as findings + pass|revise|block, with a signed acceptance record that `cosign verify-attestation` accepts. The sentence that sells it is '1 never activated — here's why'; the sentence that keeps it installed is '$2.14'.
ci-for-rsi.research_contribution: TITLE: 'Ties Are Free: Activation-Gated, Anytime-Valid Acceptance for Self-Modifying Agents, Evaluated on the Field's Own Ledgers and Sessions'. CLAIM (three parts, each with a number): (1) Re-analysis. Replaying the accept decisions recorded in published harness-evolution ledgers (SkillOpt-Sleep evidence.jsonl, AHE change_manifest + git, Meta-Harness evolution_summary.jsonl, Self-Harness acceptance logs, Reef records, community autoresearch results.tsv) under a sealed, paired, anytime-valid gate with a k-of-n protected floor and activation eligibility rejects a large fraction (target: >40%, the PACE band is 30-42%) of edits those loops accepted as indistinguishable from noise, and the rejected set contains the majority of the held-out regressions those papers report, at lower evaluation cost than their strict-held-out gates (sequential stopping + eligibility ties). (2) The Replay-Gap middle case. On real Claude Code and Hermes sessions, for edits proposed by real refiners (Hermes background review, Claude auto-memory, SkillOpt-Sleep), we report the first divergence-point distribution under sandbox-first branched re-execution with a same-configuration control arm: the prediction is that more than half of accepted production edits never change the action sequence on the user's own eligible past tasks, and that early divergence on previously-passing, incumbent-stable tasks predicts confirmed regression at a rate far above the control-arm floor. (3) Acceptor confusion matrix. On a Harbor-packaged benchmark that injects known-good, known-neutral and known-harmful edits (synthetic ground truth plus SkillMisevo/MLAS-style payloads, PACE's 'planted improvement among noise' and 'no-real-gain stochastic' regimes) into three loops (a SkillOpt-style skill loop, a memory loop, a Reef harness recipe), Pawl's gate dominates greedy, strict-held-out, Reef W-L margin, PACE-only and LLM-judge-only gates on the joint (false-commit, harmful-commit, false-block-on-benign, evals-per-decision) frontier while a matched-budget test-time-scaling control bounds what 'improvement' may mean. EXPERIMENT: offline ledger replay with the published per-task outcomes; online branched re-execution on >= 200 cassettes from >= 5 volunteer users (builder + hermes#96704 / SkillOpt#155 contributors), k=3 incumbent controls, cost accounted; benchmark runs with six CLIs via Harbor adapters, 5 seeds, BWT/FWT reported separately, safety decay via the canary bank with a held-out probe split. BASELINES: greedy keep-if-up (autoresearch, Meta-Harness), strict held-out no-ties (SkillOpt, Self-Harness, auto-harness), Reef pooled W/L with min_win_margin, PACE per-candidate e-process without floor/activation, SEA confidence-sequence gate, LLM-judge-only acceptance (SkillClaw-style), human approval queue (OpenClaw), and AI2's parallel-K / sequential-K test-time-scaling control at matched budget. FALSIFIERS: the claim is false if (a) held-out regressions are as frequent among edits Pawl accepts as among edits greedy accepts (rejection does not concentrate harm), (b) at equal false-commit rate Pawl costs more evaluations than the strict-held-out gate (eligibility ties and sequential stopping buy nothing), (c) the divergence point does not predict confirmed regression beyond the control-arm distribution (AUC <= 0.6), or (d) the incumbent self-replay floor is not stable across days/model versions so that 'protected' tasks flip in the control arm at rates comparable to candidate arms (the noise model is not a noise model). A secondary, cheaper result is the null-effect audit: on volunteers' stores the counterfactual lift of most LLM-written artifacts is indistinguishable from zero at matched budget, reported per artifact class.
ci-for-rsi.adoption_path: Adoption follows the issue corpus, not the paper. Day 1 value with zero risk: `pawl init` backfills from transcripts that already exist, runs no model calls, and answers the questions users actually file (what changed since yesterday and from which session, did my memory load or truncate, which skills never load, undo what that background review did, what does the loop cost). Observe-only is the default and stays free on the pass path; hold and block are per-store opt-ins that users turn on after the digest has shown them a would-have-blocked. This is the one-sided invisibility the practitioner lens demands, and it puts the primitives in the order users demand them (feed/receipts, undo, provenance, cassette, hidden statistics, operational canary, sealed evaluator, benchmark). Second, attach where someone else pays and it runs off the hot path, which is the pattern that actually spread (ClawHub scanning, OpenClaw Workshop): the OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin is the only substrate contract written for exactly this role and has zero third-party implementations, so the first real evaluator there is a visible win in a 389k-star ecosystem; the DSH marketplace already hosts verification plugins in this slot; Hermes has an open in-tree RFC (#96704) whose cheapest arm Pawl ships; SkillOpt's maintainers endorsed the exact replay backend (#155) and a contributor volunteered; Reef's decide policy is a one-PR integration with an open issue (#356) asking for it. Third, speak both languages: 'git + CI for the state your agent writes to itself' for users (no user issue says RSI), and 'the verification layer for harness-RSI' for the ICLR RSI workshop, the survey authors and the AI2/UW evaluation group; the same code and the same signed record serve both. Fourth, be the record, not the competitor: emit aggregate-result.json so verdicts ride Anthropic's report surface, the OpenClaw envelope so they show on the Workshop board, and an in-toto/EEE/OTel profile so registries (ClawHub, LobeHub, agentskills.io) can display effect evidence next to malware scans without adopting a new format; file the profile in the venues that have adjacent items (in-toto #554, OTel GenAI SIG, EvalEval) rather than founding a standard. Fifth, ship the Harbor benchmark and the ledger re-analysis so every harness-evolution paper has a reason to cite the gate and every maintainer has a number for their own acceptor. The trap to avoid is the one that killed SkillClaw and hermes-agent-self-evolution: an integration that works at the API level and breaks at the plumbing level (discovery paths, validators, deploy step). Hence the version-pinned conformance suite and the rule that Pawl never mutates a harness's config or intercepts its model traffic.

nearest_competitors.name: PACE (arXiv 2606.08106) — paired anytime-valid commit evaluation
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: PACE is the decision rule Pawl builds on (paired discordant-pair betting e-process, commit at 1/alpha) and it supplied the field's only acceptor-level measurement (greedy = 30-42% false commits). It has no code, is validated only on 0.5B-3B Qwen prompt edits with binary GSM8K/SVAMP/ARC metrics, controls only per-candidate error, has no per-task floor, no multi-objective, no tri-state, and no notion of activation. Pawl implements it in a harness, adds the harm-direction e-process and k-of-n protected floor on incumbent-stable tasks, cost as a second e-process, SEA's CTHS run-level spend schedule, tri-state outcomes, activation-eligibility partitioning (ties at $0), the asymmetric disposition set, and a continuing test after admission — and evaluates it on real sessions and published ledgers rather than a toy loop.

nearest_competitors.name: SEA (arXiv 2607.00871) — self-evolving agents with anytime-valid certificates
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SEA's certificate schema (decision ACCEPT/HOLD/REJECT/NSF, delta spent, cumulative delta) and its horizon-free CTHS spending schedule are reused. But SEA's harness-edit gate (ALG4) accepted zero edits at ~50 tasks, cost ~90 min per round (13x the rest of the loop) and was switched off, while the components that moved the metric ran ungated. Pawl's answer is structural: evidence accumulates across many cheap rounds and across days on live sessions, no-ops are admitted provisionally instead of held forever, blocking is faster than certifying, and the expensive arm only runs on eligible cassettes. SEA has no public code; Pawl is a CLI.

nearest_competitors.name: Causal Agent Replay (arXiv 2606.08275) — counterfactual attribution by do-interventions
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: CAR supplies the intervention vocabulary (do_policy, do_context), the rule that a counterfactual is a distribution with CIs and an explicit abstain state, and the sanity floor (the factual run must reproduce before a counterfactual is trusted); all three are adopted. CAR is post-hoc failure attribution with mocked tools, abstains ~80% of the time on real traces, and its author's power analysis shows more rollouts cannot fix replay fidelity. Pawl is a gate, not a debugger: it re-executes stateful tools in a git-snapshot sandbox, treats abstention as HOLD with an expiry, uses the incumbent's own replay as the control distribution, and only spends rollouts on activation-eligible sessions.

nearest_competitors.name: The Replay Gap (arXiv 2608.08239)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A negative result Pawl takes as binding rather than a competitor: log-stitching replay scores the wrong world (3-8% valid states after early interventions, every success-relevant outcome mispredicted, T=0 not deterministic). Pawl's replay is therefore branched re-execution with a same-configuration control arm, prefers late fork points, and reports the divergence-point distribution for harness edits (a smaller perturbation than a model swap) as a measured object — the middle case the paper leaves open.

nearest_competitors.name: SafeEvolve / SkillMisevo-Gym (arXiv 2608.12851)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SafeEvolve is the closest thing to a harness-agnostic acceptance layer for one artifact class (SKILL.md): admission audit at write plus revocation at reuse, a GovernableStore proven across Claude Code/Codex/OpenClaw/Hermes, and the LLM-independent invariant that a revision may not drop an ancestor's verification requirement (reused verbatim). It is post-hoc governance with the same-model critic as the evolving backbone, judges artifact content rather than outcomes, costs ~13pp carryover utility, and barely beats a static scanner on fresh-session harm. Pawl puts safety inside accept() as a hard constraint with a mechanical override, seeds probes from the operational incident classes users actually file (destructive action, credential persistence, egress, permission-rule deletion) rather than refusal alone, uses a cross-family judge, covers memory/rules/config as well as skills, and pairs the safety term with an outcome gate so utility cost is measured, not assumed.

nearest_competitors.name: Reef (Human-Agent-Society) — continual-learning release pipeline
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Reef is the most likely first institutional adopter, not a rival: its propose -> paired-evaluate -> decide recipe contract, versioned releases and canary/shadow routing are exactly the lifecycle Pawl's verdicts feed. Reef's gate is a pooled W/L tally over a tiny task suite with one-step rollback and AlwaysSelect for weights (#356); it is an LLM proxy that requires repointing model traffic and has no protected seed-suite floor, no activation check, no per-session receipts and no cross-harness ledger. Pawl ships as a Reef decide policy and Harbor conversion, and separately runs on hooks/plugins where a proxy is unacceptable (SkillClaw's fate: 'broke the harness', 'deprecated').

nearest_competitors.name: SkillOpt-Sleep (Microsoft) — nightly skill evolution with a strict held-out gate
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SkillOpt-Sleep is a proposer plus gate coupled to one artifact type: strict-improvement on a val-slice mean (per-task regressions accepted; gate_no_regression opt-in), an optimizer that copies judge regexes into skills (#154/#175), and a replay backend its maintainers want but do not have (#155). Pawl is gate-only, proposer-agnostic, evaluates any writer (Hermes review, Claude auto-memory, Prime refine) on the user's own sessions, keeps grader text away from the proposer, adds the per-task floor as a default, and implements the AgenticReplayBackend #155 asked for under its three constraints.

nearest_competitors.name: agentdescent (Birfy) — Beta-posterior acceptance with regression guard
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: agentdescent treats the gate as the load-bearing component and contributes rules Pawl reuses: commit decisions read only full-eligible evidence (sub-samples rank, never veto), discount evidence counts by kappa when a proxy judge is involved and bind the rectifier to a verifier version, freeze the oracle by name. It is an in-process Python engine coupled to its own types, its default oracle is tautological, blast radius is declared not estimated, and there is no post-commit monitoring, canary or rollback. Pawl is an out-of-process CLI with a sealed evaluator, a measured (not declared) impact surface via receipts, and post-admission continuation with auto-revert.

nearest_competitors.name: auto-harness (NeoSigma) — gating.py exit 0/1 with PROGRAM.md
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: auto-harness proved the right interface shape (a dumb CLI with exit codes, any coding agent as the optimizer, an abstract run(task_ids) -> reward) and Pawl copies that shape. But its gate state (best score, regression suite, config, PROGRAM.md) lives inside the agent-writable surface, acceptance is single-run tie-accepting on ~27 tasks, and trace isolation is enforced in the file the agent edits. Pawl keeps gate state host-side and sealed, hashes the split and evaluator into receipts, and replaces the monotone ratchet with paired sequential statistics.

nearest_competitors.name: Hermes Agent (Nous) — skill_manage guards, ledger, write_approval
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Hermes is the largest deployed self-writer and the best negative-result corpus: write-origin provenance, ownership/pin guards, read-before-write, a fail-closed ledger and a staged approval queue all held up in production, while every prompt-level quality rule was bypassed and the loop was silently dead for weeks (#95976) and the approval queue rotted (#105770). Hermes's ledger is 'telemetry, not a gate' and none of it is portable. Pawl consumes Hermes's pending queue, ledger and provenance, adds the missing verdict, receipts, funnel alarms, undo that restores whole bundles, and path-level enforcement that closes the write_file/patch bypass (#99729).

nearest_competitors.name: Prime Agent /refine (Prime Intellect)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Prime's typed, versioned harness_state.json with before/after snapshots and refinements.jsonl is a good candidate substrate, but acceptance is the refiner's own judgment, expectedOutcome is free text never checked, the overview injects an alphabetical 6-entry head slice so most entries never enter context, and '/refine is invisible' was closed unfixed. Pawl turns each refinement into a candidate with a checked expected_effect, shows the diff before apply, emits the load receipt that reveals the head-slice bug, and gates on outcomes.

nearest_competitors.name: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: dsh ships the best-specified attachment map in the field (typed pre-execute decisions, deny-only guards, fail-closed ApprovalOutcome, revertible Cordis effects, a session log with model-visible <=> logged) and explicitly deferred the evaluator 'until its authority, isolation, and provider contract are designed'. Pawl is that contract, implemented as a dsh plugin, and because dsh runs Claude Code/Codex hooks.json unmodified, one adapter covers three harnesses.

nearest_competitors.name: OpenClaw Skill Workshop + `claude plugin eval` (vendor measurement tooling)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: OpenClaw's proposal-first, hash-bound, event-ledgered Workshop and Anthropic's with/without plugin eval are the vendor pieces Pawl plugs into rather than competes with: the Workshop has an evaluator seam with zero third-party implementations and fail-open semantics, checks only safety regexes and hashes, and defaults to ungoverned auto; plugin eval has no paired statistics, no sealed split, a haiku judge by default, and lets the proposer author its own cases. Pawl is the first Workshop evaluator, wraps plugin eval as a sealed backend with cassette-derived graders the proposer cannot edit, and emits both vendors' formats.

risks: Replay fidelity and power: even sandbox-first re-execution diverges from itself (T=0 is not determinism; provider model updates mid-week invalidate control arms), so the protected corpus may be small and lift certification rare; if fewer than ~20 stable, eligible cassettes exist per user the gate is mostly a regression/safety detector, which must be stated honestly rather than sold as fitness.

Hooks are bypassable: Codex documents that some tool paths opt out, Hermes write_file/patch reach the skills dir directly, OpenClaw auto mode skips proposals, and Claude Code auto-memory may write through internal paths; until harnesses expose rooted write surfaces, enforcement is best-effort plus post-hoc quarantine, and a bypass in block mode is a silent hole unless the watcher alarm is loud.

Adapter churn is the real cost: Hermes shipped 947 commits in four days, OpenClaw breaks plugins per release, Claude Code's memory slug is unstable across versions; a 1-3 person team can keep at most three adapters conformance-green at a time, so sequencing (Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes first) and a pinned conformance suite are load-bearing.

Cost on paid plans: sandbox replays spend real model tokens (tens of thousands per cassette arm); without eligibility ties, early stopping, cached incumbent arms, per-store caps and a printed cost line the loop will be disabled exactly as Codex Memories and skill-creator evals were.

Fail-closed can become starvation: 'evaluator unavailable = reject' in block mode is correct for integrity but reproduces the approval-queue rot users hate unless holds expire loudly, defaults are computed, and observe mode remains the default.

Goodhart of the gate itself: a proposer that sees pass/fail per task can still learn to satisfy the protected corpus or the canary bank; sealing cassettes and probes, rotating held-out subsets, never exposing rationale, and leak-scanning candidates reduce but do not eliminate this, and the field has no seeded testbed for gate-gaming yet (we build one in month 3).

Statistical honesty under reuse: cassette reuse across candidates creates dependence no theorem covers; corpus rotation and the full-evidence invariant mitigate it, and the paper must report empirical false-commit rates under reuse rather than claim a guarantee.

The asymmetric disposition can be misread: researchers may see ADMIT_PROVISIONAL as 'no gate'; the benchmark must show it blocks harm quickly, or the design loses credibility with exactly the audience that would cite it.

Privacy and DLP: cassettes contain user prompts, code and secrets; a scrub failure or an over-eager share feature is a worse incident than any regression; local-only by default, provider-boundary rule, and no cross-user sharing in v1.

Vendor pre-emption: Anthropic (plugin eval) and OpenClaw (Workshop) could ship their own decision rules; Pawl's defensibility is cross-harness coverage, the neutral record profile, and the acceptor benchmark, none of which a single vendor is incentivized to build.

Operational canary false positives: scanner-style false positives without an override path convert a gate into a bypass incentive (hermes#94353); the false-block rate on the user's own benign edits must be a first-class reported metric.
open_questions: What fraction of real sessions are replayable to a terminal check across harnesses beyond Claude Code (measured so far: 7 sessions, 2,062 tool calls, one machine), and does that fraction rise if the recorder captures the user's test command explicitly at Stop time?

How stable is the incumbent self-replay noise floor across days and provider model updates, and what k and alpha does the observed per-task stability distribution justify? Is a floor keyed on model_served enough, or does the control arm need re-measurement on every model version?

How far do mechanical adherence predicates go before a cross-family judge is needed, and what is the judge's false-pass rate on 'followed' (Blind Curator's cliff at ~0.45 says retirement decisions cannot rest on it)?

How should observational pooled statistics from live sessions (confounded) be combined with paired replay evidence (unbiased but sparse) without overstating attribution — a kappa-style discount, or strictly separate labels?
Should the gate ever admit on rung-3 (judge-only) evidence for non-verifiable work (writing, research), or is human-on-the-loop the only honest disposition there?

Which Claude Code auto-memory writes are actually hookable via PreToolUse on the memory dir, and which arrive through internal paths that only the watcher can see? The same question for Codex Memories.
Does the dsh hook-protocol bridge preserve PostToolUse updatedToolOutput semantics so that served-result replay works under DSH, or does DSH need its own tools/post-execute replace path?

What is the right owner of the signing key for acceptance records (user, evaluator host, or both), and will the in-toto/OTel/EEE communities accept a learned-artifact-acceptance predicate alongside the tool-call-authorization predicates they are standardizing?

How much of the statistical machinery survives when tasks are non-exchangeable and arrive in a non-stationary stream (the user's work changes week to week) — is corpus rotation a fix or a new confound?

Can the same layer govern shared stores (SkillClaw groups, Hermes Skill Sync, ClawHub) via local re-verification on receivers' cassettes, and does that generalize to a federated merge protocol, or is per-environment forking the only honest answer?

Where is the line between 'candidate' and 'L4/L5 event' when an agent edits hooks, settings or the evaluator's config on its own machine — can the layer detect that mechanically in every harness, or only in those with typed surfaces?

artifact-lifecycle.name: Clade
artifact-lifecycle.tagline: A package manager for what your agent learns: content-addressed skills and memories with provenance taint, quarantine → canary → promote → retire, deterministic staleness, clade-pooled attribution, and a verified federation — one lifecycle across Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, DeepSeek Harness and Codex.
artifact-lifecycle.stance: LEARNED-ARTIFACT LIFECYCLE MANAGER, product-first. The unit is not the write (Pawl-style CI) nor the score (Hermetic-style sealed evaluator) nor the gate's confusion matrix (Turnstile-style benchmark); it is the ARTIFACT AS A PACKAGE with a lifecycle. Every SKILL.md bundle, memory entry, instinct, prompt note and instruction block on the machine gets: a content-hash identity and lineage (clade), machine-checkable environment assertions ("engines"/"peerDependencies" for the world it was born in), a provenance taint level, an owner and write authority, a lifecycle state (quarantine → canary → promoted → dormant | stale | retired | yanked), pooled outcome statistics over its clade conditioned on activation, a value-of-information trigger that decides whether to create/patch it at all, and a lockfile per environment that says exactly which versions are live for which harness. The acceptance gate (paired, activation-conditioned, anytime-valid) is one check inside `clade promote`, the way tests are one check inside `npm publish`; it is a means. The product is `clade status / diff / log / undo / audit / outdated / why / retire / publish / install` — the thing hermes-agent#12238 (r=38, "git for ~/.hermes"), prime-agent#1208, claude-code#82056 and hermes#96704 are literally asking for — plus a registry where sharing a skill means sharing receipts, not copying a file. Ships as a Claude Code plugin, a Hermes plugin, the first third-party OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` implementation, a DSH SkillProvider + pre-execute plugin, a pi/Prime `session_before_refine` extension, and a Reef recipe, all driven by one host-side lifecycle engine. Complements Hermetic (Tier-3 replay scores consume its receipts) and Turnstile (our lifecycle policies are a subject it can benchmark); differs from Pawl by governing what happens to an artifact for its whole life (activation, attribution, staleness, retirement, federation), not only the moment it is written.
artifact-lifecycle.thesis: Every mass-market substrate now ships a PROPOSER (Hermes background review + curator + /learn, Codex Memories, Claude Code auto-memory, ECC instincts, OpenClaw Workshop, Prime /refine) and none ships a LIFECYCLE: artifacts are files written on the writer's say-so, aged by timestamp (Hermes curator .usage.json), never bound to the environment they were born in, never attributed to outcomes, never retired on evidence, propagated by file copy (SkillClaw, Collective Wisdom, EvoMap Hub, ClawHub) and invisible to their owner. Five independent 2026 results say LLM-written artifacts have near-zero causal effect (CTA +0.3pp; SkillsBench 0 vs +16.2 human; Continual Harness 6.4% reuse; Demystifying Agent Skills precision 29.6→3.3% at 100 skills; SkillOpt gains carried by 1–4 edits), production stores are dominated by dormant, duplicated and stale entries (hermes#96704: 182 skills, many use_count=0, three same-topic clusters; #83580 51/62 archived skills unrecoverable), and the worst incidents are mutations of previously good artifacts (gfpyc's chrome-devtools rewrite at 02:17), truncation of the newest memory lines (claude-code#92998), secrets persisted (#101351, codex#41711) and rollbacks that do not restore (#96962). Therefore the dominant lifecycle operations are DON'T-WRITE, DEDUPE, RETIRE and UNDO — not ACCEPT — and the right abstraction is the one software already uses for exactly this problem: a package manager. Package managers have identity (content hash), versions and lineage, environment binding, signed provenance, install/upgrade/rollback, per-environment lockfiles, audit, outdated, dedupe and yank. Applying those semantics to learned artifacts makes staleness deterministic (an assertion fails on probe, no outcome statistics needed), makes attribution reach sample sizes a personal store never reaches on its own (pool outcomes over the clade and over the federation), makes "when not to evolve" a computable value-of-information decision instead of a "be ACTIVE" prompt, and makes federated sharing a resolution problem (base + per-environment overlays + receipt quorum) instead of an LLM merge. Because tiers 0–2 need zero model calls and run on logs every user already has, the layer delivers value on day one even in a world where the honest attribution verdict for most artifacts is "inconclusive" — which the null-effect literature says it will be.
artifact-lifecycle.rsi_positioning: Clade sits squarely in harness-RSI at the L2 scaffold rung (skills, memory, prompt notes; Reliable-survey L0 output / L1 model / L2 scaffold / L3 improver / L4 criterion), in the bounded, human-on-the-loop cell where the RSI survey (2607.07663) locates almost everything demonstrated, and it is the substrate-side answer to the two open problems that survey calls emptiest: "trustworthy accumulation" (persistent self-modifications lack the verification/rollback story weights have) and "governance-grade measurement of self-improvement". Positioning for RSI people: (1) Accumulation is where harness-RSI actually fails — EvoHarnessBench's harness-induced forgetting (BWT −5.3/−4.0/−34.7%), Demystifying's retrieval-precision collapse, Adaptive Auto-Harness's peak-then-decline, "Do Agent Optimizers Compound?" — and every one of these is a lifecycle failure (no retirement, no dedupe, no environment binding), not a proposer failure; Clade is the retention half of retention-vs-adaptation. (2) The verification hierarchy becomes a field on every lifecycle transition: each promote/retire record carries its rung (formal | execution | mechanical-outcome | learned-judge | none), and shared artifacts cannot be promoted below mechanical-outcome; this operationalizes "the difference between a loop that improves and one that circles is one rung of external verification". (3) The exchange rate of grounding is measured, per store, as the activation funnel (eligible → loaded → read → followed → outcome-labelled): a store whose artifacts are never activated receives zero exogenous signal no matter how many background forks run (hermes#95976: 41 forks, 0 updates, unnoticed for weeks). (4) The L3 boundary is enforced structurally: lifecycle policy, assertions probe, receipts and ledger are host-side, path-protected, and not evolvable by the loop (MetaRSI Eq. 30 sealed measurement; agentdescent freeze-by-name), so Clade keeps a harness-RSI loop bounded by construction; any proposal touching the lifecycle policy or the probe bank is an L4/L5 event routed to a human. (5) Federated stores are the propagation vector the MLAS matrix flags in its Collective row (100% payload persistence through Hermes background review; skill sync "can silently strip safety constraints"); quarantine + local re-verification + receipt quorum is the mitigation nobody has built. (6) Data-RSI and Model-RSI are out of scope, but Clade's signed acceptance records define which artifacts are training-worthy: only promoted, attributed, unstale artifacts should ever be folded into weights (WHALE/SIA-style), and MetaRSI's freshness rule (Eq. 22: evidence compiled before the last capability-altering change is stale) is applied to every clade posterior when the model or harness version changes. (7) It supplies the datasets the five surveys ask for and none ships: normalized ledgers of what production stores actually evolve (the harness/skill/memory analogue of EvoTrace) and a drift testbed for stale-artifact retirement.
what_evolves: SKILL.md bundles (agentskills.io layout: SKILL.md + references/ scripts/ assets/ templates/) in ~/.hermes/skills, ~/.claude/skills, OpenClaw skill dirs and Workshop proposals, DSH SkillProvider skills, Codex/pi skill dirs — the primary unit

Memory entries and topic files: Claude Code MEMORY.md index + typed topic files (user/feedback/project/reference), Hermes MEMORY.md/USER.md, Codex ~/.codex/memories, Mem0 entries — governed at file/topic granularity for outcome attribution and at entry granularity for lint/DLP/scope/staleness
ECC instincts (confidence-scored, scope-tagged files) — Clade implements the +confirm/−contradict/decay dynamics ECC documents but never shipped, from mechanical outcomes
Prime Agent harness_state.json entries (prompt notes, memories, skill references, subagent specs) and refinements.jsonl history
OpenClaw Workshop PROPOSAL.md → SKILL.md transitions and their append-only proposal ledger
Hand-written instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rule blocks): receipts, staleness probes, scope lint and undo only — never auto-mutated
Per-environment overlays (base skill + env-selector overlay sections) as first-class clade members in the federation
NOT in scope: harness source code, hooks/plugins configuration, model weights, and the lifecycle policy itself (frozen, host-side, outside the mutable surface)
artifact-lifecycle.fitness_and_acceptance: THE SIGNAL THAT DECIDES. Clade has no single fitness function; it has a lifecycle state machine whose transitions consume evidence from five tiers, cheapest first, with mechanical rejection overriding any LLM approval and never the reverse (PROCTOR 2609.02246). Tier 0 (deterministic, $0, every write): lint (frontmatter parses; referenced scripts/references exist; executable skill compiles; a claim labelled verified/tested must cite a tool-output span; placeholder tokens NNN/HH:MM/<your-path> never inside verified blocks — hermes#89963; session-specific facts such as ports, hostnames, absolute paths, dates never in global scope without a scope tag; Jaccard/embedding dedupe against the store — hermes#416 open since March), DLP scrub (entropy + pattern + allowlist; provider-boundary rule for background jobs per codex#41711), write-authority check (owner/unattended-writer policy per artifact, hash-at-read vs compare-at-write), provenance taint level (user text > tool output > web > other agents' artifacts; MLAS rule: agent-created origin never upgrades trust), and diff == declared modification (MetaRSI Eq. 27; AHE manifest). Tier 0 failure = quarantine or block; it costs nothing and is where most cheap field failures are caught. Tier 1 (deterministic from transcripts and hooks, $0): activation receipts per session — eligible (artifact was in a loadable location for this harness/project) → loaded (complete | truncated | not_loaded | wrong_store, with bytes available vs loaded; claude-code#82056/#92998/#90604) → read (Claude Code `Skill` tool_use or Read on the skill path; Hermes skill_view; pi resources_discover; DSH skills/change; OpenClaw runtime usage receipts) → followed (Lin et al. 2605.30621 HFR mechanical proxies: retrieval-to-use gap, answer-before-validation; an offline per-version rule extraction cached once, adherence judged only with a cross-family judge and only if that judge's false-pass rate has been audited below the Blind Curator cliff). No artifact ever receives outcome credit without a loaded+read receipt (Lin et al.: benefit is a property of the (update, consuming agent) pair; PAST-Bench 'artifacts written but never read'; CTA: 0/34 unnudged with-skill runs read the skill). Tier 2 (mechanical outcome labels, $0 marginal): per-session outcomes from harness-owned signals only — the session's own terminal verification (test command + exit code detected in the transcript), user-correction events on UserPromptSubmit following a load (Hermes' 'free negative label'), undo/revert events, task re-open within N hours, and cost/steps-to-done as continuous covariates. Never the writing model's self-judgment: Memory Reward Inflation (self-grades endorse 31–54% of wrong answers), 'More Convincing, Not More Correct' (judge pass 0.72→0.94 at flat 0.20 accuracy), Blind Curator (judge false-pass ≥ (1−τ)/2 ≈ 0.45 makes contribution-based retirement retire nothing). Tier 3 (paired sandbox replay, $, opt-in, coding sessions only): cassette + git snapshot → branched re-execution with and without the artifact in a disposable worktree/container, with a same-configuration A-vs-A′ control arm as the noise floor (The Replay Gap 2608.08239: 3–8% replay validity for early interventions, T=0 is not determinism; CTA: detectors fire identically on no-change pairs), outcomes strictly pass | fail | inconclusive with agent execution off by default (the three binding constraints microsoft/SkillOpt#155 maintainers set), terminal check = the session's own tests, wrapped on Claude Code by `claude plugin eval` (scaffold_script restores the snapshot, history_file is the prefix, --ablation with-without, runs=k) and exported as Harbor tasks elsewhere. Own measurement: pure VCR replay is dead for real sessions (idempotent prefix 0–1 calls in 7/7 sessions; 50% workspace writes, 20% external), so Tier 3 is sandbox-first and is a behavior-change/regression detector, not a fitness function. Tier 4 (safety canary): 30–100 domain-conditioned probes seeded from SkillMisevo-Bench, MemEvoBench and Agent-SafetyBench plus operational invariants from field incidents (no persisted tool-avoidance after a transient failure — hermes#6051; no secrets/PII — #101351; no deletion or weakening of standing permission rules — #105921; no destructive-action rules such as 'close ALL Chrome windows'; egress policy), run with vs without the artifact, any negative delta blocks, cross-family judge with mechanical override; re-run on reuse-in-new-context (SafeEvolve's second boundary; SkillMisevo: three exposures suffice and benign mixing does not wash them out, so per-write not periodic). TRANSITIONS. quarantine → canary: Tier 0 pass, taint policy satisfied (untrusted-derived artifacts require a human or Tier 3), VOI > 0. canary → promoted: activation observed in ≥ k eligible sessions AND clade-pooled outcome evidence clears: paired sessions (with-artifact vs held-out) feed a PACE-style testing-by-betting e-process on discordant pairs only (w=1 if with-arm passed and without-arm failed), commit at wealth ≥ 1/α with a mixture over betting fractions, run-level spend across the store's promotion stream via SEA's horizon-free CTHS schedule δ_k = δ₀/(Z·k·log²(k+1)) (Z≈3.39; the naive 1/(2k log²) schedule over-spends 1.69×), NSF (not-sufficient-evidence) as a first-class state that leaves the artifact in canary rather than rejecting it (SEA's precedence ACCEPT > NSF > REJECT > HOLD). promoted → stale: any environment assertion fails on probe — deterministic, immediate, one probe, no statistics (Grounding Agent Memory 2609.11060 does environment probing at write time; Clade probes at every load, like `engines`/`peerDependencies`). promoted → dormant: not loaded in N eligible sessions (archive, never delete; a dormant artifact still costs context tokens and retrieval precision). promoted → retired: Ratchet's rule (2605.22148) c(clade) ≤ −τ after ≥ N_min trials, τ=0.10, N_min=100, with the non-divergence floor E[pass@1] ≥ E[p0] − (τ+ε) − C·δ, where N_min is reached by pooling over the clade and the federation — the reason per-artifact retirement never fires in a personal store (use_count 0–10). Attributed harm at reuse (Tier 4 or a correction/revert pattern) retires immediately (SafeEvolve). NOISE, HONESTLY. Binary outcomes over 20–40 paired sessions detect only large lifts: own simulation (research/tools/gate_power_sim.py) — greedy 'keep if mean went up' commits 44–46% false at zero lift (reproducing PACE's 30–42%); the anytime-valid paired gate holds false-commit ≤ 4% at any N but detects +10pp only 11% of the time at N=40 (39% at N=160), +20pp 44%/98%, +30pp 98% at N=40. So the expected honest verdict for most artifacts is INCONCLUSIVE, consistent with the null-effect literature, and Clade reports tri-state plus pass rate ± stddev over replicates, never one number (hermes#96704's operators re-derived exactly this). Power is raised three ways: clade pooling (all versions, patches, forks and per-environment overlays of one root pool their sessions, HGM's clade metaproductivity applied to skills — a skill's own load count or success rate is a weak predictor of whether investing in its lineage pays, and the clade posterior, not the node posterior, drives patch-vs-create and serve-which-version), federation pooling (receipts from other environments count with a per-environment discount), and richer per-session signals (corrections count, steps-to-done, tokens, divergence step) as covariates. PER-TASK REGRESSION. Only Tier 3 has tasks. The protected corpus is past sessions with observed stability (incumbent passes k/k on replay, measured by the free A-vs-A′ baseline); a pass→fail flip counts only after k-of-n confirmation — own simulation: at Bernoulli(0.6), k=1 false-blocks 93–100%, k=2 44–91%, k=3 13–43%; test-verified coding sessions are far more deterministic than that and the per-task self-divergence rate is measured, not assumed. Retention and adaptation are reported separately (EvoHarnessBench BWT/FWT) because additive-only growth is not regression-safe. RANDOMIZED VS OBSERVATIONAL PAIRS. The e-process guarantee holds only for randomized pairs: canary alternation (artifact served on alternate eligible sessions — natively via DSH SkillProvider, Hermes skill-list filtering hook, OpenClaw plugin; on Claude Code via an active-set symlink swapped at SessionStart, applying from the next session). Where alternation is off (default for memory), pairs are matched on task signature and are labelled ADVISORY — confounded by task mix, user learning and model updates; a freshness rule discounts all evidence compiled before a model/harness version change (MetaRSI Eq. 22), and agentdescent's κ-discount on evidence counts is applied when the outcome proxy (correction detection) disagrees with a sparse verified label. SAFETY. Misevolve (memory alone drops refusal 99.4→54.4% with no adversary) and SkillMisevo (21/21 evolved configs author unsafe artifacts; carryover ASR 16→35%) make safety a transition condition, not a scanner: Tier 4 runs at canary → promoted and at reuse-in-new-context; taint-conditioned strictness; agent-created origin never upgrades trust (MLAS: Hermes scanner exempted agent-created origin → 40/40 payloads persisted); the deterministic invariant that a revision may not silently drop a verification or reversibility requirement its ancestor asserted (SafeEvolve). TAMPERING VS OVERFITTING. Tampering: the store index, snapshots, receipts, ledger, assertions, probe bank and lifecycle policy are host-side, outside every harness's write surface, path-protected on the generic write path (Claude Code PreToolUse permissionDecision, Hermes pre_tool_call fail-closed, OpenClaw before_tool_call block:true, DSH tools/pre-execute deny-only guard, Codex PostToolUse block) with a file watcher that quarantines and snapshots any direct write that slipped past (shell redirection, opted-out tool paths) — Clade is explicit that this is a containment convention, not a security boundary, and defers sealed scoring to a Hermetic-class evaluator for Tier 3; ledger entries are hash-chained and HMAC'd; a candidate whose diff ≠ declared modification is rejected. Overfitting: proposers receive failure traces and the rejected-edit archive as text, never probe contents, protected-corpus identities or scoring criteria (scorer-blind feedback; SkillOpt#154 copied judge regexes verbatim); a content scan rejects candidates quoting probe or grader tokens; a random fraction of promotions is re-scored by an independent-family judge. ACTIVATION. 'Eligible but never loaded' across N sessions is an alarm, not a verdict — it caught EvoMap#624 (inject drops strategy text), AutoResearchClaw (first 5 alphabetical skills only), ECC#2599 (skills installed outside discovery paths), claude-code#82056 (truncated index). Every promotion also runs one activation smoke test per harness (a single `-p` session whose prompt should trigger the artifact; assert the load/read receipt) to catch discovery-path bugs before crediting anything. ATTRIBUTION. Causal attribution is abstention-first (Causal Agent Replay: the CI-gated locus rule abstains ~82% on real traces; more rollouts cannot fix low replay fidelity) — Clade reports helps | hurts | inconclusive per clade, uses Tier 3 do_context replay only for disputes and shared-publication, and treats attribution as a pooled posterior over the clade rather than a per-artifact verdict. COST. Tiers 0–2 cost nothing per session; Tier 3 and 4 are opt-in with a per-day cap and a circuit breaker; every report prints what the gate cost; the VOI trigger accounts for eval cost, carry cost (context tokens × sessions, and a retrieval-dilution penalty −δ per artifact beyond K per the Demystifying curve) and the class base-rate prior for expected lift (≈0 for LLM-written, updated from the user's own promoted history). Gates fail in the field by starving (hermes#105770: 241 staged writes over 8 weeks), so the default disposition is computed (Tier-0 pass → canary automatically; hold only on critical scanner finding, high taint, or authority conflict), holds expire into rejection with a reason, scanner findings have an override path, and pending-queue age/size raises an alarm — silent on pass, loud on block, never silent on hold.
artifact-lifecycle.core_technical_insight: Treat a learned artifact as a package, not a file, and three unsolved problems become tractable at once. (1) STALENESS IS DEPENDENCY RESOLUTION, NOT OUTCOME STATISTICS. Every artifact carries machine-checkable environment assertions extracted at write time (binary versions, paths, ports, hostnames, API shapes, repo commit ranges, OS) — the `engines`/`peerDependencies` of the world it was born in — and Clade probes them at every load for ~0 cost. An artifact whose assertions fail is stale immediately, before any session fails because of it; assertions with session scope (a port, a temp path) are the same lint that keeps session facts out of global rules. Competitors detect staleness only after enough failed sessions accumulate, which a personal store never provides (Ratchet's N_min=100 versus use_count 0–10), or age by timestamp (Hermes curator), which retires the wrong things. (2) ATTRIBUTION POOLS OVER THE CLADE, NOT THE NODE. HGM's finding that a parent's own fitness poorly predicts its descendants' fitness has an exact analogue for skills: a skill's own load count or success rate is a weak predictor of whether patching it further helps. Clade pools per-session outcomes, conditioned on activation receipts, over the artifact's whole lineage (versions, patches, forks, per-environment overlays, and the same content hash in other users' environments), so N_min becomes reachable and the posterior answers the two lifecycle questions the curator actually faces — invest in this lineage or start fresh, and which version to serve — while the e-process on discordant randomized pairs keeps the false-promotion rate bounded. (3) 'WHEN NOT TO EVOLVE' IS A VALUE-OF-INFORMATION CALCULATION. Expected benefit = P(recurrence of the task signature, estimated from the user's own session history) × class base-rate lift (a prior near zero for LLM-written artifacts, updated from the store's own promoted history) × value per session; minus carry cost (context tokens × expected loads, plus a retrieval-dilution penalty beyond K artifacts), minus evaluation cost. A write happens only if this is positive; a review fork is spawned only if the session carried a failure signature, a correction, or a repeated pattern. This turns Hermes' 'be ACTIVE — a pass that does nothing is a missed opportunity' into a number that says nothing-to-save is normal, and it is the same computation that decides dormancy. Because identity is a content hash, the lockfile, the undo, the funnel, the attribution and the federation are one ledger: publishing an artifact means publishing its acceptance record and receipt summary, importing means quarantine + local assertion probe + local receipts, and cross-user conflicts resolve as base-plus-overlay by environment selector with a receipt quorum, never as an LLM merge.

architecture.component: Harness adapters (Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, DSH, Codex, pi/Prime, ECC)
architecture.responsibility: Map each harness's learned-state tree, session-log location and schema, native activation events, and generic write path onto Clade's common model; expose a rooted write surface; emit load receipts. Ship with a version-pinned conformance suite (does a deny stop the write; does a rejected proposal ever reach disk; does an evaluator timeout fail closed; does a promoted artifact actually load).
architecture.interfaces: Claude Code hooks (SessionStart, InstructionsLoaded, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, FileChanged) + ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl transcripts + `claude plugin eval`; Hermes ~/.hermes/skills, MEMORY.md, pending/{skills,memory}/*.json, skill_ledger.jsonl, .usage.json, plugin ctx.register_hook(), pre_tool_call; OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate / skill_proposal_changed / skill_changed / before_tool_call; DSH SkillProvider registry, tools/pre-execute, tools/post-execute, skills/change, hook-protocol bridge; Codex ~/.codex/memories + PostToolUse; pi/Prime harness_state.json, refinements.jsonl, session_before_refine, tool_call/tool_result/resources_discover; ECC instincts dir.

architecture.component: Artifact index + content-addressed snapshot store + lockfile
architecture.responsibility: Canonicalize every artifact bundle (SKILL.md + references/scripts/assets, memory topic files, instincts, prompt notes) into a blake3 content hash; maintain lineage (parent, clade root, forks, overlays); snapshot the whole learned-state tree before any unattended write; keep `clade.lock` per environment (which version is live for which harness, state, pin, overlay, last probe); GC by policy with depth > 1.
architecture.interfaces: `clade status | log | diff | undo --session <id> | restore <artifact>@<version>`; snapshot round-trip self-test; conflict check for artifacts touched by later sessions.

architecture.responsibility: Per session and per artifact, record eligible → loaded (complete/truncated/not_loaded/wrong_store, bytes available vs loaded) → read → followed, plus outcome labels (terminal verification, corrections, reverts, re-open) and spend attributed to foreground vs background writers. Deterministic; no model calls.
architecture.interfaces: Reads transcripts and hook payloads; writes receipts.jsonl (HMAC); feeds the funnel, the clade posterior and the change feed.

architecture.responsibility: Tier-0 deterministic checks at write and at host update; secret/PII scrub; per-artifact ownership and unattended-writer policy; path-level enforcement on the generic write path plus a watcher that quarantines and snapshots any direct write that bypassed hooks; diff-equals-declared check.
architecture.interfaces: PreToolUse permissionDecision / pre_tool_call / before_tool_call / tools/pre-execute / Codex PostToolUse; fs watcher; quarantine dir.

architecture.responsibility: Extract world assertions from artifact text (versions, paths, ports, hosts, API flags, repo ranges, OS) into the manifest at write time, tag scope (session/project/global), probe them at every load and on host update, mark stale, and re-verify before retirement.
architecture.interfaces: assertions[] in manifest; `clade outdated`; probe results into the ledger; stale flag in lockfile.

architecture.component: Lifecycle engine (state machine + VOI trigger + e-process accountant)
architecture.responsibility: Drive quarantine → canary → promoted → dormant | stale | retired | yanked; compute the value-of-information decision for create/patch and for spawning background reviews; schedule canary alternation; run the PACE-style e-process and the CTHS spend schedule; compute default dispositions for the review queue with expiry and alarms; enforce that the policy itself is host-side and non-evolvable.
architecture.interfaces: Transition records (acceptance records) into the ledger; canary serving instructions to adapters; daily digest; `clade why <artifact>`.

architecture.responsibility: Pool activation-conditioned outcomes over lineage and federation into Beta posteriors per clade and per version; apply freshness discounting on model/harness epoch changes and κ-discount on proxy/verified disagreement; emit helps | hurts | inconclusive with abstention as a first-class result; decide patch-vs-create and serve-which-version.
architecture.interfaces: Consumes receipts + evidence pairs; produces clade stats consumed by lifecycle engine, curator hooks and the registry.

architecture.responsibility: Compile cassettes into paired with/without cases in a disposable worktree or container, run the same-configuration control arm as the noise floor, produce pass | fail | inconclusive, wrap `claude plugin eval` on Claude Code and export Harbor tasks for other CLIs; consume Hermetic-style sealed score receipts where available.
architecture.interfaces: cassette → case compiler; `clade audit --replay`; Harbor task.toml export; plugin-eval --json ingestion.

architecture.responsibility: Run the domain-conditioned probe bank (refusal, injection, destructive action, DLP/egress, operational invariants) with vs without the candidate at promotion and at reuse-in-new-context; cross-family judge with mechanical override; probe bank sealed from proposers and rotated.
architecture.interfaces: Probe bank versioned by hash; results attached to the transition record; block on negative delta.

architecture.responsibility: Publish = signed bundle + acceptance record + receipt summary + assertions + taint (never sessions); import = quarantine + local assertion probe + local receipts before live; per-environment overlays instead of one converging skill; receipt quorum across environments; yank propagation; org-scoped trust first.
architecture.interfaces: DSSE/in-toto statement with predicateType artifact-acceptance/v0.1; `clade publish | install | yank`; hub API; agentskills.io evidence/ convention.

architecture.responsibility: Change feed with receipts, batched push-notified review with diff + evidence + activation history + default disposition + expiry, spend ledger and caps, self-serve `clade audit` (does my store help me?), and chat-surface integrations.
architecture.interfaces: CLI, daily digest, Hermes /skills and gateway buttons, OpenClaw Workshop UI, DSH web UI plugin, Claude Code slash commands.
