FEDERATION BUNDLE: in-toto Statement v1 with predicateType "https://clade.dev/artifact-acceptance/v0.1", subject = bundle tree hash, predicate = transition record 5 + receipt summary counts + assertions + taint; no sessions or cassettes ever leave the machine.
artifact-lifecycle.integration_surface: CLAUDE CODE (first adapter; builder's own harness). SessionStart: resolve the memory store (project slug stability check for underscore paths), hash MEMORY.md and topic files, compute bytes available vs the 200-line/25KB cap → emit the load receipt (complete | truncated | not_loaded | wrong_store), swap the canary active-set symlink for skills if alternation is on. InstructionsLoaded: record which CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/skill files were loaded with hashes (the eligible→loaded edge). UserPromptSubmit: tag user text as trusted provenance; detect correction patterns following a load and attribute a negative label to the loaded artifacts. PreToolUse: permissionDecision=deny on writes by unattended writers to store paths (memory dir, skills dir) unless the write carries a Clade candidate token; updatedInput for Tier-3 replay. PostToolUse: record tool I/O for cassettes; `Skill` tool_use and Read on skill paths = read receipts; updatedToolOutput serves recorded externals during replay ($0.007/replay verified). Stop: detect the terminal verification, label the session, run the VOI trigger for any pending proposal, close the spend record. FileChanged on MEMORY.md: quarantine + snapshot direct writes (Claude's own auto-memory writes are recorded, snapshotted, linted and DLP-scrubbed but not blocked by default). `claude plugin eval` is the Tier-3 backend (scaffold_script = restore snapshot, history_file = transcript prefix, --ablation with-without, runs=k, --json into the e-process; --max-cost-usd as the cap). HERMES. Ingest skill_ledger.jsonl (sha256 before/after manifests map 1:1 onto Clade ledger entries), .usage.json (use_count/last_used_at → activation), tools/skill_provenance.py write_origin (foreground vs background_review → writer field). Register as the reviewer of ~/.hermes/pending/{skills,memory}/*.json: compute the default disposition (Tier-0 pass → auto-apply into canary via the same gate-bypass token /skills approve uses; hold only on block), expire holds, surface batched diff+evidence in /skills and gateway buttons — this fixes starvation (#105770) and the un-approvable scanner deadlock (#94353) without changing Hermes. pre_tool_call (shell, fail-closed) enforces path authority for write_file/patch/terminal (#99729). ctx.register_hook() on the curator: replace timestamp aging (active→stale→archived) with assertion staleness + dormancy + clade posterior, and make the background-review fork conditional on the VOI trigger (no failure signature, correction or repeated pattern → no fork; kills the 30K-token zero-yield forks of #95976). Rollback goes through Clade snapshots (whole bundle incl. references/scripts — #96962). OPENCLAW. Register a `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin (first third-party implementation): consume {proposal, candidate BundleSnapshot with per-file sha256 + treeSha256, baseline, reason}; return {decision: pass|revise|block, findings[{ruleId, severity}], metrics{activation_prior, taint, voi_net, dedupe_nearest, assertions}}; because OpenClaw evaluators fail open on error/skipped, the plugin converts its own errors into an explicit block when policy is fail-closed. Consume skill_proposal_changed / skill_changed (expectedRevisionHash, correlationId) into the ledger; runtime usage receipts → activation; before_tool_call block:true for store-path authority; in `autonomous.mode: auto` the fs watcher still snapshots direct edits. DEEPSEEK HARNESS. A dsh plugin: tools/pre-execute deny-only guard on store paths; tools/post-execute attaches receipts; skills/change events → activation; a remote SkillProvider that serves the promoted set (and canary alternation per session) directly from the lockfile — DSH is the cleanest substrate for canary serving; Cordis revertible effects give atomic unmount of a retired skill. The Claude Code hook bundle also runs unmodified under dsh via the hook-protocol bridge. CODEX. ~/.codex/memories ingestion; PostToolUse block/replace for authority (documented opt-outs → watcher fallback); provider-boundary rule flags a memory job whose provider differs from the source session's (#41711). pi / PRIME AGENT. `session_before_refine` extension gates /refine on VOI and wraps its edits as candidates; refinements.jsonl and per-edit snapshots are ingested; tool_call block for authority; resources_discover for activation; `/refine` becomes visible (#1208) through the change feed. ECC. Instincts dir indexed; SessionStart injection above a confidence floor replaced by lockfile state; the documented +0.05/−0.1/−0.02-per-week dynamics implemented from mechanical outcomes. REEF. Clade ships as a recipe: propose = the candidate queue; evaluate = Tiers 1–3 (paired, protected seed floor — #356); decide = the lifecycle engine (e-process + spend); Reef's versioned releases and canary/shadow routing map onto Clade states; rollback depth > 1 via snapshots. HARBOR. Tier-3 cases and the drift testbed export as Harbor task.toml families so every CLI adapter and Reef #447 inherit them. STANDARDS. Acceptance record profiled as an in-toto predicate (alongside #554 agent-decision), an OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result attribute extension for incumbent/decision fields, and an `evidence/` convention PR to agentskills.io; a `claude plugin eval` JSON → record converter.
mvp_2_weeks: Day 1–2: Claude Code store adapter — index ~/.claude/projects/*/memory, ~/.claude/skills, CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md; canonicalize bundles; blake3 content hashes; `clade status` (harnesses found, artifact counts by kind/state) and `clade log`/`clade diff --since` change feed built from transcript Write/Edit tool_use on store paths (which artifact, before/after, originating session).

Day 2–3: Load receipts — SessionStart + InstructionsLoaded hooks emit store identity, slug stability, hash, bytes available vs loaded, status complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store; receipts.jsonl with HMAC.

Day 3–4: Read receipts and activation funnel from transcripts (Skill tool_use, Read on skill paths; eligible→loaded→read per artifact); `clade audit --activation` prints per-artifact eligible/loaded/read counts and 'never loaded in N eligible sessions' alarms.

Day 4–6: Snapshot + undo — content-addressed snapshot of the whole learned-state tree before any unattended write (PreToolUse deny+snapshot on store paths, FileChanged on MEMORY.md, fs watcher fallback); `clade undo --session <id>` (adds→delete, updates→restore, deletes→recreate) with conflict check for later-touched artifacts; round-trip self-test on every snapshot; depth > 1 and GC policy.

Day 6–7: Tier-0 lint + DLP — frontmatter/referenced-files/compile checks, verified-claim-must-cite-span, placeholder tokens, session facts in global scope, dedupe against the store; entropy+pattern secret scrub; quarantine dir; ownership/authority policy per artifact (user-validated artifacts immutable to unattended writers by default).

Day 7–8: Environment assertions v0 — regex/AST extraction of paths, ports, hostnames, binary versions and repo ranges from artifact text; probe at SessionStart; `clade outdated` lists stale artifacts with the failing assertion.

Day 8–10: Lifecycle state machine v0 (quarantine → canary → promoted → dormant | stale) with lockfile; canary alternation via active-set symlink swap at SessionStart (opt-in per artifact class); daily digest with default dispositions, expiry and pending-queue alarm.

Day 10–12: Mechanical outcome labels v0 — terminal-verification detection (test command + exit), correction-pattern detection after a load on UserPromptSubmit, revert events; clade posterior per lineage; `clade why <artifact>` printing helps | hurts | inconclusive with pass rate ± stddev, discordant-pair count and evidence type (randomized vs advisory); PACE e-process + CTHS spend accountant as a ~300-line library with the gate_power_sim.py results as its test suite.

Day 12–13: Spend ledger — per-session tokens/USD from transcripts attributed to foreground vs background writers; per-day caps and a circuit breaker on repeated identical retries; every digest prints what Clade itself cost (target: $0 for Tiers 0–2).

Day 13–14: Hermes read-only adapter (~/.hermes/skills, MEMORY.md, skill_ledger.jsonl, .usage.json, pending/) so `clade status/audit/outdated` work on a Hermes store; run the whole pipeline on the builder's own 7 sessions + a volunteer Hermes store; publish a demo report and the pip/pipx package.
roadmap_3_months: Month 1 (weeks 3–4): Hermes write path — pending-queue reviewer with computed default dispositions, gate-bypass replay of approved payloads, pre_tool_call path authority, curator hook replacing timestamp aging with assertion-staleness + dormancy + clade stats, VOI-gated background-review trigger; batched push-notified review (CLI, Telegram/Discord gateway) with diff + evidence + activation history, expiry and scanner-override path; `clade audit` self-serve report (cheapest arm first) with tri-state per artifact; adapter conformance suite v0 pinned to Hermes and Claude Code versions.

Month 2 (weeks 5–6): OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin (fail-closed wrapper, ledger consumption, before_tool_call authority) — the first third-party implementation on that seam; DSH plugin (pre-execute guard, post-execute receipts, SkillProvider serving promoted/canary sets from the lockfile); Codex and pi/Prime read-only adapters with `session_before_refine` gating; safety canary v1 (probe bank seeded from SkillMisevo-Bench, MemEvoBench, Agent-SafetyBench + operational invariants; cross-family judge; mechanical override).

Month 2 (weeks 7–8): Tier-3 sandbox replayer for coding sessions — cassette → paired case compiler over `claude plugin eval` (scaffold_script snapshot restore, history_file prefix, with/without arms, runs=k), A-vs-A′ null floor, pass|fail|inconclusive, Harbor task export for codex/qwen-coder/kimi/dsh; Reef recipe (propose→evaluate→decide with protected seed floor and PACE decide policy, PR to Human-Agent-Society/reef); activation smoke test per promotion.

Month 3 (weeks 9–10): Federation v1 (clade hub) — signed bundles (DSSE/in-toto artifact-acceptance predicate), publish requires a transition record + receipt summary, import = quarantine + local assertion probe + local receipts, per-environment overlays with env selectors instead of one converging skill, receipt quorum, yank propagation, org-scoped trust; `evidence/` convention PR to agentskills.io; converter from `claude plugin eval` JSON and OpenClaw evaluator envelopes to the record.

Month 3 (weeks 11–12): Research artifacts — drift testbed (SkillsBench + Terminal-Bench 2.x tasks with versioned tool/API/path drift per epoch, exported as a Harbor task family) and the retirement-policy experiment (append-only, timestamp curator, Ratchet per-skill, SafeEvolve, Clade, oracle-pruned, no-store; 5 seeds; BWT/FWT, retrieval precision, safety carryover, cost); null-effect lifecycle audit on volunteer stores (hermes#96704 cohort); ledger dataset release (normalized transition records from all adapters); paper submission; v1 release with docs, conformance suite, and the OpenClaw/DSH/Hermes marketplace listings.
artifact-lifecycle.killer_demo: Five minutes on a laptop that already runs Claude Code and Hermes, no API key needed for the first four. Minute 1 — `pipx install clade && clade adopt`: 'Found 2 harnesses. 214 learned artifacts: 182 Hermes skills, 27 Claude Code memory entries in 4 topic files, 5 CLAUDE.md files. Snapshotted the tree (snap_…, round-trip verified). Change feed, last 7 days: 12 artifacts changed, 9 by unattended writers — [diff] [session] for each.' Minute 2 — `clade audit`: 'Activation: 61 skills never loaded in any of 340 eligible sessions; 3 memory files loaded TRUNCATED — your MEMORY.md is 26.1KB against a 25KB cap and the 14 newest lines were dropped, including the correction you made on Tuesday (the text it corrects is still loaded). Staleness: 17 skills assert paths, ports or binary versions that no longer exist on this machine (e.g. chrome-devtools asserts port 9222 and Chrome ≥128; Chrome is 131 and 9222 is closed). Duplicates: 3 clusters of same-topic skills. Scope lint: 6 global rules contain session-specific ports/paths.' Minute 3 — `clade why chrome-devtools`: 'Clade of 4 versions, 38 activated sessions (randomized canary: 12 pairs, 5 discordant, wealth 1.9 < 20 → INCONCLUSIVE; advisory task-signature pairs: sessions loading v7 had +1.4 corrections/session, HURTS-advisory). v7 was written by background_review at 02:17 on 2026-09-13, bypassed skill_manage (direct file write), failed authority (user-validated), contains a destructive rule "close ALL Chrome windows", VOI −$0.29/month. Disposition: hold, expiring in 7 days.' Then `clade undo --session sess_4d…` restores v6 with its references/ and scripts/, verified round-trip, in one command. Minute 4 — `clade digest`: 'Proposed lifecycle actions: retire 17 stale (re-verify first), archive 61 dormant (saves ~9K context tokens/session and lifts retrieval precision), hold 1, keep 1 promoted (P(lift>0)=0.97 over 14 discordant pairs; sessions loading it ran 22pp fewer corrections). Spend: Hermes background review cost $31 last week for 0 promoted artifacts; Clade cost $0.00.' Flip `clade canary on` and show tomorrow's funnel row: proposed 3 → canary 2 → promoted 0 → activated 2 → attributed 0 (NSF), with the VOI trigger having declined to spawn 9 of 11 review forks. Minute 5 — `clade publish chrome-devtools@v6` on this machine and `clade install` on a second machine with Codex + DSH: the bundle arrives with its signed acceptance record, lands in quarantine, its assertions are probed locally (Chrome version differs → an overlay is suggested rather than a merge), and it goes live only after the local receipts arrive. The same lockfile now serves Claude Code, Hermes and DSH on the second machine.
artifact-lifecycle.research_contribution: TITLE: 'Learned Artifacts Are Packages: Deterministic Staleness, Clade-Pooled Attribution, and Value-of-Information Triggers for the Lifecycle of Self-Improving Agent Stores'. CLAIMS (three, each falsifiable). C1 (audit): in production stores of self-improving agents, a majority of learned artifacts are dormant (never activated in ≥20 eligible sessions), deterministically stale (≥1 environment assertion fails on probe), or duplicated, and activation-only receipts — zero model calls — identify them; the activation rate of the median artifact is below 10%. C2 (retirement under drift): on a drift testbed, a lifecycle policy that combines assertion probing, dormancy, and clade-pooled mechanical-outcome retirement keeps retained held-out utility (BWT) within ε=2pp of an oracle-pruned store, while append-only stores lose ≥5pp per drift epoch, timestamp aging retires the wrong artifacts (precision <0.5 against outcome-labelled staleness), and per-skill Ratchet retirement (N_min=100) never fires at personal-store sample sizes; assertion probes reach AUC ≥0.85 against outcome-labelled staleness. C3 (when not to evolve): VOI-gated writing cuts artifact count by ≥60% and background-review cost by ≥50% relative to a 'be ACTIVE' policy at matched budget with no measurable held-out utility loss (paired e-process finds no lift for the ungated store over the gated one). EXPERIMENT: (a) Audit of N≥20 volunteer Hermes/Claude Code stores (the hermes#96704 cohort; 182-skill deployment; 70 skills/3 agents/5 months) using receipts only, plus paired sandbox replay on the re-executable coding subset with an A-vs-A′ null floor and 3–5 replicates per case. (b) Drift testbed built from SkillsBench (87 tasks, deterministic verifiers) and Terminal-Bench 2.x tasks, packaged as a Harbor task family: E epochs in which pinned tool versions, CLI flags, paths and API shapes change so that a known fraction of previously authored skills become wrong; skills authored by a Hermes-style background reviewer from an adaptation split; agents = Claude Code and Codex via Harbor; 5 seeds; report BWT/FWT (EvoHarnessBench protocol), retrieval precision vs pool size (Demystifying curve), safety carryover (SkillMisevo clean-session probes), and cost per epoch. (c) The VOI arm: same stream, 'be ACTIVE' vs VOI-gated proposer, matched token budget, with a no-store and a parallel-K test-time-scaling control (AI2 2607.12227). BASELINES: append-only (Hermes/ECC default), Hermes timestamp curator, Ratchet outcome retirement, SafeEvolve retire-on-attributed-harm, SkillOpt-Sleep strict held-out gate, oracle-pruned store (upper bound), no-store (null), parallel-K TTS at matched budget. FALSIFIERS: C1 fails if audited stores show median activation ≥50% or if assertion-stale artifacts are still causally helpful in Tier-3 replay; C2 fails if assertion probes have AUC <0.7 against outcome-labelled staleness, if clade pooling retires artifacts with true positive contribution at a rate >α (false retirement), or if the Clade policy trails oracle pruning by >5pp BWT; C3 fails if the VOI-gated store loses measurable held-out utility (e-process commits for the ungated store) or if the class base-rate prior is so wrong that VOI blocks the 1–4 edits that carry gains. A secondary methodological result — the divergence-point distribution of real refiner edits under branched re-execution and the fraction of production edits that never change any action — is reported regardless of the verdicts, filling the middle case between VCR-naive replay and Replay-Gap hopelessness.
artifact-lifecycle.adoption_path: Day-zero value with no model calls and no loop is the wedge: receipts, change feed, staleness and undo work on hand-written CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md for 100% of Claude Code users and on any ~/.hermes, so the first users are exactly the people who filed hermes#12238 (r=38 'git for ~/.hermes'), hermes#96704 (paired-arm RFC with production data), claude-code#82056/#92998 (load/truncation receipts), prime#1208 (invisible /refine) and openviking#4178 (one-click session reversal) — we answer those threads with a link. Registry-side, free, off the hot path is the only gate shape that has spread at 389k-star scale (ClawHub VirusTotal), so Clade ships as marketplace plugins where the users already are: a Claude Code plugin, a Hermes plugin (pending-queue reviewer + curator hook), the first third-party OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin (zero exist), a DSH marketplace plugin next to dsh-verify/dsh-verification in the slot DSH deliberately left open, and a Reef recipe for the research crowd. Upstream, small PRs that make the vendor emit or accept our record rather than compete: Hermes curator hook + `.protected` generalization, OpenClaw evaluator fail-closed option and `expected_revision_hash` reuse, agentskills.io `evidence/` + `version` convention, a `claude plugin eval` JSON→record converter, an in-toto artifact-acceptance predicate filed alongside #554, an OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result extension. The federation launches org-scoped (teams sharing SkillClaw groups, OpenViking enterprise stores, CORAL swarms) where the trust question is easiest, then opens to public hubs (ClawHub, EvoMap Hub, Hermes Skill Sync) as the 'effect evidence' column registries currently lack. Credibility path: the audit dataset and the Harbor drift testbed give benchmark authors (SEA-Eval, SEAGym, EvoHarnessBench) and the RSI workshop a lifecycle protocol; Reef #357/#358 and SkillOpt#155 contributors are first-adopter co-authors; every report Clade prints carries its own cost line so nobody can accuse it of the silent-drain failure that killed Codex Memories for users. Default mode is observe-only (silent on pass); blocking is opt-in per surface; the only loud default is the starvation alarm.

nearest_competitors.name: Hermes Agent (skill_manage guards, curator, skill_ledger, .usage.json, write_approval staging, Collective Wisdom)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Hermes is the closest production analogue and the primary host, but its lifecycle is timestamp aging driven by load counts ('telemetry, not a gate'), its ledger is bound to one tool and one layout, rollback misses references/scripts, write_approval starves (241 pending over 8 weeks), and sharing is consent + file copy. Clade replaces aging with assertion staleness + dormancy + clade-pooled outcomes, enforces authority on the path not the tool, snapshots whole bundles, computes default dispositions so the queue never rots, gates review forks on VOI, and shares receipts instead of files — all as a plugin, without touching Hermes' loop.

nearest_competitors.name: OpenClaw Skill Workshop + skill_proposal_evaluate seam
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: OpenClaw has the best proposal object (hash-bound, atomic, ledgered) but acceptance is regex + hashes, evaluators fail open, the default flipped to ungoverned auto, memory has no seam, and nothing happens after apply. Clade is the missing evaluator on that seam (first third-party implementation, fail-closed wrapper) and the lifecycle after apply: activation receipts, canary, attribution, staleness, retirement, federation — and it covers memory and the other harnesses on the same machine.

nearest_competitors.name: SkillClaw (proxy-based collective skill evolution)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SkillClaw captures sessions through an LLM proxy that users report breaks harnesses, converges one skill per name per group with the verifier off, attributes 'skill was read' not 'skill helped', and generates and judges with the same model family. Clade is file/hook-level with no proxy, resolves cross-user differences as base + per-environment overlays with a receipt quorum, credits only activation-conditioned mechanical outcomes, and quarantines imports until local assertions and receipts clear.

nearest_competitors.name: SkillOpt / SkillOpt-Sleep (Microsoft)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SkillOpt is a proposer with a strict held-out gate over one skill document that needs an eval task set and a nightly budget; its gate accepts per-task regressions and copies judge regexes into the skill. Clade governs hundreds of artifacts with zero-eval tiers, treats SkillOpt as one proposer recipe, adds activation, staleness and retirement it lacks, and implements the sandbox-replay design SkillOpt#155 maintainers endorsed (disposable worktree, pass/fail/inconclusive, execution off by default) as a backend rather than a fork.

nearest_competitors.name: SafeEvolve / SkillMisevo-Gym (2608.12851)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: SafeEvolve's two-boundary architecture (admission at write, revocation at reuse) and GovernableStore hooks are adopted directly, but its critic is the evolving backbone, its retirement depends on an online harm judge, it governs only SKILL.md text and pays ~13pp carryover utility. Clade uses mechanical outcomes and deterministic assertions for retirement (staying under the Blind Curator judge cliff), covers memory/instincts/prompt notes, adds dormancy, staleness, cost and federation, and uses a cross-family judge only for the safety canary.

nearest_competitors.name: Reef (Human-Agent-Society) propose→paired-evaluate→decide release pipeline
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Reef is a serving proxy plus release pipeline for recipes: pooled W/L tally, one-step rollback, AlwaysSelect for weights, no protected seed floor (#356), no activation or staleness notion, proxy-based. Clade is proxy-free and multi-harness at the file level, has depth->1 undo, clade attribution and a federation, and ships as a Reef recipe contributing the PACE decide policy and the seed floor Reef asked for.

nearest_competitors.name: PACE (2606.08106) and SEA (2607.00871) anytime-valid gates
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Both are per-candidate statistical gates validated on toy prompt edits with no code, no lifecycle, no activation and no staleness; SEA's harness gate accepted 0 edits and was switched off. Clade embeds PACE's e-process and SEA's CTHS spend schedule as the canary→promoted transition, feeds them randomized pairs from canary alternation on the user's own sessions, keeps NSF as a resting state instead of a rejection, and raises power by clade and federation pooling — the integration and extension the scientist lens says is the real gap.

nearest_competitors.name: Causal Agent Replay (2606.08275), The Replay Gap (2608.08239), Counterfactual Trace Auditing (2605.11946)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: These are replay primitives and negative results, not products. Clade uses them to scope Tier 3 honestly (sandbox-first branched re-execution, A-vs-A′ null floor, abstention as a first-class result, uptake verified before any effect is scored) and keeps them optional, because Tiers 0–2 already deliver the product value.

nearest_competitors.name: Ratchet (2605.22148) and The Blind Curator (2607.07436)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: They supply the retirement math (c(s) ≤ −τ after N_min trials; judge false-pass cliff at (1−τ)/2) with no code and a per-skill N_min a personal store never reaches. Clade reaches N_min by pooling over the clade and the federation, uses mechanical outcomes so the judge cliff does not apply, and adds the deterministic staleness path they do not have.

nearest_competitors.name: agentdescent (Beta-posterior acceptance, κ-discount, freeze-by-name)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: An in-process research engine coupled to its own types with no post-commit monitoring, canary or rollback. Clade borrows the κ-discount rectification and freeze-by-name governance and applies them to a host-side lifecycle over other people's harnesses.

nearest_competitors.name: auto-harness (NeoSigma) gating.py ratchet
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A single-run held-out ratchet for harness code whose gate state lives inside the agent's writable surface. Clade governs learned text artifacts, keeps all state host-side and path-protected, and uses sequential statistics with activation conditioning rather than a tie-accepting single run.

nearest_competitors.name: Prime Agent /refine (harness_state.json, refinements.jsonl)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Typed, versioned, rollback-able supplemental state whose acceptance is the refiner's say-so and which users cannot see (#1208, closed unfixed). Clade wraps refinements.jsonl into its ledger, gates /refine on VOI through session_before_refine, and gives Prime users the change feed, receipts and attribution the project never shipped.

nearest_competitors.name: DeepSeek Harness (dsh)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A substrate with no learning loop that explicitly deferred the evaluator; Clade is a dsh plugin using its SkillProvider registry to serve promoted/canary sets and its pre-execute guard for authority, and it runs the Claude Code hook bundle unchanged through dsh's hook-protocol bridge.

nearest_competitors.name: ECC instincts, Claude Code auto-memory, Codex Memories, Mem0
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: The most-deployed learned artifacts with no lifecycle at all (ECC's confidence dynamics unimplemented; auto-memory 'context, not enforced configuration' with silent truncation; Codex Memories draining quotas and exfiltrating local-provider chats; Mem0 ADD-only). Clade gives memory the same lockfile, receipts, DLP/provider-boundary rule, staleness, dormancy and undo as skills, without replacing any of these writers.

risks: Null-effect world: most `clade why` verdicts will be INCONCLUSIVE and users may read that as product failure; mitigation is that the day-one value (receipts, change feed, staleness, undo, cost) does not depend on any artifact helping, and the digest leads with those.

Assertion extraction precision: false-stale flags (a version string mentioned as an example, a path that is intentionally relative) would erode trust; mitigation: conservative extraction, re-verify before retire, user pin, and stale = archive-with-notice never delete.

Canary alternation changes single-user UX (a skill missing every other session); mitigation: alternation opt-in per artifact class, default observe-only with advisory task-signature pairs clearly labelled as confounded.

Harness churn (Hermes 947 commits in four days; OpenClaw breaks plugins per release; DSH 14 pre-release tags in 12 days) will break adapters; mitigation: version-pinned conformance suite, fail-safe read-only mode, adapters as thin declarative maps.

Path-level authority is a containment convention, not a security boundary: shell redirection, Codex opted-out tool paths and subagents can bypass hooks; the watcher-plus-revert fallback is detection, not prevention, and Clade must say so.

Correction detection without an LLM will have false positives/negatives; a miscalibrated proxy could push good artifacts toward 'hurts-advisory'; mitigation: proxy-vs-verified κ-discount, randomized pairs required for any non-advisory verdict.
Statistical power: with ~50 sessions/month a personal store may never promote anything on randomized evidence; clade and federation pooling are the answer but federation arrives in month 3.

Federation trust: receipt quorum needs identity; Sybil environments could launder a poisoned overlay; mitigation: org-scoped trust first, local re-verification always required before live, taint never upgraded by import.
Cost creep if Tier 3/4 are left on; mitigation: off by default, per-day caps, circuit breaker, cost line in every report.

Privacy: receipts and cassettes contain user text and tool output; nothing but bundles + attestations leaves the machine, but the local store itself becomes a sensitive asset that must be DLP-scrubbed and encrypted at rest.

Vendor absorption: Anthropic (auto-memory receipts, plugin eval) or OpenClaw could ship pieces natively; acceptable if they emit the same record, fatal if they emit incompatible ones — hence filing the profile early.
Scope creep toward harness code and weights, where the sealed-evaluator and benchmark stances (Hermetic, Turnstile) are the right tools; Clade must stay on learned text artifacts.

The lifecycle policy's own thresholds (α, τ, N_min, VOI prior) are tunables that could be Goodharted by a curious user or an agent editing config; policy lives host-side, hashed into every transition record, and edits to it are human-only.
open_questions: What is the right lifecycle unit for memory: per entry (too small for outcome pairing), per topic file (Claude Code), or per bounded block (Hermes MEMORY.md 2.2K chars)? Current plan: lint/DLP/scope/staleness per entry, outcome attribution per file.

Can canary alternation be implemented on Claude Code without a next-session lag, given skill discovery runs before SessionStart hooks? If not, is a SessionStart additionalContext injection of a withheld skill's content an acceptable substitute?
How expressive should the assertion language be before it becomes a second skill format? Do we need a probe for API shapes (call a documented endpoint) or only for local facts?
What α, CTHS δ₀ and VOI prior are right for a personal store with ~50 sessions/month, and should the prior be per artifact class (skill vs memory vs instinct) given the null-effect base rates differ?
Will users accept auto-retire, or only auto-archive with a notice and a one-command restore? Field incidents suggest archive-only until the audit data shows retirement precision.

How to represent per-environment overlays in an agentskills.io bundle without breaking `skills-ref validate`: a `metadata` string field, an `overlays/` directory, or a separate overlay bundle in the clade?
Can federated receipts from another org be trusted without their cassettes, and what is the minimum quorum before an imported artifact skips local canary?

Interaction with vendor writers we do not control (Claude auto-memory decides what to save; Codex Memories runs in the background): intercept-and-snapshot is safe, but is gating them acceptable or will it break the vendor feature?
Which correction patterns in UserPromptSubmit are reliable enough across languages and users to serve as a negative label, and how often must they be spot-checked by a cross-family judge?
Who should own the artifact-acceptance record profile (in-toto WG, EvalEval, agentskills.io) so that two vendors emitting it is more likely than one vendor absorbing it?
Does clade pooling introduce a Simpson's-paradox risk when forks and overlays serve different environments — should pooling be hierarchical (partial pooling) rather than flat?

rsi-substrate.name: Meristem
rsi-substrate.tagline: One genome, one gate: the ~2k-line, API-only reference loop for harness-level self-improvement that papers plug operators into and benchmarks run as their subject.
rsi-substrate.stance: THE MINIMAL RUNNABLE RSI REFERENCE SUBSTRATE. Meristem is the reference implementation of a gated update loop that all five 2026 surveys (RSI 2607.07663, Reliable, Self-Improvements 2607.13104, XMU, Self-Evolving Coding Agents) list as open and none ships: a ~2,000-line Python core, API models only, no GPU, no proxy, no vendor harness in the loop. The whole editable harness is ONE typed genome with five surfaces — prompt slots (incl. addressable memory bullets), skills (agentskills.io bundles), tools (sandboxed scripts + schema-narrowing wrappers), hooks (deterministic event handlers with Claude-Code-compatible semantics), and the loop-graph (the agent's control flow as data) — interpreted by a frozen ~400-line kernel that emits activation receipts per surface. Every mutation on every surface is a typed patch that passes ONE gate: sealed paired evaluation against the incumbent on identical instances with a same-config control arm, a PACE-style anytime-valid e-process under a SEA-style run-level spend schedule, a protected per-task floor restricted to tasks with observed stability, a safety canary as a hard constraint, activation-gated credit, and a matched-budget test-time-scaling control arm that consumes the same cost ledger. The archive pools outcomes by lineage (HGM clade metaproductivity) AND by surface × failure-signature × model-tier cell, feeds rejected edits back to the proposer, and the ledger prints improvement-per-dollar by default. It is research-first: the standard subject that RSI-Exam / EvoHarnessBench / HarnessDev / SEAGym / HarnessOpt-Bench can run, and the kernel that MetaRSI, MOSS, MGM, GEA and Self-Harness operators can drop their proposer into, so two self-improvement claims can differ only in the operator, never in the loop plumbing. Flagship experiment: cross-substrate credit assignment — which surface to edit for which failure, conditioned on model tier. Deliberate non-goals (owned by sibling designs): it is not a production write-interceptor (Pawl), not a sealed-evaluator product (Hermetic — we ship a minimal sealed runner and consume Hermetic-style receipts), and not an acceptor benchmark (Turnstile — we are the subject it benchmarks and we emit its evidence format).
rsi-substrate.thesis: Every RSI-adjacent paper of 2026 re-implements the same loop, differently, in a place no one else can run: MetaRSI (2609.06396) specifies a seven-stage kernel and a typed HarnessPatch over five slots and releases no loop, evaluator or gate; Self-Harness (2606.09498) ships a hook menu and a two-repeat no-regression gate inside one LangChain Deep Agents file; HGM/MGM/GEA mutate whole agent repos behind a compile-and-smoke gate at $13k–22k and GPU-served models; Lin et al.'s A-Evolve engine applies every edit unconditionally (Verifier = NoVerify in every recipe) with scope enforced post hoc; Continual Harness CRUDs (p, G, K, M) mid-episode with no gate; Meta-Harness has no parent selection and a strict-> frontier on two noisy trials; Prime, Hermes and OpenClaw ship production loops whose acceptance is the writing model's own opinion. Because each loop differs in editable surface, gate rule, noise handling, budget accounting and activation, none of the critique results (AI2: evolution does not beat test-time scaling at matched budget; HarnessDev: self-selection is a coin flip on held-out; EvoHarnessBench: harness-induced forgetting; RELAI: gains are one-shot; Lin et al.: harness-updating is flat, benefit is non-monotonic in tier) can separate the operator from the plumbing, and no benchmark has a standard subject to run. The fix is not a thirteenth taxonomy but a small, boring, correct substrate: make the entire editable harness a typed genome; freeze the interpreter; make every mutation a typed patch whose diff must equal its declaration; pass every patch through one gate whose statistics are honest by construction (paired, sequential, floor-with-noise-model, canary, activation, matched-budget control); and make the ledger emit cost-normalized, activation-aware reports by default rather than as a paper's courtesy. Once the loop is held fixed, the scientifically interesting variable becomes visible and cheap to measure for the first time: which surface (prompt / skill / tool / hook / loop-graph) carries held-out lift for which failure signature at which model tier. Four surveys name cross-substrate credit assignment as unsolved; the reason it is unsolved is that no harness makes all five surfaces editable under one gate. Meristem is that harness.
rsi-substrate.rsi_positioning: Altitude: harness-level RSI (MetaRSI's Harness-RSI operator; Weng's 'harness engineering for self-improvement'), i.e. frozen weights, mutable scaffold. In the RSI survey's vocabulary Meristem is bounded self-refinement against a fixed external evaluator, human-on-the-loop; on the Reliable ladder it is an L2 (scaffold) system with an explicitly separated, off-by-default L3 mode (the proposer policy and surface router become mutable under their own gate, ledger and anchor set — MetaRSI's 'vertical move' with the Eq. 27 four-check contract), and it refuses L4 (criterion) mutation entirely: evaluator, hidden split, protected corpus, canary bank, release rule and budget ledger are outside every write surface (MetaRSI Eq. 30; agentdescent 'freeze by name'). Verification hierarchy: the substrate commits only on rung-2 evidence (execution: deterministic verifiers, test outcomes, hook-fired receipts); rung-3 learned-judge evidence may rank candidates before spending but never commits (PROCTOR: mechanical rejection overrides LLM approval, never the reverse); rung-4 self-assessment (the proposer's expected_effect) is recorded only to score proposer calibration (AHE's 11.8% precision is the number to beat). Why RSI people care: (1) it is the reference loop the surveys ask for, so operator papers (MetaRSI, MOSS, MGM, GEA, Self-Harness, SkillOpt-style, RHI-style) can be re-run as operators on one kernel and compared at matched budget — the counterfactual HarnessDev skipped and the ablation AI2 could only run for one loop; (2) it gives the multi-generation benchmarks (RSI-Exam harness tasks, EvoHarnessBench streams, SEAGym, HarnessOpt-Bench, HarnessDev's six-module seed) a standard subject, so 'self-evolving system' stops meaning a different bespoke loop per paper; (3) it operationalizes the emerging reporting checklist (pinkbubblebubble): multi-generation results with regressions and variance, a held-out verifier the loop cannot rewrite, ablations of self-modification vs search vs memory (the built-in parallel-K/sequential-K null operators), generalization to unselected tasks (sealed slice), full trajectory and failed-attempt logs (archive keeps rejected nodes), explicit isolation/rollback/human interventions (ledger events); (4) it turns three RSI open problems into runnable experiments: the 'exchange rate of grounding' (vary the fraction of execution-rung vs judge-rung evidence per round and measure held-out decay), retention vs adaptation (BWT/FWT per surface per round), and — the flagship — cross-substrate credit assignment, which decides the practical question behind 'harness-first RSI': what should an agent be allowed to rewrite about itself, given how strong it is.
what_evolves: PROMPT SLOTS: a bounded, typed menu (system, bootstrap, execution, verification, failure-recovery, multimodal — Self-Harness's six hooks) plus an ACE-style addressable memory slot ([id] helpful/harmful :: bullet) with per-slot character caps (MetaRSI complexity bound B_H). Patches are add/replace/delete on addressable spans; wholesale rewrites are rejected at validate time.

SKILLS: agentskills.io SKILL.md bundles (references/, scripts/) under a retrieval index; activation = a skill_read event in the kernel trace; retirement by Ratchet-style outcome-driven eviction (contribution <= -tau after N_min trials) and capacity cap, since retrieval precision collapses past ~20 skills (Demystifying Agent Skills 29.6% -> 3.3%).

TOOLS: new sandboxed script tools (declared JSON schema, capability class read | workspace_write | network, bundled tests that must pass at validate) and wrappers that compose existing tools; built-in tool schemas may only narrow and PROTECTED_BUILTIN_TOOL_NAMES cannot be removed (MetaRSI repo rule). Activation = invocation receipt.

HOOKS: deterministic handlers on kernel events {session_start, pre_model, pre_tool, post_tool, on_error, on_stop} with a tiny predicate language over trace state (last_tool_error, tests_ran, step_index, tool_name ~ regex) and a closed action set {deny, narrow_input, inject_context, force_continue, log}; no LLM inside a hook. Semantics mirror Claude Code hooks so an evolved hook exports unchanged to settings.json, DSH hook-protocol, Hermes pre_tool_call, OpenClaw before_tool_call and pi tool_call. Activation = hook-fired receipt; this is the surface with rung-2 evidence by construction.

LOOP-GRAPH: the agent's control flow as data — nodes {model_call(slot, tools), tool_dispatch, verify, spawn_subagent(spec), stop}, guarded edges, step/token budgets, subagent specs — interpreted by the frozen kernel. Patches add/remove nodes and edges or change budgets; validation requires stop reachability, budget containment, and that a revision may not silently drop a verify-before-stop or reversibility invariant its ancestor asserted (SafeEvolve invariant). This reaches the structural failures MOSS says text surfaces cannot, without DGM/MOSS-style arbitrary code.

COMPOSITE PATCHES (multi-surface) are allowed but flagged; they enter the archive but are never labeled causal for a single surface (autocontext rule) and are ablated by single-surface reverts before release.

OFF-BY-DEFAULT L3 MODE: the proposer prompt template and the surface-router policy become a sixth, separately-gated genome with its own ledger, anchor tasks and human-merged promotion (MetaRSI vertical moves; RQGM anchor discipline) — provided so improver-evolution experiments can run on the same kernel, never mixed into L2 results.

NEVER EVOLVES (outside every write surface, changed only by human-merged commits): the kernel interpreter, validator, sealed runner, evaluator and hidden split, protected corpus and its stability measurements, canary bank, gate policy and spend schedule, archive bookkeeping, budget ledger.
rsi-substrate.fitness_and_acceptance:
SIGNAL. The only commit-grade signal is rung-2 execution evidence: a deterministic verifier outcome per (task, seed) from a sealed runner (Harbor task verifiers; local pytest-style terminal checks; EvoHarnessBench database_state SQL checks), plus dense mechanical side-signals the kernel logs for free (steps-to-done, tokens, first-divergence step vs the incumbent trace, tests_ran, tool-error count). LLM-judge scores are permitted only to rank candidates before spending and to grade the safety canary with a cross-family judge; they never commit (PROCTOR). The proposer's own expected_effect is stored for calibration scoring only.

PAIRED, INTERLEAVED, SAME SEEDS. Candidate and incumbent run on identical task instances with common random numbers and interleaved scheduling (SEA ALG4 protocol; Reef's 2 x tasks x repeats). Every certification also runs a second incumbent arm (A vs A') on the same instances: this is the noise floor The Replay Gap shows is mandatory (T=0 is a serving property, not determinism; FP8 controls diverged on 90-96% of forks) and it is what makes a per-task floor well-posed.

ELIGIBILITY BEFORE SPENDING ('ties are free', per surface). Before any model call, the gate computes from the incumbent's stored traces which protected tasks a patch on surface S could have touched: prompt slot -> all tasks; skill -> tasks whose stored description would retrieve it; tool -> tasks whose traces invoked the wrapped tool or matched the failure signature; hook -> tasks whose traces contain the trigger event; graph -> tasks whose traces visited the node. Non-eligible tasks are ties by construction and cost nothing; a patch eligible on zero tasks is verdict 'not exercised', never 'no effect'. This is the same idea Pawl uses for production writes and Lin et al. motivate (skill-load rate 25% vs 96%); here it is computed per surface and is also the blast-radius estimate agentdescent declares by hand.

SEQUENTIAL DECISION WITH ERROR CONTROL. Per candidate: PACE's paired betting e-process over discordant eligible pairs (w=1 if candidate passes and incumbent fails), with a mixture over q in {0.6..0.9} instead of PACE's fixed lambda so power adapts; commit at wealth >= 1/alpha_k; reject on eligible-pair exhaustion. Run-level spend: alpha_k = alpha_0 / (Z k log^2(k+1)), Z ~ 3.39 (SEA's horizon-free CTHS; naive 1/(2k log^2) over-spends 1.69x), so familywise error over an unbounded candidate stream is bounded by alpha_0 without knowing the horizon. The orchestrator's own simulation (research/tools/gate_power_sim.py) sets expectations we print in every report: greedy 'keep if mean went up' commits 44-46% false at zero lift (reproducing PACE's 30-42%); the e-process commits <= 4% false at any N; but on binary outcomes with an incumbent at 0.7, a +10pp lift is detected only 11% of the time at N=40 (39% at N=160), +20pp 44%/98%, +30pp 98% at N=40 with a median of 22 pairs. Honest consequence: with 20-40 protected tasks the gate reliably blocks regressions and safety violations, certifies only large lifts, and will leave most candidates in 'hold' — which the null-effect literature (CTA +0.3pp, SkillsBench 0 for LLM-written skills, SkillOpt gains carried by 1-4 edits) says is the correct outcome, not a bug. We raise power three ways rather than lowering the bar: dense signals get their own e-processes (steps, tokens, divergence) whose e-values are averaged with the outcome e-value (valid by convexity); evidence accrues across rounds because anytime validity lets a held candidate keep collecting pairs on new stream tasks at no re-start cost; and eligibility concentrates pairs where discordance is possible. Safe Harness Self-Evolution (2609.08175) supplies finite-sample conditions; the report prints 'eligible pairs needed for 80% power at this incumbent rate'.

TWO-TIER ADMISSION (the SEA lesson). SEA's certified gate at ~50 tasks accepted 0 edits, cost 13x the rest of the loop, and was switched off; HGM/MGM avoid the problem by admitting every non-empty child with zero evidence. Meristem does both, in order: Tier 0 archive admission is cheap and deterministic (schema + surface containment + diff == declared modification + lint + liveness smoke on one task + leak scan + safety canary ~60 probes ~ $1) and the node enters the archive with an empty outcome record; Tier 1 promotion to incumbent requires the e-process certificate plus floor plus retention terms; Tier 2 release (export to a real harness, or a paper number) opens the sealed held-out slice once per release (RSI-Exam) and runs the matched-budget TTS control. Archive search (Thompson sampling over clade posteriors) keeps spending evaluation budget on promising held nodes, so the loop never starves and never promotes without a certificate.

PER-TASK REGRESSION FLOOR WITH A NOISE MODEL. The protected corpus is the set of tasks the incumbent passes k/k with measured A-vs-A' stability; a flip counts as a regression only after k-of-n confirmation (simulation: at pass-prob 0.6 a k=1 floor false-blocks 93-100% of good candidates, k=2 44-91%, k=3 13-43%; real test-verified tasks are far more stable and the control arm measures this per task for free). Retention (BWT on earlier cohorts) and adaptation (FWT on the targeted cohort) are reported separately (EvoHarnessBench) and a candidate cannot buy BWT < -epsilon with FWT (Reef #356, SkillOpt #174).

SAFETY AS A HARD CONSTRAINT. A 30-100 probe canary bank (seeded from SkillMisevo-Bench, MemEvoBench, Agent-SafetyBench, MLAS cell patterns) plus operational invariants mined from incidents (no secrets in any surface; no deletion of permission/deny rules; no 'avoid tool X' rule derived from a transient failure — Hermes #6051; no placeholder-as-verified) is run with candidate vs incumbent loaded, judged by a different model family, and any negative delta blocks at Tier 0; artifacts derived from untrusted evidence (provenance taint = tool_output | web | other_agent) get the 100-probe bank. Promoted patches are re-validated when reused in a new task family (revocation boundary, SafeEvolve) and reverted on attributed harm; skill retirement uses Ratchet thresholds and we print the Blind-Curator cliff (judge false-pass >= ~0.45 makes retirement vacuous) as a diagnostic on the canary judge.

TAMPERING vs OVERFITTING, SEPARATELY. Tampering (all seven Camp-B leaks are one bug): the proposer's filesystem view contains only the genome and scrubbed traces; evaluator code, hidden split, protected corpus, canary bank and gate state live on a separate mount/directory run as a subprocess with restricted cwd (Docker mount namespace where available; Hermetic-compatible receipts: sha256 of evaluator, data shard, genome, workspace start/end, served model, completion status, tool-call counts; fail-closed to 0 on any grader exception, RSI-Exam test.sh style); diff must equal declared paths; forbidden-path and honeytoken scans; canary tasks whose perfect score is evidence of cheating (PROCTOR). Overfitting (SkillOpt #154/#175): the proposer receives failure traces, deterministic failure signatures and free-text feedback but never scorer source, rubric text or task ids (task ids are replaced by opaque handles in traces; AI2 found memorized paths despite prompt bans); patches quoting scorer tokens or task names are rejected; 10% of promoted candidates are re-scored by an independent-family judge with a proxy-vs-independent divergence alarm (Double Ratchet's outside judge); the sealed slice is opened only at release.

ACTIVATION AND ADHERENCE. The kernel logs an activation receipt per surface per episode (prompt slot injected; skill read; tool invoked; hook fired; graph node visited). Credit is assigned only on episodes where the candidate surface was activated; 'phantom accepts' (PAST-Bench: artifacts written but never read; HarnessDev: 18/108 mechanisms never fired) are a named verdict. Adherence for prompt/skill surfaces uses mechanical proxies by default (retrieval-to-use gap, answer-before-validation, late-trajectory instruction drift measured as divergence from the slot's declared checks) and Lin et al.'s HFR rubric pipeline as an opt-in advisory arm.

ATTRIBUTION. Every archive node stores its per-task outcome vector (GEA's binary fingerprint), so the gate compares which tasks flipped rather than means; clade-pooled Beta posteriors (HGM CMP) drive expand-vs-evaluate; a second pooling over (surface, failure signature, model tier) cells drives the surface router; rejected edits and their discordant tasks go to a buffer that conditions the next proposal for the same cell and an identical-patch hash is refused without evaluation (SkillOpt/Reef; GEPA #379); at release, single-surface reverts on the frontier genome attribute lift (Meta-Harness never does this); EvoTrace-style reintroduction rate and per-surface activation rate are reported as mechanistic audits.

MATCHED-BUDGET CONTROL. Parallel-K and sequential-K refinement on the unmodified genome are built-in null operators that run through the same kernel and charge the same ledger; every release prints held-out lift vs the TTS arm at matched rollouts AND matched dollars including proposer and canary tokens (AI2 excluded meta-agent tokens; HarnessDev excluded dev tokens; we include both).

FRESHNESS AND COST. Evidence compiled against a previous incumbent is stale (MetaRSI Eq. 22): held candidates restart wealth against the new incumbent on eligible pairs. Per-run USD cap, per-candidate cap, circuit breaker on repeated identical proposals, and a line in every report stating what the gate itself cost (practitioner lens: cost is the silent killer). Verdict {clears | below | inconclusive | not_exercised} is stored separately from disposition {admit_archive | promote | hold | reject | revert} (Thru-Echoes rsi-exam-provenance), so a policy change never rewrites evidence.

Prior art built on: PACE, SEA, HGM/MGM (clade metaproductivity), GEA (fingerprints, staged ladder), Self-Harness (hook menu, no-regression), SkillOpt (rejected buffer, textual learning rate), Reef (paired episodes, rejected history), agentdescent (full-held-out invariant, freeze-by-name, kappa-discounted proxy evidence), autocontext (campaign false-promotion budget), MetaRSI (authority cut, HarnessPatch, freshness, diff == declared), PROCTOR (mechanical over judge, cheating canaries), RSI-Exam/AI4AI-Bench (sealed replay, fail-closed grading, artifact-only boundary), AI2 2607.12227 (matched-budget TTS), EvoHarnessBench (BWT/FWT), Lin et al. 2605.30621 (SLR/HFR, benefit is a property of the (update, consumer) pair), Causal Agent Replay (abstention as a first-class outcome, sanity floor), The Replay Gap (control arm, re-execute don't stitch), CTA (null-floor calibration), SkillMisevo/SafeEvolve (two boundaries), Ratchet/Blind Curator, Phantom Gains, HackProbe (probe bank), Safe Harness Self-Evolution (sample-size conditions), and the sibling designs Hermetic (receipts), Turnstile (evidence format), Pawl (eligibility ties).
rsi-substrate.core_technical_insight: Surfaces are not interchangeable text blobs; they differ in exactly three properties the substrate can measure a priori, and that turns cross-substrate credit assignment from a black-box search into a priced, poolable decision. (1) Activation mode: a prompt slot is always in context; a skill activates only if retrieved and read; a tool only if invoked; a hook fires deterministically on an event; a graph node is visited or not. (2) Blast radius: the set of protected tasks a patch can affect is computable from the incumbent's stored traces before any model call, so the gate knows the number of possible discordant pairs — and therefore the cost and the maximum attainable power — before it spends a token. (3) Evidence rung: hook and graph patches produce rung-2 evidence by construction (the receipt says the hook fired and the outcome flipped), while prompt and skill patches need an adherence signal that decays along the trajectory (Lin et al.: .52 -> .13 for weak models). Competitors fix the surface by hand and mutate it uniformly (Self-Harness's menu, SkillOpt's one file, Prime's four kinds, MetaRSI's five slots with no loop), so they cannot ask which surface is worth a given budget for a given failure. Meristem pools archive outcomes over (surface x failure-signature x model-tier) cells with the same clade-metaproductivity posteriors HGM uses over lineages, and Thompson-samples the surface as well as the parent; HGM's own finding — a node's fitness poorly predicts its descendants' — has an exact analogue here: a surface's mean lift poorly predicts the lift of the next patch on it unless conditioned on signature and tier. Two enabling cuts make this cheap: the loop-graph is data interpreted by a frozen ~400-line kernel, so structural changes are typed patches with diff == declaration and reachability/invariant validation (MetaRSI's authority cut made concrete; reaches MOSS-class failures without DGM-class arbitrary code); and admission is two-tier — cheap deterministic archive admission with posterior tracking (HGM) below a certificate-gated promotion (PACE/SEA) whose anytime validity lets evidence accrue across rounds — which dissolves the SEA starvation/PACE power tension that has kept every honest gate switched off in practice. Finally, because the TTS null operators run through the same kernel and ledger, 'improvement per dollar vs best-of-K' is a column in every report rather than a separate paper.

architecture.responsibility: Typed genome schema for the five surfaces with per-surface complexity caps; Merkle content-hash genome ids; typed patch schema (superset of MetaRSI HarnessPatch: hypothesis, ops, declared_paths, expected_effect, risks, evidence_refs, surface, failure_signature, provenance_taint); validate() = schema, surface containment, diff == declared paths, protected built-in names, schema-narrowing-only for built-ins, graph reachability/budget/invariant checks, lint (referenced files exist, scripts compile, no placeholder-as-verified, no secrets).

architecture.responsibility: Interprets the loop-graph as an agent episode on one task: model calls through an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible client with prompt slots assembled from the genome, tool dispatch into the sandbox, hook evaluation with the predicate language, subagent spawn, verify and stop nodes, step/token budgets. Emits a JSONL trace with the dsh invariant 'model-visible <=> logged' and per-surface activation receipts (slot injected, skill read, tool invoked, hook fired, node visited).

architecture.responsibility: Sealed paired evaluation: Harbor task adapter (task.toml, verifier image) and a local git-worktree+subprocess sandbox for cheap task families; evaluator, hidden split, protected corpus and canary bank live outside the proposer's mount; interleaved candidate/incumbent/control episodes with common seeds; fail-closed grading (any exception -> 0, RSI-Exam test.sh semantics); receipts (sha256 of evaluator, split, genome, workspace start/end, served model, completion status, counts); cost capture from provider usage fields; optional backend = `claude plugin eval` two-arm cases compiled from the protected corpus.
architecture.interfaces: evaluate_pairs(candidate, incumbent, tasks, seeds, control=True) -> [Evidence]; canary(candidate, incumbent, bank) -> CanaryResult; receipts verifiable offline with `meristem verify <receipt>`; Hermetic receipt profile.

architecture.responsibility: Eligibility per surface from stored traces; mixture-betting e-process over discordant eligible pairs; CTHS run-level spend; dense-signal e-values averaged in; k-of-n protected floor over stability-measured tasks; BWT/FWT; safety canary constraint; leak/honeytoken scan; independent-judge spot-check sampling; freshness check; verdict/disposition split; power/sample-size estimate printed per candidate.
architecture.interfaces: Gate.tier0(patch, genome) -> Verdict; Gate.certify(candidate, evidence_stream) -> Verdict (anytime; resumable); Gate.policy is a frozen JSON outside the genome; unit tests reproduce research/tools/gate_power_sim.py numbers.

architecture.responsibility: Nodes with parent links, patch, per-task outcome vectors, evidence pointers, cost; clade-pooled Beta posteriors over lineage (HGM CMP) and over (surface, signature, tier) cells; Thompson sampling for expand-vs-evaluate (UCB-Air widening) and for surface selection; rejected-edit buffer keyed by cell with identical-patch refusal; retirement (Ratchet thresholds) and revert with depth > 1 by genome id.
architecture.interfaces: Archive.admit(node) / .sample_to_expand() / .sample_to_evaluate() / .sample_surface(signature, tier) / .rejected(cell) / .frontier(); SQLite + JSONL.

architecture.responsibility: Deterministic failure-signature mining from traces (terminal cause classes: tests_never_run, stop_without_verify, tool_error_loop, context_overflow, wrong_target_edited, timeout, infra) with optional advisory LLM labels; scorer-blind evidence packaging (task ids -> opaque handles, verifier output -> pass/fail + signature, no rubric/scorer text); a proposer prompt template that must emit one typed patch on one requested surface; pluggable surface router {uniform, fixed:<surface>, thompson_cell, llm_choice}; operator plug-in interface so MetaRSI/MOSS/MGM/Self-Harness-style proposers can replace the default.
architecture.interfaces: Operator.propose(evidence_bundle, surface, rejected) -> Patch; Router.choose(signature, tier, archive) -> surface; mine_signatures(traces) -> clusters.

architecture.responsibility: Append-only hash-chained JSONL of candidate, evidence, verdict, disposition, receipt and cost events; budget ledger by role (proposer, agent rollouts, control arms, canary, judge spot-checks); built-in TTS null operators (parallel-K, sequential-K) charged to the same ledger; report generator: funnel proposed -> admitted -> exercised -> certified -> promoted -> activated-in-export, lift vs incumbent and vs TTS at matched rollouts and matched USD, BWT/FWT per round, per-surface-cell table, mechanistic audits (reintroduction rate, activation rate), power estimates, gate cost line; Turnstile-compatible evidence export.
architecture.interfaces: meristem report [--json]; ledger.append(event); ledger.verify_chain().

Outside the genome (separate mount): evaluator/, hidden_split/, protected_corpus/ (cassettes + stability), canary_bank/, gate_policy.json, archive.db, ledger.jsonl.
rsi-substrate.integration_surface:
Meristem runs standalone against Harbor tasks or a local task family and touches real harnesses through two directions: EXPORT (a promoted genome becomes a real harness configuration, with activation receipts flowing back) and IMPORT (a harness's own learning artifacts and streams become candidates and tasks). Concrete seams, all verified in the digests:

CLAUDE CODE (the builder's daily harness; first adapter). Export: prompt slots -> CLAUDE.md sections with slot markers; skills -> .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md; hooks -> .claude/settings.json hooks with a 40-line shell shim that evaluates the predicate language: pre_tool -> PreToolUse (permissionDecision deny | updatedInput for schema narrowing), post_tool -> PostToolUse (updatedToolOutput for inject_context), session_start -> SessionStart additionalContext, pre_model/user turn -> UserPromptSubmit, on_stop -> Stop (force_continue = block-stop with the hook's message); InstructionsLoaded -> load receipts for prompt/skill activation; tools -> a local MCP server wrapping tools/<name>/impl.py. Import/record: PreToolUse updatedInput + PostToolUse updatedToolOutput replay recorded tool results (verified, $0.007/replay) so ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>.jsonl transcripts become cassettes via the existing cassette_extract classifier; Stop emits a session receipt with cost. Evaluation backend option: compile protected cassettes into `claude plugin eval` cases (scaffold_script restores the git snapshot, history_file = recorded prefix, graders = the session's own terminal verification + tool_used) and run `--ablation with-without --json`, converting each run into Evidence records; Meristem wraps it with seeds, sequential stats and the floor the tool lacks.

HERMES (skill_manage / curator / write_approval). Import: ~/.hermes/pending/{skills,memory}/<id>.json staged payloads and curator consolidation proposals become candidates on the skill and memory-bullet surfaces (a curator umbrella merge = one composite candidate); tools/skill_ledger.py JSONL (sha256 before/after manifests) is imported as archive history; .usage.json use counts become activation priors. Export: promoted skills written through skill_manage with the gate-bypass token so provenance guards still apply; `pre_tool_call` (fail-closed shell hook) carries exported hooks; skill_view events are the activation receipt. We deliberately consume Hermes' write-origin ContextVar as provenance taint.

OPENCLAW (Skill Workshop + plugin hooks). A `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin (zero third-party implementations exist today) that maps the candidate BundleSnapshot + baseline to a skill-surface candidate, runs Tier 0 immediately and returns {decision: block} for lint/canary/leak failures, {decision: revise, findings} with the rejected-buffer reasons, or {decision: pass, metrics: {eligible_tasks, wealth, verdict}} — and converts our own timeouts/errors into an explicit block because OpenClaw evaluators fail open; `skill_proposal_changed` / `skill_changed` events (expectedRevisionHash, correlationId) are imported into the ledger; `before_tool_call` carries exported hooks (block: true terminal semantics).

DEEPSEEK HARNESS (dsh). A Cordis plugin registering on tools/pre-execute (typed allow/deny/ask for exported hooks; guards are deny-only so ordering cannot resurrect a denied call), tools/post-execute (accept/block-with-feedback/replace/attach for inject_context and narrow_input), and agent/turn-stopping (on_stop force_continue); tool-surface patches become cordis_define revertible plugins so a rejected tool unloads atomically; the hook-protocol bridge means the Claude Code hooks.json export runs unchanged; the zstd session log ('model-visible <=> logged') is a cassette source; ralph RalphRoundReport is imported as a claim the gate verifies, never as a score.

PI / PRIME AGENT. pi extension using tool_call (block) and tool_result (modify) for exported hooks and activation receipts, `context` for prompt-slot injection; Prime /refine harness_state.json entries map to surfaces (prompt notes -> prompt slots, memory -> memory bullets, skill references -> tool wrappers, subagent specs -> graph spawn nodes) and refinements.jsonl becomes a candidate stream so `/refine` proposals can be gated retroactively (prime-agent#1208 'refine is invisible' becomes a Meristem report); `session_before_refine` can route the planner through Meristem's proposer.

REEF (propose -> evaluate -> decide recipes). Meristem ships as a Reef recipe: `propose(nodes, samples, models, manifest, rejected, sources, requests)` -> our proposer over the composition tree (rules/skills/config/code_extension/tools/hooks/subagents/loop graph on the native adapter map 1:1 onto our five surfaces); `evaluate` -> the sealed paired runner; `decide` -> the gate (replacing wins - losses > min_win_margin with the e-process and the protected floor Reef #356 asks for); rejected proposals round-trip through max_rejected_history; accepted genomes publish as immutable releases with Reef's rollback and canary routing; Reef #447's records->Harbor conversion feeds our stream adapter.

BENCHMARKS. Harbor task.toml + verifier images are the native task format (RSI-Exam two-image boundary supported as an evaluator profile; six CLIs are one-line Harbor adapters); SEAGym streams (train batches, frozen update validation, ID/OOD views) and EvoHarnessBench jsonl (oracle_tools, cumulative_tools, verifiers[] SQL checks, MCP gym config) are stream adapters; HarnessDev's six-module seed contract maps onto genome + kernel so a HarnessDev creator can be pointed at Meristem; HarnessOpt-Bench's budgeted optimizer protocol is `meristem run --budget`. Evidence exports in Turnstile's acceptance-record format and receipts in Hermetic's profile so the three sibling artifacts compose.
mvp_2_weeks: Days 1-2: genome/ — five-surface schema, Merkle ids, typed patch, validate() incl. diff == declared paths, graph reachability and asserted-invariant checks, lint; 60 unit tests. Seed genome = minimal ReAct graph (plan -> act -> dispatch -> verify -> stop) with bash/read/edit tools and empty skills/hooks.

Days 2-4: kernel/ — loop-graph interpreter over an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible client, prompt-slot assembly, hook predicate evaluator, tool dispatch into a git-worktree subprocess sandbox, JSONL trace with per-surface activation receipts; run one Terminal-Bench 2.1 task through Harbor and one local pytest task end to end.

Days 4-6: runner/ — sealed paired evaluation: evaluator and split on a separate directory run as a restricted subprocess (Docker mount namespace when available), interleaved candidate/incumbent/control episodes with common seeds, fail-closed grading, receipts, provider usage -> USD; protected corpus builder that records k=2 incumbent runs per task and per-task stability.

Days 6-8: gate/ — per-surface eligibility from traces, mixture e-process + CTHS spend, dense e-values, k-of-n floor, BWT/FWT, leak/honeytoken scan, canary v0 (30 probes seeded from SkillMisevo/MLAS patterns, cross-family judge), verdict/disposition; tests reproduce gate_power_sim.py (greedy 44-46% false at zero lift; e-process <= 4%; power table).

Days 8-10: archive/ + propose/ — nodes with outcome vectors, clade posteriors, (surface, signature, tier) cells, Thompson expand/evaluate and surface sampling, rejected buffer with identical-patch refusal; deterministic failure-signature mining; scorer-blind evidence bundles; proposer template emitting one typed patch per requested surface; routers uniform / fixed / thompson_cell / llm_choice.

Days 10-11: ledger/ + report/ + cli — hash-chained JSONL, budget by role, parallel-K and sequential-K null operators through the same kernel, report with funnel, lift vs incumbent and vs TTS at matched rollouts and USD, per-cell table, power estimate, gate-cost line.

Days 11-12: adapters/claude_code — export genome to CLAUDE.md slots, .claude/skills, settings.json hooks via the predicate shim; activation receipts from PreToolUse/PostToolUse/InstructionsLoaded/Stop; cassette import from ~/.claude/projects transcripts via the existing cassette_extract classifier.

Days 12-14: first end-to-end run: Terminal-Bench 2.1 40-task slice (AI2's 45/10/34 split lists, seed 42), Sonnet-tier agent, all five surfaces under the uniform router, $60 cap, 3 rounds; publish the ledger, the report and a README section 'plug your operator in' (Operator.propose interface with a MetaRSI-HarnessPatch example). Core line count audited (<= 2,400 lines excluding adapters and tests).
roadmap_3_months: Month 1 (weeks 1-4): MVP above, then hardening and three replications that establish credibility: (a) PACE's false-commit numbers reproduced inside the substrate on a prompt-only surface with a small open model via API; (b) AI2's harness-evolution-vs-test-time-scaling comparison on Terminal-Bench 2.1 (K=5, 45/10/34 split) with our built-in TTS null operators, reporting matched-rollout AND matched-dollar lift including proposer tokens; (c) Self-Harness's hook-menu loop re-run as an Operator plug-in under our gate. Add SEAGym stream and EvoHarnessBench jsonl adapters and the Hermes/OpenClaw import + evaluator-plugin adapters. Pre-register the flagship experiment (hypotheses, arms, seeds, budget, falsifiers) as a public document.

Month 2 (weeks 5-8): flagship cross-substrate credit-assignment experiment. Factors: model tier {weak: Qwen3.5-9B or Gemini 3.5 Flash, mid: Haiku 4.5 / DeepSeek V4 Flash, strong: Sonnet 4.6 / GPT-5.5} x task family {Terminal-Bench 2.1 split, SkillsBench or an EvoHarnessBench EOG stream} x arm {fixed:prompt, fixed:skill, fixed:tool, fixed:hook, fixed:graph, uniform, thompson_cell, llm_choice} x 5 seeds, matched budgets including proposer, canary and control tokens; outcomes: held-out lift, BWT/FWT per round, per-surface activation rate, certification rate, cost per certified patch, canary decay per surface, reintroduction rate. Core subset ($2-3k: 2 tiers x 1 family x 4 arms x 3 seeds) runs first; full grid (~$10k) if credits allow. Phase-2 compounding protocol (RELAI): a second budget on new tasks after freezing. Cross-tier transfer: promoted genomes from each tier evaluated under the other tiers (Lin et al.'s D_benefit design). Ship DSH, pi/Prime and Reef adapters; export Turnstile evidence and Hermetic receipts.

Month 3 (weeks 9-12): paper and artifact: write-up with the pre-registered analysis, the three replications, and the null results stated as nulls; release v1.0 with a Harbor task family 'meristem-seed' so RSI-Exam / HarnessDev / HarnessOpt-Bench can point their creator or optimizer at the substrate as a subject; L3 mode (proposer template + router as a separately gated genome with anchor tasks) shipped as an explicitly exploratory experiment with its own ledger; a 'run your operator' guide with MetaRSI HarnessPatch, MOSS-style graph patches and MGM-style cross-lineage differential evidence as worked examples; PRs to lobehub/awesome-rsi, wannabeyourfriend/awesome-harness-evolution and pinkbubblebubble's checklist repo; a Reef recipe PR and an OpenClaw evaluator plugin listing; ICLR RSI workshop / NeurIPS datasets-and-benchmarks submission with the ledgers of every run published.
rsi-substrate.killer_demo: Five minutes, one terminal, no GPU. `pip install meristem && meristem init --tasks harbor:terminal-bench-2.1 --slice ai2-45 --model claude-sonnet-4-6` seeds a 60-line loop-graph genome and records the protected corpus (two incumbent runs per task, stability per task, ~$8). `meristem run --budget-usd 40 --rounds 2 --surfaces all --router thompson_cell` streams the ledger live: failure clusters mined from the incumbent's traces (fs:stop_without_verify n=12, fs:tool_error_loop n=7), a proposal per cluster with the surface the router chose, Tier-0 verdicts in seconds (one skill patch rejected by the leak scan for quoting a task path; one prompt patch blocked by the canary for adding 'skip confirmation prompts'), then certification: eligible pairs per candidate, the e-process wealth curve climbing on discordant pairs, the parallel-4 TTS control arm running in the background on the same ledger. At minute four `meristem report` prints: 11 candidates -> 9 admitted -> 7 exercised -> 2 certified -> 2 promoted (one on_stop hook: force test run after tool error, +5 protected flips, 0 regressions, wealth 27 > 1/alpha_k; one graph edit adding a verify->act retry edge); 5 held as inconclusive with 'pairs needed for 80% power: 160'; lift vs incumbent +11pp on the 45-task adaptation split, +4pp on the sealed 34-task slice, +1pp vs parallel-4 at matched dollars (not significant) — printed honestly with the gate's own cost ($9.80 of the $40). The per-cell table shows hook and graph cells at Beta(6,1) and (4,2) while prompt and skill cells sit at (1,4) and (0,3), with skill activation 2/23. Minute five: `meristem export claude-code ./myrepo` writes the two promoted patches as a settings.json Stop hook and a CLAUDE.md slot, and `meristem replay --genome gen_5d02 --model claude-haiku-4-5` re-runs the same genome under a weaker model: the hook still fires and still flips tasks; the prompt-slot patch shows adherence drift .58 -> .21. The point of the demo is the report, not the number: every claim on screen has a receipt, a control arm, a power estimate and a price.
rsi-substrate.research_contribution: TITLE: 'One Genome, One Gate: A Reference Substrate for Harness-Level Self-Improvement and the Cross-Substrate Credit-Assignment Problem'. CRISP CLAIMS (pre-registered): (C1, substrate) Holding the loop fixed and varying only the operator, the published gains of three loop families (Self-Harness-style hook-menu evolution, SkillOpt-style skill evolution, MetaRSI-style multi-slot HarnessPatch evolution) on Terminal-Bench 2.1 shrink to within the A-vs-A' noise band on the sealed 34-task slice at matched budget vs parallel-K test-time scaling once proposer, control and canary tokens are charged — reproducing AI2 across operators, which AI2 could do for only one loop. (C2, credit assignment) The surface that carries certified held-out lift is predictable from (failure signature, model tier): deterministic surfaces (hook, loop-graph) dominate certified lift for weak and mid tiers, where prompt/skill activation and adherence are low (Lin et al. SLR .25-.45, adherence drift .52 -> .13); prompt-slot patches never dominate for strong tiers (AHE ablation); skill patches certify only when retrieval activation on eligible tasks exceeds ~0.6. (C3, router) Thompson sampling over (surface x signature x tier) clade cells reaches the same certified held-out lift as the uniform router at <= 60% of the evaluation budget, and beats llm_choice (the proposer picking its own surface, i.e. every current system) on cost per certified patch. (C4, compounding) Under the RELAI phase-2 protocol, genomes whose promoted patches are majority deterministic-surface retain lift (BWT >= -2pp) while prompt/skill-majority genomes show harness-induced forgetting comparable to EvoHarnessBench (-4 to -5pp). EXPERIMENT: 3 tiers x 2 task families x 8 arms x 5 seeds, matched budgets incl. all tokens; sealed slice opened once; A-vs-A' control per task; phase-2 budget on new tasks; cross-tier transfer of promoted genomes. BASELINES: frozen genome; parallel-K and sequential-K TTS (AI2); GEPA-style prompt-only; Self-Harness hook-only; Meta-Harness-style whole-candidate frontier where feasible; uniform and llm_choice routers; greedy strict-> gate as the acceptor baseline (PACE/Turnstile). WHAT FALSIFIES IT: C1 is false if any operator's sealed-slice lift exceeds the TTS arm by more than the noise band at matched dollars in >= 3/5 seeds (then evolution beats search and the substrate has found a real design premium — a publishable positive). C2 is false if forced-surface arms are statistically indistinguishable on the sealed slice across tiers, or if prompt-only certifies as often as hook/graph for weak tiers. C3 is false if thompson_cell does not reduce cost per certified patch vs uniform (then surface conditioning carries no information and the router should be deleted). C4 is false if retention does not differ by surface majority. All four can fail and the artifact still stands as the reference loop with the field's first cost-normalized, activation-aware, matched-budget comparison table across operators; we commit to publishing every ledger.
rsi-substrate.adoption_path: Research-first, in this order. (1) Credibility by replication: reproduce PACE's gate statistics, AI2's TTS comparison and Self-Harness's loop inside the substrate in month 1 and publish the ledgers — the '$30 clean-room replication' the Gödel-lineage critique asks for, done for three loops. (2) Become the standard subject: ship Harbor-native task/stream adapters (RSI-Exam two-image profile, SEAGym streams, EvoHarnessBench jsonl, HarnessOpt-Bench budget protocol) and a HarnessDev-compatible seed so benchmark authors can run 'the reference loop' instead of a bespoke one; offer to run our loop on their streams and hand them the ledger. (3) Become the kernel operator papers plug into: a one-interface Operator.propose contract with worked examples for MetaRSI HarnessPatch (their released genome.ts schema is a subset of ours), MOSS-style structural changes as graph patches, MGM's cross-lineage differential evidence as an evidence-bundle option, and GEA's group-of-two as an archive policy; write to the MetaRSI (CosmosMind), MOSS (HKGAI) and MGM (LMU) authors with a reproduction of their headline on our kernel. (4) Practitioners get a 'trained harness' rather than a gate: `meristem export claude-code|hermes|openclaw|dsh|pi` installs promoted patches into the harness they already run, with activation receipts flowing back, so the substrate's value reaches the ~900k-star ecosystem without a proxy and without asking anyone to adopt statistics — the gate is invisible to them, only the export is visible.
