(5) Compose with the sibling artifacts rather than compete: emit Turnstile evidence records (so Meristem's gate is benchmarked like any acceptor), consume Hermetic receipts (so the sealed runner can be swapped for the product version), and let Pawl's production interceptor use Meristem's gate library as its engine. (6) Venues and lists: ICLR RSI workshop, pinkbubblebubble's reporting checklist (we satisfy every item by construction and say so), lobehub/awesome-rsi and awesome-harness-evolution PRs, a Reef recipe PR (Reef #357/#358 opened the exact need), the first third-party OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate plugin. (7) Governance: the 2k-line core stays MIT, adapters are separate packages, and the gate policy, canary bank and protected-corpus builder are versioned with changelogs so a paper can cite 'meristem-gate/0.3' as a fixed acceptor.

nearest_competitors.name: MetaRSI / RSI² (CosmosMind, arXiv 2609.06396)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: The closest formal statement of our loop: seven-stage kernel, single authority cut, typed HarnessPatch over five slots, freshness rule, sealed evaluator, strict-improvement promotion. But it releases no loop, evaluator, gate or Record Gates (only the HarnessPatch schema and a Pi config), its promotion is strict > on an adaptation split with no noise model, no activation term, no per-surface attribution, no TTS control, and the same model plays every seat. Meristem is the runnable kernel MetaRSI describes, with error-controlled gating, activation-gated credit, surface-cell clades and matched-budget reporting; its HarnessPatch is a subset of our candidate format so its Harness-RSI operator can be plugged in directly.

nearest_competitors.name: Self-Harness (Shanghai AI Lab, 2606.09498)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Hook menu (six prompt slots, subagents, skills, tools, middleware, permissions), one hook per candidate, 'no split drops and one improves' over 2 repeats, linear lineage in one LangChain file, held-out split consulted by the gate. We generalize the menu into five typed surfaces incl. a loop-graph, add an archive with clade posteriors, replace the 2-repeat gate with a paired anytime-valid e-process plus a stability-conditioned floor, seal the held-out slice, add activation and safety terms, and charge the proposer's tokens. Self-Harness runs unchanged as an Operator on our kernel.

nearest_competitors.name: HGM / MGM / GEA (Gödel lineage: metauto-ai/HGM, RealLcz/MGM, UCSB-AI/GEA)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Whole-repo genomes, compile-and-smoke admission, clade metaproductivity (HGM), comparative evidence operators (MGM), group experience sharing (GEA); single runs, no held-out inside the loop, private test patches shown to the diagnoser, $13k-22k per run on GPU-served models. We keep the two ideas that survive independent replication (clade posteriors; cross-lineage differential evidence) and apply them to a typed genome under an API-only, <= $100-per-run loop with sealed evaluation, leak scans and a certificate for promotion; whole-code mutation is out of scope by design.

nearest_competitors.name: A-Evolve / a-evolve (A-EVO-Lab, 779 stars) and Lin et al.'s A-Evolve UnifiedEngine
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: The nearest 'substrate' competitor: ae.Evolver(agent, benchmark).run() with Reader/Operator/Verifier slots. In every published recipe the Verifier is NoVerify, scope is enforced by post-hoc byte-snapshot restore, the evolver edits via an unsandboxed bash tool, and there is no activation, noise, or cost accounting. Meristem is gate-first: the verifier slot is the load-bearing component, surfaces are typed rather than 'the workspace', and Lin et al.'s own SLR/HFR diagnostics become gate inputs.

nearest_competitors.name: Reef (Human-Agent-Society, ~1.3k stars)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Release pipeline with pluggable propose/evaluate/decide recipes, paired episodes, rejected history, one-step rollback, W/L > min_win_margin decide, pooled tally with no protected floor (#356). Meristem is both a Reef recipe and a standalone research loop; it contributes the e-process decide, per-surface eligibility and floor, TTS control and cost ledger Reef lacks, and it does not own serving, versioned releases or canary routing, which we defer to Reef when exporting.

nearest_competitors.name: SkillOpt / SkillOpt-Sleep (Microsoft, 17k stars)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: One SKILL.md surface, strict held-out gate on a val-slice mean (per-task regressions accepted, #174), textual learning rate, rejected-edit buffer, optimizer sees judge regex source (#154). We keep the rejected buffer and edit budget, extend to five surfaces, make the gate paired-sequential with a per-task floor, blind the proposer to scorer text, and add activation receipts; SkillOpt's optimizer is a valid Operator for the skill surface.

nearest_competitors.name: agentdescent (Birfy)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Beta-posterior acceptance with a hard regression guard, async keyed-diff merging, full-held-out invariant, freeze-by-name, kappa-discounted proxy evidence. We reuse the AcceptancePolicy contract shape and the full-held-out invariant, but replace posterior thresholds with anytime-valid certificates plus a spend schedule, add a typed multi-surface genome with a loop-graph, and treat multi-worker merging as out of scope.

nearest_competitors.name: auto-harness (NeoSigma, 537 stars)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: PROGRAM.md + gating.py exit 0/1 held-out ratchet with an 80% regression suite; gate state, best score and program live in the agent's writable surface; single-run tie-accepting gate on ~27 tasks. We keep 'any coding agent can be the proposer' but own the gate state outside the mutable surface, seal the split, and use a noise-aware sequential test.

nearest_competitors.name: PACE (2606.08106) and SEA (2607.00871)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: The gate mathematics we implement and extend: PACE is prompt-only on 0.5B-3B models with per-candidate error control, fixed lambda and no code; SEA's certified harness gate accepted 0 edits at ~50 tasks and was switched off. We add mixture betting, CTHS run-level spend, dense-signal e-values, per-surface eligibility, and the two-tier admission that keeps the loop alive while evidence accrues.

nearest_competitors.name: Causal Agent Replay (2606.08275) / The Replay Gap (2608.08239)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Attribution and negative-result primitives, not loops. We adopt CAR's abstain-as-outcome and sanity floor and The Replay Gap's control arm and re-execute-don't-stitch rule as gate requirements; we do not attempt trajectory-level do-interventions inside the substrate.

nearest_competitors.name: SafeEvolve / SkillMisevo-Gym (2608.12851)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Two-boundary governance (admission at write, revocation at reuse) for SKILL.md only, critic = the evolving backbone, utility cost ~13pp. We apply both boundaries to all five surfaces inside the gate with a cross-family canary judge, and treat their gym as a safety stream to run the substrate on.

nearest_competitors.name: Hermes (Nous), Prime Agent /refine, OpenClaw Skill Workshop, DeepSeek Harness
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Production loops or substrates with no outcome-based acceptance (Hermes: writing model's judgment; Prime: refiner's judgment, expectedOutcome never checked; OpenClaw: regex + hashes, evaluator seam with zero implementations; DSH: evaluator deliberately deferred). We are the research reference that imports their artifacts as candidates and exports promoted genomes into them; we do not intercept their production writes (Pawl does).

nearest_competitors.name: Continual Harness (Princeton) / JIT-Agent / HarnessX / Ouroboros
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Continual Harness CRUDs (p,G,K,M) mid-episode with no gate; JIT-Agent fixes a 4-module code protocol and gates by Pareto frontier with a fail-open review; HarnessX's AEGIS uses a deterministic seesaw gate but whole-harness variants; Ouroboros gates by multi-model diff review quorum on core code. We take Continual Harness's CRUD taxonomy as surfaces, JIT-Agent's contract-first idea as the frozen kernel, HarnessX's manifest-vs-trace check as diff == declared, and Ouroboros's immutable constitution as the out-of-genome gate policy — none of them offers a typed, API-only, error-controlled loop others can run.

nearest_competitors.name: Sibling designs: Hermetic, Turnstile, Pawl
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Hermetic sells evaluator admissibility (sealed runtime, receipts, honeytokens, Goodhart gym); we ship a minimal sealed runner and consume its receipt profile. Turnstile benchmarks acceptors with planted streams and audits production stores; we are the standard subject it benchmarks and we export its evidence format. Pawl intercepts every production self-write at the path level; we are the research loop whose gate library Pawl can embed and whose exports Pawl governs. The three cover integrity, measurement and production; Meristem covers the loop.

risks: Flagship nulls: with binary outcomes and 20-45 protected tasks, most candidates will hold as inconclusive and forced-surface arms may be indistinguishable on the sealed slice; mitigated by pre-registration, dense-signal e-values, evidence accrual across rounds, and treating the null as a result — the substrate and the cost-normalized comparison table stand regardless.

Cost: a certification on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with a Sonnet-tier agent is $10-30 per candidate even with eligibility filtering; the full flagship grid is ~$10k. Mitigations: weak/mid tiers for most cells, cheaper task families (SkillsBench subsets, EOG MCP gyms), the core $2-3k subset first, and credits; the report always prints the gate's own cost so the trade-off is explicit.

Loop-graph expressiveness: a typed DAG with a predicate language may not express real harness loops (Claude Code's subagent orchestration, DSH's ralph rounds), making exports lossy and the graph surface less interesting than hoped; scoped to ReAct-family graphs in v1, with adapters documenting what does not export.

Serving nondeterminism and model drift: T=0 is not determinism and provider snapshots change mid-experiment; mitigated by recording served model ids in receipts, re-measuring the A-vs-A' floor per session, pinning snapshot ids where providers expose them, and reporting per-seed results.

Scorer-blindness is heuristic: task-id scrubbing and leak scans cannot prove the proposer did not infer task identity from traces (AI2 saw memorized paths despite bans); honeytokens and the sealed slice bound the damage but do not eliminate it.

Failure-signature mining may be too coarse or too benchmark-specific to define stable (surface x signature) cells across task families, weakening the router claim; we ship a small deterministic taxonomy and report cell counts so sparsity is visible.
2k-line discipline: the core will balloon if adapters, Harbor plumbing or the canary bank creep in; the line-count audit is a release gate and adapters live in separate packages.

Sibling overlap and community confusion: three designs from one research effort could be read as one product; clear boundaries (integrity / measurement / production / loop) and shared record formats are the mitigation.

Adoption asymmetry: research users may adopt while practitioners ignore a 'trained harness' export; the export adapters and receipts are the bridge but the practitioner-facing value (diff, undo, budget) belongs to Pawl.

Harbor/Docker dependency on macOS and E2B/Daytona costs for sandboxed task families; a local git-worktree sandbox covers cheap task families but is not a security boundary (SkillOpt #155 maintainers' constraint), so real execution stays off by default outside containers.

Canary judge validity: cross-family LLM judging of safety probes inherits the More-Convincing-Not-More-Correct failure; the Blind Curator cliff diagnostic is printed but a bad judge still passes bad artifacts.

The L3 mode (evolving the proposer/router) invites optimizer-optimizee collapse if users mix it into L2 results; it ships off by default with its own ledger and anchors, and the paper reports it separately or not at all.
open_questions: Is a loop-graph surface worth its complexity, or do hooks alone capture the structural failures MOSS attributes to code (the flagship's fixed:graph vs fixed:hook arms answer this; if graph never beats hook, remove it).
Should memory bullets be a sixth surface with their own eligibility (retrieval-conditioned) rather than a prompt-slot sub-kind, given memory is the most-deployed and least-gated artifact?

What is the right familywise unit for the CTHS spend: per candidate stream (PACE), per surface cell, or per run? Spending alpha per cell would let the router's exploration be error-controlled but weakens the run-level guarantee.

How should composite (multi-surface) patches be credited when single-surface reverts are themselves noisy at n=2 — is release-time ablation affordable, or should composites be banned from certification?
Can judge-rung evidence be used as a cheap pre-screen for ranking candidates before spending without leaking rubric text into the proposer's feedback (the SkillOpt #154 channel)?
Which deterministic failure-signature taxonomy transfers across task families (coding vs enterprise-ops MCP tasks) so that surface cells are comparable?
How to score proposer calibration (expected_effect vs realized flips) so that a well-calibrated proposer earns a cheaper certification — and whether that creates a new Goodhart target.
What anchor set and human-merge policy make the L3 mode (evolving the proposer template and router) meaningful without self-confirmation (RQGM/Double Ratchet anchors did not fire at small budgets)?
Cross-tier transfer: should a genome promoted under a strong tier be re-certified before export to a weaker consumer, given Lin et al.'s non-monotonic benefit, and who pays for that certification?

Whether the substrate should support weight-touching operators (WHALE/SIA-style LoRA candidates via hosted fine-tuning APIs) as a sixth surface behind the same gate, or remain strictly harness-level to stay API-only and cheap.
Name and license: Meristem vs alternatives; MIT core with Apache adapters, or one license.

wildcard.name: Precedent
wildcard.tagline: Every correction becomes a test. Precedent mines the rulings you already gave your agent, compiles them into enforced and executable checks you confirm with one keystroke, and grades every skill, memory, harness change and model upgrade against that private, self-growing exam — before it reaches you.
wildcard.stance: WILDCARD / FIRST PRINCIPLES. The unit of evolution is the CRITERION — the human-agent contract and its executable checks — not the agent's skills, memory, prompts or code. Authorship is flipped: humans author criteria (by correcting the agent and confirming a mined proposal), machines do all verification labor (mining, validating on recorded sessions, enforcing via hooks, replaying, reporting). Everything the field calls 'self-improvement' (skills, memories, CLAUDE.md edits, harness config, model swaps, the proposals of Hermes/Prime/SkillOpt/OpenClaw loops) becomes bounded self-refinement graded against a user-owned exam that no proposer authored. Precedent never proposes skills, never certifies capability lift, and never lets an LLM admit a check; it is the L4 (criterion) layer evolving under exogenous human anchors — the one cell of the RSI grid that cannot confirm itself.
wildcard.thesis: Five independent 2026 results say LLM-written persistent artifacts have ≈0 causal effect (CTA +0.3pp; SkillsBench 0 gain for LLM-written vs +16.2 for human-written skills; Demystifying Agent Skills precision 29.6→3.3% at 100 skills; SkillOpt gains carried by 1–4 edits; Hermes ran weeks with 0 skill updates and nobody noticed) — while human-written rules work and the field's bottleneck has moved to verification (Anthropic Institute: human review is the Amdahl bottleneck; RSI survey 2607.07663: the uncharacterized 'exchange rate of grounding'; SEA: 'what is gated does not move and what moves is not gated'). The highest-signal exogenous event in every deployed agent is the user's correction, and no system treats it as data: ECC deliberately does not capture user prompts; Hermes' deep read calls a correction after a skill load 'a free negative label that is not attributed back'; claude-code#75334/#76408 users repeat '4 to 6 identical corrections'; Lin et al. show adherence to advisory rules decays .52→.13 across a trajectory; arXiv 2608.11095 shows CLAUDE.md grows +226% because rules are added and never retired; Phantom Guardrails (2607.13083) shows LLM proposers fabricate guardrails for failures that never happened in 15/60 runs; SEAL and 'Self-Authored Verification Is Unreliable' show the proposer cannot be allowed to author its own tests. The tools that do learn from corrections (claude-reflect 1.4k★, claude-smart 777★, Kiro Crew 3.8k★, ECC instincts) compile them into MORE advisory prose — the artifact class shown to decay and bloat. First-principles conclusion: the artifact that reliably compounds is not the policy but the criterion. A correction is a labeled policy violation with the violating action recorded; that is planted ground truth, so a check can be born with fail-on-base evidence at zero model cost, enforced at the deterministic rung by hooks every harness already has (so it cannot decay), moved out of the context window (so CLAUDE.md shrinks), and used as the evaluator for every future candidate — including the model upgrade that The Replay Gap shows invalidates everything else. One human keystroke then verifies an unbounded number of future sessions: that is the exchange-rate lever, and it is what makes criterion co-evolution safe (every admission is anchored by an exogenous human act and mechanically validated on recorded behavior). Precedent is the first framework whose loop is correction → check → exam → grade-everything, whose product is a private, non-stationary, user-specific held-out set for the 100% of users who have no benchmark, and whose research object is the measured exchange rate of grounding.
wildcard.rsi_positioning: Altitude: harness-level (L2–L3) bounded self-refinement, but Precedent occupies the layer above it — L4 'criterion' in the Reliable survey's ladder (Tencent/ZJU: L0 output, L1 model, L2 scaffold, L3 improver, L4 criterion; 'RSI begins at L3'), i.e. the layer whose evolution the RSI survey (2607.07663) calls the dangerous cell (self-evaluation × closed loop) and whose safe form — evaluator co-evolution without self-confirmation — all five 2026 surveys list as open with no code. Precedent's answer: the criterion evolves, but admission requires (a) an exogenous human act (the correction that generated the proposal and the keystroke that confirms it) and (b) mechanical validation on recorded behavior (fail-on-base, quiet-on-uncorrected), so the loop never grades itself with its own opinion. Verification hierarchy as schema: every precedent carries a rung (deterministic hook > executable test > learned judge), deterministic rejection overrides LLM approval (PROCTOR), and the judged rung never gates (Blind Curator cliff; 'More Convincing, Not More Correct'). Which of the surveys' four open problems it addresses: (1) a runnable reference for gated update — as the evaluator side, consumed by any gate; (2) regression/retention protocol — the private exam re-run on model swaps and on every candidate, i.e. the Replay Gap's real-world scenario (model switching) made testable per user; (3) evaluator co-evolution without self-confirmation — human-anchored criterion growth with an anti-phantom birth gate; (4) trustworthy accumulation — rules migrate from context (advisory, decaying) to exam (enforced, receipted). What RSI people get that nobody has: the first deployed measurement of the exchange rate of grounding (human confirmations and estimated human-seconds per avoided correction and per enforced invariant), a public schema and dataset of (correction, check, outcome) triples, and a controlled test of the ordering hypothesis — 'human criteria + machine verification compounds where LLM artifacts + human/no verification is ≈0'. Honest framing: this is human-on-the-loop bounded refinement in Weng's sense ('move up the stack, not out of the loop'), not open-ended RSI; it does not certify capability lift (AI2: harness evolution ≯ matched-budget TTS) and it is deliberately the complement, not the competitor, of acceptance layers, sealed-evaluator runtimes and gate benchmarks — they need an evaluator the user cares about; Precedent is where that evaluator comes from.
what_evolves: The precedent set — the human-agent contract: typed records {rule text, checks, scope (global/project/path), authority (who confirmed), status (proposed/active/advisory/dormant/demoted/retired)} — grown from human corrections, confirmations, reverts and external verdicts (CI, PR review), never from an LLM's unprompted reflection.

Check implementations per verification rung: deterministic (hook-enforced deny/ask/rewrite on tool inputs, file-state lints, post-conditions after writes), executable (a command with an expected outcome bound to a cassette snapshot, e.g. the tests the user actually ran), judged (a rubric line judged on transcripts by a cross-family model; report-only, never gating) — with promotion pressure from judged to executable to deterministic.

The exam's case corpus (the task distribution the agent is graded on): recorded sessions selected by eligibility for each precedent, with workspace snapshots, incumbent stability measured by self-replay, aging/rotation as the user's real work drifts — the non-stationary, per-user held-out set that no benchmark supplies.

Context policy: which rules remain in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/system prompt (advisory) versus exam-only (enforced or executable) — rules leave the context once enforced, reversing catastrophic-remembering growth; the compact 'active advisory' block injected per session is itself versioned.

Retirement and revision state: overrides, evasions (the agent found another path), dormancy (never eligible), quiet-and-enforced (success) — the lifecycle signals that decide demotion to advisory, re-docketing, or retirement.

Shared precedent bundles (team/organization standards): signed sets with provenance of who confirmed on which sessions, imported under quarantine and re-validated locally on the importer's own cassettes before enforcement.

Explicitly NOT evolved by Precedent: skills, memories, prompts, harness code and models — these are candidates it grades; and the miner heuristics, compiler prompts, birth-gate thresholds, examiner and hook adapters are outside the mutable surface and change only by human-merged PR (dsh trusted-branch pattern; changes to the gate are L4/L5 events).
wildcard.fitness_and_acceptance:
There are two acceptance decisions and they are deliberately at different rungs, with different ground truth.

(A) ADMITTING A PRECEDENT (a check) INTO THE EXAM. Ground truth is planted by the user: the recorded sessions in which the user corrected the agent, with the violating action recorded. Birth gate — deterministic, zero model calls — adapted from Double Ratchet's detector birth gate (fire on the failure cluster, clean on known-good) and SEA's fail-on-base admission for self-authored oracles: (1) discriminates: the check fires on ≥2 distinct corrected sessions for its topic (fail-on-base); (2) is quiet: fires on ≤ε of the uncorrected sessions in which it was eligible (default ε = 2%, always shown as counts, e.g. 9/9 vs 1/203); (3) is executable at its declared rung: deterministic checks are run against the recorded tool-call streams; executable checks must run in the sandbox against the snapshot and reproduce the pre-correction failure (Causal Agent Replay's sanity floor: the factual run must reproduce before any counterfactual is trusted); (4) is not a phantom: a check with zero fires on corrected sessions is refused for enforcement even if the human likes it — Phantom Guardrails (2607.13083) measured 15/60 LLM-proposed guardrails addressing failures that never happened; it may be admitted as 'advisory' only; (5) is confirmed by a human in the weekly docket with one keystroke (edit allowed). The LLM drafts checks; it never admits them (SEAL; 'Self-Authored Verification Is Unreliable'; 'More Convincing, Not More Correct': judge pass 0.72→0.94 while accuracy stays 0.20). Unconfirmed proposals expire after 14 days into 'declined' with reason; nothing is enforced before confirmation, so the queue can never starve the agent and can never rot into hermes#105770's 241 un-applyable items. Post-admission live false-positive floor: every override (the user allows a denied action or edits the rule) is logged; ≥3 overrides in 30 days without a confirming correction auto-demotes the precedent to advisory and re-dockets it. Retirement is by exercise, not by age: 'dormant' = eligible in 0 sessions for 60 days (not exercised, kept but flagged); 'quiet-and-enforced' = eligible, never fires = success (kept in the exam, dropped from context). Distinguishing 'fixed' from 'never exercised' is the activation problem and is answered by eligibility counts, not by fire counts.

(B) GRADING A CANDIDATE (skill, memory rewrite, CLAUDE.md edit, hook/config change, model swap, any other loop's proposal) AGAINST THE EXAM. Three rungs with strictly ordered authority — deterministic rejection overrides LLM approval, never the reverse (PROCTOR); the RSI survey's hierarchy used as a schema field on every verdict:
- Deterministic rung. Mechanical checks evaluated over the candidate's tool-call stream on eligible cases. Live: enforced by hooks, no replay needed — a denied/rewritten action is a fail recorded in the session receipt. Offline (pre-deployment): replay cassettes with the candidate, sandbox-first — git snapshot + container, workspace operations re-executed, EXTERNAL and NONDETERMINISTIC calls served from the recording keyed by (tool, normalized input) via PostToolUse updatedToolOutput ($0.007 per served replay, verified on Claude Code 2.1.258). The builder's own measurement (2,062 tool calls, 7 sessions: 50.4% workspace writes, 19.8% external, 13.2% nondeterministic; idempotent prefix 0–1 calls in every session) says pure VCR replay is dead on arrival, consistent with The Replay Gap (3–8% valid states after early forks) — so replay is re-execution, and late fork points are preferred. A violation is deterministic given the stream, but the stream is stochastic: replay k = 3 and require a violation in ≥2/3 for FAIL_CONFIRMED (report FAIL_OBSERVED at 1/3). Noise floor: the incumbent's own k = 3 replays on the same case (The Replay Gap's same-configuration control arm; T = 0 is not determinism). If the incumbent violates on ≥1/3, the case is 'unstable' and excluded from BLOCK decisions — agentdescent's rule that sub-samples rank but never veto, and the builder's own simulation showing per-task floors on stochastic tasks are 93–100% false-block at k = 1 unless stability is observed rather than assumed.
- Executable rung. Terminal checks (the session's own verification command with its expected outcome) on cassette snapshots; paired candidate vs incumbent per case; tri-state pass/fail/inconclusive per case (the binding requirement microsoft/SkillOpt#155's maintainers stated: worktree is disposable state, outcomes must be pass/fail/inconclusive, agent execution off by default). A case counts as a regression only with k-of-n confirmation and observed incumbent stability. Across cases, a paired anytime-valid e-process (PACE: discordant pairs only, commit at wealth ≥ 1/α, α = 0.05; run-level spend via SEA's horizon-free CTHS schedule δ_k = δ₀/(Z·k·log²(k+1))) decides only whether the candidate is WORSE. Precedent never certifies 'better': capability-lift claims require matched-budget test-time-scaling controls (AI2 2607.12227) that belong to acceptance layers, and the null-effect literature says most such claims are within noise; our simulation shows the e-process detects a +10pp lift only 11% of the time at N = 40 binary outcomes but blocks regressions and safety violations from a handful of discordant pairs — so we use its asymmetric strength and refuse its weak side.
- Judged rung. Rubric lines judged on transcripts by a cross-family model (2-of-3 votes, arm-blinded, Lin et al.'s HFR protocol: locked rubric extraction, blinded per-instruction adherence judging), reported as adherence with a bootstrap CI and the null floor from incumbent-vs-incumbent judging (CTA's lesson: its detectors fired identically on A-vs-A' pairs). NEVER a gate (Blind Curator: judge false-pass ≥ ≈0.45 silently disables retirement; judges are gameable). A judged precedent the human wants enforced must be compiled down to a deterministic/executable check or stay advisory.
Disposition: BLOCK on any FAIL_CONFIRMED deterministic/executable failure on a stable case, or any safety-class precedent failure (safety precedents are hard constraints, not Pareto terms: e.g. 'ask before force-push', 'never write secrets into tracked files', operational canaries seeded from incidents — hermes#101351 PAT into .git/config, #105921 review deleted four permission rules, gfpyc's 02:17 'close ALL Chrome windows' rewrite, openclaw#84882 46 memory files deleted by dreaming — plus optional Misevolve/SkillMisevo refusal probes at the judged rung); ADMIT otherwise with a per-check report; INCONCLUSIVE when fewer than 5 stable eligible cases exist or the e-process is unresolved, printed as 'needs N more cases'. Executable checks bind only to coding cassettes with a re-executable terminal verification; browser/API/OS sessions get the deterministic rung only (honest scope).

TAMPERING vs OVERFITTING (two failure classes, two mechanisms). Tampering: the exam directory (.precedent/), the hook configuration and the ledger are outside the agent's write surface — PreToolUse denies Read/Write/Edit/Bash touching them for any agent origin, the exam is content-addressed and git-backed, and every report carries a receipt hashing (precedent set, case set, candidate digest, harness version, model id, examiner version) in the RSI-Exam/AI4AI spirit ('only the artifact crosses'; fail-closed to BLOCK on examiner error). Precedents enter only through the docket; the compiler process has read access to the corpus and no write path to the exam. Overfitting: deterministic checks cannot be overfit by prose (a hook denies), but they can be EVADED (python -m pip instead of pip); evasion is the next correction — the human sees it, the check is revised with the new fire, and the evasion rate is reported per precedent. Judged-rung overfitting is moot because judged never gates. Executable checks are the user's own tests re-run, not LLM-authored assertions; a CoEvoSkills-style surrogate verifier is never admitted without a fail-on-base fire and a human keystroke.

ACTIVATION. Per-session receipt from InstructionsLoaded/SessionStart/Stop: which instruction files resolved, store identity + hash, bytes available vs loaded, status complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store (claude-code#82056's four indistinguishable failure modes, including the unstable project-slug case); which precedents were eligible (trigger domain matched ≥1 tool call or prompt), fired, overridden, obeyed-without-firing. Funnel per precedent: proposed → confirmed → eligible → fired/obeyed → corrections-after. Alarms: 'MEMORY.md truncated in k of the last n sessions', 'precedent X eligible 0 times in 60 days', 'corrections on topic T continue despite enforcement (evasion?)', 'examiner has not run in 30 days'.

ATTRIBUTION. The exogenous ground truth is the human correction rate per topic. We claim only what an interrupted time series on the user's own log supports: correction rate on topic T before vs after enforcement, against control topics (corrected topics the user chose not to compile) to absorb secular drift, reported with eligible-session counts and never as a causal certificate. For candidates, attribution is per check, not per aggregate score, so 'which precedent did the new model break, on which case, at which turn' is direct. Lift attribution for skills/memories is explicitly out of scope and delegated to acceptance layers.

COST AND STARVATION. Mining, birth gate and the deterministic rung are model-free. Compilation is one small-model call per topic (~$0.01). Executable-rung replays run only on demand (a candidate or a model swap), with a per-exam budget cap, a spend line in every report, and a circuit breaker on repeated inconclusive results. The judged rung is opt-in and capped. No decision waits on the human: enforced precedents act, unconfirmed proposals expire, and the weekly docket carries a default disposition with a one-line diff and evidence, surfaced where the user already is (terminal, PR comment, chat gateway).
wildcard.core_technical_insight: Human corrections are a free, exogenous, per-user labeled dataset of policy violations with the violating action already recorded — so a check can be born with planted ground truth (it must fire on the corrected sessions and stay quiet on the uncorrected ones) at zero model cost, which is precisely what LLM-authored artifacts lack (no ground truth at all) and what Phantom Guardrails shows self-proposed guardrails fabricate. Making the CRITERION rather than the policy the unit of evolution has four consequences competitors do not get: (1) it compounds — one human keystroke verifies every future session, candidate and model swap for free, which is the exchange-rate-of-grounding lever the RSI survey names and nobody measures; (2) it is enforceable at the deterministic rung through hooks every harness already ships (PreToolUse, pre_tool_call, before_tool_call, tools/pre-execute, tool_call), so it cannot decay in adherence the way advisory text does (.52→.13) and can leave the context window entirely (reversing +226% CLAUDE.md growth); (3) it is executable ground truth the proposer never authored — the input every gate, sealed evaluator and gate benchmark in the field needs and none can source for real users, and the thing DeepSeek Harness explicitly deferred and OpenClaw's evaluator seam has been waiting for; (4) it makes evaluator co-evolution safe: the criterion evolves, but every admission is anchored by an exogenous human act and mechanically validated on recorded behavior, so the loop cannot confirm itself. The corrections→prose tools (claude-reflect, claude-smart, Kiro Crew, ECC instincts, Hermes/Codex/Claude memory) stop at advice; the outcome gates (SkillOpt, Self-Harness, Reef, acceptance layers) grade artifacts on signals within noise; the sealed evaluators (RSI-Exam, AI4AI) grade against tests benchmark authors wrote. None turns the user's own rulings into the evaluator, and none moves rules from the context window into an exam.

architecture.responsibility: Reads each harness's existing session logs with no new instrumentation — Claude Code ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl (user turns, assistant text, tool_use/tool_result incl. structured toolUseResult), Hermes session logs + skill_ledger JSONL + .usage.json, Codex rollouts, DSH zstd session JSONL (model-visible ⇔ logged), OpenClaw SQLite — into one typed event stream (user/assistant/tool_use/tool_result with replayability class IDEMPOTENT_READ / WORKSPACE_WRITE / EXTERNAL / NONDETERMINISTIC) plus a workspace snapshot ref when the cwd is a git repo. Adapter validation per CTA PR#2 (conservation, alternation, vocabulary coverage, degenerate-session SKIP vs FAIL).
architecture.interfaces: precedent.reader.load(path) -> Cassette; per-harness adapter registry; cassette JSON on disk under .precedent/cassettes/ (local only, secret-scrubbed).

architecture.responsibility: Detects human rulings deterministically first: corrections (negation/imperative user turn following an agent action; 'I said / again / instead'; user re-issuing an instruction; user reverting agent edits per git; interrupts/Stop markers), confirmations (explicit approval of a plan/diff), reverts, and external verdicts (CI results, gh PR review comments when available). Clusters repeats into topics keyed by normalized tool-input n-grams and file paths; optional cheap-model classifier arm calibrated on a human-labeled set with reported precision/recall. Repetition across sessions is the signal (≥2 corrections on a topic = candidate).
architecture.interfaces: precedent.mine(cassettes) -> [CorrectionEvent], topics.json; UserPromptSubmit hook tags live user turns as trusted origin and pre-marks likely corrections for the Stop-time miner.

architecture.responsibility: For each topic, drafts candidate checks at the highest achievable rung: deterministic (hook rule: deny/ask/rewrite on tool-input regex or structured fields; file-state lint; post-condition after Write/Edit), executable (bind the session's own verification command + expected outcome to the snapshot), judged (rubric line). LLM-assisted drafting with a small model; the draft is validated deterministically and can never write to the exam. Emits scope suggestions (project vs global) from where the corrections occurred.
architecture.interfaces: precedent.compile(topic) -> [PrecedentDraft]; grader export to `claude plugin eval` formats (tool_used input_match max:0, regex over trace/files, tool_order, file_exists).

architecture.responsibility: Runs every draft against the corpus: fires on corrected sessions (must be ≥2), fires on uncorrected eligible sessions (≤ε), reproduces the pre-correction failure for executable checks in the sandbox, refuses phantoms. Presents a weekly docket (TUI/CLI, PR comment, or chat card) with one-line diff, evidence counts, example fires, default disposition; one-key confirm/edit/reject/snooze; 14-day expiry to 'declined with reason'.
architecture.interfaces: precedent docket [--pr | --slack]; docket.json; only path that writes to the exam; records confirmed_by/at in the ledger.

architecture.responsibility: Content-addressed, git-backed store of precedents, cases (cassette bindings with snapshots and measured incumbent stability), starter packs and receipts, outside every agent's write surface (hooks deny reads/writes for agent origins; separate directory/user; hash-pinned set id in every receipt). Versioned; every change is a ledger event with actor = human or examiner, never an LLM.
architecture.interfaces: .precedent/exam/{precedents,cases,packs}/; `precedent exam show|diff|export`; export as evaluator bundle (Harbor task family; in-toto/EEE-profile acceptance record).

architecture.responsibility: Applies deterministic precedents in real time and emits receipts: Claude Code (SessionStart, InstructionsLoaded, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse permissionDecision deny|ask + updatedInput rewrite, PostToolUse post-conditions, Stop receipt), Hermes shell pre_tool_call (fail-closed) + plugin ctx.register_hook, OpenClaw before_tool_call (block:true / requireApproval), DSH tools/pre-execute typed Decision + tools/post-execute block/attach (and the hook-protocol bridge that runs the Claude Code hooks.json unchanged), pi tool_call block / tool_result modify, Codex PostToolUse block/replace. Also seals .precedent/ and the hook config against agent writes.
architecture.interfaces: `precedent hooks install <harness>`; hook scripts read the compiled rule table (JSON) and never call a model; conformance suite asserts each seam actually stops the write.

architecture.responsibility: Grades a candidate against the exam: deterministic rung over replayed tool streams; executable rung via sandbox-first replay (git worktree + container, workspace ops re-executed, externals/nondeterministic served from recording, k=3, incumbent control arm, k-of-n confirmation, PACE-style 'worse' e-process with CTHS spend); judged rung via cross-family 2-of-3 judge, report-only. Uses `claude plugin eval` as an alternative sealed backend (throwaway home, history_file = transcript prefix to the fork turn, scaffold_script restores the snapshot, precedents exported as graders, --ablation with-without, --json into the report). Fail-closed: examiner error → BLOCK with reason.
architecture.interfaces: `precedent exam run --candidate <skill|memory|claudemd|model:<id>|harness:<ver>>`; exposed as OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate plugin, Reef evaluate/decide recipe, Hermes pending-queue reviewer, DSH evaluator plugin; emits ExamReport + receipt.

architecture.responsibility: Append-only, hash-chained ledger of every event (correction detected, precedent proposed/confirmed/demoted, session receipt, exam report, override, evasion); per-session load receipts (complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store); per-precedent funnel proposed→confirmed→eligible→fired/obeyed→corrections-after; alarms (truncation, dormancy, evasion, examiner silence); spend meter per exam; exchange-rate metrics (confirmations, estimated human-seconds, corrections avoided, invariants enforced).
architecture.interfaces: `precedent report [--since]`; ledger.jsonl; OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result-compatible event export; acceptance-record profile.

architecture.responsibility: Moves rules from context (advisory block injected at UserPromptSubmit/SessionStart) to exam-only once enforced; demotes on overrides; flags dormancy and evasion; ages cases out of the corpus as the user's work drifts and adds cases from new corrections; keeps CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md diffs minimal and explicit (Precedent writes only a fenced, hash-stamped block).
architecture.interfaces: `precedent context sync` (writes/updates the fenced block); lifecycle rules as human-editable YAML outside the agent's surface.

architecture.responsibility: Signed precedent packs (e.g. python-uv, git-safety, secrets-hygiene, incident canaries) with provenance of who confirmed on how many sessions; import = quarantine → local birth gate on the importer's own cassettes (must not fire on their uncorrected sessions) → staged enforcement; per-project overrides instead of LLM merge (SkillClaw's one-skill-per-group failure); the team adoption story is 'ESLint config for agent behavior, written by your team's corrections'.
architecture.interfaces: `precedent pack publish|import|verify`; bundle JSON with DSSE signature; registry-agnostic (git repo, ClawHub-style hub).

wildcard.integration_surface:
CLAUDE CODE (first adapter, the builder's own harness; all hooks below verified in the local CLI). SessionStart: register the session, pin the exam-set hash, record the workspace snapshot ref (HEAD + dirty patch), start the spend meter, inject the compact advisory block (only 'advisory' precedents; never exam contents). InstructionsLoaded: emit the load receipt — which CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md/skills resolved, store identity + hash, bytes available vs loaded, complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store (the claude-code#82056 receipt; works with no learning loop at all). UserPromptSubmit: tag the human turn as trusted origin, run the cheap correction pre-marker, and (optionally) add a one-line 'active precedents for this topic' context. PreToolUse: enforce deterministic precedents with permissionDecision deny|ask and updatedInput rewrites (e.g. pip→uv), seal .precedent/ and settings hooks against agent origins, and during offline replay route calls into the sandbox worktree. PostToolUse: post-condition checks after Write/Edit/Bash (secret patterns into tracked files, forbidden paths), and during replay serve recorded EXTERNAL/NONDETERMINISTIC results via updatedToolOutput. Stop/SubagentStop: finalize the cassette, run the miner, write the session receipt, and print docket nudges only when something changed. `claude plugin eval`: precedents export as graders (tool_used with input_match and max:0, regex over trace/files, tool_order, file_exists), so plugin/skill authors can run precedent-conformance in Anthropic's sealed runner; cases compile to eval cases (scaffold_script restores the snapshot, history_file = transcript prefix to the fork turn, runs=3, --ablation with-without for skills, model: for swaps, --json feeds the report). `precedent context sync` maintains one fenced, hash-stamped block in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md and removes rules that became enforced.

HERMES (skill_manage / curator / background review). Enforcement: shell pre_tool_call (fail-closed) applies deterministic precedents to every tool, including write_file/patch/terminal paths that bypass skill_manage (#99729); a plugin via ctx.register_hook emits receipts. Grading: a reviewer daemon reads ~/.hermes/pending/{skills,memory}/<id>.json (skills.write_approval staging) and grades each pending write — a memory line or skill that contradicts an active precedent (e.g. instructs bare pip, codifies a placeholder as 'Verified', or drops a verification requirement its ancestor asserted per SafeEvolve's invariant) is dispositioned reject/hold with the precedent cited; approved payloads replay through skill_manage. Curator: consolidation proposals are graded the same way; the curator's YAML summary is reconciled against the ledger. Reader: session logs + tools/skill_ledger.py JSONL + .usage.json supply cassettes and activation; skill_provenance write-origin is carried into receipts. Landing zone: hermes#96704's RFC (three arms, cheapest arm first) and #416 (validation) — precedents supply the deterministic lint arm.

OPENCLAW. before_tool_call: block:true for deny precedents, requireApproval for ask precedents (first requireApproval wins; timeouts leave state unchanged). skill_proposal_evaluate: a plugin receives {proposal, candidate BundleSnapshot, baseline, reason} and returns {evaluatorVersion, mode:'baseline-comparison', decision: pass|revise|block, findings:[{ruleId: 'prec_0042', severity, message, file, line}], metrics:{violations, stable_cases, cost_usd}} — block on confirmed failures; because the seam is fail-open (error/skipped do not veto) the plugin converts its own errors into an explicit block when policy is fail-closed. skill_proposal_changed / skill_changed feed the ledger. This is the first third-party evaluator on that seam.

DEEPSEEK HARNESS. Native plugin: tools/pre-execute returns the typed allow/deny/ask Decision for deterministic precedents (guards are deny-only so listener order cannot resurrect a denied action), tools/post-execute attaches the receipt or blocks on post-conditions, agent/turn-stopping emits the session receipt; the zstd session log (model-visible ⇔ logged) is the reader source. Zero-work path: dsh's hook-protocol bridge runs the Claude Code hooks.json unchanged, so the same enforcer runs under dsh today. Positioning: the user-owned criterion occupies the evaluator slot dsh deferred 'until its authority, isolation and provider contract are designed' — authority = human docket, isolation = sealed exam, provider = the examiner; it complements dsh-verification-style 'claimed-done → actually-done' plugins by supplying what 'done right' means for this user.

PI / PRIME AGENT. pi extensions: tool_call (block) and tool_result (modify) for the deterministic rung; context rewriting injects the advisory block. Prime /refine: refinements.jsonl entries and harness_state.json snapshots are candidates graded against the exam before apply (`precedent exam run --candidate prime:refinement:<id>`), which also renders the diff-before-apply users asked for (#684, #1208); precedents may be emitted as prompt-kind entries whose free-text expectedOutcome is replaced by a check id.

REEF. Recipe: evaluate = exam run paired candidate-vs-incumbent on eligible cases; decide = zero FAIL_CONFIRMED ∧ e-process not 'worse' (a rejection leaves the previous version serving, as Reef guarantees); x-reef-report feedback and scores are ingested as verdict events and corrections; canary/shadow routing continues the e-process on live sessions. Addresses #356 (pooled tally hides seed-suite regressions: per-check verdicts on a protected, stability-measured corpus) and #447 (records → Harbor tasks: the exam exports as a Harbor task family).

CODEX. PostToolUse block/replace for deterministic precedents; ~/.codex/memories graded before injection where hooks allow; provider-boundary rule as a precedent class ('memory jobs may not send local-provider transcripts to another provider' per codex#41711) enforced where the harness exposes the call.

STANDARDS. Exam reports are also emitted as an acceptance-record profile (candidate digest, incumbent digest, paired evidence, decision rule, verdict, disposition, activation, cost) over in-toto Statement v1 / EEE instance records / OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result attributes, so existing tooling can verify them; the exam itself exports as a Harbor task family so external gates and benchmarks can consume it.
mvp_2_weeks: Day 1–2: Reader for Claude Code (~/.claude/projects/<slug>/*.jsonl → cassette JSON with user turns, tool I/O, structured toolUseResult, replayability class, git snapshot ref); reuse research/tools/cassette_extract.py; secret scrub; local only.

Day 2–4: Miner v0 — deterministic correction detectors (negation/imperative after agent action, 'I said/again/instead', repeated instruction, git revert of agent edits, interrupt markers) + topic clustering by normalized tool-input n-grams and paths; `precedent init` prints the correction report in <10 s with zero model calls ('143 corrections in 212 sessions; 31 repeat; top topics; 12 already in CLAUDE.md and violated in 40% of loaded sessions').

Day 4–6: Compiler v0 — deterministic checks only (Bash/Edit/Write input regex → deny/ask/rewrite; file-glob post-conditions), drafted by a small model, validated deterministically; birth gate computing fires-on-corrected / fires-on-uncorrected-eligible with counts; anti-phantom rule.
Day 6–7: Docket TUI/CLI — one-key confirm/edit/reject/snooze, evidence and example fires, 14-day expiry; ledger (hash-chained JSONL) and the sealed .precedent/exam/ layout.

Day 7–9: Enforcer — `precedent hooks install claude-code` writes settings.json hooks: PreToolUse deny/ask/updatedInput from the compiled rule table, PostToolUse post-conditions, sealing of .precedent/ and hook config; SessionStart/InstructionsLoaded/Stop receipts (complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store); override capture; `precedent context sync` fenced block.

Day 9–11: Examiner v0 via `claude plugin eval` — compile 5–10 eligible cases (history_file prefix + scaffold_script snapshot), export precedents as graders, run --ablation with-without for a skill candidate and model: for a model swap, ingest --json into an ExamReport with per-precedent verdicts and the spend line; deterministic rung only; k=3; incumbent control arm.

Day 11–13: `precedent report` (funnel per precedent, truncation/dormancy alarms, exchange-rate line: confirmations, corrections-after vs before), three starter packs seeded from incidents (python-uv, git-safety incl. ask-before-force-push, secrets-hygiene incl. no tokens into tracked files), README with the 5-minute demo, and a 20-session self-dogfood on the builder's own transcripts (7 sessions/2,062 tool calls already extracted).

Day 13–14: Release 0.1 (pipx), a screenshot-able report, and an issue-tracker landing post on claude-code#75334/#82056, hermes#96704 and microsoft/SkillOpt#155 describing the compile-to-check design and asking for consenting log donors for the study.
roadmap_3_months: Weeks 3–4: Executable rung — sandbox-first replay (git worktree + container; workspace ops re-executed; EXTERNAL/NONDETERMINISTIC served from the recording via PostToolUse updatedToolOutput; late fork preference), incumbent control arm, k-of-n confirmation, tri-state outcomes, PACE-style 'worse' e-process with CTHS spend, per-exam budget caps and circuit breaker; `precedent exam run --candidate model:<id>` becomes the headline feature ('your new model breaks 3 of your rules').

Weeks 4–5: Miner v1 — human-labeled calibration set (500 user turns from consenting donors + the builder's own), reported precision/recall per detector, optional cheap-model classifier arm; confirmation/revert/CI-verdict mining; scope inference (project vs global).

Weeks 5–6: Hermes adapter — shell pre_tool_call enforcer, pending-queue reviewer with precedent-cited dispositions, curator reconciliation, ledger/.usage.json reader, receipts; conformance test that a deny actually stops write_file/patch/terminal paths.

Weeks 6–7: OpenClaw plugin — before_tool_call enforcement and the first third-party skill_proposal_evaluate evaluator (fail-closed conversion of own errors to block), ledger ingestion from skill_proposal_changed; DeepSeek Harness — hook-protocol bridge validation plus a native tools/pre-execute + post-execute plugin and zstd session reader.

Weeks 7–8: pi/Prime adapter (tool_call/tool_result; refinements graded before apply with diff-before-apply) and the Reef recipe (evaluate/decide with per-check verdicts; feedback ingestion); Codex PostToolUse enforcer.

Weeks 8–9: Judged rung (cross-family, 2-of-3, arm-blinded, null floor from incumbent-vs-incumbent) as report-only; lifecycle v1 — override-driven demotion, evasion detection and re-docketing, dormancy, case aging/rotation; context-policy migration that measurably shrinks CLAUDE.md.

Weeks 9–10: Bundles — signed precedent packs, quarantine + local birth gate on import, per-project overrides; 8–10 incident-seeded packs (python-uv, git-safety, secrets-hygiene, memory-scope hygiene from Hermes #89963/#416 lint rules, provider-boundary from codex#41711, permission-rule protection from #105921); team mode (shared exam with per-member provenance).

Weeks 10–11: Exports and standards — Harbor task-family export of an exam; acceptance-record profile (in-toto/EEE/OTel fields); `claude plugin eval` grader export polished; conformance suite across the five seams published as a version-pinned matrix.

Weeks 11–12: Study and v1.0 — the consenting-user study (target 15–30 donors across Claude Code and Hermes), interrupted-time-series analysis with control topics, exchange-rate metrics, the model-swap regression experiment, paper draft; v1.0 release with docs, the 5-minute demo video, and a public dataset of anonymized (correction, check, outcome) triples where donors consent.
wildcard.killer_demo: Five minutes on a Claude Code user's own laptop, nothing pre-arranged, no API key needed for the first two minutes. 0:00 — `pipx install precedent && precedent init`. Ten seconds, zero model calls, it reads ~/.claude/projects and prints: 'Found 212 sessions. You corrected the agent 143 times; 31 corrections repeat. Top: use uv not pip (×9), don't run the full test suite, run the file (×7), ask before force-push (×5), stop rewriting my docstrings (×4). 12 of these are already in CLAUDE.md — and were violated in 40% of the sessions where CLAUDE.md loaded. MEMORY.md was truncated in 9 of your last 12 sessions; your six newest corrections never reached the model. 0 of 31 are enforced.' The audience recognizes their own week. 1:00 — `precedent docket`. Three proposed precedents with evidence: 'uv-not-pip: deterministic rewrite on Bash pip install → uv pip install; fires on 9/9 corrected sessions, 1/203 uncorrected (that one was a throwaway venv)'; 'ask-before-force-push: ask on git push --force*; 5/5, 0/203'; 'targeted-tests: rewrite pytest with no path → pytest <last-edited test file>; 7/7, 3/203 — shown as advisory by default because precision is 0.7'. Confirm two with one key each; the third is edited to a narrower regex and confirmed. `precedent hooks install claude-code`; `precedent context sync` removes two now-enforced lines from CLAUDE.md. 2:00 — Live: open Claude Code, ask it to add a dependency. It reaches for pip; the hook rewrites to uv silently and the receipt line at Stop reads 'precedents: eligible 3, fired 1 (rewrite), overridden 0'. Then it tries a force-push; the hook asks; the user declines; nothing to correct, nothing to repeat. 3:00 — `precedent exam run --candidate model:claude-sonnet-5` (or a freshly generated skill from skill-creator). Fourteen eligible cases, thirteen stable (the incumbent's own replays were cached), k=3, externals served from the recordings, cost cap $3. Live table: 'uv-not-pip: candidate violates 3/13 (3,3,2), incumbent 0/13 → FAIL_CONFIRMED; targeted-tests: executable rung, candidate 5/6 vs incumbent 6/6, control floor 6/6, k-of-n 2/3 on case_091 → FAIL_CONFIRMED; docstrings: judged rung, adherence 0.71 vs 0.80, null floor ±0.06 → report only.' Disposition: BLOCK — 'the new model breaks two of your rulings; here are the turns.' Cost line: $1.87, 42 model calls. 4:00 — `precedent report --since 30d`: 'Corrections on enforced topics: 21 → 2 (control topics: 17 → 15). Human cost: 6 confirmations, ~4 minutes. 3 precedents quiet-and-enforced, 1 dormant (never eligible), 1 evasion detected (python -m pip) and re-docketed. CLAUDE.md: 18.4 KB → 11.2 KB. Exam: 37 precedents, 61 stable cases, examiner ran 3 times this month.' Close on the one-liner: every correction you ever gave your agent is now a test that runs on every skill, every memory and every model it will ever use — and you wrote it with six keystrokes.
wildcard.research_contribution: TITLE: 'Every Correction Is a Test: Human-Anchored Criterion Evolution and the Exchange Rate of Grounding in Deployed Self-Improving Agents'. CLAIMS: (C1, compilability and phantom rate) On N ≥ 15 consenting Claude Code and Hermes users' logs (≥ 3,000 sessions), a large fraction of user corrections repeat across sessions (prediction: ≥ 25% of corrections belong to a topic corrected ≥ 2 times) and a majority of repeated topics compile to deterministic or executable checks that pass a fail-on-base / quiet-on-uncorrected birth gate (prediction: ≥ 50% compile rate at ε = 2%), while LLM-proposed checks without a correction anchor are phantoms (fire on zero corrected sessions) at a rate consistent with Phantom Guardrails' 15/60. (C2, enforcement beats advice) Under an interrupted time-series design on each user's own log with control topics (corrected topics the user chose not to compile), enforced precedents reduce the per-topic correction rate substantially more than advisory CLAUDE.md rules for the same topics (prediction: ≥ 60% relative reduction vs ≤ 20% for advisory), and adherence to advisory rules decays with trajectory length (Lin et al.'s .52→.13 pattern) while enforced checks do not by construction; CLAUDE.md size falls as rules migrate to the exam. (C3, the human anchor has measurable value) Checks confirmed by a human keystroke are more discriminative on held-out corrected sessions (temporal split) than unconfirmed LLM-drafted checks admitted by an LLM judge (prediction: precision ≥ 0.9 vs ≤ 0.7 at matched recall), and the measured exchange rate — human-seconds of confirmation per avoided correction and per enforced invariant — falls below one minute per avoided correction within 30 days. (C4, the private exam catches what outcome gates miss) On model swaps and on LLM-authored skills/memories from real loops (Hermes background review, Claude auto-memory, skill-creator, SkillOpt-Sleep), per-check exam failures are frequent and deterministic (prediction: ≥ 30% of swaps/candidates violate ≥ 1 active precedent on a stable case) while the same candidates' outcome deltas on the users' own terminal checks sit inside the incumbent's self-replay noise floor — i.e. the criterion detects regressions that capability metrics cannot, at ≤ 10% of the outcome-gate's evaluation cost. EXPERIMENT: donor logs → mining with a human-labeled 500-turn calibration set (inter-annotator agreement reported); compile with the birth gate; randomized per-user assignment of compiled topics to enforced vs advisory-only arms for 30 days (with never-compiled control topics); model-swap and candidate exams with k = 3 replays, incumbent control arms, tri-state outcomes; cross-family judged rung reported but never gating; all costs logged. BASELINES: CLAUDE.md-only advisory rules (the claude-reflect / claude-smart / Kiro Crew compile target); Hermes memory/skill loop and Claude auto-memory as-shipped; LLM-self-authored checks without human confirmation (SEA ALG8 / CoEvoSkills-style); outcome-only paired gates (strict held-out, PACE-only) on the same candidates; no-precedent control topics. FALSIFIERS (any one kills the thesis): (F1) repeated corrections are rare or idiosyncratic — compile rate < 20% or ≥ 50% of admitted checks are one-off task facts rather than policy; (F2) enforced checks do not reduce correction rates beyond advisory rules once control-topic drift is subtracted, or overrides/evasions exceed 30% of fires (the constraints are wrong more often than right); (F3) human confirmation adds no discriminative power over an LLM judge admitting LLM-drafted checks (the keystroke is theater); (F4) exam failures on model swaps/candidates do not correspond to user-visible regressions (validated by donors rating a sample of flagged turns), i.e. the criterion is brittle rather than meaningful; (F5) the evasion arms race is unbounded — the same topic needs > 3 revisions per quarter. Reporting follows the emerging RSI checklist: multi-period results with variance, a held-out criterion the agent cannot rewrite, ablations (mining vs compile vs enforcement), generalization to unselected topics, full cost and human-intervention logs.
wildcard.adoption_path: Stage 0 (value with zero commitment): `precedent init` needs no API key and no hooks; it produces a screenshot-able correction report and the memory-truncation receipt — the two things users of ten issue trackers actually ask for (diff, receipt, 'did it even load'), and the report is inherently shareable ('my agent was corrected 143 times about 31 things'). Stage 1 (enforcement): installing hooks turns the top three repeats into rewrites/asks; the user feels it in the same session and the CLAUDE.md shrinks — invisible until it blocks, loud only on a block, with an override path. Stage 2 (the exam): the first model upgrade or the first generated skill is where `precedent exam run` earns trust — 'your new model breaks 3 of your rulings' is the moment competitors have no answer for. Stage 3 (packs and teams): precedent packs are the ESLint-config of agent behavior — shareable, deterministic, provenance-carrying, locally re-validated; teams adopt the shared exam as executable engineering standards (with per-member provenance), which is the org market without building an org product. Stage 4 (vendors and loops): adapters land where seams already wait — the first third-party OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate evaluator, the dsh evaluator slot via hook-protocol, the Hermes pending-queue reviewer requested in #96704/#416, Reef's evaluate/decide (#356/#447), Prime's diff-before-apply (#684/#1208), and `claude plugin eval` grader export so skill authors ship precedent-conformance in Anthropic's own runner. Why it can reach tens of thousands of stars where gates do not: it is not a gate the user pays for per session — it is free, local, off the hot path, gives a visible artifact on day one, is composable into packs, and its adoption story ('ESLint for your agent, written by your corrections') is one sentence. Why it is defensible against vendors shipping 'corrections → rules' natively: vendors will ship advisory text (the cheap version); the sealed, cross-harness, receipted exam with birth-gate evidence and model-swap grading is the part that needs a neutral home, and the acceptance-record export makes vendor tooling a consumer rather than a competitor. Research credibility comes from the donor study and the public (correction, check, outcome) dataset; community credibility from landing in the trackers that asked for it.

nearest_competitors.name: claude-reflect (1.4k★), ReflexioAI/claude-smart (777★), Kiro Crew (AWS, 3.8k★), ECC continuous-learning instincts (256k★)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: These are the 'corrections → durable lessons' archetype and they all compile into advisory text (CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md lines, preferences, instincts injected above a confidence floor). Advisory text is the artifact class shown to decay in adherence (.52→.13), to bloat (+226%), and to be violated while loaded (claude-code#75334). Precedent compiles corrections into hook-enforced and executable checks with planted ground truth (fail-on-base on corrected sessions, quiet on uncorrected), refuses phantoms, emits load/adherence receipts, retires by exercise, moves rules out of the context window, and uses the resulting exam to grade skills, memories and model swaps — none of which a text-sync tool can do. ECC additionally never sees user prompts (no UserPromptSubmit), so it cannot mine corrections at all.

nearest_competitors.name: Hermes Agent skill_manage / curator / background review (245k★)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Hermes proposes from an LLM reflecting on sessions under a 'be ACTIVE' prompt and accepts on the writing model's judgment; its scanner let 40/40 laundered payloads persist (MLAS), its loop was silently dead for weeks (#95976), and its approval queue rots (#105770). Precedent's proposals come only from human rulings, its checks are human-confirmed and mechanically validated, and it plugs into Hermes as the pre_tool_call enforcer (closing the write_file/patch/terminal bypass in #99729) and as the pending-queue reviewer that grades Hermes' own memory/skill writes against the user's precedents — the reviewer #96704 and #416 asked for.

nearest_competitors.name: Prime Agent /refine (20k★)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Typed, versioned harness_state with before/after snapshots, but acceptance is the refiner's say-so, expectedOutcome is free text never checked, and '/refine is invisible' was closed unfixed. Precedent grades refinements against a user-owned exam before apply, renders the diff users asked for (#684/#1208), and replaces free-text expected outcomes with check ids that actually run.

nearest_competitors.name: DeepSeek Harness (222k★) and its dsh-verify / dsh-verification / dsh-llm-verifier marketplace plugins
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: dsh consciously deferred the evaluator 'until its authority, isolation and provider contract are designed' and its verification plugins check that a claimed-done task is actually done. Precedent supplies the other half — what 'done right' means for this user — as a sealed, human-authorized criterion on tools/pre-execute + post-execute (and runs unchanged today through dsh's hook-protocol bridge for Claude Code hooks.json), answering authority (human docket), isolation (sealed exam), and provider (the examiner).

nearest_competitors.name: OpenClaw Skill Workshop + skill_proposal_evaluate seam (389k★)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A hash-bound, event-ledgered proposal path whose evaluation is a regex scanner, whose evaluators fail open, and whose seam has zero third-party implementations. Precedent ships the first outcome-bearing evaluator on that seam: per-precedent findings with ruleIds, a baseline-comparison decision that blocks on confirmed failures, fail-closed conversion of its own errors, and before_tool_call enforcement — while never authoring skills itself.

nearest_competitors.name: SkillOpt / SkillOpt-Sleep (Microsoft, 17k★)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: A skill optimizer with a strict held-out gate on a small val-slice mean that accepts per-task regressions and was Goodharted by copying judge regexes into the skill (#154/#175); its maintainers want a real-CLI replay backend (#155). Precedent does not optimize skills; it grades SkillOpt's candidates against the user's precedents on the user's cassettes with exactly #155's constraints (disposable worktree, pass/fail/inconclusive, execution off by default), and its judged rung never gates so there is no judge to copy.

nearest_competitors.name: Reef (Human-Agent-Society, 1.3k★)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Release infrastructure with a propose→paired-evaluate→decide contract whose gate is a pooled W/L tally over a tiny task list (#356: seed-suite regressions hidden) and single-episode stochastic verdicts. Precedent is a Reef recipe whose evaluate returns per-check verdicts on a stability-measured corpus and whose decide is 'zero confirmed failures'; Reef feedback receipts become correction events; the exam exports as the Harbor task family #447 wants.

nearest_competitors.name: auto-harness (NeoSigma, 537★) and Self-Harness (Shanghai AI Lab) self-growing regression suites
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Both grow regression suites from tasks that flipped to passing, inside the agent-writable surface (auto-harness's suite, best score and PROGRAM.md are agent-editable) and from benchmark tasks, not human rulings. Precedent's suite is built from what humans corrected, sealed from every agent, cross-harness, receipted, and applied to model swaps and memory writes, not only to harness code.

nearest_competitors.name: PACE (arXiv 2606.08106) and SEA (arXiv 2607.00871)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Statistical acceptance for candidate-vs-incumbent lift, validated on 0.5B–3B prompt edits with no code (PACE) and switched off at ~50 tasks because it admitted nothing (SEA ALG4). Precedent reuses PACE's discordant-pair e-process and SEA's CTHS spend only for the executable rung's 'worse' decision and refuses to certify 'better'; most of its verdicts are deterministic and need no statistics — the asymmetry that keeps it from starving.

nearest_competitors.name: Causal Agent Replay (2606.08275), The Replay Gap (2608.08239), Counterfactual Trace Auditing (2605.11946)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Replay/attribution primitives, not gates: CAR's do-ops and abstain state, the Replay Gap's control arm and late-fork lesson, CTA's null floor and uptake verification are all adopted. Precedent binds them to human criteria (a case is graded on 'did it violate a ruling', not 'did behavior diverge'), which turns divergence from noise into a per-check verdict.

nearest_competitors.name: SafeEvolve / SkillMisevo-Gym (2608.12851), Misevolve
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Safety governance of skill artifacts by an LLM critic with admission/revocation boundaries, costing ~13pp carryover utility and barely beating a static scanner. Precedent treats safety rulings as hard deterministic constraints (ask-before-force-push, no secrets into tracked files, incident-seeded operational canaries) enforced by hooks with no LLM authority, and reuses SafeEvolve's LLM-independent invariant ('a revision may not drop a verification/reversibility requirement its ancestor asserted') as a precedent class when grading memory/skill writes.

nearest_competitors.name: Double Ratchet (2607.12790), CoEvoSkills (COLM 2026), Red Queen Gödel Machine (evaluator co-evolution)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: The evaluator co-evolves via LLM-synthesized detectors/assertions with birth gates and anchors, or via challenger judges replacing incumbents at sparse checkpoints (which does not fire at practical budgets: 0 replacements at 128 outcomes). Precedent's criterion evolves only through human corrections and confirmations, its birth gate uses planted ground truth (corrected sessions) rather than LLM-labelled clusters, and enforcement is live rather than offline — the same problem (criterion evolution without self-confirmation) solved with an exogenous anchor that every deployed agent already produces.

nearest_competitors.name: PROCTOR (2609.02246), HackProbe (2609.04665), Phantom Guardrails (2607.13083), Grounding Agent Memory (2609.11060)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Rules and detectors without a runtime: mechanical-override, probe banks, the phantom-guardrail failure mode, and environment-probing before commit. Precedent implements the mechanical-override ordering as its rung authority, the anti-phantom rule as a hard admission criterion, and environment verification as the executable rung's fail-on-base reproduction — as a shipped, cross-harness tool with receipts.

nearest_competitors.name: Claude Code auto-memory and `claude plugin eval` (Anthropic)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: Auto-memory is 'context, not enforced configuration' with no acceptance seam and known truncation failures (#82056/#92998); plugin eval is a sealed with/without runner with per-case thresholds and a haiku judge but no source of user-meaningful graders. Precedent supplies the load receipts memory lacks, grades memory writes against precedents, and exports precedents as plugin-eval graders, using the eval runner as one sealed examiner backend.

nearest_competitors.name: The acceptance-layer, sealed-evaluator and gate-benchmark stances (CI/CD-for-agents layers, Hermetic-class receipt runtimes, acceptor benchmarks)
nearest_competitors.how_we_differ: They decide whether an agent's artifact is admissible or improved and measure how well gates decide; each needs an evaluator the user cares about and each sources it from benchmark tasks or the session's own terminal tests. Precedent is upstream of all of them: it is where a user-owned, non-stationary, receipted criterion comes from, it never claims capability lift, and it emits the acceptance-record profile they consume — complement, not rival.

risks: Corrections may be rarer or more idiosyncratic than assumed: if most corrections are one-off task facts rather than policy, compile rate collapses (falsifier F1) and the product degrades to a report; mitigation is to measure this on the builder's own 212 sessions in week 1 and pivot the packs toward incident-seeded invariants if repeats are scarce.

Deterministic checks cover only a slice of what users correct (tool-input patterns, file state, ordering); the long tail is judged-rung only, which we refuse to enforce — users may feel the tool is toothless on the corrections they care most about.

False positives and over-constraint: a hook that denies or rewrites can block legitimate work, make the agent worse at problem solving, or ossify a workflow after the project changes; mitigations are the precision floor with counts, ask-not-deny defaults for low-precision rules, one-line override with capture, override-driven demotion, and evasion tracking — but the user experience of a wrong deny is loud by design.
Evasion arms race: the agent may route around a mechanical check (python -m pip, aliases, subshells); if topics need many revisions the criterion never stabilizes (falsifier F5).

Mining accuracy: correction detection from transcripts without model calls is heuristic; false 'corrections' produce noisy topics and false 'quiet' sessions inflate precision; requires the labeled calibration set and honest per-detector precision/recall in the report.

Replay fidelity: the executable rung depends on git-snapshot sandboxes and recorded externals; The Replay Gap and the builder's own measurement say divergence is the norm, so many cases will be INCONCLUSIVE; browser/API/OS sessions get no executable rung at all.

Privacy and secrets: transcripts contain credentials and private code; everything must stay local, be scrubbed before any model call, and bundles must never carry session content — one leak incident would end adoption.

Harness API drift: Claude Code hooks, OpenClaw's evaluator envelope, Hermes internals and dsh pre-release APIs change fast (Hermes 947 commits in four days; dsh 14 tags in 12 days); the conformance suite must be version-pinned and re-run per release.

Vendor pre-emption: Anthropic/OpenAI/Nous could ship 'corrections → rules' natively; the defensible core (sealed cross-harness exam, receipts, model-swap grading, packs) must be visible early or the project reads as a feature.

Attribution is observational: interrupted time series on a user's own log with control topics cannot separate 'the check worked' from 'the user changed behavior'; claims must stay modest or reviewers will reject C2.

Approval fatigue in a new guise: if the weekly docket is noisy, users stop confirming; expiry and default dispositions help, but the compile rate must be high-precision or the docket becomes the rotting queue we set out to avoid.

Scope for a 1–3 person team: five harness adapters plus an executable replay engine plus a study is a lot; the mitigation is a strict Claude-Code-first MVP with adapters gated on demand signals from the trackers.
open_questions: What fraction of real corrections are policy (repeatable, compilable) versus task facts, and does this differ between Claude Code, Hermes chat-gateway users and teams? (Answerable in week 1 on the builder's own logs; decisive for the whole thesis.)
What is the right admission threshold on the birth gate (ε for false fires, minimum corrected sessions) and how should it scale with corpus size to keep both phantom rate and false-deny rate low?

Should any judged-rung precedent ever gate, and if so under what independence conditions (cross-family judge, calibrated false-pass estimate below the Blind Curator cliff) — or is 'compile down or stay advisory' the permanent rule?
How should scope be inferred and enforced (project vs global vs path), and how are conflicting precedents from different team members or different projects resolved without an LLM merge?

Does moving rules out of the context window into enforcement change agent behavior in unintended ways (e.g. the agent no longer explains a constraint it never sees), and should a minimal 'why this was rewritten' message be injected on each fire?
How does the exchange rate of grounding evolve over time — does the human-seconds-per-avoided-correction curve flatten (saturation) or keep falling (compounding), and does it differ by rung?
Can the model-swap exam predict which user-visible regressions a new model causes well enough to recommend per-user upgrade timing, and how many stable cases are needed for a trustworthy verdict?
What is the correct case-aging policy for a non-stationary corpus — when does a cassette stop representing the user's work, and can eligibility drift be detected automatically?

How should imported team bundles be re-validated when the importer has few or no corrected sessions on that topic (no fail-on-base evidence locally) — trust the source's provenance, require a local trial period as advisory, or both?

Is there a principled way to convert corrections into executable checks for non-coding agents (browser, API, OS) where the terminal verification is not re-executable — e.g. state assertions over recorded observations?

Which acceptance-record fields do external gates and standards bodies (in-toto agent-decision, OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result, EEE) actually need from an exam report so that the profile is adopted rather than becoming a 13th format?

Does the presence of enforced precedents change what the user corrects next (the correction distribution shifts toward the long tail), and how should the miner and the study account for that feedback?
