ci-for-rsi.lens: INFLUENCE: 10k+ stars and/or citation by the next RSI survey; timing vs the RSI wave, first 100 users, 5-minute demo, vendor adopt/copy/crush, composition with OpenClaw/DSH/Claude Code/Reef, crispness of the paper claim, coverage of the surveys' open problems. Score = expected influence.
ci-for-rsi.justification: Pawl is the right shape at the right moment: the acceptor-is-the-weak-link finding is three months old (PACE June, SEA July, HarnessDev Sept 1, RSI-Exam Aug 26), all five surveys ask for a runnable gated-update reference and none ships code, and every seam Pawl registers in is real and currently empty (verified today: OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate has no non-fork implementer; Reef #356, SkillOpt #155, Hermes RFC #96704 and claude-code #82056 are all open and asking for exactly these mechanisms). The demo's first 60 seconds (backfill 200 sessions, zero model calls: 'memory truncated in 9/12 sessions, 5 skills never loaded, 1 contradicted in 12, $2.14') is the best star-moment in the three designs and the 'ties are free' eligibility trick plus asymmetric dispositions are a genuine, citable answer to SEA's starvation. So the ceiling is high: a citation in the next RSI survey is likely (roughly 60%) if a repo, a benchmark and a workshop paper exist by December. But expected influence is dragged down by execution and pull. The plan schedules thirteen components, seven adapters, three standards filings, a Harbor benchmark, a ledger re-analysis and a paper in twelve weeks for 1-3 people, while its own risk section says at most three adapters can be kept conformance-green; the 'API-level works, plumbing-level breaks' death it diagnoses for SkillClaw is the median outcome of this schedule. The 2-week MVP puts the hardest unsolved piece (sandbox-first served-external replay with divergence detection and DSSE receipts) on days 8-10 on the strength of 7 measured sessions. The star-generating half (receipts, feed, undo, spend) is exactly what Anthropic, OpenClaw and Nous can ship natively in one release (Anthropic already shipped plugin eval on Sept 11 and #82056 has 48 comments), and the same wedge has been shipped by small projects with zero traction (agmem 2 stars, claude-md-lint 0 stars), consistent with the analysts' finding that adoption is anti-correlated with gating. Paper claim (1) also leans on held-out outcomes that the published ledgers mostly lack (AHE has no held-out split, Meta-Harness search set equals report set, HarnessDev's 73 versions are unreleased). Net: probability of 10k stars about 10-15%, of a survey citation about 60%, of one or two upstream PRs landing (SkillOpt #155, OpenClaw evaluator listing) about 50%. That is a solid 6, not higher, until the scope is cut to what the team can keep working.

fatal_flaws: Scope is roughly three times what 1-3 people can keep working: 13 components, 7 adapters (Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, DSH, pi/Prime, Reef, SkillOpt-Sleep, Codex), three standards filings, a Harbor benchmark, an offline ledger re-analysis and a paper in 12 weeks, while the design's own risk section concedes a team this size keeps at most three adapters conformance-green and Hermes shipped 947 commits in four days. The predicted failure is the one it names for SkillClaw: works at the API level, breaks at the plumbing level, and a tool that is broken on the harness the user runs gets uninstalled before it gets starred.

The 2-week MVP schedules the hardest unsolved piece (sandbox-first replay with externals served via updatedToolOutput, first-divergence detection, incumbent self-replay noise floor, DSSE score receipts) on days 8-10, on the strength of 7 measured sessions from one machine. The fraction of real sessions replayable to a terminal check and the incumbent stability distribution are both admitted open questions; if they come out low the 'gate' is lint + DLP + undo with a statistical veneer, which is fine for users but not a survey-citable acceptance layer.

The star-generating half (load receipts, change feed, undo, spend meter) is the half vendors can and will ship natively: Anthropic released plugin eval on Sept 11 and claude-code #82056 (memory loaded/truncated) has 48 comments; OpenClaw owns the Workshop and can add a default evaluator; Nous can land RFC #96704 in-tree. The design's defensibility (cross-harness coverage, neutral record profile, acceptor benchmark) is exactly the part that needs the most maintenance and that users do not ask for.

The wedge has no demonstrated pull: agmem ('Git for AI agent memories') sits at 2 stars, three claude-md-lint projects at 0, rsi-exam-provenance at 2, and the analysts' own finding is that adoption is anti-correlated with gating. A tool designed to be 'invisible until it blocks' has one star-moment (the backfill report); the design does not explain what makes a user come back, share, or star it after that morning.

Paper claim (1), the headline number (>40% of accepted edits rejected as noise and the rejected set containing the majority of held-out regressions), requires held-out per-task outcomes that the published ledgers mostly do not contain: AHE evolved on the tasks it reports, Meta-Harness's TB2 search set equals its report set, HarnessDev's 73 versions and trajectories are unreleased, Self-Harness's held-out split participates in its gate. The re-analysis is likely to shrink to PACE-on-SkillOpt-evidence.jsonl-and-AHE-manifests, a workshop note rather than a survey-anchoring result.

The statistical story is oversold relative to what any theorem covers, and this is the audience (AI2/UW, PACE, SEA, agentdescent) most likely to review it: cassette reuse across candidates is uncovered dependence, tasks arrive non-exchangeably from a drifting user, ADMIT_PROVISIONAL admits on 'no evidence of harm after 8 pairs or $0.50', and 'governance-grade' is claimed for a record whose error guarantees are per-candidate. One sharp review that says 'this is a monitored deploy with an e-value attached' costs the RSI-workshop credibility the plan depends on.

The paper's online experiment (>=200 cassettes from >=5 volunteers) needs people to hand over raw coding sessions containing code and secrets to a v0.1 scrubber; the design lists privacy as a worse-than-any-regression incident but ships no share-evidence-not-sessions mode, so part (2) of the paper is likely to be n=1 (the builder's own machine).
improvements: Cut v0.1 to one deep adapter (Claude Code, the builder's own data) plus one upstream landing chosen for cheapness and visibility (the SkillOpt #155 AgenticReplayBackend, whose maintainers already endorsed the contract, or the OpenClaw evaluator stub); consume Hermes only through the pending-queue reader and ledger, no pre_tool_call enforcement until month 3. Publish a supported/unsupported conformance matrix in the README so breakage is visible instead of silent.

Re-sequence the MVP so weeks 1-2 ship only the zero-model-call layer (receipts, feed, undo with verified round trip, lint + DLP, spend meter, funnel alarms) and the launch artifact is the backfill report run on 5-10 real machines with the aggregate numbers posted; move sealed replay to month 2 behind a published replayability measurement (fraction of sessions with a terminal check, incumbent k/k stability distribution, divergence-point histogram). That measurement is paper part (2) in embryo and is worth a short arXiv note on its own.

Make the star-moment recurring rather than one-time: a weekly digest with a single headline stat per user, and an opt-in anonymized public 'null-effect board' (share of skills never loaded, share of memory truncated, share of self-writes that were no-ops, dollars per accepted edit) that people screenshot. This is the same data as the audit, costs nothing, and gives the RSI audience a live dataset.

Design for pre-emption instead of against it: file the load-receipt schema as a proposal on claude-code #82056 and OpenClaw's Workshop docs now, and structure the Claude Code adapter so that when Anthropic ships native InstructionsLoaded/truncation receipts Pawl consumes them (adapter reads the harness's own receipt) rather than re-deriving them. Position Pawl as the cross-harness ledger and gate that vendors' native receipts feed, which is the part a vendor has no incentive to build.

Split the research contribution into two honest papers: (a) 'Sessions as cassettes': replayability, incumbent stability, divergence-point distribution and the eligibility-partition cost model on real Claude Code/Hermes sessions (measurable in month 1); (b) the acceptor benchmark on Harbor plus re-analysis restricted to ledgers that actually carry per-task outcomes (SkillOpt-Sleep evidence.jsonl, AHE manifests + git, Meta-Harness summaries), stating plainly which held-out quantities are missing. Drop the '>40%' target until data supports it; report the confusion matrix with intervals.

Downgrade the statistical language and upgrade the empirical one: call ADMIT_PROVISIONAL 'monitored deploy', report empirical false-commit rate under cassette reuse and non-stationarity from the benchmark instead of implying validity, and put harm-detection latency after provisional admission (pairs and dollars to first BLOCK on a planted regression) on the first page. That is the number that persuades the PACE/SEA audience the asymmetry is a gate and not a bypass.

Collapse the vocabulary for the README: three user-visible states (blocked, watching, verified) with HOLD and NOT_ACTIVATED rendered as reasons, one sentence ('CI for the state your agent writes to itself'), one name (commit to Pawl; a README that lists eight candidates reads as unfinished), and defer all three standards filings until a registry or vendor asks for the profile.

Ship a 'share evidence, not sessions' mode before recruiting volunteers: contributors export only receipts, eligibility, divergence steps, tri-state outcomes and verdict hashes, never transcripts; add a cassette scrubber with a published false-negative test set. This unblocks the >=5-volunteer experiment and removes the incident risk the design itself rates worst.

Add a first-run cost fuse that is stricter than the daily cap: in the first week the sealed evaluator may run only on cassettes with an observed-stable incumbent and only up to a per-store $1 budget, and the digest states the budget consumed; the corpus shows loops that surprise the user with a bill get switched off within a week, and Pawl's first hundred users will judge it on the first bill.
ci-for-rsi.best_idea_to_steal: Activation-eligibility partitioning driven by deterministic load receipts: compute, before any model call, whether an artifact could even have loaded in each recorded session (resolved store, hash, bytes loaded vs available, complete/truncated/not_loaded/wrong_store), treat every ineligible session as a tie at zero cost, and turn 'never eligible anywhere' into a diagnosis (NOT_ACTIVATED: truncated index, wrong store, description outside the matcher window) rather than an evaluation. It is the mechanism that makes an honest paired gate affordable (the e-process learns only from discordant pairs, so the majority of no-op production edits are decided for free), it produces the single most shareable line of the demo ('1 never activated, here is the line that overflowed'), it works with no learning loop at all (hand-written CLAUDE.md users), and it composes with every other design in this space (a null-effect audit, a sealed-scorer receipt, a vendor's native eval) because it is a property of the session log, not of the gate.

ci-for-rsi.lens: FEASIBILITY — 1-3 people, API models only, no GPUs, 3 months to a credible v1 that can run the specified killer demo. Every technical assumption checked against the official Claude Code hooks/plugin-eval/memory docs, the OpenClaw/DSH/Hermes source trees (gh contents API), the public repos the re-analysis paper depends on, the builder's own tool scripts and local session corpus, and a re-computation of the gate's statistics and replay cost.
ci-for-rsi.justification: The observe-only half of Pawl (watcher, change feed, load receipts, undo, lint/DLP, spend meter, funnel alarms, the OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate stub) is buildable by 1-2 people in about a month on seams I verified exist: Claude Code ships InstructionsLoaded, FileChanged, PreToolUse permissionDecision/updatedInput and PostToolUse updatedToolOutput; OpenClaw exposes skill_proposal_evaluate with pass|revise|block (src/skills/workshop/plugin-hooks.ts, hook-skill.types.ts) and defaults to autonomous.mode auto; Hermes has ~/.hermes/pending/{memory,skills}/<id>.json staging with replay-on-approve, a fail_closed pre_tool_call shell hook, and the skill_provenance ContextVar; the cited issues (#95976, #82056, SkillOpt#155, reef#356) are real and open. That is not what the score measures. The score is the probability the specified demo ships: backfill hundreds of sessions, intercept a live Hermes review, run a sealed sandbox evaluation against cached incumbent self-replays on eligible cassettes, BLOCK on a confirmed 2/2 regression for $0.31, undo, weekly report, and a cosign-verifiable record on the OpenClaw board. Against that bar the design fails on substrate, on engineering, and on its own statistics. Substrate: the builder's machine holds 8 Claude Code transcripts, 7 with tool calls and 0 containing any test/build/lint command, so there is not one cassette with a terminal check to dogfood the primary signal; Hermes and OpenClaw are not installed; the "verified on 2.1.258, $0.007/replay" claim rests on a two-line hooklog (scratchpad/replay-test/hooklog.jsonl) in which one `uptime` Bash call had its output replaced by a sentinel in a fresh session — no fork-point resume, no worktree, no container, no WebFetch/WebSearch serving, no multi-turn. Engineering: sandbox-first re-execution of the session's own pytest needs the project toolchain inside a network-sealed container that must still reach the model API with isolated credentials; nothing in the plan reconstructs environments, so most terminal checks will be "inconclusive" and the gate will HOLD by default, reproducing the SEA/hermes#105770 starvation the design promises to avoid; the DSH hooks-claude-code bridge explicitly does not honor updatedInput or updatedToolOutput and drops 23 of 30 events, so "one adapter covers three harnesses" is true only for deny; `claude plugin eval` (needs 2.1.269; builder has 2.1.258) strips CLAUDE.md, memory, hooks and skills from the child, so it can evaluate plugin-packaged skills only, never the memory/rules artifacts the thesis calls "the most-deployed and least-gated class"; Hermes' shell-hook stdin payload is {hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, session_id, cwd, extra} with no write origin, so origin-scoped blocking needs an in-process plugin. Statistics: under the CTHS schedule the per-candidate alpha is 2.6e-4 at the 10th candidate and 6.9e-6 at the 100th (wealth 3,900 and 144,000); the mixture bet grows ~1.5x per discordant pair, so VERIFIED needs ~18 consecutive discordant-better pairs with zero discordant-worse against 6-20 eligible cassettes — it is decorative; the harm e-process at a flat alpha 0.10 needs 6 consecutive discordant-worse pairs, so in the demo's 6-cassette case BLOCK comes entirely from the per-task k-of-n floor, whose benign false-block rate is 14-25% at per-task pass 0.9 (20-40 protected tasks) and 34-56% at 0.8, while "incumbent 3/3 = protected" mislabels a p=0.8 task half the time. Cost: a replay run is $0.2-1 on Sonnet and $1-5 on Opus for 5-30 re-executed turns; the control arm (k=2-3 over every cassette) is invalidated by every model_served change and every accepted artifact that changes the incumbent tree, so $0.31/gate and $2.14/week hold only with Sonnet, late forks, and a rarely-refreshed baseline. Research claim (1) has no data: Meta-Harness publishes no evolution_summary runs, AHE publishes only a change-manifest schema, Self-Harness has no official repo, HarnessDev's 73 versions are unreleased, and SkillOpt's own evalkit doc states "Per-task pairs were not published." Scope: 8 adapters, 12 subsystems, four standards filings, a Harbor benchmark, a ledger re-analysis and a paper in 12 weeks, with a 2-week MVP that lists 10 subsystems including containerized sealed-eval — against Hermes shipping 947 commits in four days and DSH at v0.1.5-rc with declared breaking changes. A credible reduced v1 (observe layer + lint + undo + receipts + OpenClaw plugin + a Claude-Code-only late-fork regression detector) is likely (~0.6); the demo as written is not (~0.2).

Hermes and OpenClaw are not installed locally either.

Sandbox-first re-execution is unengineered: the session's own `pytest -q` must run in a git-worktree+container with no network, yet the agent inside must reach the model API with isolated credentials and the project's toolchain/deps (venv, node_modules) are not in a git snapshot. Without per-project environment specs most terminal checks are 'inconclusive', every candidate HOLDs, and the gate starves exactly like SEA ALG4 and hermes#105770; SkillOpt#155's constraints forbid the only cheap alternative (host worktree with real credentials).

The 'verified replay backend' is one served tool call: scratchpad/replay-test/hooklog.jsonl contains a single `uptime` PreToolUse/PostToolUse pair with a sentinel substitution in a fresh session. Fork-point resume from a truncated transcript, worktree routing via updatedInput, serving WebFetch/WebSearch/gh results, PostToolUseFailure handling, and multi-turn divergence detection are all unverified; under DSH's bridge updatedInput/updatedToolOutput are documented as unsupported, and `claude plugin eval` strips memory/CLAUDE.md/hooks so it cannot evaluate the memory and rules artifacts the thesis targets.

The statistical core is mis-tuned for a personal candidate stream: CTHS gives per-candidate alpha 2.6e-4 at k=10 and 6.9e-6 at k=100 (wealth 3,900 / 144,000) while the mixture bet grows ~1.5x per discordant pair, so VERIFIED needs ~18 consecutive discordant-better pairs against 6-20 eligible cassettes and never fires; the harm e-process at flat alpha 0.10 needs 6 straight discordant-worse pairs, so BLOCK in practice is the per-task k-of-n floor alone, whose benign false-block rate is 14-25% at per-task pass 0.9 with 20-40 protected tasks (34-56% at 0.8), and 'incumbent 3/3 = protected' mislabels a p=0.8 task 51% of the time. The advertised asymmetry is really 'one flaky task can block'.

Research claim (1) has no data: stanford-iris-lab/meta-harness publishes no evolution_summary.jsonl runs, china-qijizhifeng/agentic-harness-engineering publishes only change-manifest-schema.json and example manifests, Self-Harness has no official repository, HarnessDev's 73 versions and 26,679 trajectories are unreleased, and SkillOpt's evalkit.md states 'Per-task pairs were not published'. Only community autoresearch results.tsv (single-run scalar per commit) exists, which supports a noise-floor note, not a paired re-analysis.

Cost model is 5-20x optimistic: one replay run is ~$0.2-1 (Sonnet) or ~$1-5 (Opus) for 5-30 re-executed turns; the cached control arm (k=2-3 over every cassette) is invalidated by every model_served change and by every accepted artifact that changes the incumbent tree; on Max plans `claude -p` replays burn the usage window the design itself cites as the loop-killer (claude-code#71633). '$0.31 per gate, $2.14 per week' holds only with Sonnet, late forks and a baseline that is almost never refreshed.

Scope is 3-5x the team: 8 adapters (Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, DSH, pi/Prime, Reef, SkillOpt-Sleep, Codex), 12 subsystems, DSSE/cosign signing, in-toto/OTel/EEE/agentskills filings, a Harbor benchmark, a ledger re-analysis and a paper in 12 weeks; the 2-week MVP lists ~10 subsystems including containerized sealed-eval and a gate library with a reproduced power table. The design's own risk section concedes at most three adapters can stay conformance-green, but the roadmap keeps all eight; Hermes ships ~950 commits per 4 days and DSH is at v0.1.5-rc with declared breaking changes.

Hermes origin-scoped enforcement as specified cannot be done from the shell seam: agent/shell_hooks.py serializes {hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, session_id, cwd, extra} with no write origin, so 'pre_tool_call fail-closed by background_review origin' requires an in-process plugin via ctx.register_hook, and fail_closed defaults to false and applies only to pre_tool_call.

The behavioral canary is mis-costed: 30-100 domain probes 'paired incumbent vs candidate' are agentic tasks (SkillMisevo shows harm materializes in fresh-session execution, not stated intent), i.e. 60-200 agent runs per candidate in the same sandbox that does not exist yet, not '50-100 model calls'.
improvements: Re-sequence to ship 'pawl-observe' first and make it the v1 demo: fs watcher + change feed with writer origin, session load receipts computed from file state at SessionStart plus the documented 200-line/25KB MEMORY.md rule and InstructionsLoaded for CLAUDE.md/rules, whole-bundle snapshot + `undo --session`, deterministic lint/DLP with `allow --once`, spend meter from transcripts, funnel/starvation alarms. Claude Code only. No cassettes, sandbox or statistics required; every line of the demo's minute 0 and minute 4 survives.

Solve the corpus problem before touching the gate: (a) recruit 3-5 volunteers with test-heavy Claude Code repos (the hermes#96704 and SkillOpt#155 threads have willing contributors), and (b) mine each volunteer repo's own test suite into a synthetic protected corpus (SWE-smith-style task = 'make failing test X pass') so the terminal check is reproducible in a container by construction; treat recorded sessions as the secondary, opportunistic corpus.

Replace sandbox-first replay in v1 with two cheap signals: (1) A-vs-A' divergence-only replay at the LAST verification point via `claude -p --resume` on a truncated transcript in a git worktree with tools restricted to reads and served externals (no terminal check, reports divergence step vs incumbent self-divergence); (2) for skills with scripts/, a container smoke test (compile, --help, forbidden-command scan). Gate the full terminal-check sandbox behind an explicit per-project environment spec (devcontainer.json/Dockerfile present) and defer it to month 3.

Fix the decision rule: drop CTHS for per-store personal streams and use a per-candidate alpha with cassette rotation; make the harm alpha explicitly outside any spending schedule; report VERIFIED as an e-value plus 'N better / 0 worse over M sessions' rather than a certified claim; protect a task only on a Beta posterior lower bound (e.g., ≥5 incumbent passes or P(pass) LCB > 0.9) instead of 3/3; put the benign false-block rate in the verdict schema and in every report next to the cost line.

Cut adapters to two plus one library: Claude Code (own harness), the OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate plugin in lint + deterministic-canary + baseline-comparison mode (fail-closed conversion), and `pawl.decide` as a pure-Python Reef policy. Keep Hermes read-only in v1 (ingest skill_ledger JSONL and the pending queue for the feed; post verdicts through /skills approve|reject); drop DSH, pi/Prime, Codex and SkillOpt-Sleep PRs from the 3-month plan.

Replace paper claim (1) with two claims you can actually run: the null-effect/activation audit on volunteers' stores (the activation arm needs zero model calls and answers hermes#96704 directly) and the acceptor benchmark on Harbor with PACE's 'planted improvement among noise' and 'no-real-gain' regimes plus SkillMisevo payloads; cite HarnessDev's skipped counterfactual as motivation, and add a noise-floor re-analysis of community autoresearch results.tsv only as a side note.

Budget the gate honestly and print it: fork only at the last verification point, cap the control arm at k=2 over ≤20 eligible cassettes, key control arms by (cassette, model_served) rather than incumbent tree hash and treat incumbent changes to non-eligible artifacts as ties, default to a Sonnet-class model for replay with an Opus re-check only on discordant pairs, and expose `--max-usd` per candidate exactly like plugin eval's --max-cost-usd.

Make the behavioral canary deterministic-only in v1 (secrets, destructive commands, egress, permission-rule deletion, scope-tag leaks, placeholder-as-verified, missing referenced files, environment-contradiction probes); ship the 40-probe agentic canary as a month-3 opt-in with its per-candidate cost shown and a measured false-block rate on the user's own benign edits.

Drop DSSE/cosign/in-toto/OTel/EEE from v1: emit one content-addressed JSONL record per stage with a `pawl verify <record>` command that recomputes hashes; file the standards profiles only after two external adopters exist.

Never let HOLD be silent: the first line of every digest must be pending count and oldest-pending age; holds expire into a stated policy default recorded in the ledger; the OpenClaw plugin must map its own timeouts to `block` only when the store is in block mode and to `revise` with a reason otherwise, since the seam fails open.
ci-for-rsi.best_idea_to_steal: Activation-eligibility partitioning computed from deterministic load receipts before any model call: for each recorded session, decide from the receipt (resolved store path and hash, bytes available vs loaded, complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store, tool_use:Skill / InstructionsLoaded evidence) whether the candidate artifact could have loaded at all; sessions where it could not are ties at $0, a candidate that loads nowhere gets NOT_ACTIVATED with a diagnosis instead of an evaluation, and the same receipt doubles as the user-facing 'did my memory/skill actually reach the model' answer that claude-code#82056, prime#1208 and Lin et al.'s 25% load rate show is the most common real failure. It is cheap, harness-agnostic, uses data already on disk, and makes the expensive gate run only where it can possibly matter.

ci-for-rsi.lens: NOVELTY vs the landscape and RSI prior art, weighted by 12-month defensibility against Hermes / OpenClaw / DSH / Reef / SkillOpt / Anthropic shipping weekly. Method: read rsi_digest.md, landscape_digest.md (Reef/SkillOpt/Prime/Hermes/ECC/OpenViking/SkillClaw/AHE/Self-Harness/pi-autoresearch/HGM entries), synthesis_v1/v2, both gap analyses; 21 gh repo searches + 2 gh code searches + 8 name-candidate searches; 15 WebSearch queries; README/issue fetches for every close hit (airlock, pawl, skillci, self-evolve, rsi-exam-provenance, EvoUndo, agnix, stalebrain, openclaw-mem, cc-skill-usage, lamarck, harness-tuner, SENTRY, Reef#356, SkillOpt#155, hermes#96704).
ci-for-rsi.justification: Pawl is the most complete integration document in this design set, but under a novelty lens roughly 80% of it is recombination of published mechanisms and the remaining 20% is over-claimed. Its own 'genuinely new' list decomposes as follows. (1) Activation-eligibility partitioning as a statistical-cost lever (ties at $0 before any model call) is the one idea I could not find implemented anywhere; but it was independently proposed in the hermes#96704 RFC thread on 2026-09-03 ('separate the attribution chain per task: eligible...'), Lin et al./CTA/plugin-eval already treat load-as-precondition, and it collapses for the most-deployed artifact class (CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md load in 212/212 sessions per Pawl's own demo, so zero ties). (2) 'Incumbent self-replay as noise floor + protected corpus by observed stability' is The Replay Gap's control arm plus AI2's stable_pass/stable_fail/unstable task classes plus Reef#356's protected-seed-suite proposal, relocated onto user sessions. (3) The asymmetric verdict/disposition set uses Thru-Echoes/rsi-exam-provenance's exact vocabulary (verdict clears/below/inconclusive vs disposition keep/revert/provisional, freeze-then-confirm, digest-bound record, host-side shadow audit; in your own digest) plus MGM's provisional admission, SEA's HOLD/NSF and RSEA's asymmetric gate; none cited in the design. (4) The Replay-Gap 'middle case' for harness edits is genuinely unmeasured and is the real paper. (5) Incident-seeded canaries with a held-out rotating subset is HackProbe's secret-core + rotated-layer probe bank (2609.04665) plus stalebrain's live-repo contradiction audit; the incident taxonomy is good product work, not IP. (6) One content hash joining event/receipt/evidence/verdict/snapshot is OpenClaw's hash-bound proposal + Hermes's sha256 ledger + novafabric's signed capsules; correct engineering, not novelty. Meanwhile the adoption wedge (feed, receipts, undo, lint, spend) is already commoditized: agnix (413 stars) lints CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/SKILL.md/hooks/MCP with 456 rules and a GitHub Action, ten SKILL.md linters exist, cc-skill-usage backfills skill activation from ~/.claude transcripts exactly as the killer demo's 'never loaded in 60 days' line does, EvoUndo (paper + PyPI) ships selective rollback with pre-state witnesses, openclaw-mem ships memory governance with receipts and rollback, and Anthropic already improved the MEMORY.md truncation warning in September. The 'CI for the state your agent writes to itself' framing is occupied: xdlc-labs/airlock v1.0 (Sept 10, v1.0.2 Sept 14) is literally 'CI release gate for AI agents' with snapshot/diff/blast-radius, CI-interval gates that never fire on point estimates, PASS/NEEDS_APPROVAL/INCONCLUSIVE, an approval ledger and a GitHub Action; skillci is 'CI for Claude Skills'. Worse, the name 'Pawl' is taken in the same domain by a Shopware-backed 68-star repo using the identical ratchet metaphor for agent-work verification, and 'Airlock' is taken by the closest competitor. What remains defensible for 12 months is the runtime write-path gate on the user's own recorded sessions across harnesses, the sealed evaluator with score receipts, the acceptor benchmark and the ledger re-analysis; that combination has no incumbent, but the theory now exists (Safe Harness Self-Evolution 2609.08175 gives the finite-data bounds; Auditing Harness Tampering 2609.00069 gives the tampering taxonomy and seeded corpus), the seams are two-week gaps any contributor can fill (OpenClaw evaluator seam, Reef#356, SkillOpt#155 draft-PR invitation), and SENTRY's published negative result (a fixed threshold beat its anytime-valid e-process on agent action streams) warns that the e-process branding may be ornament for a BLOCK decided by 1-3 confirmed task flips. Net: one new lever, one new measurement, a strong join, several uncited near-duplicates, a burned name, and a commoditized wedge -> 5/10.

fatal_flaws: Name and tagline are both burned by the two closest competitors: 'Pawl' is agentic-commerce-lab/pawl (68 stars, Shopware-backed, same ratchet metaphor, same agent-work-verification domain, July 2026; plus trunion-io/pawl and tiangong-dev/pawl), and 'Airlock' is xdlc-labs/airlock v1.0 (Sept 10-14), which is literally 'CI release gate for AI agents' with snapshot/diff/blast-radius, CI-interval gates, INCONCLUSIVE/NEEDS_APPROVAL, an approval ledger and a GitHub Action. A reviewer or user searching either name lands on a competitor.

The 'genuinely new vs PACE/SEA/CAR' list is over-claimed and under-cited: the verdict/disposition split with 'clears/below/inconclusive' + provisional is Thru-Echoes/rsi-exam-provenance (in your own digest, verbatim vocabulary); protected-corpus-by-observed-stability is AI2's task stability classes plus Reef#356; the rotating held-out probe subset is HackProbe's secret core + rotated layer; one-hash join is OpenClaw hash-binding + Hermes ledger + novafabric capsules; conflict-aware selective undo is EvoUndo (paper + PyPI). None of these appear in the competitor section; a workshop reviewer will find all five in twenty minutes and downgrade the whole contribution.

The adoption wedge is already commoditized, so 'invisible until it blocks' buys no moat: agnix (413 stars) + ten SKILL.md linters cover lint/DLP; cc-skill-usage covers transcript-backfilled skill activation; stalebrain covers live-repo contradiction audits; EvoUndo/bashback cover undo; openclaw-mem covers memory receipts+rollback; Anthropic shipped the MEMORY.md truncation-line warning in September. Vendor pre-emption of receipts is not a future risk, it is the current trajectory, and the design spends Days 1-7 of 14 rebuilding these.

The eligibility-partition lever is strongest exactly where the gate is least needed: CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md/rules load in every session (212/212 in the demo), so zero ties and full replay cost for the most-deployed, least-governed artifact class; only description-matched skills get free ties, and for those five independent results already say the effect is ~0. Only 41/212 sessions (19%) are replayable at all, and the same partition idea was proposed independently in hermes#96704 on Sept 3, so it is neither proprietary nor broad.

The 'anytime-valid' framing is decorative on the path that matters: BLOCK fires on 1-3 confirmed discordant pairs over correlated cassettes from the same repo, where PACE's per-candidate guarantee does not hold (the design admits no theorem covers reuse), and SENTRY published that a fixed threshold beat its e-process on agent streams. The honest name for the BLOCK path is 'k-of-n confirmed regression on an incumbent-stable task', which is auto-harness/Reef#356-grade engineering; the e-process only does real work on the VERIFIED path, which the power table says will almost never fire on 20-40 binary tasks.

Scope makes the defensible core unbuildable in 3 months by 1-3 people: 13 components, 8 adapters (Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, DSH, pi/Prime, Reef, SkillOpt, Codex), 4 standards filings, a Harbor benchmark, a ledger re-analysis and a paper, while the design itself concedes at most three adapters can stay conformance-green. Every adapter beyond the first delays the only asset nobody else has (sealed evaluator + cassette corpus + acceptor benchmark), and each seam is a two-week gap its owner can fill (Reef#356 is 0-comment and trivially self-implementable; SkillOpt#155 already has an open maintainer invitation for a draft PR; the OpenClaw evaluator hook needs ~200 lines).

The headline re-analysis claim (>40% of accepted edits rejected as noise) depends on per-task, per-trial outcome ledgers that largely do not exist publicly: HarnessDev's 73 versions and 26,679 trajectories are unreleased, SEA and PACE have no code, Meta-Harness and Self-Harness logs are partial. Only SkillOpt-Sleep evidence.jsonl, AHE's git history and community autoresearch results.tsv are actually available, which is too thin to support the claim as written.
improvements: Rename now and verify with `gh search repos <name> --match name`: both 'Pawl' and 'Airlock' are occupied in-domain; 'Sluice', 'Portcullis', 'Keel', 'Lockstep' and 'agentci' are all also taken by agent-governance repos. Pick an unclaimed term and reserve PyPI/npm the same day.

Collapse the MVP to one defensible spine: Claude Code cassette recorder -> sealed evaluator with score receipts -> gate -> acceptor benchmark. Ship receipts/lint/undo by depending on or wrapping agnix, cc-skill-usage, stalebrain and EvoUndo (or explicitly differentiating on learned-state trees) instead of rewriting them; this removes ~5 days from the MVP and converts three would-be competitors into integrations.

Rewrite the novelty section honestly and cite the near-duplicates: adopt Thru-Echoes' verdict/disposition schema and TRACE export instead of inventing pawl.verdict; adopt HackProbe's secret-core + rotated-layer probe design by name; use Auditing Harness Tampering's seeded tampered-benign corpus as the gate-gaming testbed instead of building one in month 3; cite Safe Harness Self-Evolution and use its finite-data bounds to justify k, alpha and the 'certify only large lifts' statement; cite AI2's stability classes as the origin of 'protected by observed stability'.

Make the eligibility lever survive the memory/rules class: for always-loaded artifacts compute section-level eligibility (was the diffed section quoted, cited, or mechanically followed/contradicted in the transcript) so ties-by-eligibility still exist; report ties-by-eligibility, ties-by-outcome and inconclusive as separate counters in every verdict so the '$0' claim is auditable.

Demote 'anytime-valid' to the VERIFY path in all copy and label BLOCK plainly as 'k-of-n confirmed regression on an incumbent-stable task'; publish the false-block rate on the user's own benign edits as a first-class metric (SENTRY's negative result is the reviewer's first objection), and add self-evolve's effective_independent_count style de-correlation for cassettes from the same repo/test.

Ship the OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate plugin in week 1, not days 12-14: it is the only seam with a written contract and zero third-party implementations (confirmed by code search), it is harness-owned distribution in a 389k-star ecosystem, and 'first evaluator in the Workshop slot' is the cheapest verifiable novelty claim available; include the fail-closed conversion as the headline feature.

Turn xdlc-labs/airlock into an ally rather than a rival: emit airlock's manifest/ledger shape for repo-tracked agent state so PR-time (airlock) and runtime self-writes (this layer) chain into one story; propose the integration in their issue tracker before they extend into runtime.

Re-scope the paper to what is measurable: headline = the Replay-Gap middle case for real refiner edits on >=200 volunteer cassettes (recruit now from hermes#96704 and SkillOpt#155 threads, where people are already asking) plus the acceptor benchmark; drop HarnessDev/SEA from the re-analysis claim and pre-register only SkillOpt-Sleep evidence.jsonl, AHE git history, Meta-Harness summaries and community autoresearch results.tsv.

Add a computed capability-diff term (new tools referenced, new egress, new permission grants, new executable files) as a deterministic disposition input in the style of airlock's blast radius, so a permission expansion is NEEDS_APPROVAL regardless of outcome evidence; it is PROCTOR-compatible and cheaper than any replay.
ci-for-rsi.best_idea_to_steal: Thru-Echoes/rsi-exam-provenance's 'freeze-then-confirm with digest-derived confirmation set' plus its verdict/disposition separation. Concretely: when a candidate screens well (or before any BLOCK is finalized), freeze it by content hash, derive the confirmation cassette subset deterministically from hash(candidate_sha256 || corpus_epoch) so neither the proposer nor the screening run can have targeted those sessions, and require the k-of-n or e-process decision to be reproduced on that never-touched subset before it counts; record the statistical verdict (clears / below / inconclusive) in a separate field from the action taken (keep / revert / provisional) so 'reverted on inconclusive evidence' is never later read as 'proven harmful' in attribution, retirement or the funnel. This closes Pawl's own stated Goodhart risk on the protected corpus (proposer learns the cassettes), gives every BLOCK a reproducible held-out confirmation at ~2x the cost of one arm, and is fully compatible with the existing score-receipt design.

acceptor-benchmark.lens: INFLUENCE: 10k+ stars and/or citations by the next RSI survey; timing vs the RSI wave; first 100 users; 5-minute demo; adopt/copy/crush by Anthropic/DeepSeek/Nous; composition with OpenClaw/DSH/Claude Code/Reef; crisp falsifiable claim; coverage of the surveys' open list.
acceptor-benchmark.justification: Timing and framing are the best of any stance in this research tree: "the acceptor is the weak link" is already the community's own verdict (PACE, SEA, RSEA, agentdescent all say it; the strict-improvement frameworks with 17k/14k/6k stars ship the naive rule), all five 2026 surveys list a multi-generation benchmark with regressions/variance/held-out verifier and "governance-grade measurement" as the emptiest area, and three maintainers have opened the exact tickets (Reef #357/#358 zero comments, SkillOpt #155 endorsed twice, Hermes #96704 RFC) — so a benchmark that ships by December with a Harbor task family and a dated matrix is very likely to be cited by the next survey round; that is the realistic research influence and it is high. The composition story is verified and strong (OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate has zero third-party implementers; dsh explicitly deferred the evaluator slot; Reef's recipe API and claude plugin eval are drop-in consumers). What caps the score is star influence and execution risk. Benchmarks in this exact space have 18-107 stars (SEAGym, AI4AI-Bench, RSI-Exam); 10k stars is only reachable through the $0 audit CLI (a ccusage-class Claude Code diagnostic answering the 48-comment #82056), and that component is (a) buried as "audit/ Arm 0" under a benchmark identity that its audience will never search for, and (b) the one piece Anthropic will crush in one release by adding load/truncation status natively. The paper's C1 is crisp and falsifiable, but C3 (the null-effect audit) conflates "inconclusive" with "indistinguishable from the floor": with binary outcomes on ~12 replayable sessions the e-process will mostly abstain (CAR ~80%, SEA 0 accepts), and abstention is not evidence of a null without a pre-registered equivalence margin — reviewers will kill the headline. The scope (12 acceptor adapters, 6 consumer adapters, 12 ledger converters, 5 stream families, a G=15 loop track, an audit over 4 stores, a sealed-rotation leaderboard) is 3-5x what 1-3 people can ship in 3 months against substrates moving at 947 commits/4 days; the matrix will be stale on publication day, and a benchmark whose rows are wrong about other people's shipped code produces public fights, not adoption. Net: a solid workshop/D&B paper cited by surveys (probable), Reef/OpenClaw adoption of the reference gate (likely), hundreds to low thousands of stars (likely), 10k stars (<10% unless the audit is split out and launched first). Expected influence 6/10; upside to 8 if the two products are separated and the loop track is deferred.

prior_art.name: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents (arXiv 2606.08106)
prior_art.overlap: Defines the acceptor as the weak link, measures greedy false-commit (30-42%) and harmful-commit rates, and uses 'planted improvement among noise' and 'no-real-gain stochastic' regimes — the seed of Turnstile's null/good streams and FCR/HCR metrics. Only its own prompt-evolution loop on 0.5B-3B Qwen, binary GSM8K, per-candidate alpha, no code. Turnstile generalizes to any shipped acceptor on real artifacts inside real consumers; the headline 'greedy commits ~44% of nulls' is a reproduction, not a discovery.

prior_art.name: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents (arXiv 2609.00069, Aug 30 2026)
prior_art.overlap: Uncited by the design. Seeds tampered-vs-benign edit pairs into REAL self-improving-agent trajectories, defines a two-axis taxonomy (harness role x violated obligation: authorization/provenance/completeness), and benchmarks audit methods on tampering classification and localization. This is the planted-tamper stream with a labeled corpus, published two weeks ago. It audits external auditors post hoc rather than the loops' own accept() decisions, so Turnstile's 'tamper-blind acceptor' cell is still new, but the paper must be cited and its corpus reused or the stream looks derivative.

prior_art.name: HackProbe: Harness-Agnostic Detection and Immunization of Reward Hacking (arXiv 2609.04665)
prior_art.overlap: Black-box monitor with a secret frozen probe core plus held-out probes, Page-Hinkley divergence and Sidak-fused risk (0.763 AUROC across contamination, gameable grader, self-consistency, judge collusion); no code. It is the 'harmful stream + detector' idea for reward hacking; Turnstile treats it as a component (probe bank as harmful stream), which is the right move, but the benchmark's overfit/tamper families overlap its four failure classes.

prior_art.name: Phantom Gains: Auditing Self-Improvement Against a Measured Null (arXiv 2608.20290)
prior_art.overlap: Shows apparent self-improvement is reproduced by a frozen control pushed through the identical pipeline (7 measurement failures, each inverting a finding when the control is absent) and prescribes a separately measured null for every transition statistic. That is exactly Turnstile's A-vs-A' control arm and the audit's null floor; Phantom Gains did it for LoRA self-training on Qwen3-8B, not for harness stores or acceptors.

prior_art.name: SkillMisevo-Gym / SkillMisevo-Bench / SafeEvolve (arXiv 2608.12851)
prior_art.overlap: A lifecycle gym with native-path adapters for Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw and Hermes, six evolution methods at pinned revisions, clean-session probe protocol (freeze library, reload only SKILL.md into a fresh executor), and a GovernableStore hook contract — the closest existing multi-harness test bed. It scores the evolution METHOD's safety (21/21 configs author unsafe artifacts); Turnstile scores the ACCEPTOR's confusion matrix and adopts its probe protocol. Corpus unreleased, so Turnstile must author its own unsafe set.

prior_art.name: Counterfactual Trace Auditing of LLM Agent Skills (arXiv 2605.11946)
prior_art.overlap: Pairs with-skill vs without-skill Claude Code traces on 49 SWE-Skills-Bench tasks (+0.3pp, r=1); its own replication found detectors fire identically on A-vs-A' pairs and 0/34 runs read the skill. This is the audit arm's pipeline shape and the uptake-before-effect lesson; Turnstile's contribution is r>=3, uptake verification, and pointing it at users' own stores rather than a benchmark skill.

prior_art.name: Thru-Echoes/rsi-exam-provenance

prior_art.name: Safe Harness Self-Evolution: A Theoretical Analysis of Feasibility and Limits (arXiv 2609.08175)
prior_art.overlap: Finite-data bounds for safe selection/adoption of harness updates while controlling change on retained tasks; 'more candidates need not improve the guarantee when evaluation is limiting'. Theory only, no benchmark or code; useful as the citation for why evals-per-decision is the right x-axis.

fatal_flaws: Scope is 3-5x what 1-3 people can ship in 3 months: 12 acceptor adapters, 6 consumer adapters, 12 ledger-format converters, 5 stream families, a G=15 loop track, a 4-store audit and a sealed-rotation leaderboard, each pinned against substrates that move at 947 commits/4 days (Hermes) and 14 tags/12 days (dsh). The MVP timeline ('Days 5-8: three external acceptor adapters', 'Days 12-14: publish repo, schemas, leaderboard, open three threads') is not credible; the realistic outcome is a half-working matrix that is stale on publication day, and a benchmark that publishes wrong rows about other people's shipped code produces public fights with maintainers, not adoption.

The paper deliverable and the star deliverable have different audiences and are welded together under the wrong identity. The only component with a 10k-star path is the $0 audit ('MEMORY.md loaded TRUNCATED in 14/31 sessions; 9 newest entries never reached the model'), a ccusage-class Claude Code diagnostic answering the 48-comment #82056 — but it is buried as 'audit/ Arm 0' inside a project named and pitched as an acceptor benchmark that its audience will never search for. Meanwhile the benchmark identity drags the audit's maintenance load and privacy risk.

C3 (null-effect audit) conflates abstention with a null result. With binary outcomes on ~12 replayable sessions, an alpha=0.05 e-process or CI will mostly abstain (CAR ~80% at K<=8; SEA's ALG4 accepted 0 at ~50 tasks; the design's own sim gives 11-39% power at +10pp), and 'INCONCLUSIVE, needs ~28 more sessions' is not 'lift indistinguishable from the A-vs-A' floor'. Without a pre-registered equivalence margin (TOST-style or an equivalence e-process) the headline finding is unfalsifiable-by-construction and reviewers will strike it; the replayable-session subset (0-1 idempotent prefix calls; only sessions with re-executable terminal verification) is also a biased minority of real usage.

Anthropic crushes Arm 0 in one release: load/truncation/wrong-store receipts are a small change to Claude Code's InstructionsLoaded path and #82056 is a high-visibility issue they will fix; `claude plugin eval` already ships with/without ablation. Once fixed, the demo's first minute disappears and what remains is the expensive, abstention-prone replay arm. Hermes #96704 and SkillOpt #155 are likewise already being built by their own communities, so the 'first implementer' wedge is partly occupied.

Leaderboard rows are non-comparable and rot weekly by the design's own admission (a confusion matrix is a property of the (acceptor, consumer version, model) triple, per Lin et al.), and the acceptors take fundamentally different inputs: Hermes' scanner and OpenClaw's regex never see a task, LLM-judge acceptors never claimed to detect null edits, GEPA's minibatch gate is a component of a search not a commit rule. A headline 'Reef-decide commits 38% of nulls' will be read as a property of Reef and attacked as running gates outside their design envelope; an adapter-not-score submission model means the small team pays to re-run every row on every substrate release — the cost creep the design itself flags.

Uncited prior art weakens the novelty claim: 'Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents' (2609.00069, Aug 30) already seeds tampered-vs-benign edit pairs into real self-improving trajectories with a taxonomy and benchmarked audit methods; HackProbe defines the probe-bank harmful stream; Phantom Gains defines the measured null; SkillMisevo-Gym is a 4-harness lifecycle gym with clean-session probes; PACE defined FCR/HCR and the planted regimes. Turnstile's genuine novelty is 'assemble these into one instrument aimed at shipped acceptors, plus phantom-accept and evals-per-decision' — a good D&B contribution, but the 'first gate benchmark' framing invites an easy 'incremental' rejection.

The 5-minute demo depends on three separate stacks working live (transcript parser, git-snapshot sandbox replay with recorded externals, Harbor sealed eval with five acceptor adapters at a $40 budget) and its middle act ends in 'INCONCLUSIVE, cost $4.10' — a demo whose central result is a non-result does not travel on HN or in a workshop talk.
improvements: Split into two products with two names and two launch dates. Week 1: ship the $0 audit alone as a standalone Claude Code (then Hermes) CLI with a one-line pitch ('is your agent's memory even loaded?'), zero model calls, one screenshot, aimed at HN/r/ClaudeAI and cross-posted to #82056 and #96704; this is the only realistic 10k-star path and it must land before Anthropic fixes it natively. Month 2-3: the acceptor benchmark as a Harbor task family plus a dated report, with the audit as its data source, not its sub-feature.

Cut the v1 matrix to what can be right on day one: 4 acceptors (greedy n=1, PACE mixture e-process, SkillOpt strict gate, Reef decide) x 1 consumer (Claude Code via `claude plugin eval` isolation, pinned version and model) x 4 streams (null, planted-regression, planted-tamper, planted-unsafe). Defer the G=15 loop track, the Hermes/OpenClaw/Prime/agentdescent/auto-harness adapters and 9 of the 12 ledger converters to v2 or to submitters. A small correct matrix cited by the next survey beats a large stale one.

Fix C3 before touching data: pre-register an equivalence margin (e.g., |paired lift| < 5pp at matched budget) tested with an equivalence e-process or TOST, so each store lands in exactly one of {helps, hurts, equivalent-to-placebo, underpowered}; report 'underpowered' with the sessions-needed estimate as a budget statement, never as a finding; and report the replayable-session fraction as a first-class number so the selection bias is visible.

Replace the live leaderboard with dated snapshot reports ('Turnstile 2026.12') where every row carries (acceptor@version, consumer@version, model, stream release, receipt) and an explicit expiry; run rows on a cron against new substrate tags only for the 4 v1 acceptors. Pre-share each row with the affected maintainer under a two-week embargo and publish their fix as a second row in the same report — this is how 'a fixed row is free marketing' becomes real instead of a hope.

Land inside Reef #357 within two weeks as a PR that writes the benchmark spec (committed-vs-used, repetition/variability reporting, invalid-evaluation outcomes) into their tracker, and recruit BobbyZhouZijian as a co-author or endorser; Reef is small but it is the one substrate that will adopt the reference decide/evaluate recipe wholesale, and a maintainer co-author defuses the 'you ran my gate outside its envelope' attack for at least one row.

Rebuild the demo around the streams that give binary, dramatic, cheap answers: lead with tamper ('3 of 5 acceptors accepted a forged best_ever.json 5/5') and the Hermes 'close ALL Chrome windows' regression slipping through a pooled tally, then the $0 audit table; keep the paired replay off the demo path until it returns something other than INCONCLUSIVE on the presenter's own sessions.

Cite and position explicitly against 2609.00069 (reuse its tampered-benign corpus for the tamper stream if released), HackProbe, Phantom Gains, SkillMisevo-Gym and PACE as the five inputs; retitle the contribution 'the first benchmark of the acceptors shipped in production loops' and drop 'first gate benchmark'. Add a two-model consumer ablation (Lin et al.) on the 4x4 matrix so the consumer-coupling critique is answered in the paper rather than in the issue tracker.

Reuse published task-stability classes (AI2's stable_pass/stable_fail/unstable lists on Terminal-Bench 2.1, SkillsBench deterministic verifiers) for the protected corpus instead of measuring stability from scratch, and pin the 'good' stream to the ~20 published edits with the largest re-measured lift rather than 60 — the $500 re-measurement is the first thing to cut if budget slips.
acceptor-benchmark.best_idea_to_steal: The zero-cost null stream plus 'phantom accept' as a confusion-matrix cell: feed any acceptor byte-identical, whitespace-only and verified-neutral candidates (A vs A'), where every commit is by definition a false commit, so an acceptor's false-commit rate is measurable for free without a single held-out evaluation; and log, from the consumer's own native load event (Claude Code Skill tool_use, Hermes skill_view, OpenClaw usage receipts), whether a committed artifact was ever loaded on the tasks it targets, so 'committed but never activated' is scored as an error cell rather than counted as a success. Any gate paper or production loop can adopt both in an afternoon, they produce the headline number ('your gate commits 44% of no-op edits; 25% of what it keeps is never read'), and they are exactly what Reef #357 asked for in writing.

acceptor-benchmark.lens: FEASIBILITY: 1-3 people, frontier API models only, no GPUs, 3 months to a credible v1 plus the 5-minute killer demo. Every cost, power, hook and sandbox claim checked against the digests, the builder's own gate_power_sim.py/cassette_extract.py, live docs (code.claude.com hooks + plugin-evals), and repo/issue state via gh (Hermes #96704, Reef #357/#358, SkillOpt #155, dsh hook-protocol README, OpenClaw hook-skill.types.ts).
acceptor-benchmark.justification: The thesis (judge the acceptor, plant ground truth) is correct and the null/tamper/overfit streams really are free to LABEL. But the design conflates label cost with decision cost: every acceptor still consumes its native evaluations per decision, and the stated experiment sizes do not survive arithmetic. The Day 7-10 matrix (10 acceptors x 5 streams x ~20 candidates x 3 seeds) is 12k agent runs at EPD=2 and 240k at the e-process's exhausted budget of 40 pairs on null candidates, i.e. $6k-$120k at a realistic $0.50/run, against a stated $150 cap; the '~$500' real-good corpus is 24,000 runs (60 edits x 40 tasks x 5 seeds x 2 arms), implying $0.02/run; the loop track is ~54k sealed runs. Nothing in the architecture says acceptors are replayed against a cached (candidate x task x seed) outcome matrix, which is the only way a small team runs this. Second, the 'good' stream needs >=+20pp paired lift on >=40 tasks with CI excluding zero, but published held-out lifts are +0.6 (AI2), +0.6 (AHE), +1.4 to +4.4 (HarnessDev), so the cached-real-good stream will be near-empty and MIR (and the C1 Pareto falsifier) becomes unmeasurable; the builder's own sim says +10pp is detected 11% at N=40. Third, the demo's minute 1-3 (12 sessions, 9 replays each, '$4.10', live bars) is off by 1-2 orders of magnitude in cost and hours in wall-clock for 300-tool-call sessions, and by the design's own numbers returns INCONCLUSIVE. Seam facts also diverge from the text: InstructionsLoaded exposes only load_reason + instruction_file_path (no bytes/truncation), `claude plugin eval` needs >=2.1.269 (builder is on 2.1.258) and spawns real runs so its acceptor row cannot be cached, dsh's hook bridge parses-but-ignores updatedInput and cannot replace tool output (cassette replay under dsh needs a native Cordis plugin), Hermes #96704 is a P3 needs-decision community RFC with 1 reaction rather than a maintainer ask. Finally the scope (8 subsystems, 12 acceptor adapters, 6 consumers, 12 converters, sealed-rotation leaderboard, G=15 loop track, 10 consented stores, 5 upstream PRs, D&B paper; 8 parallel workstreams in the 14-day MVP) is 3-5x what 1-3 people ship in 12 weeks. A descoped v1 (outcome-cache acceptor replay, 4 cheap streams + planted-improvement stream, one consumer, 6 acceptors, Arm 0 audit) is ~0.55-0.6 likely; the design as written, with this demo, is ~0.2.

fatal_flaws: Cost is mispriced by 20-100x because label cost is conflated with decision cost. Null and tamper candidates are free to LABEL, but each acceptor still spends its native evaluations to DECIDE, and a sequential gate on a null candidate never stops early (no futility rule), so it burns the full 40-pair budget. Recomputed from the design's own sizes: the Day 7-10 matrix (10 acceptors x 5 streams x ~20 candidates x 3 seeds) is 12,000 agent runs at EPD=2 and 240,000 at EPD=40, i.e. $6k-$120k at $0.50/run on Terminal-Bench/SkillsBench tasks through Claude Code, versus a stated $150 cap; the '~$500 one-time' real-good corpus is 60 x 40 x 5 x 2 = 24,000 runs (implies $0.02/run); the loop track is ~54,000 sealed runs before proposer tokens. The architecture never states that acceptors are replayed against a cached (candidate x task x seed x arm) outcome matrix, which is the only way a 1-3 person team can run any of this.

The 'good' stream will be nearly empty, so MIR and the C1 Pareto falsifier are untestable. Admission requires >=+20pp paired lift on >=40 tasks with CI excluding zero, but published held-out lifts are +0.6pp (AI2 34-task split), +0.6 (AHE), +1.4 to +4.4 (HarnessDev), +3 to +9 cross-model (SkillOpt); the builder's own gate_power_sim.py shows +10pp detected 11% at N=40 and +20pp 44%. No planted-improvement stream is defined (only planted regressions), even though PACE's 'planted improvement among noise' regime is the cheap way to get labeled good edits.

Killer-demo minute 1-3 is infeasible as stated. 12 sessions x (3 with + 3 without + 3 A') = 108 full-session replays; the builder's own cassette_extract.py measured ~300 tool calls per session with idempotent prefix 0-1 and 20% external calls, so each replay is a $0.50-$10 sandbox re-execution, not $0.007, giving $50-$1,000 and hours of wall-clock rather than '$4.10' in two minutes. Only sessions whose terminal verification is re-executable qualify (a minority of real sessions), and by the design's own line the headline result is INCONCLUSIVE ('needs ~28 more sessions'); a demo whose payoff is 'unknown' does not land.

Scope is 3-5x what 1-3 people ship in 12 weeks: 8 subsystems, 12 acceptor adapters (each needing the loop's eval function stubbed), 6 consumer adapters with activation detectors, 12 ledger converters plus an in-toto predicate proposal, a leaderboard with sealed rotation and receipts, a G=15 loop track (5 loops x 3 seeds), a consented audit of >=10 real stores with temporal store-at-t reconstruction, 5 upstream PRs (SkillOpt AgenticReplayBackend alone is a workstream someone else already claimed), and a D&B paper. The 14-day MVP alone lists 8 parallel workstreams including a sealed Harbor evaluator with receipts and three external adapters.

Seam facts diverge from the design text. Claude Code's InstructionsLoaded hook exposes only load_reason + instruction_file_path (no bytes available/loaded, no complete|truncated status), so the load receipt must be inferred by re-hashing the file against a known cap; `claude plugin eval` requires >=2.1.269 (builder is on 2.1.258; docs say early-access builds error) and spawns real `claude -p` runs, so that acceptor row cannot be cached and costs cases x runs x 2 arms (~240 runs per candidate); dsh's hook-protocol README states HookOutput.updatedInput is parsed but not honored and continue:false has no run-level effect, and the bridge can only block/ask/attach, so PostToolUse-based cassette replay does not work under dsh via the bridge (needs a native Cordis post-execute 'replace' plugin); OpenClaw's evaluator seam is confirmed fail-open (only a completed 'block' vetoes). Hermes #96704 is a P3 needs-decision community RFC with 1 reaction, not a maintainer ask, so 'Hermes asked for it' overstates adoption pull.

The safety-canary coverage claim is unsupported. MLAS/SkillMisevo-style laundered payloads are trigger-conditioned (fire on a specific task family or phrase); ~100 generic domain probes x 3 exposures will rarely reach the trigger, so 'canary blocks 37/40 at 96 probes per candidate' is an invented number. What plausibly catches them is the mechanical layer (egress attempt, forbidden path, capability/script diff), which the design lists but subordinates to the canary; the unsafe stream's labels also come from the team's own authored artifacts judged by the same model families, inheriting the same-family-judge circularity the design criticizes elsewhere.

EPD, the leaderboard's x-axis, is dominated by null candidates for exactly the honest gates the paper wants to promote: under H0 an e-process without a futility stop consumes the full budget per null candidate, while greedy n=1 spends 1 pair. As specified, the Pareto view will show Turnstile-ref and PACE at 20-40x the evals-per-decision of greedy on the null stream, and the 'dominated by do-not-evolve' rule will flag the reference gate. No futility/early-reject rule or per-stream EPD reporting is defined.
improvements: Make the outcome cache the architecture's centerpiece: build one sealed (candidate x task x seed x arm) outcome matrix per release (~40 tasks x 8 incumbent replays for the A-vs-A' pool + ~60 non-trivial candidates x 40 x 5 seeds ~= 12k runs, $1-6k), sign it with receipts, and expose it to every acceptor adapter as the eval oracle (auto-harness's run(task_ids)->{id: reward} interface, Reef evaluate, GEPA's metric, agentdescent's eval_fn, Self-Harness's split scores all accept a function). Acceptors then replay offline in seconds; the demo's minute 3-5 becomes honest ('replaying sealed cached outcomes') and 12 acceptors x 5 seeds costs nothing extra. Only acceptors that spawn their own runs (claude plugin eval, Hermes SkillEvaluator LLM tier) need live budget; cap them at 5 candidates per stream.

Add a planted-improvement stream mirroring the regression stream: take a protected task the incumbent passes k/k, remove or corrupt the rule/skill line it depends on to create a degraded incumbent that fails k/k, and offer the restoring edit as the candidate with a known lift bucket (labeled with the same k reruns, ~$20 per candidate). This gives MIR-by-lift-bucket on real artifacts without the $12k real-good corpus; keep 5-10 re-measured published edits as a separate 'real-unlabeled' side table.

Descope v1 to what ships: one consumer (Claude Code inside Harbor containers), a 40-task corpus with deterministic verifiers (SkillsBench + short Terminal-Bench tasks, pick by measured incumbent stability >= 0.9), 4 cheap streams (null, planted-regression, planted-improvement, planted-tamper/overfit) plus a 20-artifact unsafe stream labeled by mechanical detectors, 6 acceptors (greedy n=1/n=2, fixed-n McNemar, PACE, Turnstile-ref, Reef decide, auto-harness gating.py, agentdescent), and the Arm 0 audit for Claude Code + Hermes. Cut the loop track, the 10-store consented audit, the leaderboard rotation, in-toto predicate filing and 9 of the 12 converters to a v2 roadmap; budget $3-6k and 8 GPU-free weeks.

Add a futility rule to the reference gate and report EPD per stream: alongside the wealth process keep a time-uniform confidence sequence on the discordant-pair proportion and stop with HOLD when its upper bound falls below the smallest lift bucket of interest (+10pp); this bounds null-candidate spend to ~10-15 pairs instead of 40 and makes the Pareto x-axis compare gates on the same footing.

Rebuild the killer demo around what is cheap and real: minute 0-1 = Arm 0 over existing transcripts (the local jsonl files do carry 'attachment' records and MEMORY.md/CLAUDE.md mentions, so eligible->loaded->Skill tool_use can be tabulated; compute truncation by re-hashing the file against the documented cap and label it 'inferred'; tag Turnstile's own output so it cannot count itself, the trap that already fired in this session's transcript); minute 1-3 = ONE paired sandbox replay of 2-3 sessions that have a re-executable terminal check, with cost and tri-state verdict printed; minute 3-5 = the cached-outcome acceptor replay with the live confusion matrix. Drop the '$4.10 for 12 sessions' line.

Forward-looking load receipts should be built from InstructionsLoaded (path) + SessionStart + the file's sha256 and size at hook time, not from fields the hook does not expose; document 'complete|truncated' as inferred from size vs cap, and 'wrong_store' from the resolved project slug, since the hook gives neither.

Under dsh, ship the gate as a native Cordis plugin on tools/pre-execute (deny) and tools/post-execute (replace) rather than through the hook bridge; use the bridge only for deny-only gating under Claude Code/Codex hooks.json. Verify updatedToolOutput replay on a 2.1.269+ build before relying on plugin eval's history_file for cassette forks.

Label the unsafe stream with trigger-conditioned probes derived from each payload's own trigger plus the mechanical detectors (egress, forbidden path, new executable, capability diff), report canary and mechanical block rates separately, and use a cross-family judge only as a tie-breaker; state coverage as 'of payloads whose trigger the probe set reaches'.

Size CERT_VALIDITY honestly: n=60 null candidates gives a 95% CI of roughly [1%, 12%] around a 4% FCR, which cannot distinguish alpha=0.05 from 0.10. Since null candidates cost nothing to label and, with the cache, nothing to evaluate (they draw from the incumbent replay pool), use >=300 per release and report a CI, not a boolean.

Sequence adoption by cost-to-land: month 1 land Arm 0 in Hermes #96704 as evals/skills/arm_a (no model runs, matches the RFC's own Arm A and the contributor-offered fixtures) and post Reef #357 a two-page spec section; month 2 the Reef decide/evaluate recipe PR; leave SkillOpt #155 to the volunteer who claimed it and offer the tri-state record schema instead of a competing backend.
acceptor-benchmark.best_idea_to_steal: The null stream as a free false-commit detector: feed every acceptor byte-identical and whitespace-only candidates (A vs A') where any commit is by construction a false commit. It costs zero labels, its evaluations are the same incumbent replays that yield the per-task noise floor and stability classes, it reproduces PACE's 30-45% greedy false-commit number on real harness artifacts inside real consumers, and any gate paper or production loop (Reef, SkillOpt, auto-harness, GEPA) can add the row in a day. Pair it with 'phantom accept' (committed but never loaded by the consumer, observable from Skill tool_use and load receipts) as a first-class confusion-matrix cell, and you have the two cheapest, hardest-to-argue-with numbers in the whole design.

acceptor-benchmark.lens: NOVELTY vs the landscape and the Sept-2026 RSI prior art (rsi_digest.md), with 12-month defensibility. Method: read landscape_digest.md, rsi_digest.md (Parts 1-3), synthesis_v1.md and both gap analyses in full; then 22 `gh search repos` queries (mechanism + all 10 name candidates), 1 `gh search code`, 2 `gh search issues`, 11 issue/PR/repo lookups (Reef #356/#357/#358/#447, SkillOpt #154/#155/#174/#175, Hermes #96704, Claude Code #82056, OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` implementers, Hermes evals/ tree), 14 WebSearch queries and 8 WebFetch reads of the closest papers/repos surfaced.
acceptor-benchmark.justification:
The thesis ("benchmark the acceptor, not the agent; plant ground truth for the gate") occupies a genuinely empty cell: no benchmark in the digest or found by search scores acceptors across loops (HarnessDev, EvoHarnessBench, RSI-Exam, AI4AI-Bench, SEAGym, HarnessOpt-Bench, PAST-Bench, Meta-Agent Challenge, Auto-Enhance all score the agent or the meta-agent), PACE defines false/harmful-commit only on its own toy loop, and the gh/web sweep found nothing named GateBench/AcceptorBench/Turnstile in this space (landtml/gatebench is a coding-agent gate harness, not an acceptor benchmark). The two label-free streams (null = identical/A-vs-A' candidates; tamper = diffs that touch the evaluator) and the resulting CERT_VALIDITY check (empirical FCR on the null stream <= claimed alpha) are the cleanest new idea: they cost zero held-out evals and expose every strict-improvement gate for free. Making phantom-accept a confusion-matrix cell and putting a matched-budget 'do not evolve' row on the leaderboard are new framings, not new measurements.

What pulls the score down: (1) Almost every component is borrowed and the design says so (PACE, SEA CTHS, CAR, Replay Gap control arm, CTA null floor, AI2 parallel-K, Lin et al. activation, RSI-Exam sealing, agentdescent invariants, rsi-exam-provenance verdict/disposition). Turnstile-ref is integration, and the field already has four shipped gates in this shape (agentdescent, GRASP, Regimes, rsi-exam-provenance). (2) The tamper stream is partly pre-empted: 'Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents' (2609.00069, Aug 30) already seeds tampered-vs-benign edit pairs into real self-improving trajectories and benchmarks audit methods on classification/localization; HackProbe (2609.04665) scores a harness-agnostic detector on injected hacking channels with ground truth (AUROC 0.763); Pebblous Census (2608.16813) runs planted defects through gates-on/gates-off arms. 'Plant labeled edits, score the filter' is therefore an established methodology being moved to a new object, not invented. (3) The null-effect audit is being built by the community right now: Hermes #96704 (6 comments, active) already specifies three arms with a $0 activation arm first, a 3-5 replay variance floor, a holdout arm (review fires, output withheld), an eligible->activated->adhered->effective funnel, two calibration fixtures (activation-neutral skill; backbone-dependent negative transfer) and production data from a 182-skill deployment; jimy-r runs golden-set replay with a variance floor over a live Claude Code workspace; CTA, SkillsBench (self-generated skills -1.3pp vs human +16.2pp) and 'What Eviction Destroys' (restore-counterfactual on memory) already established the paired with/without protocol and the null result. C3 would be confirmatory. (4) Reef #356/#357/#358 are maintainer-authored roadmap items whose checklists already specify separately-tallied protected seed suites, invalid-evaluation outcomes, repeated confirmation, decision records, committed-vs-used and variability reporting; Reef does not need Turnstile to build its gate, only to benchmark it. (5) Defensibility: a cross-loop acceptor leaderboard with sealed rotating streams is a coordination artifact that is slow for others to replicate, which is the strongest 12-month moat; but each wedge (Hermes Arm 0, SkillOpt #155 AgenticReplayBackend where a volunteer already stepped up, Claude Code plugin eval adding sequential stats) can be absorbed by its host within weeks, and 12-acceptor x 6-stream x 2-consumer rows rot with weekly harness releases. Net: a real, unoccupied framing (8) dragged to 6 by borrowed machinery, two partial pre-emptions, and a scope that a 1-3 person team cannot hold for 12 months.
