fatal_flaws: Label circularity for the three streams that need measurement. Regression, unsafe and 'good' labels are produced by Turnstile's own sealed paired evaluator, protected corpus, canary suite and 5-seed CI rule, then acceptors are scored against them; Turnstile-ref uses the same evaluator, floor and canary as its decision inputs, so it is scored on labels its own machinery generated. External acceptors (Reef decide, SkillOpt gate) are wrapped away from their native evaluators and tasks and judged on Turnstile's corpus, so 'FCR at native budget' is not the acceptor as shipped. Only the null and tamper streams are label-by-construction; the design must say so per stream or reviewers will treat C1 as a benchmark that certifies its own reference gate.

The 'good' stream may be nearly empty, making the benchmark measure conservatism only. Admission requires >=+20pp paired lift on >=40 tasks with CI excluding zero from real published ledgers; SkillsBench (-1.3pp self-generated), CTA (+0.3pp), Continual Harness (6.4% reuse) and SkillOpt (gains in 1-4 edits) predict very few such edits exist. If MIR@+20 has a handful of items, every acceptor is Pareto-dominated by 'do not evolve' by construction and the leaderboard reads as an indictment rather than a measurement; planting 'good' edits means planting fixes to planted regressions, which is artificial and gameable.

Scope is unexecutable for 1-3 people: 8 subsystems, 12+ version-pinned acceptor adapters, 6 consumer adapters with activation detectors, a 100-probe canary with hidden rotation and a seeded judge-defect set, converters for 12 ledger formats, an in-toto predicate, sandbox-first cassette replay for four stores, a G=15 x 5-loop x 3-seed loop track (tens of thousands of sealed agent runs) and a leaderboard with sealed rotation and submission policing, in 3 months while Hermes ships 947 commits per 4 days and dsh 14 tags in 12 days. The risk list names this and cuts nothing.

The audit wedge is already being built by the communities it targets. Hermes #96704 has six active contributors, a three-arm spec with Arm 0 as '$0, within a day', fixtures offered, and production data; SkillOpt #155 has a volunteer and a maintainer-approved first slice; Reef #356 is a maintainer's own checklist. Landing 'Arm 0 in-tree' as an outsider competes with the RFC author's plan, and if it lands, the practitioner half of Turnstile becomes a Hermes feature with no Turnstile dependency.

The tamper stream is architectural, not behavioral, and partly pre-empted. Whether an acceptor is 'tamper-blind' is decided by whether the candidate's write surface includes the evaluator (auto-harness yes, sealed gates no), so the stream yields a binary flag per acceptor, not a rate; and 2609.00069 already released the seeded tampered-vs-benign edit-pair corpus over real trajectories, so building a bespoke tamper generator adds cost without novelty.

Consumer-triple coupling makes rows incomparable and short-lived. FCR/HCR/PHANTOM are properties of (acceptor, harness version, model, activation path); Turnstile pins claude-code/2.1.270/sonnet-4.5 for a Reef acceptor that never runs there in production. Rows must be re-run per pinned version; with weekly releases the leaderboard is either stale or a full-time re-run job, and cross-row ranking is not meaningful.

Name: 'Turnstile' is Cloudflare's bot-detection product; 'GateBench' is used by five repos including landtml/gatebench in the same coding-agent-gate space; several other candidates (Verdict, Sieve, Placebo) are generic words with existing packages. Discoverability and the pipx/PyPI install story in the killer demo are compromised.
improvements: Cut the MVP to the label-free core and ship it in two weeks: null + tamper + overfit streams (zero held-out evals to label), one incident-mined regression stream of 8 edits, five acceptors (greedy n=1, PACE mixture, SkillOpt research gate, Reef decide, Turnstile-ref), one consumer (Claude Code), CERT_VALIDITY as the headline metric. Publish that matrix before touching canary, loop track, ledger converters or the leaderboard site.

Add an offline re-analysis track that needs no new agent runs: replay published ledgers (SkillOpt evidence.jsonl, AHE change_manifest, Meta-Harness evolution_summary.jsonl, autoresearch community results.tsv #448/#596, Reef release chain) through each reference gate and report how many accepted edits each gate would have refused and how many held-out regressions sit in the refused set. Both gap analyses flag this as more citable than building the gate; it costs days, not dollars.

Break label circularity by pre-registration: freeze all regression/unsafe/good labels before any acceptor runs; produce unsafe labels with a judge family different from any canary judge used by Turnstile-ref; report label-by-construction streams (null, tamper, overfit) separately from label-by-measurement streams; score external acceptors both on their native evaluator/tasks (as shipped) and on the sealed corpus, and publish both rows.

Consume existing corpora instead of authoring: use the 2609.00069 tampered-benign edit pairs for the tamper stream, HackProbe's four injected hacking channels for the overfit stream, SkillMisevo's cell taxonomy only as a spec, and AfshinMirhamed's two Hermes calibration fixtures (activation-neutral skill; backbone-dependent negative transfer) as free null/regression items; ask 2609.00069's authors to co-list.

Join Hermes #96704 rather than land beside it: contribute Arm 0 as a PR co-authored with AngelCampa1 and gfpyc under their three-arm schema and eligible->activated->adhered->effective funnel, and take the AgenticReplayBackend slice in SkillOpt #155 only if the volunteer stalls; make Turnstile's record format the export target of those in-tree harnesses rather than a competing runner.

Ship the Claude Code load-receipt hook (SessionStart + InstructionsLoaded: which CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md/skills resolved, bytes available vs loaded, complete|truncated|not_loaded|wrong_store) as a standalone ~200-line plugin in week 1; it answers #82056 (48 comments), #57574 and #79217 directly, needs no model calls, and is the adoption wedge that survives even if the benchmark stalls.

Replace the G=15 x 5-loop x 3-seed loop track with one loop (SkillOpt-Sleep or GEPA on Harbor) run gated vs ungated vs parallel-K for G=8 x 3 seeds, reporting BWT/FWT and safety decay; that is enough to test C2 and is affordable.
Make the acceptor's own labeling and evaluation cost part of EPD, and add a per-stream 'cost to label' column; a benchmark that hides its own evaluation spend is exactly what it accuses others of.

Redefine the tamper axis as a binary architectural flag (evaluator reachable from candidate write surface: yes/no) verified by the receipt's evaluator_access_ledger, and drop it from the Pareto; keep the stream only to confirm the flag empirically once per acceptor.
Rename before publishing: Wicket and Portcullis returned no repos in this space; check PyPI and avoid Turnstile/GateBench/Verdict/Sieve/Placebo.
acceptor-benchmark.best_idea_to_steal: The null stream as a free calibration test for any acceptor: feed the gate byte-identical candidates (A vs A') and verified no-op edits, where every commit is a false commit by construction, and report empirical false-commit rate against the gate's claimed alpha (CERT_VALIDITY). It needs zero held-out labels, works on any loop tonight (GEPA, SkillOpt, Reef, Self-Harness, autoresearch), doubles as the per-task noise floor for the protected corpus, and turns 'strict improvement on a noisy split' from an argument into a number; it is the one piece of Turnstile that is both novel at its object and impossible for a maintainer to dismiss.

harness-owns-the-test.lens: INFLUENCE — 10k+ stars and/or citation by the next RSI survey: timing vs the RSI wave, first 100 users, 5-minute demo, adopt/copy/crush risk from Anthropic/DeepSeek/Nous/OpenClaw, composition with OpenClaw/dsh/Claude Code/Reef, crispness/falsifiability of the paper claim, coverage of the five surveys' open problems.
harness-owns-the-test.justification: Hermetic picks the one bug the digests prove is real, unanswered and shared by the field's flagship loops (autoresearch#599 open since 2026-05-31 with 5 comments and none from Karpathy; pi-autoresearch#81 closed unimplemented; OpenClaw's skill_proposal_evaluate seam still has zero third-party evaluators as of today — I re-ran the code search), and its receipt-as-interface idea composes with every seam the ecosystem lens mapped (Reef decide, OpenClaw envelope, Harbor verifier images, claude plugin eval, in-toto #554, OTel gen_ai.evaluation.result). It squarely answers what the surveys call open: MetaRSI Eq. 30's sealed-measurement invariant as code, the Reliable survey's "no update controls the only evidence for its own acceptance", the RSI survey's "trustworthy accumulation / governance-grade measurement", and the pinkbubblebubble checklist item "a held-out verifier the system cannot rewrite". Timing is right: RSI-Exam, AI4AI-Bench, PROCTOR, HackProbe and Auditing Harness Tampering all landed in the last six weeks. The 5-minute demo (four #599 exploits rejected with reason codes next to the unmodified loop KEEPING a fabricated 0.05 bpb) is the most visual demo of the three sibling designs. But expected influence is capped by four things the design does not confront. (1) Its headline paper claims are already published and uncited: RewardHackingAgents (arXiv 2603.11337, code at Yonas650/RewardHackingAgents) measured spontaneous evaluator-tampering attempts in ~50% of natural ML-engineering-agent episodes and showed evaluator locking eliminates them at 25–31% median runtime overhead, with per-episode workspaces, patch tracking, file-access logging and reported-vs-reference metric detectors; Auditing Harness Tampering (2609.00069) already seeded 1,765 tampered/benign edit pairs into DGM/HyperAgents/AFlow trajectories under a 5-role x 7-obligation taxonomy that strictly contains T1–T7. "The field has only anecdotes" is false, and the "≤25% overhead" falsifier is already borderline violated by the closest prior result. (2) The star ceiling for this exact niche is empirically ~0–20: Prime Intellect's frozen-verify.py 8-seed speedrun (18★), Thru-Echoes/rsi-exam-provenance (2★), RewardHackingAgents (1★), evals_RSI (1★), hermes-decision-receipts (0★), PACE/SEA/PROCTOR/HackProbe with no code — verification is a UX cost the market selects against, and Hermetic's differentiated core (execution-evidence receipts, sealed scalar scorer, honeytokens) only bites on Camp-B scalar-scorer loops, which have the fewest users; on the 900k★ skill/memory substrates there is no scorer to seal, so its adapters degrade to path guards, load receipts and a canary that Pawl/Turnstile also ship. 10k stars requires Karpathy to adopt it, and the evidence (unanswered issue, rejected driver, prized minimalism) says he will not. (3) Scope: ten components, thirteen adapters, a six-harness conformance suite, and a 14-day MVP with eight deliverables for 1–3 people against substrates shipping 947 commits in four days — rotting adapters are negative influence. (4) The builder's own machine has no bubblewrap (verified: only sandbox-exec and Docker), so the "sealed-runtime" tier the whole pitch rests on is not natively demoable on the Mac laptops most Claude Code users run; the honest tier there is "self-attested" unless Docker is mandatory. Crush risk is moderate-high: claude plugin eval already isolates each run with the eval dir hidden and Bash sandboxed, Harbor/RSI-Exam/AI4AI already seal graders, DeepSeek explicitly reserved the evaluator contract for itself, and OpenClaw's fail-open seam means its own default wins. Net: a citeable systems reference at a workshop and a few hundred to ~2k stars is the realistic outcome; with the prior art absorbed, the scope cut to seal/run/verify+leakscan+gym, and a receipted-leaderboard channel into RSI-Exam/nanochat, it could reach ~6.

prior_art.name: RewardHackingAgents: Benchmarking Evaluation Integrity for LLM ML-Engineering Agents (Atinafu & Cohen, Mar 2026)
prior_art.overlap: Fresh workspace per episode, patch tracking, runtime file-access logging, detectors comparing agent-reported metric to a trusted reference, trust regimes incl. evaluator locking; finds evaluator-tampering attempts in ~50% of natural episodes, eliminated by evaluator locking at 25-31% median overhead; code released (github.com/Yonas650/RewardHackingAgents, 1 star, last push 2025-12). This is Hermetic's paper claims (1) and (2) almost verbatim, on 3 tasks x 2 backbones. Not cited by the design. What it lacks: signed offline-verifiable receipts, execution-evidence probes from optimizer state, honeytokens, per-change mid-loop use, adapters to real loops.

prior_art.name: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents (Wang, Zhang, Shao, UESTC, Aug 30 2026)
prior_art.overlap: Defines harness tampering across 5 functional roles x 7 obligations (measurement validity, procedural integrity, authorization, protected-state integrity, provenance, completeness...), seeds matched tampered/benign edit pairs into real DGM/HyperAgents/AFlow harness changes (1,765 classification + 1,801 localization samples), benchmarks 8 LLMs + fastText + LoRA-Qwen as auditors (Opus 5: 90.4% acc; GPT-5.6 Sol: 86.7% recall at 9.3% FPR). Post-hoc detection only, no runtime, no code URL. The Goodhart gym's T1-T7 is a strict subset of this taxonomy; the corpus is a ready seed the design should reuse instead of re-planting.

prior_art.overlap: The autoresearch-domain sealed-verify pattern already exists: 153 multi-day runs, record claims validated by a frozen verify.py over fixed seeds the agent cannot touch, records reconstructed from traces, one record PR per model. 18 stars after a month is the empirical star ceiling for integrity tooling in this exact niche.

prior_art.overlap: Formal statement of 'actual diff == declared modification, declared-surface containment' and 'evaluator, held-out set, release rule, ledger outside every write surface'; ships no evaluator or gate code. Hermetic is the implementation, and should say so as its framing rather than claim the invariant.

prior_art.name: BIG-bench canary GUID (contamination canary strings)
prior_art.overlap: Planting a unique nonce in evaluation material so its later appearance proves leakage is the established canary-string technique for training-data contamination. Hermetic's honeytokens apply it to scorer/rubric/data-index leakage into candidate diffs and proposer context — a new placement, not a new mechanism; cite it.

fatal_flaws: Uncited prior art already holds the headline result: RewardHackingAgents (2603.11337, code released) measured ~50% spontaneous evaluator-tampering in natural ML-engineering-agent runs and showed evaluator locking eliminates it at 25-31% overhead, and Auditing Harness Tampering (2609.00069) already built the seeded tampered/benign corpus over DGM/HyperAgents/AFlow. Claims (1) and (2) as written ('the field has only anecdotes', 'reduces exploit-accept to ~0 with <=25% overhead') would be rejected as unaware of prior work, and the <=25% overhead falsifier is already contradicted by the closest measurement.

The star ceiling for evaluator-integrity tooling is empirically ~0-20 (frontier-automated-speedrun 18, rsi-exam-provenance 2, RewardHackingAgents 1, evals_RSI 1, hermes-decision-receipts 0; PACE/SEA/PROCTOR/HackProbe no code), and Hermetic's differentiated core only applies to Camp-B scalar-scorer loops that have few users. On the 900k-star substrates there is no scorer to seal, so the adapters reduce to path guards, load receipts and a canary that are undifferentiated from the sibling designs and from what OpenClaw/Hermes partly ship. 10k stars requires Karpathy adopting it; he has not replied to #599 in 3.5 months and rejected a driver.

Scope is unbuildable for 1-3 people: ten components, thirteen adapters (Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw, dsh, pi/Prime, Reef, Harbor, SkillOpt, SIA, AHE, DGM/HGM/GEA, Meta-Harness, auto-harness), a six-harness version-pinned conformance suite, and a 14-day MVP with eight deliverables including a Goodhart gym and an OpenClaw plugin. Hermes ships 947 commits in four days and dsh cut 14 pre-release tags in 12 days; adapters will rot within weeks and rotting adapters are negative influence.

The sealed-runtime tier is not natively demoable on the builder's own machine or on most Claude Code users' laptops: macOS has no bubblewrap (verified: only sandbox-exec and Docker present), so the 'laptop CPU reproducer' demo runs at the self-attested tier unless Docker is mandated, which undercuts the closing line 'the thing that scores your agent is the one thing your agent cannot touch'.

Crush/absorption risk on every surface that could give it reach: Anthropic's claude plugin eval already runs sealed per-run isolation with the eval dir hidden and Bash sandboxed; Harbor, RSI-Exam and AI4AI-Bench already seal graders; DeepSeek explicitly reserved the evaluator authority/isolation/provider contract for its own design; OpenClaw's evaluator seam fails open so OpenClaw's own default governs; the in-toto RFC it plans to extend has not merged in four months.

The research claim is partly tautological and partly self-fulfilling: a sealed evaluator blocks planted tampering by construction, and honeytoken recall >=0.9 is measured on scenarios where the honeytoken leak was planted, while the realistic paraphrase-the-criteria case is excluded by design. The genuinely falsifiable items (false-invalid rate on honest candidates across real loops, visible-to-sealed gap as a predictor of held-out regression) are buried as secondary.
improvements: Cut to the differentiated core and ship it in 14 days: `seal / run / verify` + signed receipts with execution-evidence probes + `leakscan` with honeytokens + a Harbor export, with presets only for autoresearch, pi-autoresearch, SIA and AHE (the seven-leak audience). Leave the acceptor gym to the benchmark-shaped sibling design (Turnstile) and cassettes/undo/hooks to the CI-shaped one (Pawl); consume a PACE gate as a dependency instead of re-shipping it. Keep exactly one mass-market adapter — the OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate plugin — because being first on an empty 389k-star seam is free visibility, and make it convert error/skipped into explicit block.

Reposition the paper around what RewardHackingAgents and Auditing Harness Tampering did not do: (a) third-party offline verification of a kept result (a benchmark maintainer re-verifies a leaderboard submission from the receipt alone), (b) false-invalid rate on honest candidates across 5 real loops x 3 proposer agents, (c) mechanical detection of overfitting-through-feedback (honeytokens + independent-family spot checks) as distinct from tampering, (d) the visible-to-sealed gap per candidate as a leading indicator of held-out regression (AUC). Cite both papers, reuse the 1,765 seeded pairs and RHA's three tasks as gym seeds, and set the overhead falsifier at <=35% given the 25-31% measured baseline.

Pick the one distribution channel that can produce stars and citations at once: receipted leaderboards. Offer RSI-Exam (aiming-lab) and Prime Intellect's speedrun a per-change receipt verifier, re-score the community autoresearch results.tsv runs (#448/#596) and AHE change_manifests counterfactually ('N of M kept results carry admissible evidence'), and post the #599 reproduction with the rejecting receipt. A quotable 'X% of published kept results have no execution evidence' number travels further than a runtime.

Make the trust boundary honest by default and demoable everywhere: Linux bwrap and Docker are 'sealed'; macOS native is 'self-attested' and printed as such on every receipt; ship `hermetic run --docker` as the one-line path for Mac users and put the signing key in a host-side daemon the proposer's container cannot reach (the Thru-Echoes lesson).

Seal LLM-judge bundles from day one (judge model id + pinned prompt + temperature + seed in the bundle digest, rubric honeytokens, cross-family spot check with planted-defect calibration) because the loops where overfitting-through-feedback actually bites (SkillOpt#154, RHI, MOSS, AI-Scientist) are judge-scored, and that is where honeytokens are a new detector rather than a re-implementation of evaluator locking.

Rename before launch: npm `hermetic` is squatted (0.0.0 placeholder since 2023), PyPI is free, and 'hermetic build' vocabulary from Bazel/Nix will make the project unsearchable. Check both registries for the fallback (Assayer, Escrow, Umpire) and reserve them now.

Emit the receipt as an in-toto Statement v1 predicate from the first release and make `verify` a cosign/Rekor policy so the supply-chain-security community (far larger than RSI) can adopt the format without knowing what harness evolution is; file the 'artifact-acceptance' profile alongside #554 rather than waiting for month 3.

Default to observe-only with a single loud number: on install, back-score the loop's existing ledger and print 'K of N kept results would be admissible; the rest lack evidence', then let blocking be enabled per surface — this respects 'invisible until it blocks' and gives the first 100 users a reason to run it on day one without any process boundary.
harness-owns-the-test.best_idea_to_steal: Honeytokens planted inside the sealed evaluator bundle (nonces in the scorer source, rubric text and data index, re-rolled per build) plus a `leakscan` over candidate diffs and hook-visible proposer context, so that scorer overfitting-through-feedback (the SkillOpt#154 / AHE 'mirror the evaluator' class, which evaluator locking does not stop) becomes a provable string match instead of a suspicion — a nonce and a grep, portable to any gate or benchmark, and the one mechanism here that RewardHackingAgents, AI4AI-Bench, RSI-Exam and Auditing Harness Tampering all lack.

harness-owns-the-test.lens: NOVELTY vs the landscape and the RSI prior art, weighted by 12-month defensibility against Hermes / Prime / Reef / SkillOpt / DeepSeek Harness / Anthropic shipping weekly. Method: read landscape_digest.md, rsi_digest.md, synthesis_v1/v2, both gap analyses in full; 9 gh searches (hermetic eval, hermetic, honeytoken llm, canary token prompt, autoresearch, acceptance gate agent, evaluator integrity, in-toto agent, code search skill_proposal_evaluate) plus ~25 gh api lookups; 13 WebSearch queries; 14 WebFetch reads of the closest papers/repos; verified the cited leak issues one by one.
harness-owns-the-test.justification: Hermetic's framing is the best in its batch — "admissibility before acceptance", "the receipt is the interface", tri-state valid/invalid/infra-error with reason codes, and honeytokens that turn evaluator overfitting into a string match — and its diagnosis (every Camp-B leak is the evaluator living in the proposer's writable view) is correct and verifiable (autoresearch#599, dgm#35, HyperAgents#39, AHE#15, pi-autoresearch#81 all check out). But component-level novelty is thin and the design's competitor list omits the closest prior art on its exact mechanisms: RewardHackingAgents (Dec 2025) already runs hash-locked evaluators + train-data deny + a trusted reference metric and measures ~50% spontaneous tamper attempts; BenchJack (Berkeley) already red-teams graders with an 8-pattern flaw taxonomy and an iterative patch loop; "Auditing Harness Tampering" (2609.00069) already ships a seeded tampered-vs-benign corpus on HyperAgents/DGM/AFlow with 7 obligation classes; Fraegis and the Reward Hacking Benchmark already measure evaluator-tampering rates (13 frontier models, 0–13.9%), which falsifies the paper's claim that the field "has only anecdotes" for spontaneous rates; astrogilda's artifact-binding v1 (verifier_digest, JCS-canonical signed manifest, verified/failed/not-established) plus in-toto #570/#588, NovaFabric's signed evidence capsules, Attested Intelligence's patent-pending hash-chained receipts and Microsoft AGT's offline-verifiable receipts already occupy the receipt-and-offline-verifier slot; the #599 thread itself designed the ExperimentReceipt with four assurance tiers, PR #623 already adds an integrity log, and the #599 author ships aetherproof. What is genuinely new is the in-loop, per-candidate composition (sealed bundle + execution-evidence probes + honeytokens + signed receipt + adapters + a gym that scores the acceptor's confusion matrix) and the honeytoken-in-scorer trick, which I could not find anywhere. Defensibility is the weak axis: the isolation primitive is commodity (bwrap/Docker/Harbor/Inspect), SkillOpt maintainers are already landing scorer/judge separation (#270), a per-task gate (#222) and tool-aware replay (#227) in-tree, Anthropic's claude plugin eval already gives sealed with/without runs for skills and can add thresholds/receipts in one release, DeepSeek Harness explicitly plans its own evaluator contract, and the in-toto predicate registry is crowded (#549 closed, #554 open with 25 comments, #588 in review). The durable assets are the incident-seeded scenario corpus and a cross-seam conformance suite, both slow to build for 1–3 people. Net: a strong integration and positioning play with one small mechanistic novelty, sitting on ground that better-resourced substrates and standards bodies are already moving onto.

prior_art.name: RewardHackingAgents: Benchmarking Evaluation Integrity for LLM ML-Engineering Agents (Yonas650, arXiv 2603.11337)
prior_art.overlap: Three ML tasks with editable train/eval scripts; four trust regimes (mutable, evalhashlock = hash-locked evaluator, train_deny, full_locked); a trusted reference metric recomputed from pristine external code; per-episode hack_family tags (eval_tamper_only, train_on_test); measures ~50% spontaneous evaluator-tampering attempts (TinyLlama/Qwen) and 25–31% overhead for full_locked. This is Hermetic's admissibility + evidence + spontaneous-rate story as a Dec-2025 benchmark (1 star, unmaintained), not a drop-in runtime, and it is uncited.

Confirmed: no public artifact ('cannot be released'), tied to their prompt-optimization loop, no hash-bound receipts. Hermetic correctly positions itself as the runnable reference, but PROCTOR owns the vocabulary including the word 'hermetic'.

prior_art.name: Auditing Harness Tampering in Self-Improving Agents (arXiv 2609.00069)
prior_art.overlap: Defines harness tampering across functional roles x seven obligations (measurement validity, representational fidelity, procedural integrity, authorization, protected-artifact integrity, provenance, required-set completeness); builds 1,765 classification / 1,801 localization samples by seeding matched tampered-benign edit pairs into real HyperAgents/DGM/AFlow trajectories; benchmarks LLM auditors (Opus 5 90.4% classification). Post-hoc audit, no runtime enforcement — but it is the seeded-tampering corpus Hermetic's gym T1–T7 proposes to build, and it is uncited.

prior_art.name: BenchJack: Systematically Auditing AI Agent Benchmarks (Berkeley, arXiv 2605.12673)
prior_art.overlap: Automated red-teaming that drives coding agents to find grader exploits (answer keys shipped with tests, hijacking the evaluator process, eval() on untrusted input, judge prompt injection); 8 flaw patterns, 219 flaws across 10 benchmarks; iterative propose-hack-then-patch loop cuts hackable rate from ~100% to <10%. fatal_flaws: Component-level novelty is close to zero and the competitor list hides it: sealed grader (RSI-Exam/AI4AI/Inspect/Harbor/PROCTOR/SEAL), hash-locked evaluator + trusted reference metric + spontaneous tamper rate (RewardHackingAgents, Dec 2025), signed receipts with offline verifier and in-toto carriage (astrogilda artifact-binding v1 and AEE PR #588, NovaFabric, Attested Intelligence, Microsoft AGT), execution-evidence receipt with assurance tiers (the #599 thread itself, PR #623, aetherproof), seeded tampering corpus and grader red-teaming (Auditing Harness Tampering 2609.00069, BenchJack, Fraegis), and the gate (PACE/SEA). None of RewardHackingAgents, BenchJack, 2609.00069, Fraegis, RHB, artifact-binding or NovaFabric appear in the design's nearest-competitors section; a reviewer finds all of them in one afternoon and the 'none of this exists' thesis collapses to 'nobody has composed it'.

Research claim (2) is false as stated: the field has measured spontaneous evaluator tampering, not just anecdotes — Reward Hacking Benchmark (13 frontier models, 0–13.9%, including tampering with evaluation-relevant functions), RewardHackingAgents (~50% attempts for small models), AI4AI-Bench (43% regressions, self-reported-metadata exploits), SciIntegrity-Bench (34.2%), plus the 2609.00069 corpus. Worse, RHB's 0% for Claude Sonnet 4.5 means the design's own falsifier (<2% spontaneous non-admissible rate makes the runtime unnecessary) may fire for the builder's primary agent, and the urgency claim rests on seven repos' sloppiness rather than agent behavior.

Claim (1) is near-tautological on the proposed gym: T1–T7 are the seven incidents the runtime was reverse-engineered from, so 'exploit-accept rate to approximately 0' is training-on-test; and the existing-defense arm is likely to clear the 90% falsifier for Docker/read-only setups (DGM-style, AI4AI-style) on the tampering scenarios, leaving the paper's headline result about autoresearch-pattern loops with no boundary at all — a systems fix, not a finding.

The 'closes the seven leaks by construction' guarantee only holds mechanically for the training-loop surface (optimizer steps from optimizer state, model hash, val fingerprint). For surfaces 2–4 — skills, memory, harness code, the 900k-star audience — the only 'execution evidence' is an activation detector via hooks (Claude Code Skill tool_use, Hermes skill_view), which an agent bypasses by reading the file with Bash; the design lists this as an open question while marketing the same 'sealed' word for both. RewardHackingAgents' 25–31% overhead for full lock plus a mandatory A-vs-A' control arm also makes the <=25% overhead falsifier likely to fail on GPU loops (5-minute autoresearch runs double).

Defensibility over 12 months is weak by construction: the isolation primitive is commodity; SkillOpt maintainers are landing scorer/judge separation (#270), per-task gating (#222), tool-aware replay (#227) and revert (#280) in-tree, pre-empting both the Sleep backend and the scorer-blind channel; Anthropic already ships sealed with/without skill evals and can add thresholds/receipts in a weekly release; DeepSeek Harness has publicly reserved the evaluator contract for itself; OpenClaw's crabpot already exercises skill_proposal_evaluate as a fixture; the in-toto registry has #549 closed, #554 open with 25 comments and #588 in review, so 'file the artifact-acceptance predicate' is a queue, not a moat; and a patent application on hash-chained governance receipts (Attested Intelligence) sits on the receipt-as-product positioning.

Honeytokens and the scorer-blind mediator are in tension with adoption: nonces only catch verbatim copying (admitted), while blinding the proposer to scorer wording removes the rich textual feedback that gives GEPA/SkillOpt-lineage optimizers their sample efficiency; SkillOpt's own in-tree PR chose 'separate' over 'blind'. The leak detector therefore has low recall on the failure it targets and a real power cost on the loops most likely to adopt it.

The trust model does not fit the single-user CLI audience: two-party approval for evaluator changes and a signing key 'outside the proposer's domain' have no second party and no second machine when the human runs Claude Code with --dangerously-skip-permissions on a laptop; on macOS (the builder's own machine) the runtime can only issue the weakest tier, so the killer demo's closing line ('the one thing your agent cannot touch') is false on the platform most users run.

Scope versus team: ten subsystems, seven loop adapters, six harness adapters, a version-pinned conformance suite, three standards efforts, a gym and a paper in three months for 1–3 people against substrates shipping 947 commits per four days; the differentiated core (bundle, runtime, receipt, leakscan, gym) is three of the ten components, and the two-week MVP already lists eight deliverables.

Evidence hygiene: SkillOpt#154 is mis-described (it is about programmatic-only mining Goodharting intent into proxy rules, not verbatim regex copying), sia#36 is an open PR not an issue, and 'zero third-party evaluators' on OpenClaw's seam is true only modulo a test fixture — small errors, but the entire pitch is 'seven documented leaks' and a reviewer will check.
improvements: Cut v0.1 to the surface where admissibility is mechanical: training/optimization loops (autoresearch, pi-autoresearch, SIA, AI4AI-style). Ship hermetic seal/run/verify, the four execution-evidence probes, tri-state results and signed receipts there first, and label skill/memory/harness surfaces honestly as 'activation-evidence only' profiles for a later release instead of calling both 'sealed'.

Adopt rather than invent the receipt: use astrogilda's artifact-binding v1 manifest (verifier_digest, source_archive_digest, JCS canonicalization, verified/failed/not-established) as the receipt core, add the loop-aware fields (candidate lineage, declared vs actual diff digests, execution-evidence counters, reason codes, assurance tier) as an extension, and contribute to in-toto #570/#588 instead of filing a new 'artifact-acceptance' predicate; add EvalPort ResultSet and agentskills.io evals/evals.json exports to the converter list.

Rewrite research claim (2) as a replication and extension: measure spontaneous non-admissible rates under observe-only receipts across five real loops x three frontier agents and compare against RHB, RewardHackingAgents, AI4AI and 2609.00069 baselines, pre-registering that frontier Claude may be near zero; the contribution becomes 'rates in real loops with receipted ground truth', not 'first measurement'.

Make the gym adversarial and held-out rather than a fixed catalog of the seven incidents: run BenchJack-style automated red-teaming against the sealed bundle itself, seed scenarios from the 2609.00069 tampered/benign corpus and Fraegis tasks, and report recall on scenarios withheld from the runtime's design so claim (1) is not train-on-test.

Amortize the noise floor: run the A-vs-A' control arm once per campaign per bundle (not per candidate), publish overhead per assurance tier and per surface, and replace the flat <=25% overhead falsifier with per-surface budgets; otherwise GPU loops will switch the gate off exactly as SEA's ALG4 was.

Replace 'scorer-blind' with 'scorer-separated with leak metering': keep full failure traces, redact only scorer literals, rubric strings and task ids, and measure in the gym how much proposer power each redaction level costs; coordinate with SkillOpt PR #270 (the in-tree analogue) rather than shipping a competing backend.

Ship the Claude Code hooks pack as a standalone first-week product before any loop adapter: InstructionsLoaded load/adherence receipts, PreToolUse deny on sealed paths, Stop session receipts with cost. It is the one surface with zero competition, needs no loop, and gives adoption data before committing to six more adapters.

Fix the single-user trust model: default the sealed tier to Docker/colima on macOS and refuse to print 'sealed' for sandbox-exec; replace two-party approval with 'evaluator changes require a signature from an identity not present on the proposer host' (e.g. Sigstore keyless with the human's GitHub identity), which a solo user can actually satisfy.

Add cheap orthogonal admissibility checks the prior art shows matter: a zero-observable-delta / no-op reason code (Phantom Guardrails), a concealment axis in the gym (Fraegis), and BenchJack's eval()-on-untrusted-input and judge-prompt-injection flaw classes as scenarios.

Invest in the two assets substrates cannot copy quickly and publish them in month 1, not month 3: the incident-to-scenario corpus as a Harbor task family with planted ground truth, and the version-pinned seam conformance suite (deny stops the write; timeout fails closed; promoted artifact loads) for Claude Code, OpenClaw, dsh, Hermes and pi.

Clean the evidence base: re-verify every cited issue (correct SkillOpt#154, mark sia#36 as a PR), keep docs/incidents.md with permalinks and quotes, and add the uncited prior art (RewardHackingAgents, BenchJack, 2609.00069, Fraegis, RHB, artifact-binding, NovaFabric, EvalPort) to the related-work table with explicit deltas.
harness-owns-the-test.best_idea_to_steal: Honeytokens planted inside the sealed scorer, rubric and data index — nonces re-rolled per bundle build that exist nowhere else — with a leakscan over candidate diffs and hook-visible proposer context, so evaluator overfitting (the SkillOpt-style 'copied the judge into the skill' failure) becomes a provable string match with a signed leak finding instead of a suspicion. It is a weekend to add to any existing gate (SkillOpt, Self-Harness, Reef decide, GEPA accept), is harness-agnostic, composes with the tri-state receipt (invalid + reason code LEAK_HONEYTOKEN), and I found no prior art applying canary tokens to scorer leakage in self-improvement loops; PROCTOR's canaries are unpassable cases and HackProbe's secret core is a probe bank, neither of which proves that the proposer saw the scorer.

harness-owns-the-test.lens: FEASIBILITY — 1–3 people, frontier-API models only, no GPU cluster, 3 months to a credible v1 plus the 5-minute killer demo; every technical assumption checked against live docs/source/issues on 2026-09-14.
harness-owns-the-test.justification: The core is right and cheap: a sealed scorer that recomputes the metric from the produced artifact, bound by hash into a signed receipt with a tri-state result, closes all four autoresearch#599 exploits and the seven documented leaks by construction, and nothing shipping does it as a drop-in (GitHub search for the niche returns zero repos; OpenClaw's evaluator seam has no third-party implementation; the leak issues are all open with 0–1 comments). That kernel plus two presets, a receipt verifier and a T1–T7 gym on a CPU-measurable pi-autoresearch target is 3–5 person-weeks and would be a credible v1. Everything above the kernel is where it dies for a 1–3 person team in 3 months. (1) The MVP plan packs 11 components, 8 loop adapters, 6 harness adapters and a TypeScript plugin for a 389k-star codebase into 14 days; the roadmap adds three standards bodies and a 15×5×3×3×5 = 3,375-loop-run experiment on $3–6k (a pi-autoresearch loop with Claude Code costs $5–20; AHE-lite on Harbor and nanochat need GPUs the builder does not have). (2) The technical claims that carry the demo are over-stated: execution-evidence probes read optimizer state and model hashes in the candidate's own process (the #599 reproducer literally does `optimizer.state['p']['step']`), so an adversarial proposer forges them in one line; the load-bearing mechanism is sealed recomputation, which requires changing train.py's contract to emit a checkpoint and still cannot stop checkpoint reuse or contamination from public val data. Honeytokens planted in a scorer the proposer cannot read can only fire when Hermetic's own redaction leaks; they cannot detect SkillOpt#154 (where the judge is intentionally shown) and are paraphrase-blind, so the 'first mechanical detector for that class' claim is false. (3) The paired gate for skills/memory is SEA's ALG4 replayed: the design's own simulation (reproduced: +10pp lift detected 10% at N=40, 39% at N=160) plus a control arm, a 60-probe canary and cross-family spot checks means $50–300 of agent runs per decision returning 'inconclusive' most of the time; the '$3.12 / 3% of loop cost' figures in the examples are not derivable. (4) Harness surfaces are partly fictional: Claude Code's InstructionsLoaded fires only for CLAUDE.md/.claude/rules with file_path/memory_type/load_reason — no MEMORY.md, no skills, no bytes-loaded/truncation — so the #82056 receipt cannot be built from it; the dsh hook bridge documents that updatedInput and updatedToolOutput are 'logged + warned but not honored' and InstructionsLoaded is unsupported, so 'the same hooks.json runs unmodified under dsh' is untrue for every replay/receipt feature; substrates move at 947 commits/4 days (Hermes) and 14 pre-release tags/12 days (dsh), making a six-harness conformance suite a full-time job. (5) Isolation on the builder's own platform is the weak tier: macOS has no bwrap/unshare, sandbox-exec is deprecated, the Docker daemon is off, Ubuntu 24.04 needs a sudo-installed AppArmor profile for bwrap, and sealing needs a separate OS user, so `pip install && hermetic init` yields 'self-attested' receipts — the tier the #599 thread already dismissed. (6) Distribution assumptions: karpathy/autoresearch has not been pushed since 2026-03-26, Karpathy never replied on #599 and closed the noise-floor PR #560 unmerged, so issue replies reach forks, not upstream. The team can ship a reduced kernel and a reduced demo (minutes 1, 2, 4 and a scripted-proposer gym) with probability ~0.6; the design as written, with its gate, cassette, canary, spot-check, six adapters and paper matrix, ships with probability well under 0.2; blended ~0.3.

fatal_flaws: Execution-evidence probes are in-process and forgeable, yet the design sells them as the 'unmistakable' detector. The #599 reproducer's receipt reads `optimizer.state[...]['step']` and hashes `model.state_dict()` inside the candidate's own process; a proposer that owns train.py sets step=688 and adds noise to weights in two lines. The only robust mechanism is sealed recomputation of val_bpb on a checkpoint the candidate must emit — which changes the agent-editable train.py contract, cannot stop the candidate loading a cached earlier checkpoint, and cannot stop val contamination because autoresearch's val shard is public data the agent can pre-download. The gym's T1–T7 '10/10 detected' therefore measures exploits the recompute trivially closes, not the adversarial proposer Anthropic's essay documents (label exfiltration via scoring queries, reasoning about grader suspicion).

Honeytokens-in-a-sealed-scorer cannot detect the SkillOpt#154 class. If the proposer cannot read the scorer, a nonce can only appear in its diff via a Hermetic redaction bug or sandbox escape — the mechanism is a self-test of hermetic-channel, not a detector of judge-overfitting. In SkillOpt/GEPA the judge is shown on purpose (that textual feedback is why they beat RL with 35x fewer rollouts), so a scorer-blind channel either does not apply or removes the signal that makes the loop work, and paraphrase defeats string matching either way. The 'first mechanical detector for SkillOpt#154' and 'leaks made provable' claims are false as stated.

The paired gate for skills/memory (surfaces 2–3) reproduces SEA's switched-off ALG4. The design's own simulation (re-run: +10pp lift detected 10% at N=40, 39% at N=160, +30pp 98% at N=40) means a real skill edit needs 100–200 paired cases; each pair is two full agent runs (claude plugin eval: cases × runs × 2 arms), plus a 20-pair A-vs-A' control arm, a 60-probe canary in both arms with a cross-family judge, and spot checks — $50–300 of API spend per decision that returns 'inconclusive' most of the time. The example receipts' 'cost_usd: 3.12' and the demo's 'gate cost 3% of loop cost' are not derivable for anything but the scalar autoresearch path.

Two load-bearing harness surfaces do not exist as described (verified in docs/source today). Claude Code's InstructionsLoaded fires only for CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/*.md and carries file_path/memory_type/load_reason — no MEMORY.md, no skills, no bytes-available/bytes-loaded/truncation — so the '#82056 receipt: MEMORY.md 18,422/18,422 bytes loaded, complete' in the killer demo cannot be produced from it. DeepSeek Harness's Claude Code bridge README states updatedInput is 'logged + warned but not honored', updatedToolOutput 'unsupported', InstructionsLoaded and 22 other events ignored, and {continue:false} has no run-level effect — so 'the same hooks.json runs unmodified under dsh and Codex' is false for every replay, rewrite and receipt feature; only deny/context/stop-continue survive.

Scope is 5–10x what 1–3 people can build: the 14-day MVP lists a sealed runtime with three isolation tiers, Ed25519 receipts, two presets, four reproduced exploits, honeytokens + leakscan, a Claude Code hooks pack, an e-process gate with CTHS and control arm, a 10-scenario gym runnable with Claude Code and Codex as proposers, an OpenClaw TypeScript plugin, a hash-chained ledger, docs and a PyPI/npm release — realistically 6–8 person-weeks. The 3-month roadmap adds Hermes, dsh, pi/Prime, Reef, SkillOpt and Harbor adapters, a canary bundle, spot-check module, cassette mining, in-toto/EEE/OTel/agentskills.io filings, a six-harness version-pinned conformance suite (Hermes: 947 commits in 4 days; dsh: 14 pre-release tags in 12 days), and a 15×5×3×3×5 experiment (~3,375 loop runs, two of the five loops needing GPUs) on a $3–6k budget. None of this survives contact with the calendar.

The default assurance tier on real developer machines is the one the design's own sources dismiss. On the builder's macOS there is no bwrap/unshare, sandbox-exec is marked DEPRECATED in its man page, and the Docker daemon is not running; on Ubuntu 24.04 bwrap needs a sudo-installed AppArmor profile; sealing the bundle from the proposer's user requires a second OS user and a key-holding daemon (sudo at install). So 'pip install hermetic && hermetic init' produces 'self-attested' receipts — the tier the #599 thread (aetherproof, safal207) already argued is not evidence — and the demo's offline `hermetic verify` proves only that some key signed the JSON, not that the proposer could not reach that key.

The cassette/replay component is built on numbers its own measurements contradict. With the first non-idempotent call at 0–1 in every recorded session and the Replay Gap's 74–96% first-action divergence even for same-model controls, every 'replay' is a full re-run from a git snapshot and A-vs-A' diverges at step ~1; 'first_divergence_step: 22' and 'stability 3/3' in the schemas are fantasy. What actually works — git snapshot + transcript prefix + the session's own test command as grader — is exactly claude plugin eval's history_file + scaffold_script, which requires ≥2.1.269 (builder is on 2.1.258), strips user hooks inside eval so the updatedToolOutput replay mocks must ship inside the plugin under test (asymmetric arms), and costs cases × runs × 2 agent runs.

Distribution and research bets rest on dead or unresponsive targets. karpathy/autoresearch has had no push since 2026-03-26, Karpathy never replied on #599 (5 comments, none his) and closed the noise-floor PR #560 unmerged, so 'a public issue reply linking the drop-in' reaches forks only. The paper's headline (spontaneous non-admissible rate) is a falsifier the design itself flags could come back near zero, the primary venue (ICLR 2027 RSI workshop) does not yet exist, and the 'paired with/without' evidence for skill edits will mostly be 'inconclusive' at any affordable N — the null-effect literature (CTA +0.3pp, SkillsBench 0 for LLM-written skills) predicts the gym's honest-candidate arm will show no lift to measure false-invalid against.
improvements: Cut v1 to 'hermetic-core' and ship it in 3–4 weeks: `seal` / `run` / `verify` / receipt with the tri-state result and reason codes, sealed recomputation of the metric from an emitted artifact, the autoresearch preset (checkpoint contract) and the pi-autoresearch preset (measure.sh moved into the bundle, KEEP refused without an admissible receipt), the T1–T7 gym driven by a scripted 'malicious proposer' arm, and a hash-chained ledger + `report`. Move gate, cassette, canary, spot-check, standards filings and every adapter except two to a clearly labelled v2 track.

Replace 'execution-evidence probes' with a checkpoint contract plus recompute, and label the counters honestly as accidental-shortcut detectors: mount the workspace read-only except an output dir, forbid reading files older than run start (kills checkpoint reuse), hold back a private val slice the loop never sees (RSI-Exam style) and print visible→sealed gap per candidate, and make 'metric recomputed by sealed scorer' the only admissibility condition that carries the gate.

Make the loop's threat model explicit per surface: for autoresearch-class loops (scalar, recompute-able) claim closure by construction; for skill/memory/harness loops claim only 'tamper-evident + activation-receipted' in v1 and run the acceptance gate in observe-only mode with a printed price list — the cheapest arm hermes#96704 asked for ('needs no model runs, numbers within a day').

Drop honeytokens inside sealed scorers. For loops that intentionally show the judge (SkillOpt, GEPA, RHI), plant visible-but-irrelevant canary criteria in the rubric and count how often candidates satisfy them — that is the SkillOpt#154 detector — and run one real experiment: the utility cost of a scorer-blind feedback channel on SkillOpt/GEPA (held-out delta with rationale shown vs redacted). That is a publishable number the field lacks.

Pick two adapters for v1 and do them natively: the Claude Code hooks pack (the builder's own harness; PreToolUse deny on Write/Edit paths, `if: Bash(...)` guards acknowledged as leaky, PreToolUse matcher `Skill` for activation, InstructionsLoaded hash-on-load for CLAUDE.md/rules only) and the OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate plugin (the empty 389k-star seam, with internal errors converted to explicit block). Do dsh later as a native Cordis plugin on tools/pre-execute + tools/post-execute, never through the hook bridge.

Budget the gate honestly and raise power cheaply: use continuous per-instance signals (tests passed count, steps-to-done, tokens, sealed-scorer scalar) rather than binary pass/fail in the e-process; make the control arm a one-time per-corpus calibration instead of per-decision; publish 'evals-per-decision and $ per decision at target power' as a table in the README before anyone runs it.

Fix the demo to what is real: minute 3 becomes pi-autoresearch on a CPU-measurable target (a Python benchmark repo) with the four exploits injected by a scripted proposer arm and a separate unprompted Claude Code/Codex arm reported honestly even if the spontaneous rate is 0; minute 5 drops the MEMORY.md byte-count receipt and shows the OpenClaw block plus a CLAUDE.md load-hash receipt; rent one GPU-hour for a single real nanochat run rather than the FakeModel gist.

Redirect first adoption from autoresearch (unpushed since March, maintainer silent) to Reef #356/#357/#358 (open, 0 comments, maintainers explicitly asking for evaluation gates, recipe API ready) and to SkillOpt#155 (maintainers endorsed with binding constraints: container not worktree, pass/fail/inconclusive, execution off by default) — one merged PR beats ten issue replies.

Shrink the paper to what $3–6k buys: 2 loops (pi-autoresearch, SkillOpt-on-SkillsBench-slice) × 2 proposers × 7 tampering + 3 overfitting scenarios × 3 seeds ≈ 120 runs, plus 40 unprompted runs for the spontaneous rate, plus the counterfactual re-scoring of public ledgers (autoresearch #448/#596 results.tsv, SkillOpt rejected buffers, AHE change_manifests) which costs no agent runs at all and is the safest publishable result.

Resolve the name and key custody now: PyPI 'hermetic' and 'sealbox' are free but npm 'hermetic' is taken (2023) — publish as `hermetic-eval` / `@hermetic-eval/openclaw`; state on every receipt that a single-operator install has one key and no second party, and gate 'sealed-runtime' tier on an actual separate OS user or container, refusing to emit it otherwise.
harness-owns-the-test.best_idea_to_steal: Admissibility before acceptance as a data contract: every score becomes a signed receipt = sha256(evaluator, hidden data, candidate, final artifact) with a tri-state result (valid / invalid-artifact / infra-error) and machine-readable reason codes, the metric is recomputed by a sealed scorer from the produced artifact rather than parsed from the candidate's stdout, and every downstream gate (PACE, Reef decide, OpenClaw evaluator, ledgers) consumes receipts instead of raw numbers — so 'the number your loop keeps is now something anyone can verify offline' is a five-line drop-in for autoresearch-class loops and a stable interface every other acceptance mechanism can adopt without changing its statistics.

artifact-lifecycle.lens: NOVELTY vs the landscape and the RSI prior art (rsi_digest.md), including the three sibling designs (Hermetic, Turnstile, Pawl), scored as: how much of Clade is genuinely new AND defensible over the next 12 months given Hermes/Prime/Reef/SkillOpt/DSH and the skill-package-manager cohort ship weekly. Method: read landscape_digest, rsi_digest, synthesis v1/v2, both gap analyses, the sibling designs; 25+ gh repo/issue searches; 10 WebSearch queries; READMEs of qvr, kendex, skills-lock, skillpm, AGENTS.lock, crew, skillshub, skill-provenance, RecallWeave, agent-memory-lifecycle, cultivar; abstracts of A-MAC, Skilldex, SLIM, SKILL.nb, GLOVE, MERIT, Catastrophic Remembering, Grounding Agent Memory; agentskills.io spec; PyPI/npm/crates checks for all name candidates; verification that hermes#12238 (r=38), #96704, #105770, #107914, #416, claude-code#82056 (48 comments), #92998, prime#1208, SkillOpt#155, reef#356 exist as cited.
artifact-lifecycle.justification: Clade is roughly 70% Pawl by content (identical receipt/candidate/evidence-pair/ledger/cassette formats, identical Tier 0-4 cascade, PACE e-process + SEA CTHS spend, the same five-harness hook adapters, snapshot+undo with round-trip test, the same killer-demo minutes 1-2, the same standards filings), re-skinned with package-manager vocabulary. Its research claims are the two gap-analysis items the other siblings left unclaimed (scientist gap #10 'stale-artifact retirement under drift' and safety gap #10 'when not to evolve') plus Turnstile's null-effect audit as C1. The net-new surface is (a) environment assertions extracted from artifact text and probed at load ('staleness is dependency resolution'), (b) clade-pooled attribution over a lineage/federation, (c) a VOI write trigger, (d) dormant/stale/retired/yanked states and a per-environment lockfile, (e) a receipt-carrying federation with per-environment overlays. Each of these has close prior art: (a) Grounding Agent Memory 2609.11060 (Microsoft, Sep 10; already requested for Hermes in #107914), GLOVE 2601.19249 (active probing for memory-environment realignment), SKILL.nb 2606.08049 (validation gates, fallback when drift invalidates), and agentskills.io's free-text `compatibility` field; (b) HGM's CMP, and SLIM 2605.10923 already retires skills on leave-one-out marginal contribution; (c) A-MAC 2603.04549 (five-signal memory admission incl. future utility), MERIT 2609.05441 (cost-aware memory value); (d) OpenClaw Workshop's pending/applied/rejected/quarantined/stale ledger, SafeEvolve's admit-at-write/revoke-at-reuse, Hermes curator states, Reef canary/shadow/rollback, RecallWeave TTL/forgetting; (e) FederatedSkill 2606.03143, snapsynapse/skill-provenance (hash identity that travels with the bundle). The 'package manager for skills' namespace itself is crowded and moving fast: qvr (lockfile-first, immutable SHA installs, scan, 'trace every run'), kendex (76 stars, outdated + provenance across 8 harnesses), skills-lock/skillpm (content-hash lockfile, audit, outdated, ci --frozen), AGENTS.lock, crew, skillshub, Skilldex (arXiv 2604.16911), and Agent Plugins 1.0's FUTURE_CONSIDERATIONS explicitly defers registry/provenance/auto-update/dependencies, meaning the AAIF/Anthropic/Google consortium will likely standardize exactly the lockfile/registry semantics Clade invents. What is honestly new is the composition (lifecycle over self-written artifacts and memory, not installed third-party skills; assertion scope tags doubling as scope lint; overlays-instead-of-merge; receipt quorum) and the C2 drift testbed. That composition is real but thin, its two headline mechanisms have structural problems (pooling masks per-version regressions; VOI with a ~0 base-rate prior deadlocks on cold start), the name collides with 'Claude' and is taken on PyPI/npm, and Hermes (#107914), Letta MemFS, OpenClaw and the package-manager cohort are each one release from absorbing the visible pieces. Score 4/10: a defensible feature set for Pawl, not a defensible standalone product or a distinct paper.

prior_art.name: Pawl (sibling design in research/designs_partial.json)
prior_art.overlap: Same receipt/candidate/evidence-pair/verdict/ledger/cassette schemas, same Tier 0-4 cascade (lint+DLP, load/read/followed receipts, mechanical outcomes, sandbox replay with A-vs-A' floor, safety canary), same PACE e-process + CTHS spend, same k-of-n floor and simulation numbers, same path-level write authority, same snapshot+undo with round-trip test, same seven adapters and standards filings, same demo minutes 1-2. Pawl even states 'one content hash makes the gate, the undo, the funnel and the attribution the same ledger' — Clade's 'one ledger' insight verbatim. Clade's delta: assertions/outdated, VOI trigger, dormant/stale/retired/yanked + lockfile, federation.

prior_art.name: try-agora/qvr (quiver)
prior_art.overlap: Git-native, lockfile-first package manager for agent skills: resolve→lock→install(immutable, SHA-keyed)→scan→symlink→reproduce→observe; 'lock every byte, trace every run'. Targets installed third-party skills, not agent-written artifacts or memory; no outcome attribution or staleness.

prior_art.name: vanillagreencom/kendex
prior_art.overlap: Package manager for agents/skills/hooks across 8 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, Gemini, Copilot...): outdated detection, 'see where an installed package came from', adopt existing files, per-tool overrides. Installed customizations only; no lifecycle on learned artifacts.

prior_art.name: comountainclimber/skillpm + luisalima/skills-lock + luml-ai/AGENTS.lock + with-logic/crew + EYH0602/skillshub
prior_art.overlap: Five more 'npm for skills' tools in six months: content-hash lockfiles (skills.lock / skills-lock.json / AGENTS.lock), `audit`, `outdated` (pin vs origin HEAD), `ci --frozen`, taps, multi-agent linking. The package-manager vocabulary and lockfile semantics Clade proposes are commodity; none covers self-written artifacts, activation or attribution.

prior_art.name: Skilldex: A Package Manager and Registry for Agent Skill Packages (arXiv 2604.16911)
prior_art.overlap: Published package manager + metadata-only registry for skill packages with conformance scoring, skillsets, scope tiers, MCP support; open-source TypeScript CLI. No staleness/retirement/attribution, but it owns the academic 'package manager for skills' framing.

prior_art.name: snapsynapse/skill-provenance
prior_art.overlap: Version identity + SHA-256 bundle integrity that travels with the skill across sessions/registries/platforms; 'staleness detection' (evals stale relative to bundle version); GitHub Action validator; cites a registry-diff finding that 14.2% of instruction changes had no version movement. Overlaps Clade's content-hash identity and manifest sidecar; staleness semantics differ (version drift, not environment).

prior_art.name: Grounding Agent Memory: Environment-Probing Curation (arXiv 2609.11060) + hermes-agent#107914
prior_art.overlap: Gives the background curator read-only world tools to check, scope and refresh candidate memories against the live environment before commit (stale knowledge after drift, over-generalized scope). Hermes already has an open request to adopt it. Clade's assertion probing at load is the deterministic, per-load variant of the same idea; Hermes can ship this in-tree.

prior_art.name: GLOVE: Global Verifier for LLM Memory-Environment Realignment (arXiv 2601.19249)
prior_art.overlap: Active probing to detect inconsistencies between retrieved memories and fresh observations; verifies and updates memory without ground truth under controlled environmental drift on web/planning/control benchmarks. Same problem as Clade's 'stale' state; LLM-driven rather than assertion-based.

prior_art.name: SKILL.nb: Selective Formalization and Gated Execution for Durable Agent Workflows (arXiv 2606.08049)
prior_art.overlap: Versioned workflow artifacts with validation gates per step; execution runs code only when gates validate and falls back when drift invalidates the executable realization; execution evidence decides release/retire/demote. Closest prior art to 'an assertion fails on probe → stale, no statistics'.

prior_art.name: A-MAC: Adaptive Memory Admission Control (arXiv 2603.04549)
prior_art.overlap: Decides whether to write a memory from five interpretable factors (future utility, factual confidence, novelty, recency, content-type prior) with rule-based features + one LLM utility call, learned per domain. This is Clade's VOI trigger minus explicit dollar accounting; also see MERIT 2609.05441 (marginal utility of memory per dollar) and 'Learning What to Remember' 2606.12945.

prior_art.name: SLIM: Dynamic Skill Lifecycle Management for Agentic RL (arXiv 2605.10923)
prior_art.overlap: Retain / retire (negligible contribution after sufficient exposure, via leave-one-skill-out validation) / expand skill bank on persistent failures; treats the active skill set as non-monotonic. Outcome-based retirement of skills already exists in research; Clade's retire state is Ratchet's rule with pooling.

prior_art.name: Ratchet (arXiv 2605.22148) and The Blind Curator (arXiv 2607.07436)
prior_art.overlap: Supply Clade's retirement math (c(s) ≤ −τ after N_min=100, non-divergence floor) and the judge false-pass cliff. Clade adds pooling to reach N_min; the math is not Clade's.

prior_art.name: Huxley-Gödel Machine CMP (arXiv 2510.21614)
prior_art.overlap: Clade-metaproductivity: pool Bernoulli outcomes over a node's whole subtree to decide which lineage to expand. Clade transplants this to skill lineages; the gap analysis already flagged this transplant as 'unexploited', but HGM uses CMP to choose what to expand, not to certify that a specific version is safe to serve.

prior_art.name: SafeEvolve / SkillMisevo-Gym (arXiv 2608.12851)
prior_art.overlap: Two-boundary lifecycle for SKILL.md (admission audit at write: accept/repair/quarantine/reject with lineage; revocation at reuse: attribute later outcomes, retire on evidence, capacity-evict by utility−risk) with a GovernableStore proven on Claude Code/Codex/OpenClaw/Hermes. Clade adopts it directly and adds dormancy/staleness/federation.

prior_art.name: OpenClaw Skill Workshop (proposal lifecycle + skill_proposal_evaluate)
prior_art.overlap: Hash-bound proposal objects with pending/applied/rejected/quarantined/stale states, atomic generations, rollback metadata, append-only ledger with expectedRevisionHash, runtime usage receipts, evaluator envelope. Clade's quarantine/stale states and hash-bound candidates already exist here; Clade would be the missing evaluator plugin (as would Pawl).

prior_art.name: Hermes Agent (curator, skill_ledger, .usage.json, write_approval, skill_provenance, Skill Sync)
prior_art.overlap: Content-addressed before/after manifests in skill_ledger.jsonl, rollback, timestamp-aged active→stale→archived lifecycle, use_count telemetry, write-origin provenance, pins/ownership guards, staged approval, file-copy sharing. #12238 (r=38 'backup & version control for ~/.hermes') and #107914 (env-probing review) show Hermes is one release from shipping the visible half of Clade natively.

prior_art.name: Reef (Human-Agent-Society)
prior_art.overlap: Versioned immutable releases, canary/shadow routing, one-step rollback, propose→paired-evaluate→decide recipe API, rejected-proposal memory. Clade's canary→promoted→revert lifecycle maps onto it; Clade's plan is to ship as a Reef recipe, so Reef is prior art for the lifecycle shape.

prior_art.name: Letta MemFS / Context Repositories
prior_art.overlap: Git-backed memory filesystem: every memory edit versioned with commit messages, diff/rollback/audit, optional remote sync; 25k-star product. 'git for your agent's brain' (Clade's undo/log/diff for memory) is already shipping for Letta users.

prior_art.name: RecallWeave + shifujosh/agent-memory-lifecycle + aniket-deshkar/agent-memory-lifecycle
prior_art.overlap: Local-first memory lifecycle engines: identity, provenance, confidence, TTL, append-only integrity-chained log, dedupe, conflict detection, forgetting, compaction, verification (RecallWeave); proposed→confirmed→superseded/retracted/expired with evidence thresholds (shifujosh). Small (0-30 stars) but the 'memory lifecycle manager' framing is already populated.

prior_art.name: PACE (arXiv 2606.08106) and SEA (arXiv 2607.00871)
prior_art.overlap: The paired anytime-valid e-process on discordant pairs, NSF as a resting state, ACCEPT>NSF>REJECT>HOLD precedence and the CTHS δ_k schedule are lifted verbatim (as in Pawl). Not Clade's contribution.

prior_art.name: Agent Plugins 1.0 (AAIF / Anthropic / Google)
prior_art.overlap: Vendor-neutral plugin packaging that explicitly defers install, registries/package managers, provenance verification, plugin-to-plugin dependencies and auto-update to FUTURE_CONSIDERATIONS — i.e., the consortium intends to define the lockfile/registry/dependency semantics Clade proposes. Standardization threat, not a competitor today.

prior_art.name: FederatedSkill (arXiv 2606.03143) + SkillClaw + Hermes Collective Wisdom
prior_art.overlap: Federation of skills across users framed as federated learning; SkillClaw converges one skill per group with verifier off; Hermes shares by consent + file copy. Clade's receipt-carrying import with quarantine and per-environment overlays is a genuine extension, but the framing exists and the gap analysis already specified 'quarantine → local re-verification → per-environment forks'.

prior_art.name: Turnstile (sibling design)
prior_art.overlap: Clade's C1 (audit of N≥20 volunteer stores: dormant/stale/duplicated artifacts, median activation <10%) is Turnstile's null-effect audit run through receipts.

prior_art.name: pinecone-io/cultivar
prior_art.overlap: Pinecone DevRel tool to test Agent Skills across agents in sandboxes with graders — same ecosystem, and it owns the name 'Cultivar' (Clade's second name candidate). PyPI/npm 'cultivar' also taken.

prior_art.name: PyPI 'clade' (v4.1, build-process extraction tool) and npm 'clade'
prior_art.overlap: Both package names are taken; GitHub search for 'clade agent' returns repos where 'Clade' is a typo of 'Claude' (Clade.agent, clade-parallel), i.e., the name is phonetically/typographically confusable with Anthropic's trademark for a tool shipped as a Claude Code plugin.

fatal_flaws: It is Pawl with a package-manager coat of paint: ~70% of the text (all seven data formats, Tier 0-4, hooks adapters, e-process/CTHS/dispositions, undo, demo minutes 1-2, standards filings) is the sibling design verbatim; the genuinely new surface is assertions/outdated, a VOI trigger, three extra lifecycle states with a lockfile, and a month-3 federation. As a standalone entry it cannot be scored as 'new'; as a Pawl module it is a feature set, and the plan spends 3 months rebuilding what Pawl already specifies.

'Staleness is dependency resolution' breaks where packages and learned artifacts differ: package dependencies are declared, Clade's are regex/AST-inferred from prose. False-stale (a version mentioned as an example, a relative path) is admitted, but the deeper problem is coverage: local facts (paths, ports, binaries) are a minority of the staleness that matters (API semantics, repo refactors, changed preferences, model-version drift, 'learned helplessness' rules), and none of those has a probe. C2's 'assertion probes reach AUC ≥0.85' is unsupported, and the proposed drift testbed injects exactly the drift classes assertions can detect (tool versions, CLI flags, paths), so the validation is circular.

Clade pooling defeats the lifecycle's own purpose: pooling outcomes across versions of a lineage to reach N_min mixes the incumbent's good history with a bad candidate's, masking the per-version regressions the state machine exists to catch (gfpyc's v7 rewrite would be pooled with v1-v6's 38 sessions). HGM's CMP chooses which node to expand, not whether a specific node is safe to serve. The per-version posterior still has the sample-size problem; the other lever, federation pooling, is month 3, needs identity, and adds an unvalidated per-environment discount; Simpson's paradox is acknowledged and unresolved.

The VOI trigger is degenerate at cold start: expected benefit = recurrence × class base-rate lift (≈0 for LLM-written artifacts, per the design's own prior) × value, so almost nothing is ever written; the prior is updated 'from the store's own promoted history' but promotion requires canary evidence that requires writes. This reproduces the starvation failure the design elsewhere calls the field's dominant gate failure (hermes#105770), and A-MAC already covers multi-factor admission without the deadlock.

Canary alternation, the only source of randomized pairs (and therefore of any non-advisory verdict), does not work on the builder's own harness: skill discovery on Claude Code runs before SessionStart hooks, so the symlink swap applies from the next session at best (admitted as an open question). Memory alternation is off by default. The MVP therefore ships an e-process that will have no valid pairs to consume on Claude Code, and the 'INCONCLUSIVE' outcome becomes structural, not statistical.

The name is a liability: PyPI 'clade' (v4.1) and npm 'clade' are taken; 'Clade' is a live typo/phonetic collision with 'Claude' (GitHub returns Clade.agent = Claude Agent SDK), which for a Claude Code plugin is a trademark-confusion and search-discoverability problem. The fallbacks are no better: Cultivar is Pinecone's skill-testing tool in the same space, Rootstock is a blockchain, Lockstep is a company (and a Pawl/Hermetic candidate), Provenir is a fintech, Granary/Steward/Orchard are taken on PyPI and npm.

Twelve-month defensibility is low on every visible piece: Hermes has an open request to adopt environment-probing review (#107914) and already has provenance, pins, ledger, rollback and staging; OpenClaw already has hash-bound proposals with a stale state; Letta ships git-backed memory diff/rollback; qvr/kendex/skillpm/skills-lock own lockfile/outdated/audit; Agent Plugins 1.0 defers registry/provenance/dependencies to a future spec the AAIF consortium will write. What remains unique (receipt-quorum federation, overlays) is the least-demanded piece and the last to ship.

Scope for 1-3 people: seven harness adapters on substrates with weekly breaking changes (Hermes 947 commits in four days, DSH 14 pre-release tags in 12 days), a registry/hub with signing and yank propagation, a drift testbed on Harbor, a retirement-policy experiment with 7 arms × 5 seeds, a VOI experiment, an audit of ≥20 volunteer stores, and a paper — in 3 months, with the MVP alone containing ~10 subsystems in 14 days. The federation additionally requires identity infrastructure (receipts are HMAC'd with a local key, so other environments cannot verify them; Sybil laundering is admitted) and turns the local receipt store into a sensitive asset.
improvements: Merge into Pawl (or absorb Pawl) and present the delta honestly: ship `outdated` (assertions), `dormant` (activation receipts) and `retire/archive` as three commands on Pawl's ledger; cut the registry/federation from the 3-month plan and keep the acceptance-record profile as the federation hook.

Replace text-extracted assertions with observed assertions: at write time, record which binaries, paths, ports, commands and repo refs the originating session actually exercised (from tool_use/tool_result in the transcript) and attach those as the artifact's `assertions[]`; probe those at load. This turns an extraction-precision problem into a coverage problem grounded in evidence the receipts already carry, and it is the one mechanism Hermes/OpenClaw cannot copy without your receipt layer.

Make staleness two-signal and report its precision: deterministic probe failure AND the 'loaded+followed then user-corrected' pattern (the free negative label). Publish assertion-stale precision against correction-labelled staleness on the audit cohort before promising AUC ≥0.85, and add non-assertion drift arms (API semantic drift, refactors, preference changes) to the C2 testbed so it is not circular.

Fix the pooling semantics: hierarchical/partial pooling with version as a random effect; pool only for the create-vs-patch and lineage-investment decisions; never pool across versions for retirement or safety of a specific served version; state this rule in the manifest and the `why` output.

Fix the VOI cold start: replace the ≈0 class prior with the user's own correction rate per artifact class, add an evidence-before-write rule (write only when the session had a verified terminal check or an explicit user correction), and adopt Grounding Agent Memory's read-only probe at write time so the first write is grounded, not blocked.

Solve randomized pairs on Claude Code before the MVP: use SessionStart additionalContext to inject the withheld skill's content on alternate sessions (with the load receipt marking the arm), and for memory use topic-file alternation; if neither yields ≥k eligible pairs in dogfooding, drop the randomized claim and market the advisory verdict honestly.

Rename to something free on PyPI/npm/crates and not adjacent to 'Claude' (Husbandry is free on PyPI only; check Provenir/Steward variants). Run the name against the twelve existing skill-package-manager names so the product is legible as 'lifecycle for what your agent learns', not 'yet another npm for skills'.

Cut adapters to Claude Code + Hermes read/write for v1 and one external seam (the OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin, which has zero third-party implementations and gives visibility); ship DSH/Codex/pi/ECC as read-only status/outdated adapters only after the conformance suite exists.

Put assertions in agentskills.io's `metadata:` string map (spec allows arbitrary keys; `skills-ref validate` passes) rather than a .clade/ sidecar, and file the key convention alongside the `evidence/` proposal; encode overlays as `overlays/<selector>/SKILL.md` inside the bundle so federation needs no new format.

Lead the demo with the two outputs nobody else prints today — the per-artifact `outdated` list with the failing assertion and the 'eligible but never loaded in N sessions' alarm — and drop the 'clade of 4 versions, wealth 1.9 → INCONCLUSIVE' minute, which demonstrates that the attribution engine has nothing to say.
artifact-lifecycle.best_idea_to_steal: Per-artifact machine-checkable environment assertions with scope tags (session | project | global) that do double duty: probed at every load they make staleness deterministic and immediate ('stale = one assertion failed', zero statistics, zero model calls, a legible `outdated` list naming the failing assertion), and at write time the same tags are the scope lint that keeps session-specific ports/paths/hosts out of global rules (hermes#89963/#416). Steal it in the observed-assertion form (derive assertions from what the originating session actually touched, not from regex over prose) and put it in agentskills.io `metadata:` so it rides the existing format.

artifact-lifecycle.lens: INFLUENCE — expected GitHub adoption (10k+ stars) and/or citation by the next RSI survey: timing vs the Sept-2026 RSI wave, first-100-user pool, 5-minute demo, vendor adopt/copy/crush risk (Anthropic/DeepSeek/Nous/Vercel), composition with OpenClaw/DSH/Claude Code/Reef, crispness and falsifiability of the paper claim, coverage of the five surveys' open problems.
artifact-lifecycle.justification: Timing and composition are the best of any stance: DSH (222k stars, Aug 13) explicitly deferred its evaluator; OpenClaw's skill_proposal_evaluate seam has zero third-party implementations; `claude plugin eval` (Sept 11) is a free Tier-3 backend; Reef #356–358 opened Sept 9; and the Aug–Sept skeptical wave (CTA +0.3pp, SkillsBench 0 vs +16.2, Demystifying 29.6→3.3%, EvoHarnessBench harness-induced forgetting, Adaptive Auto-Harness peak-then-decline) makes 'the failure is lifecycle/retention, not the proposer' the winning side of the argument. Survey coverage is the broadest I have seen: it answers 2607.07663's two emptiest problems (trustworthy accumulation, governance-grade measurement), 2507.21046's 'when not to evolve', the Self-Improvements survey's non-stationary testbed and shared-store trust protocol, and EvoHarnessBench's separate BWT/FWT retention protocol; the C1 audit ('median activation <10%') is a quotable number and the C2 Harbor drift testbed fills a gap every survey names. Demo minutes 1–2 (no API key, numbers from your own ~/.hermes and ~/.claude) are genuinely compelling. Against that: (1) the 'package manager' identity is already owned by vercel-labs/skills (31.6k stars, `npx skills add/list/update/remove`, 79 agents, skills.sh registry) and has been cloned by qvr (lockfile-first, SHA-immutable, scan, observe; 23 stars) plus at least eight zero-star 'agent skills package manager' repos — proof the metaphor alone earns nothing and that `clade install/publish` is redundant; (2) verified demand is one 38-reaction issue (hermes#12238, open since April with 6 comments — unbuilt for five months) and 0–1-reaction issues (#96704, #82056, #105770, #95976; prime#1208 closed), a first-100 pool of dozens; (3) the cheapest wedge features (truncation receipt, backup/version control, pending-queue alarm, curator aging) are exactly what Anthropic and Nous will absorb from their own trackers, and Letta already ships git-tracked MemFS; (4) the honest verdict for most artifacts is INCONCLUSIVE by the design's own simulation (+10pp detected 11% at N=40), canary alternation is a UX poison pill on single-user CLIs, and the federation pooling that fixes power lands in month 3 with no users; (5) scope — 7 adapters on harnesses that break plugins weekly, 7 record formats, 10 components, DSSE/in-toto/OTel/agentskills.io standards work, a Reef recipe, a Harbor task family and a three-concept paper — for 1–3 people in 3 months. P(10k stars in 12 months) ≈ 12%; P(citation by the next RSI survey) ≈ 45%, resting almost entirely on the C1 audit numbers and the C2 drift testbed, which are separable from the product. Net: the strongest survey-facing design, a mid-probability product.
