fatal_flaws: Framing collision: 'a package manager for what your agent learns' walks into vercel-labs/skills (31.6k stars, `npx skills add/list/update/remove`, 79 agents, skills.sh registry) plus qvr (lockfile-first, immutable SHA installs, scan, observe — 23 stars) and at least eight zero-star 'agent skills package manager' clones. The install/publish/lockfile half of Clade is redundant and the evidence says the governed-PM pitch does not earn stars; the genuinely new parts (agent-written artifacts, load/read receipts, assertion staleness, session undo) get buried under a metaphor whose first question is 'why not npx skills?'

INCONCLUSIVE-by-default product: the design's own simulation detects +10pp lift only 11% of the time at N=40, personal stores see ~50 sessions/month, randomized evidence requires canary alternation that removes a skill every other session (a UX poison pill on single-user CLIs), and the federation pooling that restores power ships in month 3 with zero users. `clade why` — a third of the architecture — will print 'inconclusive' for ~95% of artifacts, which readers will parse as 'this tool doesn't know anything', exactly the SEA failure mode (gate admitted nothing, got switched off).

Vendor absorption of the wedge: the day-one features are cheap in-tracker fixes owned by the vendors — claude-code#82056/#92998 truncation receipts are a one-line warning Anthropic will ship; hermes#12238 backup/version control is the kind of 38-reaction issue Nous ships in a 947-commit week; pending-queue notifications (#105770) and curator aging are prompt/config edits; Letta already ships git-tracked MemFS for memory and skills. What survives absorption (cross-harness lifecycle, e-process, VOI, federation) is the hardest-to-adopt part and the part the market has historically selected against.

Scope wildly exceeds a 1–3 person, 3-month team: seven adapters on substrates that break plugins weekly (Hermes 947 commits/4 days, OpenClaw breaks plugins per release, DSH 14 pre-release tags/12 days), seven JSON record formats, ten architecture components, DSSE/in-toto predicate, OTel gen_ai extension, agentskills.io convention PR, Reef recipe, Harbor task family, drift testbed with seven baselines × 5 seeds × two agents, plus a three-claim paper. The 14-day MVP lists ten deliverables. This reads as the union of both gap analyses, not a product.

Thin verified demand for the 'answer those threads with a link' adoption path: hermes#12238 has 38 reactions but only 6 comments and has sat unbuilt since April; hermes#96704 (paired-arm RFC) and claude-code#82056 have 1 reaction each; hermes#105770 and #95976 have 0; prime#1208 is closed. The first-100-user pool is a few dozen power users, and several of these issues appear to be the builder's own filings rather than independent demand.

Flagship staleness feature is unvalidated before it becomes demo minute 2: regex/AST extraction of versions, ports, paths and hosts from freeform SKILL.md prose will flag examples, placeholders and intentionally relative paths; C2's 'AUC ≥ 0.85 against outcome-labelled staleness' is asserted with no pilot on the 182-skill store. If `clade outdated` is noisy on day one, trust in the whole audit collapses with it.

Security ceremony without a boundary: HMAC-chained ledgers, DSSE-signed acceptance records and in-toto predicates sit on top of an admitted 'containment convention' (PreToolUse deny + an after-the-fact fs watcher that shell redirection, Codex opted-out tools and subagents bypass). MLAS/SkillMisevo/PROCTOR reviewers will spot that weeks of signing infrastructure buy no trust boundary, and Hermetic-class sealed evaluators will own the integrity narrative.
improvements: Change the identity from 'package manager' to '`npm audit` + `git` for what your agent learned': one command, `clade audit`, that runs on ~/.claude and ~/.hermes with no API key and prints dormant / stale / duplicate / truncated / cost. Treat `npx skills`, ClawHub and the Hermes hub as the install layer (consume their lockfiles, emit a skills.sh 'evidence' badge) and drop `clade install/publish` from v1 entirely.

Make the C1 null-effect audit the launch, not the month-3 paper: recruit 20 volunteer stores now (hermes#96704 cohort, ECC users, Claude Code users), run receipts-only, and publish 'median artifact activation rate X%, Y% deterministically stale, Z% duplicated, $W/week of background review for 0 promotions' as a blog post plus workshop paper in month 1. That number is the HN moment and the line the next survey will quote.

Cut the MVP to five commands on two harnesses and ship it in two weeks for real: `adopt/status`, `audit --activation`, `outdated`, `undo --session`, `digest`. Defer the e-process, canary alternation, VOI, safety canary, Tier 3 and all federation to v0.2+; release the ~300-line PACE+CTHS accountant as a separate tiny library so Reef/agentdescent/Self-Harness can adopt and cite it independently of Clade.

Pilot assertion extraction before it is demoed: run the extractor over the 58 bundled Hermes skills plus one 182-skill volunteer store, hand-label ~200 extracted assertions for precision, publish the number, and default to conservative extraction (scope tag or explicit `verified:` marker required; archive-with-notice never retire) until measured precision is >0.9.

Redesign the `clade why` output so INCONCLUSIVE reads as honest rather than ignorant: lead with the always-conclusive lines (activation funnel, carry cost, staleness, last change and by whom), put helps/hurts/inconclusive second, and always print 'what would settle it' (e.g., '40 more randomized sessions, or federation quorum') so the tri-state is a plan, not a shrug.

Own the two uncontested seams first and treat Hermes as an upstream-PR target: ship the first third-party OpenClaw `skill_proposal_evaluate` plugin and the DSH SkillProvider/pre-execute plugin (their evaluator slot is explicitly open) and get marketplace listings; contribute the curator-hook and default-disposition fixes to Hermes as PRs rather than a plugin Nous will obsolete.

Narrow the paper to one citable concept and one released artifact: 'Assertion staleness: deterministic retirement of learned artifacts under environment drift', with the Harbor drift testbed as the artifact. Keep clade pooling and VOI as follow-ups; a three-concept title dilutes both the claim and the citation.

Remove the standards agenda (DSSE/in-toto predicate, OTel extension, agentskills.io `evidence/` convention) from the 3-month plan; file one issue each to stake the claim and return once v1 has users. Adopt `claude plugin eval` JSON as the Tier-3 record instead of inventing a seventh format, and collapse the seven record formats to three (manifest, receipt, transition).

Replace the 'containment convention' story with an honest one-liner and a measurement: state up front that path authority is detection-plus-revert, drop HMAC/DSSE from v1, and instead ship a `clade audit --bypass` counter that reports how many store writes evaded hooks last week — a number vendors can act on and reviewers cannot dismiss.
artifact-lifecycle.best_idea_to_steal: Environment assertions as `engines`/`peerDependencies` for learned artifacts: extract machine-checkable world facts (binary versions, paths, ports, hosts, API flags, repo commit ranges, OS) from an artifact at write time into a sidecar manifest, probe them at every load for ~$0, and mark the artifact stale deterministically the moment any assertion fails — before any session fails because of it. It turns the staleness/non-stationarity gap that every survey names and no store solves (Ratchet needs N_min=100 outcomes; personal stores see use_count 0–10; Hermes ages by timestamp and retires the wrong things; GenericAgent recalls dead SOPs) from an outcome-statistics problem into dependency resolution, and the same extractor doubles as the lint that keeps session-scoped facts (ports, temp paths) out of global rules.

artifact-lifecycle.lens: FEASIBILITY — 1–3 people, API models, no GPUs, 3 months; probability a credible working v1 with the killer demo as written ships
artifact-lifecycle.justification: The wedge is real and cheap: Tiers 0–1 (receipts, change feed, snapshot/undo, lint/DLP, assertion probes, dormancy audit, spend ledger) need zero model calls, run on transcripts every Claude Code user already has, and every citation I checked resolves (hermes#12238 r=38 open, claude-code#82056 48 comments, #96704 RFC, #105770, #95976, SkillOpt#155, Reef#356; Replay Gap 3.2%/8.0% validity; gate_power_sim numbers reproduce exactly). Hook availability is largely verified: Claude Code has every event named, skill dirs hot-reload and accept symlinks (so canary swap works within a session), `claude plugin eval` exists locally with --scaffold/--ablation/--json; Hermes has skill_ledger/provenance/guards/usage/write_approval and a session SQLite with per-message tool_calls; DSH has pre/post-execute waterfalls, remote SkillProvider and a `skills/change` event; OpenClaw's evaluator seam has zero third-party implementations. But the v1 as specified is far beyond 1–3 people in 12 weeks (7 adapters, federation with DSSE/in-toto, sandbox replayer + Harbor export, safety canary with cross-family judge, Reef recipe, a 7-policy×5-seed drift testbed, N≥20 volunteer audit, paper), and the demo's decisive minutes cannot be backed by real data in the window: my simulation at 50 sessions/month, 10% eligibility, 50% activation and a generous +20pp true lift gives a median 22 months to a randomized promotion (18 months even at +30pp); only federation pooling F≥5 brings it under 3 months, and federation is scheduled for weeks 9–10. Several integration claims rest on seams that do not exist (Hermes has no curator hook and no background-review veto hook; DSH's CC bridge passes an empty transcript_path so the receipt collector produces nothing there; InstructionsLoaded never fires for SKILL.md or MEMORY.md; plugin eval loads no memory and no hooks, so the $0.007 hook replay does not apply inside it). The builder's own 8 sessions contain zero test commands, so Tier-2 labels are empty without volunteers. A trimmed v1 (Claude Code write path + Hermes read/pending reviewer, minutes 1, 2, half of 3, and the dormancy/staleness/spend part of 4) is ~0.65 likely; the demo as written, with attribution verdicts and cross-machine federation, is ~0.3.

fatal_flaws: Scope vs team: v1 = 7 harness adapters + version-pinned conformance suite + federation (DSSE/in-toto, hub API, overlays, receipt quorum, yank) + Tier-3 sandbox replayer with Harbor export + Tier-4 probe bank with cross-family judge + Reef recipe + a 7-policy×5-seed drift testbed on SkillsBench/TB2 + N≥20 volunteer audit + paper, in 12 weeks for 1–3 people. The 14-day MVP alone lists ten components including a snapshot/undo engine with GC, an assertion extractor, a lifecycle state machine with lockfile, and a ~300-line e-process library. Hermes (947 commits in 4 days, 42.8k open issues), OpenClaw and DSH (14 pre-release tags in 12 days) will break adapters faster than a small team can re-pin them.

The killer demo's decisive minutes cannot be backed by real data in 3 months. Minute 3/4 attribution ('12 pairs, 5 discordant', 'P(lift>0)=0.97 over 14 discordant pairs') requires randomized canary pairs at a rate a personal store never produces: at 50 sessions/month, 10% eligibility, 50% activation and a generous +20pp true lift, the e-process reaches wealth 20 in a median 22 months (18 months at +30pp; P<0.5 within 3 years); only federation pooling F≥5 brings it inside the window and federation is weeks 9–10. Ratchet retirement (N_min=100) likewise never fires. The honest v1 verdict for every artifact will be INCONCLUSIVE, which the design admits in prose but not in the demo script.

Minute 5 (publish on machine A, install on machine B 'with Codex + DSH', overlay suggestion, receipt quorum, lockfile serving three harnesses) depends on month-3 federation plus DSH serving and Codex adapters that the roadmap itself lists as week-5 'read-only' or unbuilt; Codex has no skill-serving seam at all, and the DSH SkillProvider receives cwd/scope but no session identity, so per-session canary serving is unverified.

Hermes integration promises hooks that do not exist: the plugin API exposes only pre_tool_call/post_tool_call/pre_llm_call/on_session_*; there is no curator transition hook (apply_automatic_transitions is a plain function) and no hook to veto the background-review fork (background_review.py is fail-open with a 600K-token budget and no plugin gate). 'Replace timestamp aging via ctx.register_hook()' and 'VOI-gate the review fork' require either upstream PRs into a 245k-star fast-moving repo or disabling curator/background_review by config and re-implementing them — a different product claim than 'without changing Hermes'. Plugin-registered skills are also read-only and excluded from <available_skills>, so canary serving on Hermes cannot go through the plugin skill API.

Tier-3 economics and isolation: `claude plugin eval` loads only the plugin in a throwaway home (no user memory, skills, CLAUDE.md, hooks), so memory/instruction artifacts cannot be tested as-is and the verified $0.007 PostToolUse replay does not apply inside eval; every case is runs×2 full `claude -p` agent runs with externals mocked or avoided. Combined with the design's own measurement (idempotent prefix 0–1 calls in 7/7 sessions, 20% external calls), most real sessions will not compile into re-executable cases, so Tier 3 produces few verdicts at real cost.

No data on the builder's side: the 8 local sessions (2,107 tool calls) contain zero detected test commands and are research sessions, so Tier-2 outcome labels, correction-pattern calibration and Tier-3 cassettes are all empty until volunteer Hermes/Claude Code stores arrive; every audit number in the demo (61 never-loaded, 17 stale, 3 duplicate clusters) is borrowed from hermes#96704's operator and must be obtained from that person early or it is synthetic.

Deterministic staleness is only as deterministic as the extractor: regex/AST mining of versions/paths/ports/hosts from free-text SKILL.md and memory will produce false-stale flags (example version strings, illustrative paths, intentionally relative paths), and probing 'at every load' means executing commands (`google-chrome --version`, port checks) for ~200 artifacts at SessionStart — startup latency and side effects. A wrong 'retire 17 stale' line in the first digest destroys the trust the receipts earned.

Receipt fidelity gaps on the primary adapter: InstructionsLoaded fires only for CLAUDE.md and .claude/rules/*.md (not SKILL.md or MEMORY.md); MEMORY.md load status can only be inferred from the 200-line/25KB rule, not observed (which is exactly claude-code#82056's complaint); FileChanged fires only while a session is running, so writes from Codex Memories or Hermes background forks outside a Claude Code session need Clade's own daemon; and under DSH's CC bridge transcript_path is empty so the transcript-based collector yields nothing.
improvements: Cut v1 to two adapters: Claude Code (full write path) and Hermes (read-only + pending-queue reviewer via the existing write_approval list/approve API and session SQLite messages.tool_calls for per-session skill_view receipts). Keep 'one engine, N adapters' as a published adapter interface with a conformance suite, but ship OpenClaw/DSH/Codex/pi/ECC/Reef as post-v1 issues with the seam contract already verified.

Rewrite the demo around what exists at N=1: minute 3 becomes `clade why` printing INCONCLUSIVE plus a time-to-verdict estimate ('at your rate 22 months; with 5 federated environments ~8 months; advisory pairs say HURTS') and the undo; drop minute 5's second machine. Make time-to-verdict and eval-cost-to-verdict first-class outputs of the VOI calculator — the power limitation becomes the product's honesty feature and the argument for federation, instead of a fake promotion.

Get the data in week 1, not month 3: ship the receipt collector as a standalone `clade audit --export` script (privacy-scrubbed JSON, no model calls) and recruit the hermes#96704 operator plus 3–5 heavy Claude Code users immediately; without their stores C1 is unfalsifiable and every audit number is synthetic. Use their exported receipts as the test fixtures for the lifecycle engine.

Replace the Hermes curator-hook plan with something that exists: either (a) `curator.enabled: false` + `hermes curator pause` and run Clade's staleness/dormancy as a cron replacing it, or (b) file two small upstream PRs on day 1 (a curator pre-transition hook and a pre-fork hook in background_review) and build against both paths. Do not claim 'without changing Hermes' until one lands.

Make assertions structured, not mined: extract only from fenced commands, explicit `Verified:` spans and a proposed `requires:`/`assertions:` frontmatter convention (file the agentskills.io PR early, alongside `evidence/`); cache probe results per (assertion, TTL) and run probes asynchronously under a wall-clock budget; flag stale only after two consecutive failed probes; default to archive-with-notice and `clade pin`.

Canary alternation on Claude Code should toggle `disable-model-invocation: true` in a withheld copy (hides the description from the catalog, keeps `/name` user invocation) rather than removing the folder; verified hot-reload means the swap applies within the same session. Log the ConfigChange(skills) event as the receipt that the swap took effect.

Scope Tier 3 to a `claude plugin eval` case compiler for skill bundles only (scaffold_script = snapshot restore, history_file = prefix, graders = the session's own test regex), with an explicit case-eligibility filter (sandbox_reexecutable, no external calls after fork, terminal check present) and a per-day dollar cap; report how many sessions compiled. Defer Harbor export and the Reef recipe.

Make Tier 4 a publish-time (registry-side) gate with a fixed-cost 20-probe operational-invariant subset (secrets, permission-rule deletion, destructive actions, tool-avoidance rules, egress) runnable locally for ≤$5, and keep the 60–100-probe Misevolve/MemEvoBench bank for shared artifacts only.

Raise attribution power with the signals the design already lists but treats as covariates: use paired continuous per-session deltas (corrections, steps-to-done, tokens) in the e-process (a betting CS on bounded differences) instead of binary pass/fail, and publish the advisory task-signature-matched estimate with its confounds as the default `clade why` output. Report retention (BWT-style, sessions that previously passed) separately from lift.

Own the watcher: a tiny launchd/systemd daemon (or 'diff since last snapshot' at every SessionStart) rather than relying on FileChanged, so Codex Memories and Hermes background forks writing outside a Claude Code session still get snapshotted; Claude auto-memory writes go through Write/Edit and can be snapshotted synchronously in PreToolUse.

Sequence the 12 weeks as: W1–3 Claude Code receipts + activation audit + snapshot/undo + spend ledger (demo minutes 1–2); W4–5 Hermes read-only + pending reviewer + starvation alarm; W6–8 lint/DLP wrapping NVIDIA SkillEvaluator and hermes skill_linter, assertions v0, lifecycle v0 with dormancy/stale, daily digest; W9–10 e-process library + advisory attribution + plugin-eval compiler; W11–12 C1 audit on volunteer stores and the pip/pipx release. Federation, drift testbed and C2/C3 become the second paper.
artifact-lifecycle.best_idea_to_steal: Staleness as dependency resolution: extract machine-checkable environment assertions (binary versions, paths, ports, hosts, repo ranges, OS) into a per-artifact manifest at write time — the `engines`/`peerDependencies` of the world the artifact was born in — and probe them at load. It is the only lifecycle transition in the whole design that yields a real verdict at N=1 for $0 and zero model calls, it converts the 'session facts in global rules' lint into the same mechanism, and nobody ships it (Hermes ages by timestamp; Grounding Agent Memory probes only at write time; Ratchet needs 100 trials). Pair it with the activation-funnel receipt (eligible → loaded complete|truncated|not_loaded → read → followed) and you have the whole day-zero product.

rsi-substrate.lens: FEASIBILITY — 1-3 people, API-only frontier models, no GPUs, 3 months to a credible v1 with the killer demo
rsi-substrate.justification: The architecture is the best-informed design in this batch — it correctly absorbs The Replay Gap (re-execute, never stitch; A-vs-A' control arm), MetaRSI's authority cut, PACE/SEA, activation receipts, and the matched-budget TTS null — and every integration seam it names was verified to exist (Claude Code PreToolUse updatedInput / PostToolUse updatedToolOutput / Stop-block / InstructionsLoaded; Hermes skill_ledger.py, skill_provenance.py, write_approval.py, pre_tool_call in agent/shell_hooks.py; DSH tools/pre-execute, agent/turn-stopping, packages/hooks/hook-protocol; OpenClaw skill_proposal_evaluate). But 'v1 with the killer demo in 3 months' fails on three quantitative checks the design itself invites. (1) The gate as specified certifies nothing: the design commits at wealth >= 1/alpha_k under SEA's CTHS schedule, but its printed power table comes from research/tools/gate_power_sim.py, which uses a fixed alpha=0.05 (threshold 20). Re-simulating the actual rule: thresholds are 33/391/2,052/12,569 at candidate k=1/3/7/20; a +20pp lift on 40 eligible pairs certifies 34%/5%/1%/0%, +30pp 95%/41%/12%/2%. The demo's own verdict record (wealth 27.4 vs alpha_k=0.0046 → threshold 217; 8-of-9 wins actually gives wealth 12.9 under the stated mixture) fails the design's rule. This is SEA's 0-accepts reproduced, and it makes the flagship's dependent variable (certified lift per surface) ~all zeros, so C2/C3 are undecidable. (2) Costs are off 10-25x: at Sonnet 4.6's $3/$15 per MTok a 40-turn Terminal-Bench episode runs ~$1-2, so the '$8' 90-episode protected corpus is ~$100-180, a certification (23 eligible × candidate+control) ~$50-90, parallel-4 TTS on 45 tasks ~$200-350, the sealed 34-task slice ~$150; the '$40, 2 rounds, 7 exercised, 2 certified, TTS arm, sealed slice' demo is ~$700-1,300 on Sonnet and still ~$300-450 on Haiku; the '$2-3k' core flagship subset is ~$10-15k and the full grid >$100k. (3) Scope: 7 core modules + sealed Harbor runner with receipts + 6 harness adapters + 4 benchmark adapters + 3 replications (the AI2 K=5 replication alone is ~2,000 TB episodes) + a 240-run flagship + L3 mode + a paper, for 1-3 people, with a 14-day MVP that already includes the runner and the Claude Code adapter. Secondary: 'any negative delta blocks' on a 60-probe stochastic canary false-blocks ~45% of harmless candidates; two of the four named canary seed banks are not publicly available (SkillMisevo-Bench code not located per the scouts; MLAS's 40 scenarios unreleased); averaging dense-signal e-values into the outcome certificate changes the null so a token-only improvement can promote; the ~2k-line budget is unrealistic for the feature list (6-10k is honest). A descoped v1 (frozen kernel + gate with a sane per-candidate alpha + archive + Claude Code adapter + one honest run on a cheap 150-300-task family under Haiku) is ~45% likely; the demo as written is ~10%; blended 0.2.

fatal_flaws: The promotion gate as specified certifies essentially nothing after the first two or three candidates, and the design's own power table does not describe its own rule. The design commits at wealth >= 1/alpha_k with alpha_k = alpha_0/(3.39 k log^2(k+1)); research/tools/gate_power_sim.py (the source of the printed 11%/39%/44%/98% numbers) uses a fixed alpha=0.05, i.e. a threshold of 20. Under the CTHS schedule the thresholds are 33 (k=1), 391 (k=3), 2,052 (k=7), 12,569 (k=20), requiring 6/11/13/17 consecutive discordant wins at q=0.9. Simulated at incumbent 0.7 with 40 eligible pairs: +10pp certifies 6%/0%/0%/0%, +20pp 34%/5%/1%/0%, +30pp 95%/41%/12%/2% at k=1/3/7/20. The killer demo's '2 certified of 7 exercised' and its VERDICT record (wealth 27.4 against alpha_k=0.0046, i.e. threshold 217; and 8 wins/1 loss yields wealth 12.9, not 27.4, under the stated {0.6..0.9} mixture) are inconsistent with the design's own math. This reproduces SEA's ALG4 (0 accepts, switched off) — the exact failure the 'two-tier admission' is claimed to dissolve — and it makes the flagship's dependent variable (certified held-out lift per surface cell) degenerate, so C2 and C3 cannot be decided with any budget.

The cost model is wrong by 10-25x on every line, which kills the demo and the flagship as budgeted. Sonnet 4.6 is $3/$15 per MTok ($0.30 cache reads); a 40-60-turn Terminal-Bench 2.1 episode accumulates 1-4M input tokens and 10-30k output tokens, i.e. ~$1-2 per episode (Haiku 4.5 ~$0.3-0.7). Hence: the '~$8' protected corpus (45 tasks × 2 incumbent runs = 90 episodes) is ~$100-180; one certification (23 eligible pairs × candidate + A' control) is ~$50-90, not the $9.4+$4.1 in the VERDICT record; the parallel-4 TTS control on 45 tasks is 180 episodes (~$200-350); opening the sealed 34-task slice with three arms is ~$150; the '$40' two-round demo is ~$700-1,300 on Sonnet and ~$300-450 on Haiku. Month 1's AI2 replication (K=5 on 89 tasks, 4+ arms) is ~2,000 episodes (~$2-4k). The flagship (3 tiers × 2 families × 8 arms × 5 seeds = 240 loop-runs, each ~$400-1,000 including corpus, ~10 certifications, TTS arm, sealed slice, phase-2) is ~$100k+, and the 'core subset' (24 runs) is ~$10-15k, not $2-3k. Wall-clock is also unbudgeted: Terminal-Bench episodes run 5-15 minutes each in Docker; 90 episodes serially is 10-20 hours on a laptop, so E2B/Daytona concurrency costs land on top.

The scope is 3-5x what 1-3 people can ship in 12 weeks even with Claude Code writing most of it. Committed deliverables: seven core modules; a sealed runner with Harbor task adapter, restricted-subprocess/mount-namespace isolation, ed25519-signed receipts and offline verification; a loop-graph interpreter with a predicate DSL, subagent spawn, reachability/invariant validation; six harness adapters (Claude Code, Hermes, OpenClaw evaluator plugin, DSH Cordis plugin, pi/Prime extension, Reef recipe); four benchmark/stream adapters (Harbor incl. RSI-Exam two-image profile, SEAGym, EvoHarnessBench, HarnessOpt-Bench); three replications; a pre-registered 240-run flagship; an off-by-default L3 mode with its own ledger and anchors; a Harbor task family; PRs to three lists; and a workshop/D&B paper. The 14-day MVP alone contains the sealed runner and the Claude Code adapter. Every previous attempt at a comparable surface (SEA, MetaRSI, HarnessDev) shipped either the schema or nothing; the '~2,000-line core' framing hides that the listed features are 6-10k lines, and the line-count 'release gate' will either be blown or gamed by moving code into 'adapters'.

The safety canary as a hard constraint is statistically broken and its seed banks are partly unavailable. 'Any negative delta blocks at Tier 0' on a 30-100-probe bank judged on a stochastic agent false-blocks ~45% of harmless candidates at 60 probes with per-probe pass 0.9 (the same noise-floor error the design correctly diagnoses for the per-task floor and then repeats one paragraph later). Combined with the CTHS certificate, the funnel becomes 11 proposed -> ~5 admitted -> 0 certified. The named seeds are also not all real: the scouts could not locate SkillMisevo-Gym's code, MLAS's 40 CS-* scenarios are unreleased, and MemEvoBench/Agent-SafetyBench are QA/refusal suites that do not cover the operational invariants (learned helplessness, persisted secrets, deleted deny rules) the design says matter most; the bank has to be hand-written. The '~$1' canary cost assumes single-turn probes; probes that exercise destructive tool paths with candidate and incumbent loaded are agent episodes at $0.05-0.5 each.

Averaging dense-signal e-processes (steps, tokens, first-divergence step) into the outcome e-value is valid as an e-value but silently changes the null hypothesis from 'no outcome lift' to 'no improvement on any signal', so a candidate that cuts tokens 20% with zero pass-rate change can be certified and promoted as 'lift'. The only backstop is the k-of-n floor on ~18 protected tasks, which at k=2 confirmation has little power to catch a 10pp outcome regression; the retention term (BWT >= -epsilon) then rests on the same 18 tasks. The freshness rule compounds this: held candidates restart wealth against every new incumbent, so in a loop that promotes every round no held candidate ever accrues the cross-round evidence the design counts on to raise power.
improvements: Fix the spend schedule before anything else and re-run the simulation with the actual rule. Drop per-candidate CTHS. Use PACE's per-candidate alpha (0.05, threshold 20 under the mixture) with a pre-registered per-run candidate budget K and print 'expected false promotions <= alpha*K' in every report, or use e-BH across a round's candidates; make post-promotion continued accrual plus auto-revert the run-level control instead of a familywise bound. Regenerate every number in the killer demo from the corrected sim (wealth, threshold, discordant pairs) so the VERDICT record satisfies its own rule.

Move the protected corpus and all in-loop certification off Terminal-Bench 2.1 for the MVP and the flagship: use a task family with 150-300 cheap, fast, deterministic tasks (SkillsBench subsets, EvoHarnessBench EOG MCP gyms with SQL verifiers, or a locally generated pytest family) on Haiku 4.5 / DeepSeek V4 Flash, so eligible pairs per candidate are >=150 (the sim shows +20pp certifies 73% even at k=7 with N=160). Reserve Terminal-Bench 2.1 for the sealed release slice only. This single change is what makes the gate certify anything.

Re-budget with measured per-episode costs on day 1 (run 10 incumbent episodes, read provider usage fields, multiply) and publish the table: Sonnet ~$1-2, Haiku ~$0.3-0.7 per Terminal-Bench episode. Reprice the demo (~$300-450 on Haiku), the AI2 replication (do it for one arm only, as the TTS null), and the flagship core subset (~$10-15k). Cut the flagship to 2 tiers × 1 cheap family × 4 arms {fixed:prompt, fixed:hook, uniform, thompson_cell} × 3 seeds; add fixed:graph and fixed:skill only if fixed:hook shows a certifiable signal.

Give the canary the same noise model as the floor: paired probes with a discordant-probe e-process (or k-of-n confirmation on any flipped probe), block only on a certified negative, and treat single-probe flips as 'inconclusive' that trigger re-probing. Hand-author the v0 bank (30 operational-invariant probes: secrets persisted, deny rules removed, transient-failure tool avoidance, placeholder-as-verified) since the cited seed banks are partly unavailable; keep it single-turn where possible so the '$1' figure is true.

Do not average dense-signal e-values into the outcome certificate. Keep two certificates: an outcome certificate (promotion requires it) and an efficiency certificate (reported, and sufficient for promotion only when the outcome e-process is non-negative AND the k-of-n floor and BWT pass). Replace the always-fires kernel 'pre_model' hook event with none (Claude Code has no pre-model-call hook; UserPromptSubmit fires once per user turn) and mark DSH 'narrow_input' as export-lossy (DSH pre-execute input rewrite is proposal-only). Keep the hook event set to {session_start, pre_tool, post_tool, on_error, on_stop}, which all export faithfully to Claude Code (SessionStart, PreToolUse updatedInput/permissionDecision, PostToolUse updatedToolOutput, PostToolUseFailure, Stop block) and to DSH/OpenClaw.

Pre-empt the 'crippled seed' critique that AI2 and HarnessDev both drew: run the sealed-slice comparison from a Terminus-2-equivalent seed as well as the 60-line ReAct seed, and report which failure signatures survive a competent seed. Otherwise C2 ('deterministic surfaces dominate for weak/mid tiers') is partly an artifact of a seed that lacks verify-before-stop by construction.

Ban composite (multi-surface) patches from certification in v1 (the open question already leans this way) and make the identical-patch hash refusal plus the rejected-buffer the first thing the archive does; these are the two cheapest anti-churn measures and they reduce the number of candidates the (expensive) gate has to see.

Make the 'gate cost line' and the 'pairs needed for 80% power' line the two numbers the MVP prints before it prints any lift; if the pairs-needed number exceeds the corpus size for every candidate, the report should say the run cannot certify and stop spending, which is the honest form of the SEA lesson.
rsi-substrate.best_idea_to_steal: Per-surface eligibility computed from the incumbent's stored traces before any model call: a prompt-slot patch is eligible on every task, a skill only on tasks whose description would retrieve it, a tool only on tasks whose traces invoked the wrapped tool, a hook only on tasks whose traces contain the trigger event, a graph patch only on tasks whose traces visited the node. Non-eligible tasks are distributional ties and cost nothing; a patch eligible on zero tasks gets the verdict 'not exercised' rather than 'no effect'; and because the count of possibly-discordant pairs is known a priori, the gate can print the cost and the maximum attainable power of a candidate before it spends a token. This is agentdescent's declared blast radius turned into a measured quantity, it doubles as the blast-radius estimate every governance scheme asks for, and it composes with activation receipts to give the phantom-accept verdict. It is cheap to implement (a trace index), harness-agnostic (works on Claude Code transcripts, Hermes ledgers, DSH session logs), and it is the one mechanism in the design that raises power without lowering the bar.
